rules.heading: Using system fonts
rules.rule: Use Dynamic Type text styles or scaled custom fonts instead of fixed point sizes.
rules.anti_pattern: .font(.system(size: 14)) or Font.custom("Name", fixedSize: 14) without Dynamic Type scaling
rules.fix_swiftui: Use semantic text styles like `.font(.body)` / `.font(.subheadline)`, or `Font.custom("Name", size: 14, relativeTo: .body)` / `@ScaledMetric`.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)` or `UIFontMetrics.default.scaledFont(for:)` with `adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`.
rules.quote: Using text styles with the system fonts also ensures support for Dynamic Type and larger accessibility type sizes (where available), which let people choose the text size that works for them.

rules.heading: Ensuring legibility
rules.rule: Avoid Ultralight, Thin, and Light font weights, especially for small text.
rules.anti_pattern: .fontWeight(.ultraLight), .fontWeight(.thin), or .fontWeight(.light)
rules.fix_swiftui: Prefer `.regular`, `.medium`, `.semibold`, or `.bold` font weights for legible UI text.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `.regular`, `.medium`, `.semibold`, or `.bold` weight.
rules.quote: For example, if you’re using system-provided fonts, prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold font weights, and avoid Ultralight, Thin, and Light font weights, which can be difficult to see, especially when text is small.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Respect the systemwide appearance setting instead of forcing light/dark mode or adding an app-specific appearance toggle.
rules.anti_pattern: .preferredColorScheme(.light) / .preferredColorScheme(.dark) or overrideUserInterfaceStyle locking the app
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove `.preferredColorScheme(...)` so the app adapts to system Light/Dark/Auto modes (only keep dark-only for immersive media viewing).
rules.fix_uikit: Remove `overrideUserInterfaceStyle` unless presenting immersive media.
rules.quote: Avoid offering an app-specific appearance setting.

rules.heading: Dark Mode colors
rules.rule: Use adaptive semantic system colors or Asset Catalog Color Sets instead of hardcoded RGB/hex color values.
rules.anti_pattern: Color(red: ..., green: ..., blue: ...) or UIColor(red: ...) hardcoded in views
rules.fix_swiftui: Use semantic colors (`.primary`, `.secondary`, `Color(.systemBackground)`) or an Asset Catalog Color Set with Light, Dark, and High Contrast variants.
rules.fix_uikit: Use dynamic `UIColor.label`, `UIColor.systemBackground`, or a named Color Set in Assets.xcassets.
rules.quote: Avoid using hard-coded color values or colors that don’t adapt.

rules.heading: Vision
rules.rule: Every icon-only button or toolbar item needs a descriptive accessible label for VoiceOver and Voice Control.
rules.anti_pattern: Button { ... } label: { Image(systemName: "...") } without Label or .accessibilityLabel
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `Label("Action", systemImage: "...").labelStyle(.iconOnly)` or attach `.accessibilityLabel("Action")`.
rules.fix_uikit: Set `button.accessibilityLabel` or provide a `title` on `UIBarButtonItem`.
rules.quote: Describe your app’s interface and content for VoiceOver.

rules.heading: Mobility
rules.rule: Interactive controls on iOS/iPadOS should have a 44x44 pt hit target (minimum 28x28 pt).
rules.anti_pattern: Explicit small frame (< 28 pt) on a tappable control without expanded contentShape/padding
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)` and `.contentShape(Rectangle())` around compact icons.
rules.fix_uikit: Keep interactive control frames >= 44x44 pt or override `point(inside:with:)`.
rules.quote: Offer sufficiently sized controls.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid UIScreen.main.bounds and fixed display widths; build layouts with size classes, safe areas, and window bounds.
rules.anti_pattern: UIScreen.main.bounds used to size views or branch layout
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `@Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass)`, `ViewThatFits`, `NavigationSplitView`, or `GeometryReader` / containerRelativeFrame.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `traitCollection.horizontalSizeClass`, `view.bounds`, and `layoutMarginsGuide`.
rules.quote: Use size classes, layout margins, and safe area insets to lay out controls and content. Avoid fixed widths and display-specific dependencies.

rules.heading: Device poses
rules.rule: Branch layouts on size classes rather than device idiom (`userInterfaceIdiom == .phone`).
rules.anti_pattern: UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .phone deciding single vs. split layout
rules.fix_swiftui: Read `@Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass)` (`.compact` vs `.regular`) so iPad multitasking and iPhone Duo inner displays adapt automatically.
rules.fix_uikit: Check `traitCollection.horizontalSizeClass` instead of `UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom`.
rules.quote: Supporting the device’s various poses doesn’t mean designing a custom layout for each one: instead, use size classes so your app adapts naturally as it changes size.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid hardcoding phone screen widths (e.g. `.frame(width: 390)`) that break resizing across devices and poses.
rules.anti_pattern: Fixed frame width matching an iPhone viewport (320–440 pt)
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` or `.frame(maxWidth: 600)` with flexible padding and layout margins.
rules.fix_uikit: Pin constraints to `safeAreaLayoutGuide` or `readableContentGuide` instead of fixed width constants.
rules.quote: Avoid fixed widths and display-specific dependencies.

rules.heading: Where the material belongs
rules.rule: Apply Liquid Glass only to floating controls/navigation, never to content-layer rows, cards, or backgrounds; handle Reduce Transparency.
rules.anti_pattern: .glassEffect(...) applied to list cells/cards or without checking accessibilityReduceTransparency on custom glass
rules.fix_swiftui: Keep `.glassEffect(...)` on floating controls grouped with `GlassEffectContainer`, and use standard materials or opaque fills in the content layer.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `UIGlassEffect` / `UIGlassContainerEffect` only for floating functional controls.
rules.quote: Don't use Liquid Glass in the content layer.

rules.heading: Review checklist
rules.rule: Avoid painting an opaque background beneath a toolbar or tab bar; let the system material and scroll edge effect separate controls from content.
rules.anti_pattern: .toolbarBackground(Color..., for: .navigationBar / .tabBar) with opaque color
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove custom opaque `.toolbarBackground(...)` so system Liquid Glass and scroll edge effects work automatically.
rules.fix_uikit: Avoid replacing `UIBarAppearance.backgroundColor` with an opaque fill unless required by media chrome.
rules.quote: Content fades and blurs where it meets a bar instead of colliding with it, and no solid or semi-opaque background color is painted beneath the bar in place of the material

rules.heading: SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit
rules.rule: Remove temporary `UIDesignRequiresCompatibility` compatibility opt-out keys when targeting current SDKs.
rules.anti_pattern: UIDesignRequiresCompatibility set to true/YES in Info.plist
rules.fix_swiftui: Adopt standard system controls and remove `UIDesignRequiresCompatibility` from `Info.plist`.
rules.fix_uikit: Audit custom bar appearances and remove `UIDesignRequiresCompatibility` from `Info.plist`.
rules.quote: Apple documents it as temporary, and the system ignores it when you build for iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, or macOS 27 or later.

rules.heading: Referring to Apple Pay
rules.rule: Never use the Apple logo glyph (U+F8FF / ) in text or to hand-draw an Apple Pay button (App Review 4.9 rejection).
rules.anti_pattern: \u{F8FF} or literal  glyph next to Pay
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `PayWithApplePayButton` from PassKit/SwiftUI and write 'Apple Pay' in plain text.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `PKPaymentButton(paymentButtonType:paymentButtonStyle:)`.
rules.quote: Never use the Apple logo to represent the name Apple in text.

rules.heading: Role
rules.rule: Never assign the primary/default action role to a destructive button.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(role: .destructive) paired with .keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction) or .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
rules.fix_swiftui: Keep destructive buttons distinct (`.destructive` role) and assign `.defaultAction` / prominent style only to non-destructive primary actions.
rules.fix_uikit: Do not set `preferredAction` on a `UIAlertAction` whose style is `.destructive`.
rules.quote: Don’t assign the primary role to a button that performs a destructive action, even if that action is the most likely choice.

rules.heading: Cognitive
rules.rule: Respect Reduce Motion when using repeating or prominent custom animations.
rules.anti_pattern: .repeatForever(...) animation without checking @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)
rules.fix_swiftui: Read `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion` and disable or replace repeating/zoom motion with subtle fades when true.
rules.fix_uikit: Check `UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled` before starting repeating or spring animations.
rules.quote: When this setting is active, ensure your app or game responds by reducing automatic and repetitive animations, including zooming, scaling, and peripheral motion.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use adaptive system background colors instead of hardcoded `.white` or `.black` view backgrounds.
rules.anti_pattern: .background(Color.white) or .background(.white) / .background(Color.black)
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `Color(.systemBackground)` / `Color(.secondarySystemBackground)` on iOS or `.background(.background)` so Dark Mode and elevated surfaces adapt automatically.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `UIColor.systemBackground` or `UIColor.secondarySystemGroupedBackground`.
rules.quote: Prefer the system background colors.

rules.heading: Offering Apple Pay
rules.rule: Never build a custom button displaying 'Apple Pay'; use Apple's system Apple Pay button API (App Review 4.9).
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Apple Pay") or Button("Pay with Apple Pay") instead of PayWithApplePayButton
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `PayWithApplePayButton` from PassKit/SwiftUI instead of a custom `Button`.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `PKPaymentButton(paymentButtonType:paymentButtonStyle:)`.
rules.quote: If you use a custom button to start the Apple Pay payment process, make sure your custom button doesn’t display “Apple Pay” or the Apple Pay logo.

rules.heading: Using the system-provided buttons
rules.rule: Use `SignInWithAppleButton` / `ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton` instead of hand-building a 'Sign in with Apple' button.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Sign in with Apple") instead of SignInWithAppleButton
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `SignInWithAppleButton(.signIn) { ... } onCompletion: { ... }` from `AuthenticationServices`.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton(authorizationButtonType:authorizationButtonStyle:)`.
rules.quote: When you use the system-provided APIs to create a Sign in with Apple button, you get the following advantages.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid showing an alert immediately on app launch or view appearance.
rules.anti_pattern: Triggering an alert flag directly inside .onAppear { showAlert = true }
rules.fix_swiftui: Show inline status, placeholder/cached content, or `ContentUnavailableView` instead of popping an alert on appear.
rules.fix_uikit: Display an inline banner or `UIContentUnavailableConfiguration` instead of presenting `UIAlertController` in `viewDidAppear`.
rules.quote: Avoid showing an alert when your app starts.

rules.heading: Buttons
rules.rule: Use specific action-verb titles (e.g., 'Delete', 'Save') instead of vague 'OK' or 'Submit' button titles in alerts.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("OK") or Button("Submit") inside an action alert
rules.fix_swiftui: Replace `Button("OK")` / `Button("Submit")` with a specific verb naming the outcome (e.g., `Button("Delete", role: .destructive)`).
rules.fix_uikit: Give `UIAlertAction` a specific verb title unless the alert is purely informational.
rules.quote: Avoid using OK as the default button title unless the alert is purely informational.

rules.heading: Vertical controls
rules.rule: Group toolbar items with `ToolbarItemGroup` instead of inserting manual `Spacer()` views in `.toolbar`.
rules.anti_pattern: Spacer() placed inside .toolbar { ... } or ToolbarItemGroup { ... }
rules.fix_swiftui: Group related actions with `ToolbarItemGroup` and let the system manage spacing across horizontal and iPhone Duo vertical bars.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `UIBarButtonItemGroup` instead of manual `.fixedSpace` spacers.
rules.quote: Group related toolbar items instead of spacing them manually.

rules.heading: Where the material belongs
rules.rule: Never apply `.glassEffect` to rows, cards, or items inside `List`, `ForEach`, or `LazyVStack` (content layer).
rules.anti_pattern: .glassEffect(...) called inside List { ... } or ForEach { ... }
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove `.glassEffect(...)` from list rows/cards; use standard materials or opaque grouped fills in the content layer.
rules.fix_uikit: Remove `UIGlassEffect` from table/collection cells; reserve it for floating bars and controls.
rules.quote: Don't use Liquid Glass in the content layer.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep top-level tab bars to 5 or fewer tabs to avoid a hidden 'More' overflow tab on compact screens.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView containing 6+ tabs without sidebar adaptation
rules.fix_swiftui: Reduce top-level tabs to <= 5, or adopt `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)` / `NavigationSplitView` for deeper hierarchies.
rules.fix_uikit: Keep `UITabBarController.viewControllers` to <= 5 items or use `UISplitViewController`.
rules.quote: Avoid overflow tabs.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Include a visible grabber on resizable sheets with multiple detents (aids both discoverability and VoiceOver).
rules.anti_pattern: .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) combined with .presentationDragIndicator(.hidden)
rules.fix_swiftui: Set `.presentationDragIndicator(.visible)` (or omit `.hidden`) on multi-detent sheets.
rules.fix_uikit: Set `sheetPresentationController.prefersGrabberVisible = true` when multiple detents are configured.
rules.quote: Include a grabber in a resizable sheet.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Support text enlargement to at least 200% (140% watchOS) via Dynamic Type or custom UI.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Hello").font(.system(size: 14)) // Fixed size, ignores Dynamic Type
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Hello").font(.body) // Uses Dynamic Type automatically
rules.fix_uikit: label.adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true; label.font = UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body)
rules.quote: Make sure people can adjust the size of your text or icons to make them more legible, visible, and comfortable to read.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Use minimum 11pt (iOS/iPadOS) or 10pt (macOS) for custom type; default 17pt or 13pt respectively.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Label").font(.system(size: 8)) // Below minimum on iOS
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").font(.system(size: 11)) // Meets iOS minimum
rules.fix_uikit: UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 11) // Meets iOS minimum
rules.quote: Each platform has different default and minimum sizes for system-defined type styles to promote readability.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Ensure 4.5:1 contrast for text ≤17pt, 3:1 for ≥18pt or bold text.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Info").foregroundColor(.gray).background(.lightGray) // Insufficient contrast
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Info").foregroundStyle(.black).background(.white)
rules.fix_uikit: label.textColor = UIColor.label; label.backgroundColor = UIColor.systemBackground
rules.quote: To ensure all information in your app is legible, it's important that there's enough contrast between foreground text and icons and background colors.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Use system colors to automatically adapt to Increase Contrast and Dark Mode.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Label").foregroundColor(Color(red: 0.5, green: 0.5, blue: 0.5))
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").foregroundStyle(.primary)
rules.fix_uikit: label.textColor = UIColor.label
rules.quote: These colors have their own accessible variants that automatically adapt when people adjust their color preferences, such as enabling Increase Contrast or toggling between the light and dark appearances.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Use shapes, icons, or text labels in addition to color to convey state and function.
rules.anti_pattern: Circle().fill(status ? .green : .red) // Color-only status indicator
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Image(systemName: status ? "checkmark.circle.fill" : "xmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(status ? .green : .red); Text(status ? "Success" : "Error") }
rules.fix_uikit: imageView.image = UIImage(systemName: status ? "checkmark.circle.fill" : "xmark.circle.fill"); label.text = status ? "Success" : "Error"
rules.quote: Offer visual indicators, like distinct shapes or icons, in addition to color to help people perceive differences in function and changes in state.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Provide captions, subtitles, audio descriptions, or transcripts for all audio/video content.
rules.anti_pattern: AVPlayerViewController(player: player) // No captions or subtitles configured
rules.fix_uikit: player.currentItem?.asset.mediaSelectionGroup(forMediaCharacteristic: .legible) // Enable subtitle tracks
rules.quote: It's important that dialogue and crucial information about your app or game isn't communicated through audio alone.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Pair audio cues with haptic feedback for users with hearing loss or audio disabled.
rules.anti_pattern: AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1000) // Audio-only feedback
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Action") { action() }.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: isSuccess)
rules.fix_uikit: let feedback = UINotificationFeedbackGenerator(); feedback.notificationOccurred(.success); AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1000)
rules.quote: If your interface conveys information through audio cues — such as a success chime, error sound, or game feedback — consider pairing that sound with matching haptics for people who can't perceive the audio or have their audio turned off.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Ensure controls meet minimum size: 28×28pt (iOS/iPadOS) or 20×20pt (macOS).
rules.anti_pattern: Button("X").frame(width: 20, height: 20) // Below iOS minimum
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("X").frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
rules.fix_uikit: button.widthAnchor.constraint(greaterThanOrEqualToConstant: 44).isActive = true
rules.quote: Strive to meet the recommended minimum control size for each platform to ensure controls and menus are comfortable for all when tapping and clicking.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Add ~12pt padding around bezel elements, ~24pt around borderless elements to prevent mis-taps.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack(spacing: 2) { Button("A"); Button("B") } // Insufficient spacing
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack(spacing: 24) { Button("A"); Button("B") }
rules.fix_uikit: stackView.spacing = 24
rules.quote: Include enough padding between elements to reduce the chance that someone taps the wrong control.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Provide button/menu alternatives for all gesture-based interactions.
rules.anti_pattern: .gesture(DragGesture().onEnded { _ in dismiss() }) // Gesture-only dismiss
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { .swipeActions { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { delete() } }; Button("Done") { dismiss() } }
rules.fix_uikit: UISwipeGestureRecognizer + UIButton for same action
rules.quote: Make sure your UI's core functionality is accessible through more than one type of physical interaction.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Support Full Keyboard Access; avoid overriding system keyboard shortcuts.
rules.anti_pattern: override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) { /* custom override */ } // Breaks system shortcuts
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Action").keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)
rules.fix_uikit: addKeyCommand(UIKeyCommand(input: UIKeyCommand.inputEscape, modifierFlags: [], action: #selector(dismiss)))
rules.quote: Avoid overriding system-defined keyboard shortcuts and evaluate your app to ensure it works well with Full Keyboard Access.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Avoid auto-dismissing views; use explicit user actions to dismiss instead.
rules.anti_pattern: DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 2) { dismiss() } // Auto-dismiss
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Dismiss") { dismiss() } // Explicit action
rules.fix_uikit: addSubview(dismissButton) // User-triggered dismiss
rules.quote: Views and controls that auto-dismiss on a timer can be problematic for people who need longer to process information, and for people who use assistive technologies that require more time to traverse the interface.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Never autoplay audio/video without user controls; provide discoverable play/pause buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: AVPlayer(url: url); player.play() // Autoplay without user control
rules.fix_swiftui: VideoPlayer(player: player) // Includes built-in controls
rules.fix_uikit: playerViewController.showsPlaybackControls = true
rules.quote: Avoid autoplaying audio and video content without also providing controls to start and stop it.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Respect Reduce Motion setting; avoid rapid animations, zooms, and depth changes.
rules.anti_pattern: withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.1)) { scale = 2 } // Fast animation ignores Reduce Motion
rules.fix_swiftui: if !UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled { withAnimation { scale = 2 } }
rules.fix_uikit: if !UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled { UIView.animate(withDuration: 0.3) { } }
rules.quote: When this setting is active, ensure your app or game responds by reducing automatic and repetitive animations, including zooming, scaling, and peripheral motion.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use action sheets for choices related to intentional actions, not alerts for unexpected problems.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAlertController(title: "Delete?", message: "Are you sure?", preferredStyle: .alert) // Should be .actionSheet for user-initiated action
rules.fix_swiftui: ConfirmationDialog("Delete Draft?", isPresented: $showSheet) { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: "Delete Draft?", message: nil, preferredStyle: .actionSheet)
rules.quote: Use an action sheet — not an alert — to offer choices related to an intentional action.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use action sheets sparingly to avoid interrupting the current task unnecessarily.
rules.anti_pattern: // Showing action sheet on every minor user interaction or preference change
rules.fix_swiftui: // Reserve ConfirmationDialog for significant, user-initiated actions only
rules.fix_uikit: // Reserve UIAlertController(.actionSheet) for significant, user-initiated actions only
rules.quote: Use action sheets sparingly.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep action sheet titles short enough to display on a single line.
rules.anti_pattern: ConfirmationDialog("Would you like to delete this draft message and discard all changes you have made?", isPresented: $show) { }
rules.fix_swiftui: ConfirmationDialog("Delete Draft?", isPresented: $show) { }
rules.fix_uikit: alert.title = "Delete Draft?"
rules.quote: Aim to keep titles short enough to display on a single line.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide a message only if the title and context do not sufficiently explain choices.
rules.anti_pattern: ConfirmationDialog("Delete", isPresented: $show) { } message: { Text("This will delete the item") }
rules.fix_swiftui: ConfirmationDialog("Delete Draft?", isPresented: $show) { } // Message omitted; context is clear
rules.fix_uikit: alert.message = nil // Omit redundant message
rules.quote: Provide a message only if necessary.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include a Cancel button to reject actions that might destroy data.
rules.anti_pattern: ConfirmationDialog("Delete?", isPresented: $show) { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { } } // No cancel option
rules.fix_swiftui: ConfirmationDialog("Delete?", isPresented: $show) { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { } Button("Cancel", role: .cancel) { } }
rules.fix_uikit: alert.addAction(UIAlertAction(title: "Cancel", style: .cancel))
rules.quote: If necessary, provide a Cancel button that lets people reject an action that might destroy data.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use destructive style for destructive buttons and place them at the top of the action sheet.
rules.anti_pattern: ConfirmationDialog("Delete?", isPresented: $show) { Button("Delete") { } Button("Cancel", role: .cancel) { } } // Destructive not marked, wrong order
rules.fix_swiftui: ConfirmationDialog("Delete?", isPresented: $show) { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { } Button("Cancel", role: .cancel) { } }
rules.fix_uikit: alert.addAction(UIAlertAction(title: "Delete", style: .destructive)); alert.addAction(UIAlertAction(title: "Cancel", style: .cancel))
rules.quote: Make destructive choices visually prominent.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use action sheets for choices related to user-initiated actions, not menus for user-revealed options.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu { Button("Delete") { } Button("Save") { } } label: { Image(systemName: "ellipsis") } // Should be action sheet for action-related choices
rules.fix_swiftui: ConfirmationDialog("Save or Delete?", isPresented: $show) { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { } Button("Save") { } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: nil, message: nil, preferredStyle: .actionSheet)
rules.quote: Use an action sheet — not a menu — to provide choices related to an action.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Avoid letting an action sheet scroll by limiting the number of buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: ConfirmationDialog("Choose", isPresented: $show) { Button("Option 1") { } Button("Option 2") { } Button("Option 3") { } Button("Option 4") { } Button("Option 5") { } } // Too many buttons cause scrolling
rules.fix_swiftui: // Limit to 3-4 most relevant buttons; use hierarchical menus for complex choices
rules.fix_uikit: // Limit UIAlertAction count to prevent scrolling
rules.quote: Avoid letting an action sheet scroll.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid duplicate system actions; use custom titles for similar app-specific functionality.
rules.fix_uikit: activity.activityTitle = "Print Transaction"
rules.quote: Avoid creating duplicate versions of common actions that are already available in the activity view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use SF Symbols or center custom icons in ~70×70 pixel area for activity representations.
rules.anti_pattern:
let icon = UIImage(named: "customIcon")
// Icon size unconstrained, may appear misaligned
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "square.and.arrow.up")
rules.fix_uikit: let icon = UIImage(named: "customIcon")
rules.quote: Consider using a symbol to represent your custom activity.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Write succinct, single-verb action titles; avoid company/product names in action titles.
rules.anti_pattern: activity.activityTitle = "Share with Acme Corp's Premium Photo Uploader Service"
rules.fix_uikit: activity.activityTitle = "Upload Photo"
rules.quote: Write a succinct, descriptive title for each custom action you provide.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Exclude system activities that don't apply to your app context.
rules.anti_pattern:
let controller = UIActivityViewController(activityItems: items, applicationActivities: nil)
// Shows all system activities regardless of context
rules.fix_uikit: controller.excludedActivityTypes = [.print, .saveToCameraRoll]
rules.quote: Although you can't reorder system-provided tasks in an activity view, you can exclude tasks that aren't applicable to your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use the Share button to display activity views; avoid alternative access patterns.
rules.fix_swiftui: ShareLink(item: content)
rules.fix_uikit: let button = UIBarButtonItem(barButtonSystemItem: .action, target: self, action: #selector(share))
rules.quote: Use the Share button to display an activity view.

rules.heading: Share and action extensions
rules.rule: For share extensions, prefer system composition view over custom interface.
rules.fix_uikit: class ShareViewController: SLComposeServiceViewController {}
rules.quote: For a share extension, prefer the system-provided composition view because it provides a consistent sharing experience that people already know.

rules.heading: Share and action extensions
rules.rule: Streamline extensions to complete tasks in minimal steps.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Extension requires 5+ taps to complete share
let steps = ["Select account", "Add caption", "Choose filters", "Set privacy", "Confirm", "Review"]
rules.fix_uikit: extensionContext?.completeRequest(returningItems: nil)
rules.quote: Streamline and limit interaction.

rules.heading: Share and action extensions
rules.rule: Avoid placing modal views above extensions; alerts only if necessary.
rules.fix_uikit: let alert = UIAlertController(title: "Error", message: msg, preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.quote: Avoid placing a modal view above your extension.

rules.heading: Share and action extensions
rules.rule: For action extensions, use symbols or custom icons; share extensions auto-use app icon.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "bookmark.fill")
rules.fix_uikit: activity.activityImage = UIImage(systemName: "bookmark.fill")
rules.quote: For an action extension, prefer using a symbol or creating an interface icon that clearly identifies the task.

rules.heading: Share and action extensions
rules.rule: For long operations, continue in background and show progress in main app, not notifications.
rules.fix_uikit: extensionContext?.completeRequest(returningItems: nil)
rules.quote: Use your main app to denote the progress of a lengthy operation.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer system-provided media player unless app-specific needs require custom implementation.
rules.anti_pattern: Building a custom video player from scratch when AVPlayerViewController meets requirements.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use AVPlayerViewController via UIViewControllerRepresentable wrapper in SwiftUI.
rules.fix_uikit: Instantiate and present AVPlayerViewController directly in your view controller.
rules.quote: The built-in media player offers a standard set of controls and supports features like chapter navigation, subtitles, closed captioning, and AirPlay streaming.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Stream only primary content users expect, not background loops or contextual-only video experiences.
rules.anti_pattern: Streaming app background animations or short contextual videos via AirPlay to external displays.
rules.fix_uikit: Set usesExternalPlaybackWhileExternalScreenIsActive to false for non-primary content.
rules.quote: Avoid streaming content like background loops and short video experiences that make sense only within the context of the app itself.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support both AirPlay streaming and mirroring to maximize user flexibility.
rules.anti_pattern: Implementing only AirPlay streaming without mirroring support.
rules.quote: Supporting both features gives people the most flexibility.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support remote control events so users can control playback from lock screen, Siri, or HomePod.
rules.anti_pattern: Ignoring remote command center events, preventing lock screen playback controls.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement MPRemoteCommandCenter event handlers for play, pause, and seek commands.
rules.quote: When you do, people can choose actions like play, pause, and fast forward on the lock screen, and through interaction with Siri or HomePod.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Don't stop playback when app enters background or device locks; continue AirPlay streaming.
rules.anti_pattern: Pausing or stopping media playback when app backgrounded or device locked.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure AVAudioSession category to allow background playback; avoid stopping player on app state changes.
rules.quote: Don't stop playback when your app enters the background or when the device locks.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Don't interrupt another app's playback unless starting immersive content; use ambient audio session.
rules.anti_pattern: Auto-playing video on external display while another app's AirPlay stream is active.
rules.fix_uikit: Use AVAudioSession.Category.ambient for non-primary content to avoid interrupting other playback.
rules.quote: Don't interrupt another app's playback unless your app is starting to play immersive content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep app functional during AirPlay; prevent other in-app videos from interrupting streaming content.
rules.anti_pattern: Auto-playing inline videos when user navigates away from playback screen during active AirPlay.
rules.fix_uikit: Pause or suppress inline video playback when AirPlay is active and user navigates away.
rules.quote: When AirPlay is active, your app needs to remain functional.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Position AirPlay icon in lower-right corner of custom media player (iOS 16+ / iPadOS 16+).
rules.anti_pattern: Placing AirPlay icon in upper-left corner or center of custom player interface.
rules.fix_uikit: Position AirPlay button at CGPoint(x: playerWidth - 44, y: playerHeight - 44) or equivalent.
rules.quote: position the AirPlay icon correctly in your custom player — that is, in the lower-right corner (in iOS 16 and iPadOS 16 and later).

rules.heading: Using AirPlay icons
rules.rule: Use black AirPlay icon on white/light backgrounds when other technology icons appear in black.
rules.anti_pattern: Using white AirPlay icon on light background or black icon on dark background.
rules.quote: Use the black AirPlay icon on white or light backgrounds when other technology icons also appear in black.

rules.heading: Using AirPlay icons
rules.rule: Use white AirPlay icon on black/dark backgrounds when other technology icons appear in white.
rules.anti_pattern: Using black AirPlay icon on dark background or white icon on light background.
rules.quote: Use the white AirPlay icon on black or dark backgrounds when other technology icons also appear in white.

rules.heading: Using AirPlay icons
rules.rule: Never use AirPlay icon or name in custom buttons or interactive elements; use only non-interactively.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a custom button with AirPlay icon that triggers playback or settings actions.
rules.quote: Don't use the AirPlay icon or name in custom buttons or interactive elements.

rules.heading: Using AirPlay icons
rules.rule: Pair AirPlay icon with name below or beside it using same font; don't embed icon in text.
rules.anti_pattern: Using AirPlay icon as inline text replacement or embedding it mid-sentence without proper spacing.
rules.quote: Avoid using the AirPlay icon within text or as a replacement for the name *AirPlay*.

rules.heading: Referring to AirPlay
rules.rule: Use correct capitalization: 'AirPlay' (uppercase A and P) or all-uppercase if layout requires it.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing 'airplay', 'Airplay', 'AIRPLAY' inconsistently or in lowercase.
rules.quote: *AirPlay* is one word, with an uppercase *A* and uppercase *P*, each followed by lowercase letters.

rules.heading: Referring to AirPlay
rules.rule: Always use AirPlay as a noun, never as a verb; use 'use', 'works with', 'supports', or 'compatible'.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing 'AirPlay to your speaker' or 'You can AirPlay with [App Name]' (verb usage).
rules.quote: Always use *AirPlay* as a noun.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display alerts only for essential information; avoid informational-only alerts.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Server unavailable"), message: Text("Connection lost"), dismissButton: .default(Text("OK")))
rules.quote: Avoid using an alert merely to provide information.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid alerts for common, undoable destructive actions; reserve for uncommon, irreversible actions.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Delete email?"), message: Text("This email will be deleted."), primaryButton: .destructive(Text("Delete")), secondaryButton: .cancel())
rules.quote: Avoid displaying alerts for common, undoable actions, even when they're destructive.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not show alerts when app starts; use alternative discovery mechanisms.
rules.anti_pattern: func applicationDidFinishLaunching(_ notification: Notification) { showAlert(title: "New Feature") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Display cached data with nonintrusive label or onboarding flow.
rules.fix_uikit: Show placeholder data with status label instead of UIAlertController at launch.
rules.quote: Avoid showing an alert when your app starts.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use direct, neutral, approachable tone; avoid oblique, accusatory, or severity-masking language.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Oops!"), message: Text("Something went wrong. Try again later, maybe."))
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: "Connection Failed", message: "Unable to reach the server. Check your network connection.", preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.quote: In all alert copy, be direct, and use a neutral, approachable tone.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Write titles that clearly describe the situation; avoid generic titles like 'Error' or error codes.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Error"), message: Text("Error 329347 occurred"))
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: "Cannot Save Document", message: "The file is read-only.", preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.quote: Avoid writing a title that doesn't convey useful information — like "Error" or "Error 329347 occurred" — but also avoid overly long titles that wrap to more than two lines.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Include informative text only if it adds value; keep messages short and use complete sentences.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Delete?"), message: Text("This action will delete the item from your device permanently and you will not be able to recover it ever again in any way."))
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: "Delete Item?", message: "This cannot be undone.", preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.quote: Include informative text only if it adds value.

rules.heading: Buttons
rules.rule: Use specific, action-oriented button titles; avoid 'OK' unless alert is purely informational.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Erase all data?"), primaryButton: .destructive(Text("OK")), secondaryButton: .cancel())
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertAction(title: "Erase", style: .destructive)
rules.quote: Avoid using OK as the default button title unless the alert is purely informational.

rules.heading: Buttons
rules.rule: Always use 'Cancel' as the button title for canceling an alert; never use 'No'.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Delete?"), primaryButton: .default(Text("Yes")), secondaryButton: .default(Text("No")))
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertAction(title: "Cancel", style: .cancel)
rules.quote: Always use "Cancel" to title a button that cancels the alert's action.

rules.heading: Buttons
rules.rule: Place most likely button on trailing side (row) or top (stack); default button on trailing/top; Cancel on leading/bottom.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert with buttons: [Cancel (default), Delete] in that order
rules.fix_swiftui: Alert with buttons: [Cancel, Delete (default)] or stack with Delete on top
rules.fix_uikit: Arrange UIAlertActions with preferred action set to Delete, Cancel as cancel style
rules.quote: Place buttons where people expect.

rules.heading: Buttons
rules.rule: Use destructive style only for unintended destructive actions; not for deliberately chosen destructive actions.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert for 'Empty Trash' with .destructive(Text("Empty Trash")) button
rules.fix_swiftui: Alert for 'Empty Trash' with .default(Text("Empty Trash")) button since user deliberately chose it
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertAction(title: "Empty Trash", style: .default) when action was deliberately chosen
rules.quote: Use the destructive style to identify a button that performs a destructive action people didn't deliberately choose.

rules.heading: Buttons
rules.rule: Include Cancel button with destructive actions to provide safe exit path.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Delete?"), primaryButton: .destructive(Text("Delete")))
rules.fix_uikit: alert.addAction(UIAlertAction(title: "Cancel", style: .cancel))
rules.quote: If there's a destructive action, include a Cancel button to give people a clear, safe way to avoid the action.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use action sheets, not alerts, to offer choices related to intentional user actions.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Save draft?"), message: Text("Delete, Save, or Continue editing?"))
rules.fix_swiftui: .confirmationDialog("Choose Action", isPresented: $show) { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) {}; Button("Save") {}; Button("Cancel", role: .cancel) {} }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: nil, message: nil, preferredStyle: .actionSheet)
rules.quote: Use an action sheet — not an alert — to offer choices related to an intentional action.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Minimize scrolling in alerts by keeping titles short and messages brief.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert with very long title wrapping 3+ lines and multi-paragraph message
rules.fix_swiftui: Keep title to 1-2 lines; include only essential message text
rules.fix_uikit: Limit UIAlertController title and message to prevent scrolling
rules.quote: When possible, avoid displaying an alert that scrolls.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use caution symbol sparingly; only for actions risking unexpected data loss.
rules.anti_pattern: NSAlert with exclamationmark.triangle icon for routine save operation
rules.fix_swiftui: Use caution icon only for irreversible destructive actions
rules.quote: Use a caution symbol sparingly.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Allow users to complete a task or demo without requiring full app installation.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip that requires users to install the full app to experience core functionality or complete a task.
rules.quote: Allow people to complete a task or a demo in your App Clip.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Focus App Clip features on essential tasks only; reserve advanced features for the full app.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip that includes all features from the full app or complex advanced functionality.
rules.quote: Focus on essential features.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Do not use App Clips solely for marketing; provide real value and avoid displaying ads.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip used primarily to advertise services or products with promotional content.
rules.quote: Don't use App Clips solely for marketing purposes.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Avoid using web views; use native components and frameworks for app-quality experience.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip implemented with WKWebView or web-based components instead of native SwiftUI/UIKit.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use native SwiftUI views (Text, Button, List, etc.) instead of WebView.
rules.fix_uikit: Use native UIKit components (UILabel, UIButton, UITableView, etc.) instead of UIWebView.
rules.quote: Avoid using web views in your App Clip.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Design linear, focused UI without tab bars, complex navigation, or settings screens.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip with TabView, complex NavigationStack, or Settings screens.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use simple NavigationStack or direct navigation; avoid TabView.
rules.fix_uikit: Avoid UITabBarController; use simple UINavigationController.
rules.quote: Design a linear, easy-to-use, and focused user interface.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Launch directly to the most relevant content; skip unnecessary onboarding or setup steps.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip that shows splash screens, welcome screens, or multi-step onboarding before showing core content.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @main entry point to navigate directly to task-relevant view.
rules.fix_uikit: Set rootViewController directly to task-relevant controller.
rules.quote: On launch, show the most relevant part of your App Clip.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Include all required assets and omit splash screens; ensure immediate usability on launch.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip with missing assets, splash screens, or loading delays on first launch.
rules.fix_swiftui: Bundle all assets; use .onAppear to load data asynchronously without blocking UI.
rules.fix_uikit: Bundle all assets; load data on background thread without blocking main thread.
rules.quote: Ensure people can use your App Clip immediately.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Minimize App Clip size by reducing unnecessary code and removing unused assets.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip with large bundle size, unused frameworks, or unnecessary asset files.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use conditional compilation; remove unused dependencies.
rules.fix_uikit: Use conditional compilation; remove unused frameworks.
rules.quote: Ensure your App Clip is small.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Enable sharing of App Clip links, especially to specific points within the experience.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip without share functionality or ability to link to specific content.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use ShareLink to enable sharing of deep links.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIActivityViewController with deep link URLs.
rules.quote: Make the App Clip shareable.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Support Apple Pay for express checkout to minimize payment friction.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip requiring manual entry of payment and shipping information.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use PKPaymentButton with PassKit framework.
rules.fix_uikit: Use PKPaymentButton with PassKit framework.
rules.quote: Make it easy to pay for a service or product.

rules.heading: Designing your App Clip
rules.rule: Avoid requiring account creation before users can benefit from the App Clip.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip that requires account creation or login before accessing core functionality.
rules.fix_swiftui: Defer account creation to after task completion; use Sign in with Apple.
rules.fix_uikit: Defer account creation to after task completion; use Sign in with Apple.
rules.quote: Avoid requiring people to create an account before they can benefit from your App Clip.

rules.heading: Preserving privacy
rules.rule: Limit stored data and assume App Clip data may be deleted between launches.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip that relies on persistent local storage or assumes data survives device removal.
rules.fix_swiftui: Store sensitive data in Keychain; use UserDefaults sparingly.
rules.fix_uikit: Store sensitive data in Keychain; use UserDefaults sparingly.
rules.quote: Limit the amount of data you store and handle yourself.

rules.heading: Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.citation: app-clips.md › Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.rule: Use photography or graphics on App Clip card; avoid screenshots of app UI.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip card using a screenshot of the app's user interface as the header image.
rules.quote: Prefer photography and graphics.

rules.heading: Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.citation: app-clips.md › Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.rule: Avoid text in App Clip card header image; use 1800x1200 px PNG or JPEG.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip card with text overlay in header image or incorrect image dimensions.
rules.quote: Avoid using text.

rules.heading: Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.citation: app-clips.md › Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.rule: Use concise title (≤30 chars) and subtitle (≤56 chars) on App Clip card.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip card with title exceeding 30 characters or subtitle exceeding 56 characters.
rules.quote: Use concise copy.

rules.heading: Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.citation: app-clips.md › Creating content for an App Clip card
rules.rule: Choose action button verb (View, Play, or Open) matching App Clip type.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip card using incorrect action button verb for content type.
rules.quote: Pick a verb for the action button that best fits your App Clip.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Use NFC-integrated App Clip Code variant for physically accessible locations.
rules.anti_pattern: Using scan-only App Clip Code on tabletop, register, or storefront where NFC is appropriate.
rules.quote: If people can physically access the App Clip Code, use the NFC-integrated variant.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Use scan-only App Clip Code for digitally displayed or physically inaccessible locations.
rules.anti_pattern: Using NFC-integrated App Clip Code on posters, digital displays, or emails.
rules.quote: If you need to place your App Clip Code in an area that's physically inaccessible or you need to display it digitally, use a scan-only App Clip Code.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Include App Clip logo when space allows; omit on disposable or gambling-related items.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code with logo on playing cards, poker chips, or bar coasters.
rules.quote: Include the App Clip logo when space allows.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Place App Clip Code on flat or cylindrical surfaces only; width ≤1/6 of circumference.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code placed on deformable materials or cylindrical surface exceeding width ratio.
rules.quote: Place your App Clip Code on a flat or cylindrical surface only.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Avoid deformable materials; use rigid cards attached to flexible objects.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code printed directly on paper bags, flexible boxes, or crumpling materials.
rules.quote: Help your App Clip Code remain as flat as possible so it's easy for people to scan.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Ensure App Clip Code minimum size: 3/4 inch (1.9 cm) printed, 256×256 px digital.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code smaller than minimum size specifications.
rules.quote: Don't create App Clip Codes that are too small.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Keep App Clip Code unobstructed; never overlay, animate, or dim it.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code with text overlay, animation, or reduced opacity.
rules.quote: Make sure the App Clip Code is unobstructed.

rules.heading: Displaying App Clip Codes
rules.rule: Display App Clip Code in upright position; never rotate or angle center glyph.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code rotated or displayed at an angle.
rules.quote: Display the App Clip Code in an upright position.

rules.heading: Customizing your App Clip Code
rules.citation: app-clips.md › Customizing your App Clip Code
rules.rule: Always use generated App Clip Code; never modify, filter, or add effects.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom App Clip Code design or modified generated code with filters, glows, shadows, or gradients.
rules.quote: Always use the generated App Clip Code.

rules.heading: Customizing your App Clip Code
rules.citation: app-clips.md › Customizing your App Clip Code
rules.rule: Choose App Clip Code colors with sufficient contrast for accurate scanning.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code with low-contrast foreground and background colors.
rules.quote: Choose colors with enough contrast that ensure accurate scanning.

rules.heading: Printing guidelines
rules.rule: Use matte finishes and high-quality materials; avoid gloss, reflective, or holographic overlays.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code printed on glossy, reflective, or textured materials.
rules.quote: Use high-quality, non-textured print materials.

rules.heading: Printing guidelines
rules.rule: Print at minimum 300 dpi with 600 ppi rasterization; calibrate printer before printing.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code printed at low resolution or without printer calibration.
rules.quote: Use high-resolution images and printer settings.

rules.heading: Printing guidelines
rules.rule: Convert SVG to CMYK using relative calorimetric intent with CIELab Delta E ≤2.5.
rules.anti_pattern: App Clip Code converted to CMYK without proper color profile or intent.
rules.quote: Use correct color settings when you convert the generated SVG file to a CMYK image.

rules.heading: Printing guidelines
rules.rule: For grayscale printers, generate only grayscale App Clip Codes.
rules.anti_pattern: Color App Clip Code printed on grayscale printer.
rules.quote: If you're using a printer that only prints in grayscale, only generate grayscale App Clip Codes.

rules.heading: Printing guidelines
rules.rule: Use Type 5 NFC tags with minimum 35 mm diameter for NFC-integrated App Clip Codes.
rules.anti_pattern: NFC-integrated App Clip Code using non-Type 5 NFC tags or undersized tags.
rules.quote: For NFC-integrated App Clip Codes, choose Type 5 NFC tags.

rules.heading: Layer design
rules.rule: Use Icon Composer to define layered app icons with background and foreground layers for Liquid Glass effects.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing a flat, nonlayered PNG without importing into Icon Composer, losing system-applied specular highlights and refraction.
rules.quote: Although you can provide a nonlayered image for your icon (see Icon formats), layers give you the most control over how your icon design is represented.

rules.heading: Layer design
rules.rule: Use clearly defined edges in foreground layers to ensure system-drawn highlights and shadows render optimally.
rules.anti_pattern: Designing foreground layer shapes with soft, feathered, or blurred edges that conflict with system-applied visual effects.
rules.quote: Prefer clearly defined edges in foreground layers.

rules.heading: Layer design
rules.rule: Vary opacity across foreground layers to increase depth and liveliness in the icon design.
rules.anti_pattern: Using fully opaque foreground layers without transparency variation, reducing visual dimensionality and dynamism.
rules.quote: Vary opacity in foreground layers to increase the sense of depth and liveliness.

rules.heading: Layer design
rules.rule: Design backgrounds that stand out and emphasize foreground content using solid colors or gradients.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a busy background with complex imagery or patterns that competes with or obscures foreground elements.
rules.quote: Design a background that both stands out and emphasizes foreground content.

rules.heading: Layer design
rules.rule: Prefer vector graphics (SVG, PDF) over raster images when importing layers into Icon Composer.
rules.anti_pattern: Importing raster images like JPEG or low-resolution PNG that pixelate or blur when scaled to different icon sizes.
rules.quote: Prefer vector graphics when bringing layers into Icon Composer.

rules.heading: Icon formats
rules.rule: Provide app icons in Icon Composer format for precise control over Liquid Glass and appearance variants.
rules.anti_pattern: Submitting only a bitmap PNG without layering, forcing the system to auto-segment and losing control over effect application.
rules.quote: Provide your icon in the Icon Composer format for more flexibility and control.

rules.heading: Icon shape
rules.rule: Provide square, unmasked layers; the system applies rounded corners and masking automatically.
rules.anti_pattern: Pre-masking layers with rounded corners or custom shapes, causing jagged edges and breaking specular highlight effects.
rules.quote: Produce appropriately shaped, unmasked layers.

rules.heading: Icon shape
rules.rule: Center primary content to avoid truncation when the system applies masking and corner adjustments.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing important design elements near the edges of the icon canvas, causing them to be cropped by system masking.
rules.quote: Keep primary content centered to avoid truncation when the system adjusts corners or applies masking.

rules.heading: Design
rules.rule: Embrace simplicity in icon design; use a single core concept expressed with minimal shapes.
rules.anti_pattern: Designing overly complex icons with fine details, multiple competing elements, or busy backgrounds that confuse recognition.
rules.quote: Embrace simplicity in your icon design.

rules.heading: Design
rules.rule: Provide visually consistent icon designs across all platforms your app supports.
rules.anti_pattern: Designing drastically different icons for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, making the app appear as multiple unrelated apps.
rules.quote: Provide a visually consistent icon design across all the platforms your app supports.

rules.heading: Design
rules.rule: Include text in icons only when essential to experience or brand; avoid action verbs and context-specific labels.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding text like 'Watch', 'Play', 'New', or 'For visionOS' to the icon, cluttering the design and reducing accessibility.
rules.quote: Include text only when it's essential to your experience or brand.

rules.heading: Design
rules.rule: Prefer illustrations over photos; avoid replicating UI components or app screenshots in icons.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a photograph or screenshot of the app interface as the icon, losing detail at small sizes and across appearance variants.
rules.quote: Prefer illustrations to photos and avoid replicating UI components.

rules.heading: Visual effects
rules.rule: Let the system handle blurring and visual effects; do not include custom specular highlights, shadows, or glows.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding custom drop shadows, beveled edges, glows, or blur effects to icon layers, conflicting with system-applied Liquid Glass.
rules.quote: Let the system handle blurring and other visual effects.

rules.heading: Appearances
rules.rule: Keep icon features consistent across default, dark, clear, and tinted appearance variants.
rules.anti_pattern: Swapping elements in and out between appearance variants, making the app harder to recognize when appearance changes.
rules.quote: Keep your icon's features consistent across appearances.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Adopt app schemas for common domain areas instead of individual App Shortcuts to enable Apple Intelligence discovery.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating 10 separate App Shortcuts for standard actions (e.g., send message, make call, create note) when an app schema domain exists.
rules.quote: To surface common types of app functionality throughout the system, consider adopting app schemas instead.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Expose only the app's most common and important tasks as App Shortcuts, prioritizing straightforward single-context actions.
rules.anti_pattern: Offering 10 App Shortcuts for every possible feature, including rarely-used or deeply-nested workflows.
rules.quote: Offer App Shortcuts for your app's most common and important tasks.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include at most one optional parameter per App Shortcut with predictable, familiar values users can recall without reference.
rules.anti_pattern: Defining App Shortcuts with multiple parameters: "Start [morning/daily/sleep] meditation with [nature/rain/ocean] sounds and [5/10/15] minutes."
rules.quote: An App Shortcut can include a single optional value, or parameter, if it makes sense.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prompt for clarification when an App Shortcut request lacks required optional information; suggest defaults based on recency or context.
rules.anti_pattern: Silently failing or picking an arbitrary option when a user says "Start meditation" without specifying type.
rules.quote: Ask for clarification in response to a request that's missing optional information.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep App Shortcut activation phrases simple and easy to say aloud; avoid multi-parameter phrases that are hard to remember.
rules.anti_pattern: "Start [sleep] meditation with nature sounds and [5/10/15] minute timer and haptic feedback enabled."
rules.quote: If your phrase feels too complicated when you say it aloud, it's probably too difficult to remember or say correctly.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Surface App Shortcuts in-app via occasional tips when users perform common actions to increase discoverability and adoption.
rules.anti_pattern: Shipping App Shortcuts without any in-app hints or UI prompts; users never discover they exist.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use SiriTipUIView to display contextual tips when users perform actions with available shortcuts.
rules.quote: Make App Shortcuts discoverable in your app.

rules.heading: Responding to App Shortcuts
rules.rule: Include all critical information in full dialogue text for audio-only device compatibility; do not rely on visual-only responses.
rules.anti_pattern: Returning only a visual snippet with no spoken dialogue text; users on AirPods or HomePod receive no information.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use IntentDialog(full:supporting:systemImageName:) with complete dialogue text.
rules.quote: Provide enough detail for interaction on audio-only devices.

rules.heading: Editorial guidelines
rules.rule: Use brief, memorable activation phrases that include app name; support natural variants to improve recall and usability.
rules.anti_pattern: Defining only a single rigid phrase like "Create a new document in MyApp" without natural variants like "New MyApp document."
rules.quote: Provide brief, memorable activation phrases and natural variants.

rules.heading: Editorial guidelines
rules.rule: Use title case and plural "Shortcuts" when referring to the Shortcuts app or App Shortcuts feature in copy.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing "integrates with shortcuts" or "offers app shortcuts you can place on the action button."
rules.quote: When referring to App Shortcuts or the Shortcuts app, always use title case and make sure that Shortcuts is plural.

rules.heading: Editorial guidelines
rules.rule: Use lowercase "shortcut" when referring to individual custom shortcuts, not App Shortcuts or the Shortcuts app.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing "Run a Shortcut by asking Siri" when referring to a user-created custom shortcut.
rules.quote: When referring to individual shortcuts (not App Shortcuts or the Shortcuts app), use lowercase.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Order App Shortcuts by importance; system will later prioritize by user frequency in Spotlight and Shortcuts app.
rules.anti_pattern: Ordering App Shortcuts arbitrarily or by implementation convenience rather than user value and frequency.
rules.quote: Order shortcuts based on importance.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Assign an SF Symbol or preview image to each App Shortcut to represent its functionality in Spotlight and Shortcuts app.
rules.anti_pattern: Defining App Shortcuts without symbols or preview images; they appear as generic entries in Spotlight.
rules.quote: Each App Shortcut includes a symbol from SF Symbols that you choose to represent its functionality, or a preview image of an item that the shortcut links to directly.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Let people experience your app before requiring purchase to discover value.
rules.anti_pattern: Paywall shown immediately on app launch before any content exploration.
rules.quote: Let people experience your app before making a purchase.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Design shopping experience to match app style, not appear as separate app.
rules.anti_pattern: Purchase UI uses completely different design system, colors, typography from main app.
rules.quote: Design an integrated shopping experience.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use simple, succinct product names and descriptions that don't truncate.
rules.anti_pattern: Product name: "Premium Monthly Subscription with Advanced Analytics and Priority Support Features"
rules.quote: Use simple, succinct product names and descriptions.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display total billing price for every in-app purchase regardless of type.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing only introductory price without final billing amount after trial ends.
rules.quote: Display the total billing price for each in-app purchase you offer, regardless of type.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Hide store or explain unavailability when payments disabled by parental restrictions.
rules.anti_pattern: Store displayed and tappable even when canMakePayments returns false.
rules.fix_swiftui: Check AppStore.canMakePayments before displaying purchase UI.
rules.quote: Display your store only when people can make payments.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use system confirmation sheet; never modify or replicate Apple's purchase confirmation.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom confirmation dialog replacing system sheet for purchase verification.
rules.quote: Use the default confirmation sheet.

rules.heading: Supporting Family Sharing
rules.rule: Prominently mention Family Sharing in product names and sign-up screens.
rules.anti_pattern: Family Sharing capability exists but never mentioned in UI or marketing copy.
rules.quote: Prominently mention Family Sharing in places where people learn about the content you offer.

rules.heading: Supporting Family Sharing
rules.rule: Customize in-app messaging for both purchasers and family members viewing shared content.
rules.anti_pattern: Same welcome message shown to original purchaser and family members receiving shared access.
rules.quote: Aim to customize your in-app messaging so that it makes sense to both purchasers and family members.

rules.heading: Providing help
rules.rule: Provide custom help content before refund request, including FAQs and alternatives.
rules.anti_pattern: Refund button shown with no context, help, or alternative solutions offered.
rules.quote: Provide help that customers can view before they request a refund.

rules.heading: Providing help
rules.rule: Use simple refund action title like 'Refund' or 'Request a Refund'.
rules.anti_pattern: Refund button labeled 'Request a Refund from Apple Inc. (This will be reviewed by Apple)'
rules.quote: Use a simple title for the refund action, like "Refund" or "Request a Refund".

rules.heading: Providing help
rules.rule: Include product image, name, description, and purchase date to identify problematic purchase.
rules.anti_pattern: Purchase history showing only transaction ID and amount without product context.
rules.quote: Help people find the problematic purchase.

rules.heading: Providing help
rules.rule: Make refund-request button immediately accessible without scrolling or additional screens.
rules.anti_pattern: Refund button hidden below fold or behind another navigation level.
rules.quote: Make it easy for people to request a refund.

rules.heading: Auto-renewable subscriptions
rules.rule: Call attention to subscription benefits during onboarding with strong CTA and clear terms.
rules.anti_pattern: Onboarding completes without mentioning subscription value or benefits.
rules.quote: Call attention to subscription benefits during onboarding.

rules.heading: Making signup effortless
rules.rule: Clearly explain free trial duration and automatic billing amount when trial ends.
rules.anti_pattern: Free trial offered without stating trial length or post-trial billing amount.
rules.quote: Clearly describe how a free trial works.

rules.heading: Supporting offer codes
rules.rule: Clearly explain offer details in marketing materials for informed decision-making.
rules.anti_pattern: Offer code distributed with vague or misleading description of discount terms.
rules.quote: Clearly explain offer details.

rules.heading: Supporting offer codes
rules.rule: Custom codes must contain only alphanumeric ASCII characters, no special characters.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom offer code: "SPRING_SALE_2024" or "新年优惠"
rules.quote: A custom code can contain only alphanumeric ASCII characters.

rules.heading: Supporting offer codes
rules.rule: Tell people how to redeem custom codes via redemption URL or within app.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom code distributed without instructions on where or how to redeem it.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add 'Redeem Code' button to paywall/onboarding/settings calling presentOfferCodeRedeemSheet.
rules.quote: Tell people how to redeem a custom code.

rules.heading: Supporting offer codes
rules.rule: Supply engaging promotional image for offer code redemption screens.
rules.anti_pattern: Offer code redemption uses only app icon without custom promotional image.
rules.quote: Supply an engaging and informative promotional image.

rules.heading: Helping people manage their subscriptions
rules.citation: apple-in-app-purchase.md › Helping people manage their subscriptions
rules.rule: Display subscription summaries including upcoming renewal date in settings or account screen.
rules.anti_pattern: No subscription status or renewal date visible in app settings.
rules.quote: Provide summaries of the customer's subscriptions.

rules.heading: Helping people manage their subscriptions
rules.citation: apple-in-app-purchase.md › Helping people manage their subscriptions
rules.rule: Always make cancellation easy; never bury subscription cancellation deep in navigation.
rules.anti_pattern: Cancel subscription option hidden 4+ levels deep or difficult to recognize.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use AppStore.showManageSubscriptions(in:) to present system subscription management UI.
rules.quote: Always make it easy for customers to cancel an auto-renewable subscription.

rules.heading: Offering Apple Pay
rules.rule: Offer Apple Pay on all devices and browsers that support it; hide if unsupported.
rules.anti_pattern: Always showing Apple Pay button regardless of PKPaymentAuthorizationController.canMakePayments() result.
rules.fix_uikit: Check PKPaymentAuthorizationController.canMakePayments() before displaying button.
rules.quote: Offer Apple Pay on all devices and browsers that support it.

rules.heading: Offering Apple Pay
rules.rule: Make Apple Pay the primary payment option when credentials are available.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing Apple Pay in a separate tab or flow after checking canMakePayments().
rules.fix_uikit: Pre-select Apple Pay or display it first among payment options.
rules.quote: Make Apple Pay the primary — but not necessarily sole — payment option everywhere you use the APIs.

rules.heading: Offering Apple Pay
rules.rule: Use Apple Pay buttons only to initiate payment or setup, never for other purposes.
rules.anti_pattern: Using PKPaymentButton to toggle payment method selection or display payment status.
rules.fix_swiftui: Reserve Button with Apple Pay action for payment initiation only.
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve PKPaymentButton for payment or setup flow initiation.
rules.quote: Use Apple Pay buttons only to initiate payment or, when appropriate, the Apple Pay setup process.

rules.heading: Offering Apple Pay
rules.rule: Custom payment buttons must not display 'Apple Pay' text or logo; use Apple Pay mark instead.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom UIButton with title 'Pay with Apple Pay' or embedded Apple Pay logo graphic.
rules.fix_swiftui: Display Apple Pay mark graphic separately; use generic button label.
rules.fix_uikit: Display Apple Pay mark graphic separately; use generic button label.
rules.quote: If you use a custom button to start the Apple Pay payment process, make sure your custom button doesn't display "Apple Pay" or the Apple Pay logo.

rules.heading: Offering Apple Pay
rules.rule: Use Apple Pay mark graphic only to communicate acceptance; never as a payment button.
rules.anti_pattern: Making Apple Pay mark graphic tappable or positioning it as a clickable payment initiator.
rules.fix_swiftui: Display mark as static image; use separate Button for payment initiation.
rules.fix_uikit: Display mark as static UIImageView; use separate UIButton for payment initiation.
rules.quote: Use the Apple Pay mark graphic only to communicate that you accept Apple Pay.

rules.heading: Offering Apple Pay
rules.rule: Never hide or disable Apple Pay button; gracefully point out missing prerequisites after tap.
rules.anti_pattern: Setting button.isHidden = true or button.isEnabled = false when product size not selected.
rules.fix_swiftui: Keep button visible and enabled; show error message after user taps.
rules.fix_uikit: Keep button visible and enabled; show error message after user taps.
rules.quote: Don't hide an Apple Pay button or make it appear unavailable.

rules.heading: Streamlining checkout
rules.rule: Present Apple Pay button first, larger, or visually separated from other payment options.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying Apple Pay button at same size and position as credit card or other payment methods.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use larger frame, higher z-order, or visual separator for Apple Pay button.
rules.fix_uikit: Use larger frame, higher z-order, or visual separator for Apple Pay button.
rules.quote: If Apple Pay is available, assume people want to use it.

rules.heading: Streamlining checkout
rules.rule: Collect required fields (color, size, options) before showing Apple Pay button.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying Apple Pay button on product page without requiring size/color selection first.
rules.fix_swiftui: Disable or hide button until all required fields populated; validate before showing payment sheet.
rules.fix_uikit: Disable or hide button until all required fields populated; validate before showing payment sheet.
rules.quote: Collect necessary information, like color and size options, before people reach the Apple Pay button.

rules.heading: Customizing the payment sheet
rules.rule: Only request essential information on payment sheet; omit extraneous fields.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting shipping address for digital gift card delivery or unnecessary contact fields.
rules.fix_uikit: Set PKPaymentRequest.requiredShippingAddressFields and requiredBillingAddressFields to minimum.
rules.quote: Only present and request essential information.

rules.heading: Customizing the payment sheet
rules.rule: Use line items for charges, discounts, fees, donations, and recurring payments; not product itemization.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating separate line items for each product in cart instead of single total.
rules.fix_uikit: Use PKPaymentSummaryItem for totals, fees, discounts; show product list separately.
rules.quote: Use line items to explain additional charges, discounts, pending costs, add-on donations, recurring payments, and future payments.

rules.heading: Customizing the payment sheet
rules.rule: Display business name after 'Pay' on total line matching bank statement charge name.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing generic 'Pay $50.00' without business name or mismatched name from statement.
rules.fix_uikit: Set PKPaymentRequest.paymentSummaryItems with label 'Pay [Business_Name]'.
rules.quote: Provide a business name after the word *Pay* on the same line as the total.

rules.heading: Data validation errors
rules.rule: Provide specific, field-referenced error messages; avoid generic validation failures.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing 'Address is invalid' instead of 'Zip code doesn't match city'.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement paymentAuthorizationViewController(_:didSelectShippingAddress:completion:) with specific PKPaymentError messages.
rules.quote: Explain the problem clearly and succinctly when data is invalid or incorrectly formatted.

rules.heading: Data validation errors
rules.rule: Accept flexible input formats (Zip+4, phone dashes, country codes) without validation errors.
rules.anti_pattern: Rejecting '12345-6789' zip code when app requires exactly 5 digits.
rules.fix_uikit: Normalize input before validation; ignore extra digits or formatting variations.
rules.quote: Design a data validation process that's intelligent enough to ignore irrelevant data and infer missing data whenever possible.

rules.heading: Supporting subscriptions
rules.rule: Use line items to display billing frequency, trial terms, and regular amount after trial.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing only total amount without line items explaining recurring billing or trial period.
rules.fix_uikit: Add PKPaymentSummaryItem entries for trial amount, regular amount, and billing frequency.
rules.quote: Include line items that reiterate billing frequency, discounts, and additional upfront fees.

rules.heading: Using Apple Pay buttons
rules.rule: Always use Apple-provided API to create Apple Pay buttons; never create custom designs.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating custom UIButton with Apple Pay styling or replicating PKPaymentButton appearance.
rules.fix_uikit: Use PKPaymentButton with PKPaymentButtonType and PKPaymentButtonStyle.
rules.quote: Always use the Apple-provided API to display Apple Pay buttons.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support Apple Pencil input for all interactive controls, not just drawing surfaces.
rules.anti_pattern: Button { } .onTapGesture { } // only responds to finger, not Apple Pencil
rules.fix_uikit: Ensure UIButton and UIControl subclasses respond to UIEvent with pencilInteraction enabled.
rules.quote: Let people choose when to switch between Apple Pencil and finger input.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow marking immediately upon Apple Pencil contact without requiring mode activation.
rules.anti_pattern: // Require tap to activate drawing mode before pencil marks appear
rules.fix_uikit: Respond to pencil touches in touchesBegan without requiring prior button tap.
rules.quote: Let people make a mark the moment Apple Pencil touches the screen.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use pressure, tilt, and azimuth to vary stroke properties like thickness and opacity.
rules.anti_pattern: // Ignore force and altitude; draw uniform strokes regardless of pencil angle
rules.fix_uikit: Access UITouch.force, altitude, and azimuth; map to brush size and opacity.
rules.quote: Apple Pencil may sense tilt (altitude), force (pressure), orientation (azimuth), and barrel roll.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure Apple Pencil appears to directly manipulate content it touches, not distant UI.
rules.anti_pattern: // Pencil hover triggers action on opposite side of screen
rules.fix_uikit: Map pencil coordinates directly to content manipulation at touch point.
rules.quote: Provide visual feedback to indicate a direct connection with content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid placing controls where left- or right-handed users' hands may obscure them.
rules.anti_pattern: // Fixed button in bottom-right corner, always obscured by right-handed grip
rules.fix_uikit: Allow control repositioning or place controls in neutral zones.
rules.quote: Design a great left- and right-handed experience.

rules.heading: Hover
rules.rule: Show hover preview at middle-range values, not extremes, to remain visible and representative.
rules.anti_pattern: // Preview brush at maximum pressure; mark occludes the writing area
rules.fix_uikit: Display hover preview using mid-range opacity or brush size.
rules.quote: Prefer showing a preview value that's near the middle in a range of dynamic values.

rules.heading: Hover
rules.rule: Never initiate destructive or unintended actions via hover alone.
