rules.anti_pattern: // Hovering near delete button triggers deletion without explicit tap
rules.fix_uikit: Restrict hover to preview only; require explicit touch for actions.
rules.quote: Avoid using hover to initiate an action.

rules.heading: Double tap
rules.rule: Respect system double-tap settings (eraser toggle, tool toggle, color picker) when applicable.
rules.anti_pattern: // Ignore user's double-tap preference; always toggle to eraser
rules.fix_uikit: Query UIPencilInteraction.doubleTapAction and honor user settings.
rules.quote: Respect people's settings for the double-tap gesture when they make sense in your app.

rules.heading: Double tap
rules.rule: Never use double-tap to perform destructive or data-loss actions.
rules.anti_pattern: // Double-tap deletes selected content without confirmation
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve double-tap for reversible actions like tool/eraser toggle.
rules.quote: Avoid using the double-tap gesture to perform an action that modifies content.

rules.heading: Squeeze
rules.rule: Treat squeeze as a single discrete action, not continuous; avoid fatigue-inducing repeated squeezes.
rules.anti_pattern: // Respond to every squeeze event; require sustained squeeze to hold state
rules.fix_uikit: Respond once per squeeze gesture; display result immediately.
rules.quote: Treat squeeze as a single, quick gesture that performs a discrete — not continuous — action.

rules.heading: Squeeze
rules.rule: Never use squeeze to perform destructive or data-loss actions.
rules.anti_pattern: // Squeeze deletes current layer without undo
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve squeeze for nondestructive actions like menu reveal or tool toggle.
rules.quote: Define squeeze actions that are nondestructive and easy to undo.

rules.heading: Barrel roll
rules.rule: Use barrel roll only to modify marking behavior, never for navigation or UI control.
rules.anti_pattern: // Barrel roll opens menu or navigates to previous screen
rules.fix_uikit: Map barrel roll to stroke angle, highlight rotation, or brush orientation only.
rules.quote: Use barrel roll only to modify marking behavior, not to enable navigation or display other controls.

rules.heading: Scribble
rules.rule: Enable Scribble in all standard text fields and custom text input areas without requiring mode activation.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom text field requires tap before Scribble works; password field accepts Scribble
rules.fix_swiftui: Use TextField and TextEditor; avoid custom input requiring pre-activation.
rules.fix_uikit: Adopt UIIndirectScribbleInteraction for custom text areas; exclude password fields.
rules.quote: Make text entry feel fluid and effortless.

rules.heading: Scribble
rules.rule: Hide placeholder text and disable autocompletion while user writes to avoid visual interference.
rules.anti_pattern: // Placeholder text overlaps handwriting; autocomplete suggestions appear mid-stroke
rules.fix_swiftui: Hide placeholder on focus; disable autocorrection during active writing.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UITextInputAssistantItem.leadingBarButtonGroups to empty; hide placeholder on edit begin.
rules.quote: Avoid distracting people while they write.

rules.heading: Scribble
rules.rule: Keep text fields stationary while user writes; delay repositioning until writing pauses.
rules.anti_pattern: // Text field moves to make room for results while user is mid-stroke
rules.fix_swiftui: Defer layout changes until onEditingChanged or after writing completes.
rules.fix_uikit: Delay frame changes until UITextFieldDelegate textFieldDidEndEditing.
rules.quote: While people are writing in a text field, make sure it remains stationary.

rules.heading: Scribble
rules.rule: Disable autoscrolling of text while user writes or selects with Apple Pencil.
rules.anti_pattern: // Text autoscrolls during writing; user's selection range shifts unexpectedly
rules.fix_swiftui: Disable scrolling during active editing; resume after writing pauses.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UITextView.isScrollEnabled = false during UIScribbleInteraction.
rules.quote: Prevent autoscrolling text while people are writing and editing in a text field.

rules.heading: Scribble
rules.rule: Increase text field size before or after writing to provide comfortable writing space.
rules.anti_pattern: // Text field remains tiny; user struggles to write legibly
rules.fix_swiftui: Expand TextField frame on focus or during writing pause.
rules.fix_uikit: Increase UITextField frame size in UIScribbleInteraction delegate methods.
rules.quote: Give people enough space to write.

rules.heading: Custom drawing
rules.rule: Disable dynamic Dark Mode color adjustment when drawing over existing content like PDFs.
rules.anti_pattern: // Pencil markup colors shift in Dark Mode; visibility lost over photo
rules.fix_uikit: Set PKCanvasView.drawingGestureRecognizer.isEnabled and disable dynamic colors for overlays.
rules.quote: However, when people draw on top of existing content like a PDF or a photo, you want to prevent the dynamic adjustment of colors so that the markup remains sharp and visible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Devote maximum screen space to displaying physical world and virtual objects; minimize UI controls.
rules.anti_pattern: ARView with dense overlay of buttons, sliders, and status text covering 40% of screen.
rules.fix_uikit: Use ARView as primary content; move controls to edges or use translucent overlays in screen space.
rules.quote: Devote as much of the screen as possible to displaying the physical world and your app's virtual objects.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Update AR scenes 60 times per second to prevent object jumping or flickering.
rules.anti_pattern: ARSession rendering at 30 FPS or variable frame rates causing visual discontinuities.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure ARView preferredFramesPerSecond to 60; ensure render loop maintains consistent timing.
rules.quote: make sure your app updates scenes 60 times per second so objects don't appear to jump or flicker.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer small or coarse reflective surfaces to downplay approximation artifacts in AR reflections.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing highly reflective, mirror-like surfaces on virtual objects that expose environment map inaccuracies.
rules.fix_uikit: Use matte or rough material properties; reduce specular reflection intensity on virtual objects.
rules.quote: prefer small or coarse reflective surfaces that downplay the effect of these approximations.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Minimize text displayed in the AR environment; show only essential information.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying verbose labels, debug info, or multiple overlapping text annotations in 3D space.
rules.fix_uikit: Move non-critical text to screen-space UI; use 3D hints (visual indicators) instead of text overlays.
rules.quote: Minimize text in the environment. Display only the information that people need for your app experience.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place persistent controls in screen space using translucency to avoid blocking the AR scene.
rules.anti_pattern: Opaque control panels or buttons positioned over the center of the AR view, obscuring virtual objects.
rules.fix_swiftui: .opacity(0.7) on control overlays; position at screen edges.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIView with alpha < 1.0; anchor controls to safe area edges.
rules.quote: consider using translucency in an indirect control to help avoid blocking the underlying scene.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Communicate app requirements and environment expectations upfront to users.
rules.anti_pattern: Launching AR experience without explaining that flat surfaces or open space are required.
rules.fix_uikit: Display onboarding screen or alert explaining space/surface requirements before entering AR.
rules.quote: Clearly communicate your app's requirements and expectations to people up front to help them understand how their physical environment can affect their AR experience.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Introduce motion gradually; avoid demanding rapid or expansive movements immediately.
rules.anti_pattern: AR game requiring users to dodge projectiles or perform large sweeping motions on first interaction.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement progressive difficulty; start with stationary objects, then introduce motion after adaptation period.
rules.quote: If your app encourages people to move, introduce motion gradually.

rules.heading: Providing coaching
rules.rule: Hide unrelated app UI while ARCoachingOverlayView is displayed to focus user attention.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing coaching view with menu buttons, status bars, and other UI elements visible simultaneously.
rules.fix_uikit: Set isHidden = true on non-essential UI elements when coachingOverlayView.isActive is true.
rules.quote: Hide unnecessary app UI while people are using a coaching view.

rules.heading: Helping people place objects
rules.rule: Place objects immediately upon user tap; refine position subtly after surface detection completes.
rules.anti_pattern: Waiting for ARKit surface detection to finish before placing object, causing perceived lag.
rules.fix_uikit: Use raycast result immediately; apply ARTrackedRaycast for position refinement in subsequent frames.
rules.quote: it's best to avoid waiting for more accurate data before placing an object.

rules.heading: Helping people place objects
rules.rule: Provide visual or audible cues to guide users toward offscreen virtual objects.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing virtual object offscreen with no indicator, leaving user unable to locate it.
rules.fix_uikit: Display directional arrow or play audio cue at screen edge pointing toward offscreen object.
rules.quote: you can help people find such objects by offering visual or audible cues.

rules.heading: Designing object interactions
rules.rule: Prefer direct touch manipulation of 3D objects over indirect screen-space controls when stationary.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring users to use on-screen sliders or buttons to move/rotate objects instead of direct touch.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement gesture recognizers (UIPanGestureRecognizer, UIRotationGestureRecognizer) on ARView for direct object manipulation.
rules.quote: It's more immersive and intuitive when people can interact with onscreen 3D objects by touching them directly, than by using indirect controls in screen space.

rules.heading: Designing object interactions
rules.rule: Support standard gestures: single-finger drag for movement, two-finger rotation for spinning.
rules.anti_pattern: Using non-standard gesture combinations (e.g., three-finger tap for rotation) without clear affordance.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIPanGestureRecognizer for drag; UIRotationGestureRecognizer for two-finger rotation.
rules.quote: consider supporting a single-finger drag gesture for moving objects, and a two-finger rotation gesture for spinning objects.

rules.heading: Designing object interactions
rules.rule: Detect gestures within reasonable proximity of interactive objects, not requiring pixel-perfect accuracy.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring exact touch on small or distant objects; rejecting gestures outside tight bounding box.
rules.fix_uikit: Expand hit-test area using hitTest with larger tolerance; use ARHitTestResult with expanded bounds.
rules.quote: When your app detects a gesture near an interactive object, it's usually best to assume that people want to affect that object.

rules.heading: Communicating with people
rules.rule: Use approachable, conversational terminology; avoid technical AR jargon (ARKit, tracking, plane).
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying error: "Unable to find a plane. Adjust tracking." or "Insufficient features detected."
rules.fix_uikit: Use user-friendly copy: "Unable to find a surface. Try moving to the side or repositioning your phone."
rules.quote: avoid using technical terms like ARKit, world detection, and tracking.

rules.heading: Handling interruptions
rules.rule: Use ARCoachingOverlayView during relocalization to help users restore device position and orientation.
rules.anti_pattern: Silently attempting relocalization without user guidance; virtual objects appear in wrong positions.
rules.fix_uikit: Show ARCoachingOverlayView with goal = .relocalization when ARSession tracking state is limited.
rules.quote: you can use the coaching view to help people return the device to its previous position and orientation.

rules.heading: Handling interruptions
rules.rule: Hide previously placed virtual objects during relocalization to prevent flickering or visual artifacts.
rules.anti_pattern: Keeping virtual objects visible while relocalization updates their positions, causing visible jumps.
rules.fix_uikit: Set isHidden = true on virtual object nodes when ARSession tracking state becomes limited; restore after relocalization succeeds.
rules.quote: it can be best to hide virtual objects and redisplay them in their new positions.

rules.heading: Icons and badges
rules.rule: Use AR glyph only for initiating ARKit experiences; never alter, repurpose, or use with non-ARKit AR.
rules.anti_pattern: Modifying AR glyph color/shape; using it to launch WebAR or third-party AR frameworks.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("ARGlyph") without .renderingMode(.template) or color modifications.
rules.fix_uikit: Use unmodified AR glyph image from Resources; do not apply tintColor or image effects.
rules.quote: The glyph is strictly for initiating an ARKit-based experience. Never alter the glyph (other than adjusting its size and color), use it for other purposes, or use it in conjunction with AR experiences not created using ARKit.

rules.heading: Icons and badges
rules.rule: Maintain minimum 10% clear space around AR glyph; do not occlude or infringe with other elements.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing AR glyph adjacent to text or buttons without padding; overlapping elements.
rules.fix_swiftui: .padding(glyphHeight * 0.1) around Image("ARGlyph").
rules.fix_uikit: Set frame with 10% margin; use layoutMargins or constraints to enforce clear space.
rules.quote: The minimum amount of clear space required around an AR glyph is 10% of the glyph's height.

rules.heading: Icons and badges
rules.rule: Use AR badges only when app contains mixed AR-viewable and non-AR-viewable objects.
rules.anti_pattern: Badging all products in catalog when 100% support AR viewing.
rules.fix_swiftui: Conditionally show badge: if !allProductsHaveARSupport { ARBadgeView() }
rules.fix_uikit: Check product count with AR support; only add badge subview if < total product count.
rules.quote: Use badging only when your app contains a mixture of objects that can be viewed in AR and objects that cannot.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep box size significantly smaller than containing view to maintain visual separation effectiveness.
rules.anti_pattern: let box = UIView(); box.frame = view.bounds // Box fills entire screen, defeating grouping purpose
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Box { content }.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: 300) } // Constrain box relative to container
rules.fix_uikit: box.frame = CGRect(x: 16, y: 16, width: view.bounds.width - 32, height: 200) // Leave margin around box
rules.quote: Prefer keeping a box relatively small in comparison with its containing view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use padding and alignment for internal grouping instead of nesting multiple boxes.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Box { VStack { Box { item1 } Box { item2 } } } } // Nested boxes create visual clutter
rules.fix_swiftui: Box { VStack(spacing: 16) { item1.padding(.bottom, 8) item2.padding(.top, 8) } } // Use padding for subgroups
rules.fix_uikit: let stack = UIStackView([item1, item2]); stack.spacing = 16; box.addSubview(stack) // Single box with spaced items
rules.quote: Consider using padding and alignment to communicate additional grouping within a box.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Provide succinct introductory title to clarify box contents and aid VoiceOver users.
rules.anti_pattern: Box { content } // No title; VoiceOver users cannot predict grouped content
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(alignment: .leading) { Text("Settings").font(.headline); Box { content } } // Add descriptive title
rules.fix_uikit: let titleLabel = UILabel(); titleLabel.text = "Settings"; box.addSubview(titleLabel) // Explicit title label
rules.quote: Provide a succinct introductory title if it helps clarify the box's contents.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use sentence-style capitalization for box titles; append colon only in settings panes.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("ACCOUNT SETTINGS") // ALL CAPS violates sentence-style capitalization
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Account settings") // Sentence-style; no colon unless in settings pane
rules.fix_uikit: titleLabel.text = "Account settings" // Sentence-style capitalization
rules.quote: Use sentence-style capitalization. Avoid ending punctuation unless you use a box in a settings pane, where you append a colon to the title.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use secondary or tertiary background colors for iOS/iPadOS boxes by default.
rules.anti_pattern: box.backgroundColor = UIColor.white // Custom color ignores platform defaults
rules.fix_swiftui: Box { content }.background(Color(.secondarySystemBackground)) // Use system secondary color
rules.fix_uikit: box.backgroundColor = UIColor.secondarySystemBackground // Apply platform default
rules.quote: By default, iOS and iPadOS use the secondary and tertiary background colors in boxes.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Display box title above the box on macOS by default.
rules.anti_pattern: NSBox(); box.title = "Settings" // Title embedded inside box frame
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(alignment: .leading) { Text("Settings"); Box { content } } // Title positioned above
rules.quote: By default, macOS displays a box's title above it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use your brand's unique voice and tone consistently in all written communication.
rules.anti_pattern: let label = UILabel(); label.text = "Click here to proceed" // Generic, brand-agnostic tone
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Let's get started!").font(.body).foregroundStyle(.primary)
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Let's get started!"
rules.quote: Use your brand's unique voice and tone in all the written communication you display.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use brand accent color judiciously on primary actions and status indicators, not broadly.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Action") }.foregroundColor(.brandColor) // Every button uses brand color
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Primary Action") {}.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).tint(.brandColor)
rules.fix_uikit: button.tintColor = .brandColor
rules.quote: Using your brand color too broadly can overwhelm your interface and dilute its impact.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Custom fonts must be legible at all sizes and support Dynamic Type and bold text.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Headline").font(.custom("BrandFont", size: 12)) // Fixed size, no Dynamic Type support
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Headline").font(.system(.headline)).tracking(0.5) // Use system font or ensure custom font scales with Dynamic Type
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont(name: "BrandFont", size: UIFontMetrics.default.scaledValue(for: 16)) // Scale with Dynamic Type
rules.quote: If your brand is strongly associated with a specific font, be sure that it's legible at all sizes and supports accessibility features like bold text and Dynamic Type.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Customize component appearance to reflect brand while preserving familiar sizing, placement, and behavior.
rules.anti_pattern: struct CustomButton: View { var body: some View { Rectangle().fill(.brandColor).frame(width: 200, height: 80) } } // Unrecognizable button
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Text("Action") }.buttonStyle(.bordered).tint(.brandColor) // Familiar button with brand tint
rules.fix_uikit: button.setTitleColor(.brandColor, for: .normal) // Customize within standard UIButton bounds
rules.quote: If you need to customize a component's appearance to reflect your brand, ensure that details like sizing, placement, and behavior continue to preserve a familiar experience that's appropriate for the platform.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Branding must defer to content; do not waste screen space on decorative brand assets.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Image("logo").frame(height: 100); contentView } // Large logo reduces content space
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { contentView; Spacer() } // Integrate logo subtly or omit if not essential
rules.fix_uikit: // Prioritize content layout; embed logo only if contextually necessary
rules.quote: Ensure branding always defers to content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use standard UI patterns consistently; place controls in expected locations and use standard symbols.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom navigation with non-standard gestures and unlabeled icons
rules.fix_swiftui: NavigationStack { List { ... } } // Use standard navigation; use SF Symbols for actions
rules.fix_uikit: navigationController.pushViewController(...) // Follow UIKit conventions for navigation
rules.quote: Help people feel comfortable by using standard patterns consistently.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not display your logo throughout the app unless essential for context.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Image("logo"); navigationView; Image("logo"); contentView; Image("logo") } // Logo on every screen
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { navigationView; contentView } // Omit redundant logo; users know which app they're using
rules.fix_uikit: // Remove logo from every screen; display only when contextually necessary
rules.quote: Resist the temptation to display your logo throughout your app or game unless it's essential for providing context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not use launch screens as branding opportunities; consider welcome or onboarding screens instead.
rules.anti_pattern: // Launch screen displays large logo and brand tagline for 2 seconds
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use launch screen only for minimal UI; display branding in onboarding screen after app loads
rules.fix_uikit: // Defer branding to welcome/onboarding flow, not launch screen
rules.quote: Avoid using a launch screen as a branding opportunity.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not use Apple trademarks in app name or images; follow Apple's trademark guidelines.
rules.anti_pattern: // App name: "MyApp for iPhone" or image containing Apple logo without permission
rules.fix_swiftui: // App name: "MyApp" (no Apple trademark); use only licensed Apple assets
rules.fix_uikit: // Ensure app name and images comply with Apple Trademark List and guidelines
rules.quote: Follow Apple's trademark guidelines.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Move brand color into content layer where it scrolls beneath Liquid Glass controls.
rules.anti_pattern: // Brand color applied to all UI controls; static and overwhelming
rules.fix_swiftui: ZStack { contentWithBrandColor; LiquidGlassControl() } // Brand color in scrolling content beneath glass
rules.fix_uikit: // Layer brand color in content; keep controls neutral or system-colored
rules.quote: To express your brand through color, consider moving it into the content layer, where it scrolls beneath Liquid Glass controls and gets picked up dynamically.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure button hit region is at least 44x44 pt (60x60 pt in visionOS).
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap") }.frame(width: 30, height: 30)
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap") }.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
rules.fix_uikit: button.frame = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 44, height: 44)
rules.quote: As a general rule, a button needs a hit region of at least 44x44 pt — in visionOS, 60x60 pt — to ensure that people can select it easily, whether they use a fingertip, a pointer, their eyes, or a remote.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Always include a visually distinct press state for custom buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap") }.buttonStyle(.plain)
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap") }.buttonStyle(.bordered)
rules.fix_uikit: button.setBackgroundImage(UIImage(named: "pressed"), for: .highlighted)
rules.quote: Always include a press state for a custom button.

rules.heading: Style
rules.rule: Use one prominent button style per view to highlight the most likely action.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Button("Save") { }.buttonStyle(.filled); Button("Delete") { }.buttonStyle(.filled) }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Button("Save") { }.buttonStyle(.filled); Button("Delete") { }.buttonStyle(.bordered) }
rules.fix_uikit: saveButton.backgroundColor = UIColor.systemBlue; deleteButton.backgroundColor = nil
rules.quote: In general, use a button that has a prominent visual style for the most likely action in a view.

rules.heading: Style
rules.rule: Use button style, not size, to distinguish preferred choice among multiple options.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Button("Yes") { }.frame(width: 80); Button("No") { }.frame(width: 40) }
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Button("Yes") { }.buttonStyle(.filled); Button("No") { }.buttonStyle(.bordered) }
rules.fix_uikit: yesButton.backgroundColor = UIColor.systemBlue; noButton.backgroundColor = nil
rules.quote: Use style — not size — to visually distinguish the preferred choice among multiple options.

rules.heading: Style
rules.rule: Avoid applying similar color to button labels and content layer backgrounds.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap") }.foregroundColor(.white) // on white background
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Tap") {}.foregroundStyle(.black)
rules.fix_uikit: button.setTitleColor(.black, for: .normal)
rules.quote: Avoid applying a similar color to button labels and content layer backgrounds.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Ensure each button clearly communicates its purpose via symbol, text label, or both.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "questionmark") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Label("Help", systemImage: "questionmark.circle") }
rules.fix_uikit: button.setTitle("Help", for: .normal); button.setImage(UIImage(systemName: "questionmark.circle"), for: .normal)
rules.quote: Ensure that each button clearly communicates its purpose.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use familiar icons for familiar actions; prefer SF Symbols for consistency.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Image("custom_share_icon") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "square.and.arrow.up") }
rules.fix_uikit: button.setImage(UIImage(systemName: "square.and.arrow.up"), for: .normal)
rules.quote: Try to associate familiar actions with familiar icons.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use concise text labels starting with a verb to describe button action.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("shopping") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Text("Add to Cart") }
rules.fix_uikit: button.setTitle("Add to Cart", for: .normal)
rules.quote: Using title-style capitalization, consider starting the label with a verb to help convey the button's action — for example, a button that lets people add items to their shopping cart might use the label "Add to Cart."

rules.heading: Role
rules.rule: Assign primary role to the button people are most likely to choose.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Cancel", role: .primary, action: {})
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Confirm") {}.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)
rules.fix_uikit: confirmButton.keyEquivalent = "\r"
rules.quote: Assign the primary role to the button people are most likely to choose.

rules.heading: Role
rules.rule: Never assign primary role to destructive buttons, even if most likely choice.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Delete All", role: .primary, action: { deleteData() })
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Delete All", role: .destructive) { deleteData() }
rules.fix_uikit: deleteButton.setTitleColor(.systemRed, for: .normal)
rules.quote: Don't assign the primary role to a button that performs a destructive action, even if that action is the most likely choice.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Display activity indicator within button for non-instant actions with optional label change.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Checkout", action: { performCheckout() })
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { performCheckout() }) { HStack { ProgressView().scaleEffect(0.8); Text(isLoading ? "Checking out…" : "Checkout") } }
rules.fix_uikit: button.setTitle("Checking out…", for: .disabled); let spinner = UIActivityIndicatorView(); button.addSubview(spinner)
rules.quote: Configure a button to display an activity indicator when you need to provide feedback about an action that doesn't instantly complete.

rules.heading: Push buttons
rules.rule: Use flexible-height push button only for tall or variable-height content.
rules.anti_pattern: NSButton(frame: NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100)); button.bezelStyle = .flexiblePush
rules.fix_uikit: button.bezelStyle = .flexiblePush // only when content is two lines or tall icon
rules.quote: Use a flexible-height push button only when you need to display tall or variable height content.

rules.heading: Push buttons
rules.rule: Append trailing ellipsis to push button title when it opens another window or view.
rules.anti_pattern: button.title = "Edit"
rules.fix_uikit: button.title = "Edit…"
rules.quote: Append a trailing ellipsis to the title when a push button opens another window, view, or app.

rules.heading: Square buttons
rules.rule: Use square buttons in views only, not in window frame, toolbar, or status bar.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar.addItem(NSToolbarItem(itemIdentifier: "square", button: squareButton))
rules.fix_uikit: // Place squareButton within the view, not in toolbar
rules.quote: Use square buttons in a view, not in the window frame.

rules.heading: Square buttons
rules.rule: Prefer SF Symbols in square buttons over custom icons.
rules.anti_pattern: button.image = NSImage(named: "custom_add")
rules.fix_uikit: button.image = NSImage(systemSymbolName: "plus", accessibilityDescription: "Add")
rules.quote: Prefer using a symbol in a square button.

rules.heading: Help buttons
rules.rule: Use system-provided help button to display help documentation.
rules.anti_pattern: button.image = NSImage(named: "custom_help"); button.title = "Help"
rules.fix_uikit: button.bezelStyle = .helpButton
rules.quote: Use the system-provided help button to display your help documentation.

rules.heading: Help buttons
rules.rule: Include no more than one help button per window.
rules.anti_pattern: window.addSubview(helpButton1); window.addSubview(helpButton2)
rules.fix_uikit: // Add only one help button per window
rules.quote: Include no more than one help button per window.

rules.heading: Image buttons
rules.rule: Use image buttons in views only, not in window frame, toolbar, or status bar.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar.addItem(NSToolbarItem(itemIdentifier: "image", button: imageButton))
rules.fix_uikit: // Place imageButton within the view, not in toolbar
rules.quote: Use an image button in a view, not in the window frame.

rules.heading: Image buttons
rules.rule: Include about 10 pixels of padding between image edges and button edges.
rules.anti_pattern: button.image = NSImage(named: "icon"); button.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 20, height: 20)
rules.fix_uikit: button.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 40, height: 40) // 10px padding on each side
rules.quote: Include about 10 pixels of padding between the edges of the image and the button edges.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use charts to highlight important dataset information; avoid charts for simple data presentation without analytical intent.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying a list of numbers in a bar chart when a simple table or list would suffice.
rules.fix_swiftui: Evaluate whether Chart is necessary; use List or Table for passive data display without analytical context.
rules.quote: Use a chart when you want to highlight important information about a dataset.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep charts simple; let users choose when to reveal additional details rather than displaying all data at once.
rules.anti_pattern: Rendering 50 data series with 12 axes in a single chart without filtering or drill-down options.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @State to toggle detail levels; provide filtering controls or drill-down navigation to reveal subsets progressively.
rules.quote: Keep a chart simple, letting people choose when they want additional details.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide accessibility labels for chart values and components; include accessibility elements for chart interaction.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a Chart without .accessibilityLabel, .accessibilityValue, or .accessibilityElement modifiers on marks.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .accessibilityLabel and .accessibilityValue to each ChartMark; wrap interactive elements with .accessibilityElement(children: .combine).
rules.quote: Make every chart in your app accessible.

rules.heading: Designing effective charts
rules.rule: Prefer common chart types (bar, line) to leverage user familiarity; use novel types only with educational guidance.
rules.anti_pattern: Introducing a custom radial bubble chart without animation or explanation of how to interpret it.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use BarMark, LineMark, AreaMark, or PointMark; if using custom visualization, add onboarding animation or instructional text.
rules.quote: In general, prefer using common chart types.

rules.heading: Designing effective charts
rules.rule: Add descriptive titles, subtitles, and annotations to emphasize key information and actionable takeaways.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying a chart with no title, legend, or annotations; users cannot understand what data is shown.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add Text above/below Chart for title and summary; use .chartAngleSelection or annotations to highlight key values.
rules.quote: Aid comprehension by adding descriptive text to the chart.

rules.heading: Designing effective charts
rules.rule: Size charts to match functionality, topic, and detail level; ensure labels and annotations remain readable.
rules.anti_pattern: Using .frame(height: 60) for a complex multi-series chart with 20 annotations; text becomes illegible.
rules.fix_swiftui: Set .frame(height:) proportional to data complexity and interactivity; test with Dynamic Type to ensure readability.
rules.quote: Match the size of a chart to its functionality, topic, and level of detail.

rules.heading: Designing effective charts
rules.rule: Use consistent chart types and styles across related charts; deviate only to highlight meaningful differences.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying three trend charts in the same view using bar, line, and area marks without explanation.
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply the same ChartMark type, color scheme, and annotation style to related charts; document deviations.
rules.quote: Prefer consistency across multiple charts, deviating only when you need to highlight differences.

rules.heading: Designing effective charts
rules.rule: Maintain visual continuity (colors, marks, annotations, layout) when showing the same dataset across multiple chart views.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing a summary chart with blue bars, then expanding to a detail view with red bars and different annotations.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use consistent .foregroundStyle, ChartMark types, and annotation positions across all chart views of the same dataset.
rules.quote: Maintain continuity among multiple charts that use the same data.

rules.heading: Designing effective charts
rules.rule: Examine data from macro, mid, and micro levels to identify summaries, subsets, and specific values worth highlighting.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying raw data points without aggregations, trends, or visual emphasis on outliers or key metrics.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use RuleMark for averages/totals; apply .chartPointHoverModifier to highlight specific values; add annotations for key insights.
rules.quote: Examine the data from multiple levels or perspectives to find details you can display to enhance the chart.

rules.heading: Marks
rules.rule: Choose mark type based on the information you want to communicate about the data.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use LineMark for time-series trends, PointMark for individual value inspection, BarMark for category comparison or sums over time periods.
rules.quote: Choose a mark type based on the information you want to communicate about the data.

rules.heading: Marks
rules.rule: Combine mark types when it adds clarity, such as line with points to show trend and individual values.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add PointMark overlay on LineMark to highlight individual data points and help people understand overall trend while drawing attention to individual values.
rules.quote: Consider combining mark types when it adds clarity to your chart.

rules.heading: Axes
rules.rule: Use fixed axis range for meaningful min/max values; use dynamic range when data varies widely.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use fixed range (0...100) for battery charts; use dynamic range for Health Steps chart where bounds vary with data.
rules.quote: Use a fixed or dynamic axis range depending on the meaning of your chart.

rules.heading: Axes
rules.rule: Define lower bound based on mark type; bar charts work well with zero; line charts may need non-zero bounds.
rules.fix_swiftui: For heart rate, use dynamic lower bound (e.g., 50...120) to make meaningful differences between resting and active readings discernible.
rules.quote: Define the value of the lower bound based on mark type and chart usage.

rules.heading: Axes
rules.rule: Use familiar, common sequences for tick and grid-line labels (e.g., 0, 5, 10) not uncommon ones (e.g., 1, 6, 11).
rules.anti_pattern:
AxisMarks(values: [1, 6, 11, 16, 21])
// Uncommon sequence requires extra cognitive effort
rules.fix_swiftui: AxisMarks(values: [0, 5, 10, 15, 20])
rules.quote: Prefer familiar sequences of values in the tick and grid-line labels for an axis.

rules.heading: Axes
rules.rule: Tailor grid line density and label appearance to chart context; too many overwhelm, too few obscure values.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use fewer grid lines with light label colors when people can inspect individual points; adjust density based on chart context and interaction support.
rules.quote: Tailor the appearance of grid lines and labels to a chart's use cases.

rules.heading: Descriptive content
rules.rule: Write descriptions that help people understand chart purpose before viewing it.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .chartTitle("Expected Precipitation") and .chartSubtitle("Next hour forecast") to provide context before examining details.
rules.quote: Write descriptions that help people understand what a chart does before they view it.

rules.heading: Descriptive content
rules.rule: Summarize the main message of your chart to make it approachable and useful.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add title and subtitle summarizing key insight: "You averaged 8,500 steps this week, up 12% from last week."
rules.quote: Summarize the main message of your chart to help make it approachable and useful for everyone.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Establish consistent visual hierarchy where data is most prominent and descriptions provide context.
rules.anti_pattern:
Chart(data) { value in
  BarMark(x: .value("X", value.x), y: .value("Y", value.y))
    .foregroundColor(.gray)
}
.chartTitle("Title", position: .top)
.chartSubtitle("Subtitle", position: .top)
// Descriptions compete with data for visual prominence
rules.quote: Establish a consistent visual hierarchy that helps communicate the relative importance of various chart elements.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: In compact environments, maximize plot area width and minimize axis label length.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use short axis labels; describe units in title; place longer labels inside plot area when safe.
rules.quote: In a compact environment, maximize the width of the plot area to give people enough space to comfortably examine a chart.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Make every chart accessible; support VoiceOver and provide accessibility labels for all important elements.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .accessibilityLabel() and .accessibilityValue() to marks; use Audio Graphs; provide chart overview for VoiceOver.
rules.quote: Make every chart in your app accessible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Let people interact with data when sensible, but don't require interaction to reveal critical information.
rules.fix_swiftui: Display main message in title/subtitle; allow optional interaction (e.g., drag to inspect details) without hiding key data.
rules.quote: Let people interact with the data when it makes sense, but don't require interaction to reveal critical information.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Expand hit targets to entire plot area when marks are too small to target comfortably.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .chartAngleSelection() or .chartXSelection() to expand hit target across plot area; let people scrub to reveal values.
rules.quote: Make it easy for everyone to interact with a chart.

rules.heading: Color
rules.rule: Avoid relying solely on color to differentiate data; use shapes, patterns, or labels as alternatives.
rules.quote: Avoid relying solely on color to differentiate between different pieces of data or communicate essential information in a chart.

rules.heading: Color
rules.rule: Add visual separation between contiguous areas of color in stacked charts.
rules.quote: Aid comprehension by adding visual separation between contiguous areas of color.

rules.heading: Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.citation: charts.md › Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.rule: Provide accessibility labels for each important or interactive chart element; use Audio Graphs.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .accessibilityLabel() and .accessibilityValue() to each mark; enable Audio Graphs with chart title and summary.
rules.quote: Unlike an image — which requires one descriptive accessibility label — a chart often needs to offer an accessibility label for each important or interactive element.

rules.heading: Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.citation: charts.md › Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.rule: Write accessibility labels that support the chart's purpose, not just report raw values.
rules.anti_pattern:
.accessibilityLabel("8500")
// Only reports value without context
rules.fix_swiftui: Chart { }.accessibilityLabel("Monday, 8,500 steps")
rules.quote: Write accessibility labels that support the purpose of your chart.

rules.heading: Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.citation: charts.md › Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.rule: Use objective values in accessibility labels, not subjective terms like 'rapidly' or 'gradually'.
rules.anti_pattern:
.accessibilityLabel("Steps increased rapidly on Tuesday")
// Subjective interpretation
rules.fix_swiftui: Chart { }.accessibilityLabel("Tuesday, 12,000 steps, up 40% from Monday")
rules.quote: Avoid using subjective terms.

rules.heading: Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.citation: charts.md › Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.rule: Avoid ambiguous formats and abbreviations in accessibility labels; spell out units and dates.
rules.anti_pattern:
.accessibilityLabel("6/6, 60m")
// Ambiguous date format and abbreviated unit
rules.fix_swiftui: Chart { }.accessibilityLabel("June 6, 60 minutes")
rules.quote: Maximize clarity in data descriptions by avoiding potentially ambiguous formats and abbreviations.

rules.heading: Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.citation: charts.md › Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.rule: Describe what chart details represent, not what they look like; avoid describing colors.
rules.anti_pattern:
.accessibilityLabel("Red bar representing systolic pressure")
// Describes visual appearance (color) instead of meaning
rules.fix_swiftui: Chart { }.accessibilityLabel("Systolic blood pressure, 120 mmHg")
rules.quote: Describe what the chart's details represent, not what they look like.

rules.heading: Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.citation: charts.md › Enhancing the accessibility of a chart
rules.rule: Hide visible axis and tick labels from assistive technologies; VoiceOver users get values via accessibility labels.
rules.anti_pattern:
AxisMarks()
// Axis labels exposed to VoiceOver, redundant with accessibility labels
rules.fix_swiftui: AxisMarks().accessibilityHidden(true)
rules.quote: Hide visible text labels for axes and ticks from assistive technologies.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place Share button in toolbar or convenient location to enable easy sharing initiation.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Share") }.padding(.bottom, 200)
rules.fix_swiftui: ShareLink(item: document) { Label("Share", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.up") }.toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { ... } }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.rightBarButtonItem = UIBarButtonItem(barButtonSystemItem: .action, target: self, action: #selector(share))
rules.quote: Place the Share button in a convenient location, like a toolbar, to make it easy for people to start sharing or collaborating.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Customize share sheet only if necessary to reflect supported file-sharing methods and collaboration types.
rules.anti_pattern: let vc = UIActivityViewController(activityItems: [item], applicationActivities: nil); present(vc, animated: true)
rules.fix_swiftui: ShareLink(item: document, subject: Text("Collaborate"), message: Text("Join my document")) { Label("Share", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.up") }
rules.fix_uikit: let vc = UIActivityViewController(activityItems: [document, collaborationObject], applicationActivities: nil); present(vc, animated: true)
rules.quote: If necessary, customize the share sheet or sharing popover to offer the types of file sharing your app supports.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Write succinct permission summary phrases like 'Only invited people can edit' or 'Everyone can make changes'.
rules.anti_pattern: permissionLabel = "This document is shared with multiple people who have different access levels depending on their role and the settings you configured"
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Only invited people can edit")
rules.fix_uikit: permissionButton.setTitle("Everyone can make changes", for: .normal)
rules.quote: Write succinct phrases that summarize the sharing permissions you support.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide minimal, grouped sharing options that clarify access control and edit permissions without overwhelming users.
rules.anti_pattern: let options = ["Edit", "View", "Comment", "Suggest", "Manage", "Archive", "Duplicate", "Lock", "Expire", "Notify"]
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Access", selection: $access) { Text("Can edit").tag("edit"); Text("Can view").tag("view") }
rules.fix_uikit: let segmentedControl = UISegmentedControl(items: ["Can edit", "Can view"])
rules.quote: Provide a set of simple sharing options that streamline collaboration setup.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display Collaboration button prominently immediately after collaboration begins, typically next to Share button.
rules.anti_pattern: if isCollaborating { Button("Collaborators") { ... }.padding(.bottom, 300) }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.rightBarButtonItems = [collaborationButton, shareButton]
rules.quote: Prominently display the Collaboration button as soon as collaboration starts.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include only essential custom actions in collaboration popover; avoid overwhelming users with excessive information.
rules.anti_pattern: collaborationPopover.items = [collaborators, messages, facetime, customAction1, customAction2, customAction3, customAction4, customAction5, manageFile]
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { CollaboratorsList(); MessageButton(); ManageFileButton() }
rules.fix_uikit: let popover = UIViewController(); popover.view.addSubview(collaboratorsView); popover.view.addSubview(messageButton); popover.view.addSubview(manageButton)
rules.quote: Provide custom actions in the collaboration popover only if needed.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Customize collaboration-management button title if appropriate for your app's context.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Manage Shared File") { ... }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Manage Document") { showManagementView() }
rules.fix_uikit: manageButton.setTitle("Manage Collaborators", for: .normal)
rules.quote: If it makes sense in your app, customize the title of the modal view's collaboration-management button.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Post collaboration event notifications in Messages with universal links to relevant app views.
rules.anti_pattern: let notification = UNMutableNotificationContent(); notification.body = "Someone changed the document"
rules.fix_swiftui: let event = SWHighlightEvent(title: "Document updated", subtitle: "John made changes", universalLink: URL(string: "myapp://document/123")!)
rules.fix_uikit: let event = SWHighlightEvent(title: "Collaborator joined", subtitle: "Jane joined", universalLink: URL(string: "myapp://document/456")!)
rules.quote: Consider posting collaboration event notifications in Messages.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use standard row or grid layout; avoid custom layouts that confuse users or draw undue attention.
rules.anti_pattern: let customLayout = UICollectionViewLayout(); collectionView.collectionViewLayout = customLayout // without justification
rules.fix_swiftui: LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.flexible())]) { ... } or LazyHStack { ... }
rules.fix_uikit: UICollectionViewFlowLayout() with standard configuration
rules.quote: Use the standard row or grid layout whenever possible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer tables over collections for displaying primarily textual information.
rules.anti_pattern: UICollectionView with text-only cells instead of UITableView
rules.fix_swiftui: List { ... } instead of LazyVGrid for text content
rules.fix_uikit: UITableViewController for text-heavy content
rules.quote: Consider using a table instead of a collection for text.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide adequate padding around collection items to prevent overlap and ensure clear focus/hover states.
rules.anti_pattern: flowLayout.minimumInteritemSpacing = 0; flowLayout.minimumLineSpacing = 0
rules.fix_swiftui: .padding() or .frame(minHeight:) on collection items
rules.fix_uikit: flowLayout.minimumInteritemSpacing = 8; flowLayout.minimumLineSpacing = 8
rules.quote: Use adequate padding around images to keep focus or hover effects easy to see and prevent content from overlapping.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Add custom gestures only when necessary; rely on standard tap, touch-and-hold, and swipe interactions.
rules.anti_pattern: collectionView.addGestureRecognizer(UITapGestureRecognizer()); collectionView.addGestureRecognizer(UIPinchGestureRecognizer()); // without clear justification
rules.fix_swiftui: Use built-in .onTapGesture; add custom gestures only for app-specific workflows
rules.fix_uikit: Rely on UICollectionViewDelegate tap/selection; add UIGestureRecognizer only when required
rules.quote: By default, people can tap to select, touch and hold to edit, and swipe to scroll.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use animations when inserting, deleting, or reordering collection items to provide visual feedback.
rules.anti_pattern: collectionView.deleteItems(at: indexPaths) // without animation
rules.fix_swiftui: withAnimation { ... } around state changes that modify collection
rules.fix_uikit: UICollectionView.performBatchUpdates { ... } with deleteItems/insertItems/moveItem
rules.quote: Consider using animations to provide feedback when people insert, delete, or reorder items.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Avoid dynamic layout changes while users interact with collection; only change in response to explicit user action.
rules.anti_pattern: Timer.scheduledTimer { self.collectionView.collectionViewLayout = newLayout } // during scrolling
rules.fix_swiftui: Update layout state only in response to user gestures or explicit button taps
rules.fix_uikit: Change layout only in response to UIControl events or explicit user actions, not timers
rules.quote: Be sure any changes make sense and are easy to track.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer system-provided color picker for consistent cross-platform experience and saved color access.
rules.fix_swiftui: ColorPicker("Select Color", selection: $color)
rules.fix_uikit: let picker = UIColorPickerViewController(); picker.delegate = self; present(picker, animated: true)
rules.quote: Using the built-in color picker provides a consistent experience, in addition to letting people save a set of colors they can access from any app.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Display visual highlight on color well when clicked to confirm active state before picker opens.
rules.anti_pattern:
NSColorWell()
// No highlight feedback configured
rules.quote: When people click a color well, it receives a highlight to provide visual confirmation that it's active.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Implement drag-and-drop support between color wells and from color picker to color well on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
NSColorWell()
// No drag-drop delegates configured
rules.quote: Color wells also support drag and drop, so people can drag colors from one color well to another, and from the color picker to a color well.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Update color well display immediately after user selects new color from picker.
rules.quote: After they make a selection, the color well updates to show the new color.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use color consistently throughout your interface; avoid using the same color to mean different things.
rules.anti_pattern:
let brandColor = Color.blue
Button(action: {}) { Text("Interactive") }.foregroundColor(brandColor)
Text("Noninteractive").foregroundColor(brandColor)
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Interactive") {}.foregroundStyle(.blue); Text("Noninteractive").foregroundStyle(.gray)
rules.fix_uikit: interactiveButton.setTitleColor(.systemBlue, for: .normal); noninteractiveLabel.textColor = .systemGray
rules.quote: Use color consistently throughout your interface, especially when you use it to help communicate information like status or interactivity.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure all app colors work in light, dark, and increased contrast contexts with appropriate variants.
rules.anti_pattern:
let customColor = Color(red: 0.2, green: 0.4, blue: 0.8)
Text("Content").foregroundColor(customColor)
rules.quote: Make sure all your app's colors work well in light, dark, and increased contrast contexts.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Test app color scheme under varied lighting conditions and on different devices to ensure optimal viewing.
rules.anti_pattern: // Design colors only in Xcode simulator under standard lighting
rules.fix_swiftui: // Test on physical devices in sunlight, dim light, and standard indoor lighting; verify on multiple device models
rules.fix_uikit: // Test on iPhone, iPad, Mac with True Tone enabled/disabled; verify color appearance across lighting conditions
rules.quote: Test your app's color scheme under a variety of lighting conditions.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer system-provided color controls when allowing users to choose colors.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom color picker implementation without system integration
rules.fix_swiftui: ColorPicker("Choose Color", selection: $selectedColor)
rules.quote: If your app lets people choose colors, prefer system-provided color controls where available.

rules.heading: Inclusive color
rules.rule: Never rely solely on color to differentiate objects, indicate interactivity, or communicate essential information.
rules.fix_swiftui: Label("Error", systemImage: "xmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(.red); Label("Success", systemImage: "checkmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(.green)
rules.quote: Avoid relying solely on color to differentiate between objects, indicate interactivity, or communicate essential information.

rules.heading: Inclusive color
rules.rule: Avoid color combinations with insufficient contrast that make content hard to read or perceive.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Content").foregroundColor(.gray).background(Color.white)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Content").foregroundStyle(.black).background(.white)
rules.quote: Avoid using colors that make it hard to perceive content in your app.

rules.heading: System colors
rules.rule: Use system color APIs instead of hard-coding color values; documented values are for reference only.
rules.anti_pattern:
let systemBlue = Color(red: 0.0, green: 0.478, blue: 1.0)
Text("Link").foregroundColor(systemBlue)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Link").foregroundStyle(.blue)
rules.quote: Avoid hard-coding system color values in your app.

rules.heading: System colors
rules.rule: Use dynamic system colors only for their intended semantic purpose; do not repurpose them.
rules.anti_pattern:
Text("Background").foregroundColor(.separator)
Rectangle().fill(Color(UIColor.secondaryLabel))
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").foregroundStyle(.secondary); Rectangle().fill(.background.secondary)
rules.quote: Avoid redefining the semantic meanings of dynamic system colors.

rules.heading: Liquid Glass color
rules.rule: Apply color sparingly to Liquid Glass; reserve it for emphasis on primary actions or status indicators.
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItem { Button("Primary") { }.tint(.blue) }; ToolbarItem { Button("Secondary") { } }
rules.quote: Apply color sparingly to the Liquid Glass material, and to symbols or text on the material.

rules.heading: Liquid Glass color
rules.rule: Avoid similar colors in control labels on colorful backgrounds; prefer monochromatic or high-contrast accent colors.
rules.quote: Avoid using similar colors in control labels if your app has a colorful background.

rules.heading: Color management
rules.rule: Apply color profiles to images to ensure colors appear as intended on different displays.
rules.anti_pattern: // Export images without embedded color profile
rules.fix_swiftui: // Embed sRGB or Display P3 color profile in PNG images via Xcode asset catalog
rules.fix_uikit: // Use Xcode asset catalog to assign color profiles to image sets
rules.quote: Apply color profiles to your images.

rules.heading: Color management
rules.rule: Use wide color (Display P3) to enhance visual experience on compatible displays with richer, more saturated colors.
rules.anti_pattern: // Design only in sRGB color space
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use Display P3 color profile at 16 bits per channel; export images in PNG format
rules.fix_uikit: // Specify P3 colors in asset catalog for wide color displays
rules.quote: Use wide color to enhance the visual experience on compatible displays.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use grouped background colors for grouped table views; use system background colors otherwise.
rules.fix_swiftui: List { Section { Text("Item") } }.scrollContentBackground(.hidden).background(.background.secondary)
rules.quote: In general, use the grouped background colors (systemGroupedBackground, secondarySystemGroupedBackground, and tertiarySystemGroupedBackground) when you have a grouped table view; otherwise, use the system set of background colors (systemBackground, secondarySystemBackground, and tertiarySystemBackground).

rules.heading: App accent colors
rules.rule: Specify an accent color to customize buttons, selection highlighting, and sidebar icons; system respects user accent color settings.
rules.anti_pattern: // Hardcode button colors without respecting system accent color preference
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Action") { }.keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)
rules.quote: Beginning in macOS 11, you can specify an accent color to customize the appearance of your app's buttons, selection highlighting, and sidebar icons.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use column views for deep hierarchies where users navigate back-and-forth frequently without needing sorting.
rules.anti_pattern: Using NSBrowser for flat data structures or when table sorting is a primary requirement.
rules.quote: Consider using a column view when you have a deep data hierarchy in which people tend to navigate back and forth frequently between levels, and you don't need the sorting capabilities that a list or table provides.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display the root level of data hierarchy in the first column to enable quick navigation reset.
rules.anti_pattern: Starting NSBrowser display at a nested level without showing the root in the first column.
rules.quote: Show the root level of your data hierarchy in the first column.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display item information or preview when selected item has no nested children.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing empty space or no detail when a leaf node is selected in NSBrowser.
rules.quote: Consider showing information about the selected item when there are no nested items to display.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Enable column resizing to accommodate long item names that exceed default column width.
rules.anti_pattern: Disabling or preventing NSBrowser column resizing when item names are truncated.
rules.quote: Let people resize columns.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Populate combo box with meaningful default value from predefined list, not empty.
rules.anti_pattern:
let comboBox = NSComboBox()
comboBox.stringValue = "" // Empty default
rules.quote: Populate the field with a meaningful default value from the list.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use introductory label with title-case capitalization ending in colon.
rules.anti_pattern: label.stringValue = "select an option" // lowercase, no colon
rules.quote: Use an introductory label to let people know what types of items to expect.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide relevant, frequently-used choices in combo box list.
rules.anti_pattern: comboBox.addItems(withObjectValues: ["obscure1", "obscure2", "obscure3"])
rules.quote: Provide relevant choices.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure list items width does not exceed text field width to prevent truncation.
rules.anti_pattern: comboBox.addItems(withObjectValues: ["This is an extremely long item that will definitely truncate"])
rules.quote: Make sure list items aren't wider than the text field.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include only relevant, frequently-used commands; exclude advanced or rarely-used items.
rules.anti_pattern: contextMenu { Button("Edit mailbox settings") {} }  // Advanced action in context menu
rules.fix_swiftui: .contextMenu { Button("Reply") {} Button("Move") {} }  // Frequent actions only
rules.fix_uikit: UIContextMenuInteraction with actions limited to primary use cases for the item
rules.quote: A context menu isn't for providing advanced or rarely used items; instead, it helps people quickly access the commands they're most likely to need in their current context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit context menu to small number of items to avoid difficult scanning and scrolling.
rules.anti_pattern: contextMenu { ForEach(1...15, id: \.self) { i in Button("Action \(i)") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: .contextMenu { Button("Action 1") {} Button("Action 2") {} Button("Action 3") {} }
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu with 3–5 child actions maximum
rules.quote: Aim for a small number of menu items.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide context menu items consistently throughout app; make them available in main interface too.
rules.anti_pattern: // Context menu on list item but no toolbar button for same action
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Reply") { } in both toolbar and .contextMenu
rules.fix_uikit: Same UIAction in both UIContextMenuInteraction and UIToolbar
rules.quote: Always make context menu items available in the main interface, too.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit submenus to one level; avoid nested submenus in context menus.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu("Edit") { Menu("Format") { Menu("Text") { Button("Bold") {} } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu("Edit") { Button("Copy") {} Button("Paste") {} }  // No nesting
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu with children, no grandchildren menus
rules.quote: If you need to use submenus to manage a menu's complexity, keep them to one level.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Hide unavailable menu items; do not dim them (except Cut, Copy, Paste in macOS).
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Delete") { }.disabled(true)  // Dimmed instead of hidden
rules.fix_swiftui: if canDelete { Button("Delete") { } }  // Conditionally include
rules.fix_uikit: Exclude unavailable UIAction from UIMenu children array
rules.quote: Hide unavailable menu items, don't dim them.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place most frequently-used items first, accounting for menu position relative to trigger point.
rules.anti_pattern: contextMenu { Button("Rarely used") {} Button("Delete") {} }  // Wrong order
rules.fix_swiftui: .contextMenu { Button("Copy") {} Button("Share") {} Button("Delete") {} }
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu with actions ordered by frequency of use
rules.quote: Aim to place the most frequently used menu items where people are likely to encounter them first.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not show keyboard shortcuts in context menus; reserve for main menus only.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Copy (⌘C)") { }  // Shortcut in context menu
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Copy") { }  // No shortcut text
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Copy", image: nil)  // No keyModifierFlags display
rules.quote: Show keyboard shortcuts in your app's main menus, not in context menus.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use separators to group items; limit to approximately three groups per context menu.
rules.anti_pattern: contextMenu { Button("A") {} Button("B") {} Button("C") {} Button("D") {} Button("E") {} }
rules.fix_swiftui: .contextMenu { Button("Copy") {} Divider() Button("Delete") {} }
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu with up to 3 child menus separated by dividers
rules.quote: In general, you don't want more than about three groups in a context menu.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Include context menu title only if it clarifies the menu's effect or scope.
rules.anti_pattern: contextMenu { Text("Actions") Button("Copy") {} }  // Redundant title
rules.fix_swiftui: .contextMenu { Button("Copy") {} }  // No title needed
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(title: "", children: [...])  // Empty title when not clarifying
rules.quote: Include a title in a context menu only if doing so clarifies the menu's effect.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use system-standard icons for common actions (Copy, Share, Delete) consistently.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Copy", systemImage: "doc.fill") { }  // Wrong icon for Copy
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Copy", systemImage: "doc.on.doc") { }  // Standard Copy icon
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "doc.on.doc") for Copy action
rules.quote: Use the same icons as the system to represent actions such as Copy, Share, and Delete, wherever they appear.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Provide either context menu or edit menu for an item, not both.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Item").contextMenu { Button("Copy") {} }.editMenu { Button("Copy") {} }
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Item").contextMenu { Button("Copy") {} }  // Context menu only
rules.fix_uikit: UIContextMenuInteraction OR UIEditMenuInteraction, not both
rules.quote: Provide either a context menu or an edit menu for an item, but not both.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use graphical preview in context menu to clarify target and confirm user intent.
rules.anti_pattern: contextMenu { Button("Delete") {} }  // No preview of item being acted upon
rules.fix_swiftui: .contextMenu(menuItems: { Button("Delete") {} }, preview: { Image(...) })
rules.fix_uikit: UIContextMenuInteractionDelegate previewForHighlightingMenuWithConfiguration
rules.quote: Prefer a graphical preview that clarifies the target of a context menu's commands.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Adjust preview clipping path to match preview shape; ensure smooth animation.
rules.anti_pattern: // Preview with rounded corners but clipping path is square; corners change during animation
rules.fix_swiftui: .contextMenu(preview: { Image(...).clipShape(RoundedRectangle(...)) })
rules.fix_uikit: UIContextMenuInteractionDelegate previewForHighlightingMenuWithConfiguration with matching clipPath
rules.quote: It's important to adjust the preview's clipping path to match the shape of the preview image so that its contours, such as the rounded corners, don't appear to change during animation.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Controls must contain a symbol image and title; value is optional but recommended for state display.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Text("Action") } } // Missing symbol
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidgetButton("MyControl", systemImage: "lightbulb.fill") { }
rules.quote: Controls contain a symbol image, a title, and, optionally, a value.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer controls only for actions providing significant benefit without launching the full app.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: { openApp() }) { Text("Open Settings") } } // Trivial action
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: { toggleLight() }) { Image(systemName: "lightbulb.fill") } } // Direct state change
rules.quote: Offer controls for actions that provide the most benefit without having to launch your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Update control state when interacted with, when actions complete, or via push notifications.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: { toggleLight() }) { Text("Light") } } // No state update mechanism
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: { toggleLight() }) { Image(systemName: isOn ? "lightbulb.fill" : "lightbulb") } } // Reflects current state
rules.quote: Update controls when someone interacts with them, when an action completes, or remotely with a push notification.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use descriptive SF Symbols that convey control behavior; provide separate symbols for toggle on/off states.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidgetToggle("Garage", isOn: $isOpen) { Image(systemName: "square.fill") } // Generic symbol
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidgetToggle("Garage", isOn: $isOpen) { Image(systemName: isOpen ? "door.garage.open" : "door.garage.closed") }
rules.quote: Choose a descriptive symbol that suggests the behavior of the control.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Animate symbol transitions for toggles and indefinitely during long-running actions until completion.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: isOn ? "lightbulb.fill" : "lightbulb") // No animation on state change
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: isOn ? "lightbulb.fill" : "lightbulb").symbolEffect(.bounce, options: .repeating, value: isOn)
rules.quote: Use symbol animations to highlight state changes.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Select a tint color aligned with app branding; system applies it to toggle on-state and Dynamic Island display.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "lightbulb.fill") } } // Uses default tint
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "lightbulb.fill") }.tint(.yellow) }
rules.quote: Select a tint color that works with your app's brand.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prompt for required configuration when control is first added; allow reconfiguration anytime.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: { toggleLight(lightId: nil) }) { Text("Light") } } // No config prompt
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidgetConfiguration("Light", for: LightControl.self) { ... }.promptsForUserConfiguration()
rules.quote: If a control requires configuration, prompt people to complete this step when they first add it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide verb-based hint text for Action button controls to clarify what pressing and holding does.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "camera.fill") } } // No hint text
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "camera.fill") }.controlWidgetActionHint("Open camera") }
rules.quote: Provide hint text for the Action button.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include placeholder text when control title or value varies to clarify purpose in gallery view.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Text(lightName) } } // No placeholder when lightName is nil
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Text(lightName ?? "Light") } } // Placeholder fallback
rules.quote: If your control title or value can vary, include a placeholder.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Redact sensitive title and value on locked device; optionally redact symbol state as well.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Text("Door: \(homeAddress)") } } // Exposes address when locked
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: {}) { Text("Door") } }.privacySensitive() // Redacts on lock screen
rules.quote: Hide sensitive information when the device is locked.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Require device authentication for security-sensitive actions like lock/unlock or vehicle control.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: { unlockDoor() }) { Text("Unlock") } } // No auth check
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: { unlockDoor() }) { Text("Unlock") } }.authenticationPolicy(.required)
rules.quote: Require authentication for actions that affect security.

rules.heading: Camera experiences on a locked device
rules.citation: controls.md › Camera experiences on a locked device
rules.rule: Use identical camera UI in locked control and app; require unlock for tasks beyond capture.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: { launchCustomCameraUI() }) { Image(systemName: "camera.fill") } } // Different UI than app
rules.fix_swiftui: ControlWidget { Button(action: { launchAppCameraUI() }) { Image(systemName: "camera.fill") } } // Reuses app camera
rules.quote: Use the same camera UI in your app and your camera experience.

rules.heading: Camera experiences on a locked device
rules.citation: controls.md › Camera experiences on a locked device
rules.rule: Provide clear instructions for adding the locked camera control to help user discovery.
rules.anti_pattern: ControlWidget { Button(action: { launchCamera() }) { Image(systemName: "camera.fill") } } // No onboarding
rules.fix_swiftui: // Include in-app tutorial or help section explaining how to add camera control to Lock Screen
rules.quote: Provide instructions for adding the control.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never offer an app-specific appearance setting; respect the system-wide Dark Mode preference.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Toggle Dark Mode") { UserDefaults.standard.set("dark", forKey: "appTheme") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove custom appearance toggles; rely on system preference via .preferredColorScheme(nil).
rules.fix_uikit: Do not set overrideUserInterfaceStyle to .dark or .light; leave it as .unspecified.
rules.quote: An app-specific appearance mode option creates more work for people because they have to adjust more than one setting to get the appearance they want.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Test all content legibility in both light and dark modes, including with Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Label").foregroundColor(.black) // fails in Dark Mode
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").foregroundStyle(.primary)
rules.quote: Test your content to make sure that it remains comfortably legible in both appearance modes.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure your app looks good in both appearance modes and Auto mode, which switches throughout the day.
rules.anti_pattern: if UITraitCollection.current.userInterfaceStyle == .dark { /* hardcoded dark-only logic */ }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @Environment(\.colorScheme) var colorScheme and test both branches dynamically.
rules.fix_uikit: Override traitCollectionDidChange(_:) to re-render for both light and dark styles.
rules.quote: Ensure that your app looks good in both appearance modes.

rules.heading: Dark Mode colors
rules.rule: Use semantic system colors (labelColor, separator, controlColor) that automatically adapt to Dark Mode.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Label").foregroundColor(Color(red: 0, green: 0, blue: 0)) // hardcoded black
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").foregroundStyle(.primary)
rules.quote: Semantic colors (like labelColor and controlColor in macOS or separator in iOS and iPadOS) automatically adapt to the current appearance.

rules.heading: Dark Mode colors
rules.rule: Define custom colors in asset catalogs with separate light and dark variants instead of hardcoding values.
rules.anti_pattern: let customColor = UIColor(red: 0.2, green: 0.4, blue: 0.8, alpha: 1.0) // ignores Dark Mode
rules.fix_swiftui: Define a Color Set in Assets.xcassets with Appearances set to Any, Dark; use Color("CustomColor").
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIColor(named: "CustomColor") with asset catalog variants.
rules.quote: When you need a custom color, add a Color Set asset to your app's asset catalog in Xcode, and specify the bright and dim variants of the color.

rules.heading: Dark Mode colors
rules.rule: Maintain minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio; aim for 7:1 for custom colors and small text.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Low contrast").foregroundColor(.gray).background(Color.darkGray) // fails WCAG AA
rules.fix_swiftui: Use system colors or verify contrast with accessibility inspector before shipping.
rules.fix_uikit: Test with Accessibility Inspector; use UIColor.label and UIColor.systemBackground for safe contrast.
rules.quote: At a minimum, make sure the contrast ratio between colors is no lower than 4.5:1.

rules.heading: Dark Mode colors
rules.rule: Slightly darken white backgrounds in content images to prevent glowing in Dark Mode context.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(uiImage: whiteBackgroundPhoto) // glows harshly in Dark Mode
rules.fix_swiftui: Adjust image asset or apply a subtle overlay in Dark Mode via @Environment(\.colorScheme).
rules.fix_uikit: Create separate image assets or apply a dark overlay when traitCollection.userInterfaceStyle == .dark.
rules.quote: If you display a content image that includes a white background, consider slightly darkening the image to prevent the background from glowing in the surrounding Dark Mode context.

rules.heading: Icons and images
rules.rule: Use SF Symbols wherever possible; they automatically adapt to Dark Mode with dynamic colors.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("CustomIcon") // custom PNG may not adapt to Dark Mode
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "star.fill").foregroundStyle(.primary)
rules.quote: Use SF Symbols wherever possible.

rules.heading: Icons and images
