rules.rule: Design separate interface icons for light and dark appearances when a single asset does not work well in both.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("moon") // full moon icon lacks outline for light background, needs outline for dark
rules.fix_swiftui: Create separate assets in catalog with Appearances set to Any and Dark; use conditional logic if needed.
rules.fix_uikit: Use asset catalog with light and dark variants; UIImage(named:) automatically selects the correct variant.
rules.quote: Design separate interface icons for the light and dark appearances if necessary.

rules.heading: Icons and images
rules.rule: Use asset catalogs to manage full-color images with separate light and dark variants when needed.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(uiImage: UIImage(named: "photo")) // single asset may look poor in Dark Mode
rules.fix_swiftui: Define image set in Assets.xcassets with Appearances: Any, Dark; use Image("photo").
rules.fix_uikit: Create separate image assets in catalog; UIImage(named:) selects variant based on current trait.
rules.quote: Use asset catalogs to combine your assets into a single named image.

rules.heading: Text
rules.rule: Use system-provided label colors (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary) for all text labels.
rules.anti_pattern: label.textColor = UIColor.black // fails in Dark Mode
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").foregroundStyle(.primary)
rules.quote: Use the system-provided label colors for labels.

rules.heading: Text
rules.rule: Use system views (TextField, TextEditor, UITextField) to draw text; avoid custom text rendering.
rules.anti_pattern: Canvas { context in context.draw(Text("Custom"), at: CGPoint(x: 10, y: 10)) } // loses Dark Mode adaptation
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Placeholder", text: $text) or TextEditor(text: $text)
rules.fix_uikit: Use UITextField or UITextView; they automatically adapt to Dark Mode and vibrancy.
rules.quote: Use system views to draw text fields and text views.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use system background colors (base and elevated) to maintain depth perception in Dark Mode layering.
rules.anti_pattern: ZStack { Color.black.ignoresSafeArea() } // custom background breaks depth layering
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .background(Color(UIColor.systemBackground)) or .background(Color(UIColor.secondarySystemBackground)) for elevated surfaces.
rules.fix_uikit: Set view.backgroundColor = UIColor.systemBackground or UIColor.secondarySystemBackground.
rules.quote: Prefer the system background colors.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Add transparency to custom component backgrounds in neutral states to enable desktop tinting harmony.
rules.anti_pattern: NSView().backgroundColor = NSColor.darkGray.withAlphaComponent(1.0) // opaque, no tinting
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .background(Color.white.opacity(0.1)) for custom components in neutral state.
rules.fix_uikit: Set backgroundColor with alpha < 1.0 to allow desktop picture color to show through.
rules.quote: Include some transparency in custom component backgrounds when appropriate.

rules.heading: Purpose
rules.rule: Align every design decision with the product's core purpose and usefulness.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding features or UI elements that don't directly serve the app's primary use case or user goals.
rules.quote: At every stage of development, ask what your product is for and whether the design serves that purpose.

rules.heading: Purpose
rules.rule: Prioritize the app's most important features and make them truly great.
rules.anti_pattern: Spreading design effort equally across all features instead of focusing on core functionality.
rules.quote: Prioritize your app's most important features by aligning with how people want to use it, and focus on making those features truly great.

rules.heading: Agency
rules.rule: Avoid locking users into mandatory flows; provide escape routes to the main experience.
rules.anti_pattern: Modal flows with no dismiss option or forced multi-step wizards without skip buttons.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .navigationDestination with conditional presentation; provide explicit dismiss buttons.
rules.fix_uikit: Ensure UIViewController modals have dismiss buttons; avoid forcing sequential navigation.
rules.quote: When a guided flow is necessary, make it easy to skip or escape so people can get to the main experience quickly.

rules.heading: Agency
rules.rule: Enable users to reverse actions or return to previous state; build forgiveness into design.
rules.anti_pattern: Destructive actions without confirmation; no undo/redo support; permanent data loss on user error.
rules.fix_swiftui: Implement .onDelete with confirmation alerts; integrate UndoManager for reversible operations.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIAlertController for destructive confirmations; adopt UIUndoManager for undo/redo.
rules.quote: When people know they can reverse an action or return to a previous state, they feel free to explore, and that freedom makes your interface more inviting.

rules.heading: Responsibility
rules.rule: Be fully transparent about app purpose, permissions, and data collection from first interaction.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting permissions without explanation; collecting data without user knowledge; unclear app intent.
rules.quote: Be fully transparent about what your product does and why. You have an opportunity to build a relationship with someone from their very first interaction.

rules.heading: Responsibility
rules.rule: Collect only necessary data and protect it against misuse and unintended consequences.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting excessive permissions; storing sensitive data unencrypted; no data protection measures.
rules.quote: Only collect what your product needs to function, and handle it with care. Anticipate ways it could be misused or cause harm, and put protections in place to prevent abuse and unintended consequences.

rules.heading: Familiarity
rules.rule: Use familiar real-world concepts and standard UI patterns to make interfaces intuitive.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom controls that mimic standard behavior; non-standard gestures; unfamiliar metaphors.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use system Button, TextField, Toggle, Picker instead of custom implementations.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIButton, UITextField, UISwitch, UIPickerView with standard configurations.
rules.quote: People bring knowledge of the real world and other software to every new experience. Draw on both to make your interface feel familiar and intuitive.

rules.heading: Familiarity
rules.rule: Apply consistent visual appearance and interaction behavior throughout the design.
rules.anti_pattern: Buttons with different styles in different screens; inconsistent color usage; varying interaction patterns.
rules.fix_swiftui: Define reusable .buttonStyle modifiers; use consistent .foregroundColor and .font across views.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIAppearance proxy for consistent styling; apply tintColor uniformly.
rules.quote: Keep visuals and interactions consistent. Once you establish a behavior or appearance for an element, apply it throughout your design.

rules.heading: Familiarity
rules.rule: Provide clear feedback about control availability, content changes, and system state.
rules.anti_pattern: Silent failures; no loading indicators; disabled controls without explanation; unannounced state changes.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .alert for errors; ProgressView for loading; .disabled with explanatory text.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIAlertController for alerts; UIProgressView for progress; disable controls with tooltips.
rules.quote: Give people clear signals about what's happening as they use your app. Show when controls are available, indicate when content changes, and use system patterns to display alerts and offer choices.

rules.heading: Flexibility
rules.rule: Design inclusively with accessibility as a priority from the start.
rules.anti_pattern: Missing accessibility labels; color-only information; no keyboard navigation; ignoring VoiceOver support.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .accessibilityLabel and .accessibilityHint to all interactive elements.
rules.fix_uikit: Set accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint on UIView subclasses.
rules.quote: Design inclusively to reach the broadest possible audience and create a better experience for all.

rules.heading: Flexibility
rules.rule: Preserve user context across platforms and configurations with consistent positioning and natural animations.
rules.anti_pattern: Abrupt layout changes; jarring transitions; content repositioning on orientation change.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .transition and withAnimation for smooth state changes; maintain layout consistency.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIView.animate for smooth transitions; maintain view hierarchy across rotations.
rules.quote: Keep content and controls in consistent, predictable positions, and use natural animations to ease transitions.

rules.heading: Flexibility
rules.rule: Support multiple input methods including voice, touch, keyboard, and accessibility features.
rules.anti_pattern: Touch-only interface; no keyboard support; ignoring voice input; no mouse/trackpad support on macOS.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .keyboardType and .onSubmit for keyboard input; support voice commands.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIKeyInput; support UITextInputTraits; enable keyboard navigation.
rules.quote: Designing for as many inputs as possible — including voice, touch, keyboard, and more — means more people can use your product the way that works best for them.

rules.heading: Simplicity
rules.rule: Include only necessary elements; keep important features close and let others fall away.
rules.anti_pattern: Cluttered UI with unused features; too many options on one screen; feature bloat.
rules.quote: Simplicity isn't minimalism. Aim for a focused, useful experience that keeps the important things close by and lets the others fall away.

rules.heading: Simplicity
rules.rule: Use concise, precise wording for labels and copy to maximize clarity and universality.
rules.anti_pattern: Verbose labels; jargon-heavy text; ambiguous button titles; overly formal or casual tone.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use short, clear Text labels; prefer 'Save' over 'Persist Data'; use Label for icon+text.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UILabel text to concise, clear strings; use standard button titles.
rules.quote: When you find the simplest way to say something, it's often the most universal, and the most helpful.

rules.heading: Simplicity
rules.rule: Establish clear visual hierarchy so users understand where to go and what comes next.
rules.anti_pattern: All text same size/weight; no visual distinction between primary and secondary actions; unclear flow.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .font(.title) for headings, .font(.body) for content; vary .fontWeight.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:) for hierarchy; vary font sizes and weights.
rules.quote: When form and function are readily apparent, people know how to reach a desired outcome. Prioritize recognizable controls and a consistent structure that helps people understand where they are and what comes next.

rules.heading: Craft
rules.rule: Demonstrate care through deliberate design: stunning visuals, smooth animations, precise wording, thoughtful audio.
rules.anti_pattern: Jarring animations; inconsistent shadows; typos in UI text; harsh or missing sound design.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .animation for smooth transitions; apply .shadow and .cornerRadius thoughtfully.
rules.fix_uikit: Use CABasicAnimation for smooth effects; configure layer properties carefully.
rules.quote: Every element of your design shows people how much you care. Be deliberate with each decision, and strive for stunning visuals, smooth animations, precise wording, and thoughtful audio.

rules.heading: Craft
rules.rule: Prototype early, iterate, test in real-world settings, and maintain high quality standards.
rules.anti_pattern: Shipping without testing; ignoring user feedback; not updating after launch; low performance.
rules.quote: Prototype early, try new approaches, and be willing to discard what doesn't work. Set a high bar for every feature, refine it, and try again.

rules.heading: Delight
rules.rule: Identify the emotion you want to inspire and let it shape design decisions.
rules.anti_pattern: Generic, emotionless UI; design that contradicts app purpose (e.g., chaotic fitness app).
rules.quote: Not all software feels the same to use. A fitness app might energize; a meditation app might calm; a game might thrill. Know the feeling you want to evoke, and let it shape your design.

rules.heading: Delight
rules.rule: Add character to interactions (buttons, errors, transitions) that reflect design spirit without hindering task completion.
rules.anti_pattern: Excessive animations that slow interaction; decorative elements that obscure function; whimsy that confuses.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use subtle .animation and .transition; add personality to error messages.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIView.animate with reasonable duration; craft helpful error messages.
rules.quote: Every interaction is a chance to show what your software stands for. From a simple button press to an error message, consider whether each moment is an opportunity to add a touch of character that reflects the spirit of your design.

rules.heading: Delight
rules.rule: Balance delight with purpose; don't let decoration interfere with core task completion.
rules.anti_pattern: Animations that delay user actions; decorative UI that obscures content; whimsy over usability.
rules.quote: Keep in mind that people are trying to accomplish a task, so don't let pursuit of delight for its own sake get in the way of your product's core purpose.

rules.heading: Jump into gameplay
rules.rule: Keep initial game installation under 30 minutes; download additional content in background.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring players to download 2GB of assets before first playable moment.
rules.quote: Include as much playable content as you can in your game's initial installation while keeping the download time to 30 minutes or less.

rules.heading: Jump into gameplay
rules.rule: Use device capabilities to set optimal defaults; avoid forcing players to configure settings before play.
rules.anti_pattern: Launching game with generic 1080p resolution on all devices; requiring manual graphics settings.
rules.quote: Use information about a player's device to choose the best defaults for your game, such as the device resolution that makes your graphics look great, automatic recognition of paired accessories and game controllers, and the player's accessibility settings.

rules.heading: Jump into gameplay
rules.rule: Integrate tutorials into playable gameplay; offer written guides as optional reference, not mandatory prerequisites.
rules.anti_pattern: Forcing 10-minute unskippable tutorial cutscene before any interactive play.
rules.quote: Players often learn better when they discover new information and mechanics in the context of your game's world, so it can work well to integrate configuration and onboarding flows into a playable tutorial that engages people quickly and helps them feel successful right away.

rules.heading: Jump into gameplay
rules.rule: Request sensor/data permissions contextually during gameplay, not before; integrate requests into relevant scenarios.
rules.anti_pattern: Prompting for hand-tracking permission on app launch before any gameplay context.
rules.quote: To help people understand why you're making such a request, integrate it into the scenario that requires the data.

rules.heading: Look stunning on every display
rules.citation: designing-for-games.md › Look stunning on every display
rules.rule: Enforce minimum text sizes: iOS/iPadOS 11pt, macOS 10pt; ensure sufficient contrast with background.
rules.anti_pattern: Using 8pt system font for game UI text; low-contrast white text on light background.
rules.fix_swiftui: .font(.system(size: 11))
rules.fix_uikit: UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 11)
rules.quote: To keep text comfortably legible on each device, ensure that it contrasts well with the background and uses at least the recommended minimum text size in each platform.

rules.heading: Look stunning on every display
rules.citation: designing-for-games.md › Look stunning on every display
rules.rule: Enforce minimum button sizes: iOS/iPadOS 28x28pt, macOS 20x20pt; maintain adequate spacing between buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating 16x16pt buttons in iOS; placing buttons 2pt apart.
rules.fix_swiftui: .frame(minWidth: 28, minHeight: 28)
rules.fix_uikit: button.frame = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 28, height: 28)
rules.quote: Each platform defines a recommended minimum button size based on its default interaction method.

rules.heading: Look stunning on every display
rules.citation: designing-for-games.md › Look stunning on every display
rules.rule: Use resolution-independent textures and graphics; match device resolution if vector assets unavailable.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoding 1080p textures for all devices; not scaling assets for Retina displays.
rules.quote: If creating resolution-independent assets isn't possible, match the resolution of your game to the resolution of the device.

rules.heading: Look stunning on every display
rules.citation: designing-for-games.md › Look stunning on every display
rules.rule: Use dynamic layouts with relative constraints for in-game menus; avoid fixed layouts to support multiple aspect ratios.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoding menu button positions at fixed coordinates; not adapting to 16:10, 19.5:9, or 4:3 ratios.
rules.fix_swiftui: GeometryReader { geo in ... }
rules.fix_uikit: NSLayoutConstraint(item:, attribute: .width, relatedBy: .equal, toItem: superview, attribute: .width, multiplier: 0.5, constant: 0)
rules.quote: To help ensure your in-game menus render correctly, consider using dynamic layouts that rely on relative constraints to adjust to different contexts.

rules.heading: Enable intuitive interactions
rules.rule: Support platform-default interaction: touch on iOS, keyboard/mouse on macOS, eyes/hands on visionOS.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring game controller on iOS; forcing touch-only controls on macOS.
rules.quote: Support each platform's default interaction method.

rules.heading: Enable intuitive interactions
rules.rule: Support physical game controllers; always provide alternative interaction methods for accessibility.
rules.anti_pattern: Game controller-only controls; no touch or keyboard fallback.
rules.quote: Although the presence of a game controller makes it straightforward to port controls from an existing game and handle complex control mappings, recognize that not every player can use a physical game controller.

rules.heading: Welcome everyone
rules.rule: Never rely solely on color to convey information; provide subtitles for cutscenes; support multiple perception modes.
rules.anti_pattern: Using red-only indicators for danger; cutscenes without captions; no audio descriptions.
rules.quote: Make sure people can perceive your game's content whether they use sight, hearing, or touch.

rules.heading: Welcome everyone
rules.rule: Allow players to customize type size, control mapping, motion intensity, and sound balance.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoded text size; no remappable controls; forced motion effects.
rules.quote: Give players the ability to customize parameters like type size, game control mapping, motion intensity, and sound balance.

rules.heading: Adopt Apple technologies
rules.rule: Integrate Game Center for leaderboards, achievements, and cross-device player discovery.
rules.anti_pattern: Building custom leaderboard system instead of using Game Center.
rules.quote: Integrate Game Center to help players discover your game across their devices and connect with their friends.

rules.heading: Adopt Apple technologies
rules.rule: Support GameSave to enable cross-device game state persistence via iCloud.
rules.anti_pattern: No save synchronization; players must restart on different devices.
rules.quote: When you support GameSave, you can help people save their game state and start back up exactly where they left off on a different device.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit onscreen controls; make secondary details and actions discoverable with minimal interaction.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Menu, ContextMenu, or disclosure controls to hide secondary actions behind a single tap or long-press.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIMenu, UIContextMenuInteraction, or UIBarButtonItem with menu to surface secondary actions.
rules.quote: Help people concentrate on primary tasks and content by limiting the number of onscreen controls while making secondary details and actions discoverable with minimal interaction.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Adapt seamlessly to device orientation, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type changes.
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").font(.body).foregroundStyle(.primary)
rules.quote: Adapt seamlessly to appearance changes — like device orientation, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type — letting people choose the configurations that work best for them.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support swipe gestures for navigation and actions; place controls in middle or bottom display areas for ergonomic reach.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .swipeActions(edge: .leading) for back navigation; place primary actions in bottom or center areas using VStack with Spacer().
rules.fix_uikit: Add UISwipeGestureRecognizer for back navigation; position action buttons in lower half of view.
rules.quote: Support interactions that accommodate the way people usually hold their device. For example, it tends to be easier and more comfortable for people to reach a control when it's located in the middle or bottom area of the display, so it's especially important to let people swipe to navigate back or initiate actions in a list row.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: With explicit permission, integrate platform capabilities (location, biometrics, payments) to enhance experience without requiring manual data entry.
rules.fix_swiftui: Request CLLocationManager permission and use location data directly; use LocalAuthentication for biometric auth.
rules.fix_uikit: Request CLLocationManager and LAContext permissions; integrate results into payment and security flows.
rules.quote: With people's permission, integrate information available through platform capabilities in ways that enhance the experience without asking people to enter data. For example, you might accept payments, provide security through biometric authentication, or offer features that use the device's location.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Minimize modal interfaces and full-screen transitions; elevate content on large display.
rules.anti_pattern: NavigationStack { ... }.sheet(isPresented: $showModal) { ModalView() } for primary workflows; overusing fullScreenCover.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use NavigationStack with inline navigation; reserve .sheet/.fullScreenCover for secondary actions only.
rules.fix_uikit: Prefer UINavigationController or UISplitViewController over UIModalPresentationStyle.fullScreen for primary flows.
rules.quote: Take advantage of the large display to elevate the content people care about, minimizing modal interfaces and full-screen transitions, and positioning onscreen controls where they're easy to reach, but not in the way.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Size and density of onscreen content must account for typical 3-foot viewing distance.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap").font(.system(size: 10)) }.frame(width: 20, height: 20)
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .font(.body) or larger; ensure touch targets ≥44pt; test with GeometryReader at typical iPad distances.
rules.fix_uikit: Set minimum button size to 44×44pt; use UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:) for scalable sizing.
rules.quote: Use viewing distance and input mode to help you determine the size and density of the onscreen content you display.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support Multi-Touch gestures, keyboard, trackpad, and Apple Pencil; enable multi-input combinations.
rules.anti_pattern: Button only responds to tap; no keyboard shortcuts; no drag-and-drop support; no Pencil input.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .keyboardShortcut, .onDrop, .onContinueUserActivity; use GestureRecognizer for Pencil.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIKeyCommand, UIDragInteraction, UIDropInteraction, and PKCanvasView for Pencil support.
rules.quote: Let people use Multi-Touch gestures, a physical keyboard or trackpad, or Apple Pencil, and consider supporting unique interactions that combine multiple input modes.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Adapt seamlessly to device orientation, multitasking modes, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type.
rules.anti_pattern: struct ContentView: View { var body: some View { HStack { Text("Fixed").font(.system(size: 16)) } } } // ignores orientation, Dark Mode, Dynamic Type
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass), @Environment(\.verticalSizeClass), @Environment(\.colorScheme); apply .font(.body) for Dynamic Type.
rules.fix_uikit: Override traitCollectionDidChange(_:); use UITraitCollection.current.horizontalSizeClass; apply UIFont.preferredFont.
rules.quote: Adapt seamlessly to appearance changes — like device orientation, multitasking modes, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type — and transition effortlessly to running in macOS, letting people choose the configurations that work best for them.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Position onscreen controls where they are easy to reach and not obstructing primary content.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Spacer(); HStack { Button("Action") {} }.frame(maxWidth: .infinity) } // button at bottom, hard to reach
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .toolbar with ToolbarItemGroup(.primaryAction) or .navigationBarTrailing for accessible placement.
rules.fix_uikit: Place UIBarButtonItem in navigationItem.rightBarButtonItem or use UIToolbar at top.
rules.quote: positioning onscreen controls where they're easy to reach, but not in the way.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Place toolbars and tab bars on the side on outer display to maximize vertical content space.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing toolbars at top/bottom on iPhone Duo outer display, reducing vertical space for content.
rules.quote: The system places toolbars and tab bars on the side to maximize the vertical space for content.

rules.heading: Device poses
rules.rule: Use size classes instead of fixed widths to adapt naturally across device poses and displays.
rules.anti_pattern: let width: CGFloat = 375; // hardcoded width ignoring size classes
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) to adapt layout based on size classes.
rules.fix_uikit: Use traitCollection.horizontalSizeClass to conditionally layout views.
rules.quote: Use size classes so your app adapts naturally as it changes size.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use layout margins and safe area insets; avoid fixed widths and display-specific dependencies.
rules.anti_pattern: if UIDevice.current.model == "iPhone Duo" { /* custom layout */ }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .safeAreaInset() and GeometryReader with relative sizing instead of hardcoded values.
rules.fix_uikit: Use safeAreaLayoutGuide and NSLayoutConstraint with multipliers instead of fixed constants.
rules.quote: Use size classes, layout margins, and safe area insets to lay out controls and content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Maintain consistent functionality and state between outer and inner displays.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing different features or disabled controls on outer display vs inner display.
rules.quote: Keep functionality and the state of elements the same between displays.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide access to same controls and content regardless of device pose or how device is held.
rules.anti_pattern: Hiding critical controls when device is in certain poses or orientations.
rules.quote: Provide access to the same controls and content regardless of how someone holds or views the device.

rules.heading: Dynamic layouts
rules.rule: Build layouts with layout margins and safe area insets; avoid fixed widths tied to specific displays.
rules.anti_pattern: let contentWidth = 390 // hardcoded for specific display
rules.fix_swiftui: Use GeometryReader { geo in ... } with relative sizing based on geo.size.
rules.fix_uikit: Use safeAreaLayoutGuide with proportional constraints instead of fixed widths.
rules.quote: Build your layouts with layout margins and safe area insets, and steer clear of fixed widths or anything tied to a specific display.

rules.heading: Reserved regions
rules.rule: Use ReservedRegion API to keep important elements clear of fold, camera, and Dynamic Island.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing critical UI elements at center of inner display without accounting for fold.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .reservedRegion(.folding) or .reservedRegion(.camera) to reposition content.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIView.ReservedRegion to adapt layout around reserved areas.
rules.quote: Use the `ReservedRegion` API to keep important elements clear of the center if the system doesn't move them automatically.

rules.heading: Reserved regions
rules.rule: Prefer layout containers that adapt automatically to fold, like split views with even column counts.
rules.anti_pattern: Using fixed-width grid with odd number of columns that splits awkwardly at fold.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use NavigationSplitView or ArrangementView which adapt automatically to fold.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UISplitViewController or UIArrangementViewController for automatic fold adaptation.
rules.quote: Prefer a layout container that adapts automatically, like the split view in Notes that adjusts the width of each pane to stay clearly visible as the device folds.

rules.heading: Reserved regions
rules.rule: Move only necessary elements when device folds; avoid dramatic shifts that make controls hard to track.
rules.anti_pattern: Completely rearranging layout or hiding/showing large sections when fold state changes.
rules.quote: Move only what's necessary to keep elements visible and easy to tap.

rules.heading: Arrangement views
rules.rule: Use ArrangementView when layout already resembles two-view split or overlay pattern.
rules.anti_pattern: Using HStack/VStack manually when ArrangementView would handle fold adaptation automatically.
rules.fix_swiftui: Replace HStack/VStack with ArrangementView(primaryView: ..., secondaryView: ...) for automatic fold handling.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIArrangementViewController instead of manual view hierarchy management.
rules.quote: A layout that places two views side by side or one above the other, such as an HStack or VStack, translates directly to a split arrangement.

rules.heading: Arrangement views
rules.rule: Place navigation containers outside arrangement views, not within them.
rules.anti_pattern: Nesting NavigationSplitView inside ArrangementView.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use NavigationSplitView as parent container with ArrangementView as content.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UINavigationController as parent with UIArrangementViewController as child.
rules.quote: Keep navigation outside of arrangement views.

rules.heading: Vertical controls
rules.rule: Assign visibility priority to toolbar items; prioritize frequently used actions to keep them accessible.
rules.anti_pattern: Not setting visibility priority, allowing important actions to overflow and hide.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .toolbarItemVisibilityPriority(.high) on frequently used ToolbarItems.
rules.fix_uikit: Set visibilityPriority property on UIBarButtonItem to UIBarButtonItemVisibilityPriority.high.
rules.quote: Assign each item a visibility priority to change that order, starting with whole groups and then individual items within a group if you need finer control.

rules.heading: Vertical controls
rules.rule: Provide both title and symbol for non-text-only toolbar items; system picks right representation.
rules.anti_pattern: Using only symbol without title, or only title without symbol for toolbar items.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Label("Title", systemImage: "symbol.name") for toolbar items.
rules.fix_uikit: Set both title and image on UIBarButtonItem.
rules.quote: Provide both a title and a symbol for each toolbar item that isn't text-only.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Present more content in fewer nested levels with comfortable information density on large displays.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use multi-column layouts (NavigationSplitView) or sidebar patterns to show more content simultaneously without deep nesting.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement NSSplitViewController with multiple panes or use NSCollectionView with adaptive layouts.
rules.quote: Leverage large displays to present more content in fewer nested levels and with less need for modality, while maintaining a comfortable information density that doesn't make people strain to view the content they want.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow windows to be resized, hidden, shown, and moved; support full-screen mode.
rules.fix_swiftui: .windowResizability(.contentMinSize(width: 400, height: 300))
rules.fix_uikit: window.styleMask = [.titled, .closable, .miniaturizable, .resizable, .fullScreen]
rules.quote: Let people resize, hide, show, and move your windows to fit their work style and device configuration, and support full-screen mode to offer a distraction-free context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use the menu bar to provide easy access to all commands needed in your app.
rules.fix_swiftui: .commands { CommandGroup(replacing: .saveItem) { Button("Save") { save() }.keyboardShortcut("s") } }
rules.quote: Use the menu bar to give people easy access to all the commands they need to do things in your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Handle keyboard shortcuts to accelerate actions and support keyboard-only work styles.
rules.anti_pattern:
Button("Save") { save() }
// No keyboard shortcut defined
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Save") { save() }.keyboardShortcut("s")
rules.quote: Handle keyboard shortcuts to help people accelerate actions and use keyboard-only work styles.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support high-precision input modes for pixel-perfect selections and edits.
rules.fix_uikit: NSView with precise mouse tracking via NSTrackingArea and mouseMoved events
rules.quote: Help people take advantage of high-precision input modes to perform pixel-perfect selections and edits.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support standard trackpad gestures and touch display gestures with expanded touch targets.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Action") { }.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).contentShape(.rect)
rules.quote: Support standard gestures on trackpads and Mac devices with a touch display.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow personalization: customizable toolbars, window views, and interface colors/fonts.
rules.fix_swiftui: .toolbar(id: "main") { ToolbarItem(id: "save", placement: .primaryAction) { Button("Save") { } } }
rules.quote: Allow for personalization, letting people customize toolbars, configure windows to display the views they use most, and choose the colors and fonts they want to see in the interface.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Hide advanced details by default; place frequently-used controls at top of disclosure hierarchy.
rules.anti_pattern: DisclosureGroup { Text("Basic option") } { Text("Advanced option") } // basic hidden, advanced shown
rules.fix_swiftui: Reorder content so primary controls appear first, with DisclosureGroup wrapping secondary/advanced options.
rules.quote: Place controls that people are most likely to use at the top of the disclosure hierarchy so they're always visible, with more advanced functionality hidden by default.

rules.heading: Disclosure triangles
rules.rule: Disclosure triangle points inward when hidden, down when visible; label must describe disclosed content.
rules.anti_pattern: NSButton(title: "...", action: nil) // no label; triangle direction not managed
rules.fix_swiftui: DisclosureGroup("Advanced Options") { /* content */ }
rules.fix_uikit: NSButton(bezelStyle: .disclosure); button.title = "Advanced Options"
rules.quote: A disclosure triangle points inward from the leading edge when its content is hidden and down when its content is visible.

rules.heading: Disclosure triangles
rules.rule: Provide descriptive label indicating what is disclosed or hidden, e.g., 'Advanced Options'.
rules.anti_pattern: DisclosureGroup("") { Text("Hidden content") } // empty label
rules.fix_swiftui: DisclosureGroup("Advanced Options") { /* content */ }
rules.quote: Provide a descriptive label when using a disclosure triangle. Make sure your labels indicate what is disclosed or hidden, like "Advanced Options."

rules.heading: Disclosure buttons
rules.rule: Disclosure button points down when hidden, up when visible; switches state on click/tap.
rules.anti_pattern: NSButton(bezelStyle: .disclosure) // wrong style; should be pushDisclosure
rules.fix_uikit: NSButton(bezelStyle: .pushDisclosure)
rules.quote: A disclosure button points down when its content is hidden and up when its content is visible.

rules.heading: Disclosure buttons
rules.rule: Place disclosure button near the content it controls to establish clear visual relationship.
rules.anti_pattern: // disclosure button at top; expanded content appears far below in separate section
rules.fix_uikit: // Position disclosure button immediately adjacent to or above the content it reveals
rules.quote: Place a disclosure button near the content that it shows and hides. Establish a clear relationship between the control and the expanded choices that appear when a person clicks or taps a button.

rules.heading: Disclosure buttons
rules.rule: Use no more than one disclosure button per view to avoid complexity and confusion.
rules.anti_pattern: // View with 3 separate NSButton(bezelStyle: .pushDisclosure) controls
rules.fix_uikit: // Consolidate multiple disclosure buttons into single control or use alternative layout
rules.quote: Use no more than one disclosure button in a single view. Multiple disclosure buttons add complexity and can be confusing.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Use SwiftUI DisclosureGroup for disclosure controls on iOS, iPadOS, and visionOS.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom toggle + conditional view on iOS instead of DisclosureGroup
rules.fix_swiftui: DisclosureGroup("Label") { /* content */ }
rules.quote: Disclosure controls are available in iOS, iPadOS, and visionOS with the SwiftUI DisclosureGroup view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Duplicate Dock menu commands in menu bar or main interface to ensure discoverability.
rules.anti_pattern: Implementing a command exclusively in the Dock menu without offering it elsewhere in the app.
rules.quote: Make custom Dock menu items available in other places, too.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prioritize high-value, contextually useful actions in Dock menus; avoid low-priority or redundant items.
rules.anti_pattern: Populating a Dock menu with generic or rarely-used commands instead of frequently-needed actions.
rules.quote: Prefer high-value custom items for your Dock menu.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include window lists and actions useful when the app is backgrounded or has no open windows.
rules.anti_pattern: Omitting window navigation or background-state actions from the Dock menu.
rules.quote: Also consider listing a few of the actions that are most likely to be useful when your app isn't frontmost or when there are no open windows.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Label Dock menu items succinctly and organize them in a logical, scannable order.
rules.anti_pattern: Using verbose labels or random ordering in Dock menu items.
rules.quote: As with all menus, you need to label Dock menu items succinctly and organize them logically.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support drag and drop throughout your app using system-provided components like text fields and text views.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom text input component that does not implement UIDropInteraction or NSDraggingDestination protocols.
rules.fix_swiftui: .onDrop(of:isTargeted:perform:) modifier on drop-accepting views.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIDropInteraction and register with UIView.addInteraction(_:).
rules.quote: As much as possible, support drag and drop throughout your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide alternative ways to accomplish drag-and-drop actions via menu commands or accessibility APIs.
rules.anti_pattern: App that only supports drag-and-drop with no menu commands or accessibility descriptors for assistive technology users.
rules.fix_uikit: Set accessibilityDragSourceDescriptors and accessibilityDropPointDescriptors on draggable/droppable views.
rules.quote: Offer alternative ways to accomplish drag-and-drop actions.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Determine whether drag-and-drop within the same container moves or copies content based on user expectations.
rules.anti_pattern: Dragging text within a document performs a copy instead of a move, violating user expectations.
rules.fix_swiftui: Implement drop handler to move content when source and destination are the same container.
rules.fix_uikit: In dropInteraction(_:performDrop:), check if source and destination match to determine move vs. copy behavior.
rules.quote: In general, a move makes sense when the source and destination containers are the same — such as dragging text from one location to another within a document — and a copy makes sense when they're different, like dragging an image from one document to another.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support multi-item drag and drop when it makes sense for user convenience.
rules.anti_pattern: App that only allows dragging a single item at a time when multiple items are selected.
rules.fix_swiftui: Handle multiple items in .onDrop(of:isTargeted:perform:) closure.
rules.fix_uikit: Process all items in drop.items array within dropInteraction(_:performDrop:).
rules.quote: Support multi-item drag and drop when it makes sense.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer letting people undo drag-and-drop operations or ask for confirmation before irreversible drops.
rules.anti_pattern: Drag-and-drop operation that permanently moves content without undo support or confirmation.
rules.fix_swiftui: Implement UndoManager integration in drop handler.
rules.fix_uikit: Register undo action in dropInteraction(_:performDrop:) or present confirmation alert.
rules.quote: Prefer letting people undo a drag-and-drop operation.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer multiple versions of dragged content ordered from highest to lowest fidelity.
rules.anti_pattern: Drag operation that provides only a lossy JPEG when PDF vector and PNG alternatives are available.
rules.fix_swiftui: Return multiple NSItemProvider objects with different representations in onDrag.
rules.fix_uikit: Register multiple UTType representations in UIDragItem with NSItemProvider.
rules.quote: Consider offering multiple versions of dragged content, ordered from highest to lowest fidelity.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Consider supporting spring loading to activate controls when dragging content over them.
rules.anti_pattern: App that does not activate buttons or segmented controls when content is dragged over them.
rules.fix_uikit: Add UISpringLoadedInteraction to buttons and segmented controls.
rules.quote: Consider supporting spring loading.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Display a translucent drag image as soon as people drag a selection about three points.
rules.anti_pattern: Drag operation that shows no visual feedback or displays an opaque drag image.
rules.fix_swiftui: Provide preview closure in .onDrag with translucent Image modifier.
rules.fix_uikit: Return translucent UIImage from dragItems(for:) in UIDragInteractionDelegate.
rules.quote: Display a drag image as soon as people drag a selection about three points.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Show whether a destination can accept dragged content via insertion points, highlighting, or not-allowed indicators.
rules.anti_pattern: Drop destination that provides no visual feedback indicating whether content can be dropped.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use isTargeted parameter in .onDrop to conditionally apply highlighting or insertion point styling.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement dropInteraction(_:sessionDidUpdate:) to update visual feedback based on canAccept.
rules.quote: Show people whether a destination can accept dragged content.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Provide visual feedback when people drop an item on an invalid destination or when dropping fails.
rules.anti_pattern: Failed drop that silently disappears without animating the item back to source or showing rejection feedback.
rules.fix_swiftui: Animate dropped item back to source or fade out on drop failure.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement animation in dropInteraction(_:performDrop:) to move item back or scale/fade on failure.
rules.quote: When people drop an item on an invalid destination, or when dropping fails, provide visual feedback.

rules.heading: Accepting drops
rules.rule: Automatically scroll destination contents when necessary to help people find the right drop location.
rules.anti_pattern: Scrolling container that does not auto-scroll when dragging items near edges.
rules.fix_swiftui: System text views handle this automatically; custom containers require manual scroll implementation.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement dropInteraction(_:sessionDidUpdate:) to trigger scrolling when item is near container edges.
rules.quote: Scroll the contents of a destination when necessary.

rules.heading: Accepting drops
rules.rule: Pick the richest version of dropped content your app can accept from multiple offered representations.
rules.anti_pattern: Drop handler that accepts a lossy image when a native chart object is available.
rules.fix_swiftui: Check NSItemProvider registeredTypeIdentifiers in order of preference.
rules.fix_uikit: Iterate through drop.items and load representations in priority order.
rules.quote: When there's a choice, pick the richest version of dropped content your app can accept.

rules.heading: Accepting drops
rules.rule: Extract only the relevant portion of dropped content if necessary for the destination context.
rules.anti_pattern: Email app that displays full contact information when only name and email address are needed.
rules.fix_swiftui: Filter dropped content in drop handler to extract relevant fields.
rules.fix_uikit: Process dropped items in dropInteraction(_:performDrop:) to extract only needed data.
rules.quote: Extract only the relevant portion of dropped content if necessary.

rules.heading: Accepting drops
rules.rule: Check for the Option key at drop time to allow forced copy behavior within the same container.
rules.anti_pattern: macOS app that ignores Option key modifier during drop, always performing move instead of copy.
rules.quote: When a physical keyboard is attached, check for the Option key at drop time.

rules.heading: Accepting drops
rules.rule: Provide feedback when dropped content needs time to transfer via progress indicators or placeholders.
rules.anti_pattern: Drop handler that silently transfers large files without showing progress or placeholder.
rules.fix_swiftui: Display ProgressView and placeholder during async content transfer.
rules.fix_uikit: Show UIProgressView or placeholder cell during dropInteraction(_:performDrop:) async operations.
rules.quote: Provide feedback when dropped content needs time to transfer.

rules.heading: Accepting drops
rules.rule: Maintain the content's selection state in the destination after drop, updating source as needed.
rules.anti_pattern: Drop handler that deselects dropped content immediately after drop instead of keeping it selected.
rules.fix_swiftui: Update selection state in drop handler to select newly dropped content.
rules.fix_uikit: Set selection in dropInteraction(_:performDrop:) to highlight dropped items.
rules.quote: After a drop, maintain the content's selection state in the destination, updating it in the source as needed.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Let people sequentially add items to an in-progress drag session and accept multiple simultaneous drops.
rules.anti_pattern: iOS app that only allows dragging a single pre-selected item and rejects adding more items mid-drag.
rules.fix_swiftui: Support multiple items in .onDrop perform closure and provide flocking visual feedback.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement dropInteraction(_:sessionDidUpdate:) to accept multiple items and update UI with flocking.
rules.quote: Let people perform multiple simultaneous drag activities.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Let people drag content from your app into the Finder in a format your app can open later.
rules.anti_pattern: macOS app that does not support dragging content to Finder or uses unsupported file formats.
rules.quote: Consider letting people drag content from your app into the Finder.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Let people drag selected content from an inactive window without first making the window active.
rules.anti_pattern: macOS app that requires activating an inactive window before allowing drag of background selection.
rules.quote: Let people drag selected content from an inactive window without first making the window active.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Consider displaying a badge during multi-item drag operations to indicate the number of items.
rules.anti_pattern: macOS app that drags multiple items without showing a badge count indicator.
rules.quote: Consider displaying a badge during multi-item drag operations.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Consider changing the pointer appearance to indicate what will happen when people drop content.
rules.anti_pattern: macOS app that always shows the default pointer regardless of drop outcome.
rules.quote: Consider changing the pointer appearance to indicate what will happen when people drop content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use system-provided edit menu instead of creating custom menus with identical commands.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a custom UIMenu that duplicates Copy, Cut, Paste, Select All functionality.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIResponderStandardEditActions and system-provided UIMenu for edit operations.
rules.quote: People are familiar with the contents and behavior of the system-provided component, so creating a custom menu that presents the same commands is redundant and likely to be confusing.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Reveal edit menus only via system-defined interactions (touch-hold, pinch-hold, secondary click).
rules.anti_pattern: Implementing custom gesture recognizers or non-standard interactions to reveal edit menus.
rules.fix_uikit: Use standard UIContextMenuInteraction or system gesture handlers.
rules.quote: Let people reveal an edit menu using the system-defined interactions they already know.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Remove or disable edit menu commands that don't apply to current selection state.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing Copy, Cut, or Paste options when nothing is selected or nothing is in pasteboard.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UIAction.attributes = .disabled or filter UIMenu.children based on selection state.
rules.quote: Offer commands that are relevant in the current context, removing or dimming commands that don't apply.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Position custom commands near related system-provided commands to maintain expected ordering.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing custom formatting commands at the beginning of the menu before standard Copy/Cut/Paste.
rules.fix_uikit: Order UIMenu.children with system actions first, then custom actions in logical groups.
rules.quote: List custom commands near relevant system-provided ones.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow copying of noneditable static content like captions and status text when contextually appropriate.
rules.anti_pattern: Disabling copy functionality for image captions, social media status, or other static text.
rules.fix_uikit: Enable UIResponderStandardEditActions.copy for selectable but non-editable text.
rules.quote: When it makes sense, let people select and copy noneditable text.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Implement undo and redo support for all edit menu actions when possible.
rules.anti_pattern: Performing destructive edit menu actions (Delete, Cut) without registering undo/redo operations.
rules.fix_uikit: Register UndoManager operations for all UIMenu actions that modify state.
rules.quote: Support undo and redo when possible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid duplicate controls that replicate edit menu functionality elsewhere in the interface.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing both an edit menu Copy command and a separate copy button in the toolbar.
rules.fix_uikit: Consolidate edit operations into the system edit menu rather than redundant UI controls.
rules.quote: In general, avoid implementing other controls that perform the same functions as edit menu items.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Distinguish Delete from Cut by showing Cut only when content is copied to pasteboard.
rules.anti_pattern: Using Delete and Cut interchangeably or showing both without semantic distinction.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement Cut as UIAction that copies to UIPasteboard before deletion; Delete removes only.
rules.quote: Differentiate different types of deletion commands when necessary.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use concise verb or short verb phrases for custom edit menu command labels.
rules.anti_pattern: Using long descriptive labels like 'Copy this item to the clipboard' instead of 'Copy'.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UIAction.title to short verbs: 'Share', 'Delete', 'Archive' instead of full sentences.
rules.quote: Create short labels for custom commands.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Support both compact horizontal and vertical edit menu styles on iOS and iPadOS.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoding menu layout to only horizontal or only vertical style.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIContextMenuInteraction which automatically adapts between compact and vertical layouts.
rules.quote: Ensure your edit menu works well in both styles.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Adjust edit menu placement to avoid covering important content or interface elements.
rules.anti_pattern: Allowing edit menu to overlap critical UI or be positioned off-screen.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure UIContextMenuInteraction.location or use preferredMenuAnchorPoint to reposition menu.
rules.quote: Adjust an edit menu's placement, if necessary.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Gather information from system or user permissions rather than requesting manual entry.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Enter your location", text: $location) // when CLLocationManager available
rules.fix_swiftui: Use LocationManager to request permission and populate location automatically.
rules.fix_uikit: Use CLLocationManager or HealthKit to retrieve data with user permission.
rules.quote: Get information from the system whenever possible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display clear prompts, labels, or placeholder text describing required data format.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("", text: $email) // no label or placeholder
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("username@company.com", text: $email) or use Label with TextField.
rules.fix_uikit: Set placeholder property or add UILabel above UITextField.
rules.quote: Be clear about the data you need.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use secure text-entry fields for sensitive data, obscuring input with filled circles.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Password", text: $password) // for password entry
rules.fix_swiftui: SecureField("Password", text: $password)
rules.fix_uikit: UITextField with isSecureTextEntry = true
rules.quote: Use a secure text-entry field when appropriate.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never prepopulate password fields; always require user entry or biometric authentication.
rules.anti_pattern: SecureField("Password", text: .constant(savedPassword))
rules.fix_swiftui: SecureField("Password", text: $password) with empty initial binding.
rules.fix_uikit: Leave UITextField empty; use LocalAuthentication for biometric auth.
rules.quote: Never prepopulate a password field.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer selection components (picker, menu, list) instead of requiring text entry when feasible.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Select country", text: $country) // for fixed list of options
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Country", selection: $country) { ForEach(countries, id: \.self) { Text($0) } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIPickerView or UIMenu for predefined options.
rules.quote: When possible, offer choices instead of requiring text entry.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support drag-and-drop and paste interactions to ease data entry.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Enter data", text: $data) // no drag/drop support
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField(...).onDrop(of: [.plainText], isTargeted: $isTargeted) { ... }
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIDragInteraction and UIPasteConfiguration on UITextField.
rules.quote: As much as possible, let people provide data by dragging and dropping it or by pasting it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Validate field values dynamically and provide immediate feedback on errors.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Email", text: $email) // validation only on submit
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField(..., text: $email).onChange(of: email) { validateEmail($0) }
rules.fix_uikit: Implement textField(_:shouldChangeCharactersIn:replacementString:) for real-time validation.
rules.quote: Dynamically validate field values.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use number formatters for numeric input to restrict and format values automatically.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Amount", text: $amount) // accepts any text
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Amount", value: $amount, format: .number.precision(.fractionLength(2)))
rules.fix_uikit: Attach NumberFormatter to UITextField via delegate or formatter property.
rules.quote: For numeric data in particular, consider using a number formatter, which automatically configures a text field to accept only numeric values.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Disable Next/Continue buttons until all required fields contain valid data.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Continue") { ... } // always enabled regardless of form state
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Continue") { ... }.disabled(!isFormValid)
rules.fix_uikit: Set nextButton.isEnabled = isFormValid in validation logic.
rules.quote: When data entry is necessary, make sure people understand that they must provide the required data before they can proceed.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use expansion tooltips on macOS to show full text when fields clip or truncate content.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Enter long text", text: $text) // no tooltip for clipped content
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField(..., text: $text).help("Full text: \(text)")
rules.quote: Consider using an expansion tooltip to show the full version of clipped or truncated text in a field.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide feedback using multiple modalities (color, text, sound, haptics) to reach all users.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Upload complete").foregroundColor(.green) // Only visual, excludes blind users
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Upload complete").foregroundStyle(.green).accessibilityLabel("Upload complete").accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently)
rules.fix_uikit: label.accessibilityLabel = "Upload complete"; UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, argument: "Upload complete")
rules.quote: When you use multiple ways to provide feedback, you reach more people and give them the opportunity to receive the feedback in ways that work for them.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Integrate status feedback into the interface near relevant items instead of requiring user action.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Check status") { showAlert = true } // Forces user to tap to see status
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Text("Inbox"); Badge(unreadCount).padding(.leading, 4) } // Status always visible
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.rightBarButtonItem = UIBarButtonItem(title: "Inbox (5)", style: .plain, target: nil, action: nil)
rules.quote: When status feedback is available near the items it describes, people get important information without having to take action or leave their current context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use alerts only for critical, actionable information; avoid overuse to preserve impact.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Info"), message: Text("You have 3 new messages"), dismissButton: .default(Text("OK")))
rules.quote: By design, alerts disrupt the current context, so you need to match the importance of the information to the level of interruption.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Warn users only when data loss is unexpected and irreversible; skip warnings for expected deletions.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Delete?"), message: Text("Are you sure?"), primaryButton: .destructive(Text("Delete")))
rules.quote: Warn people when they initiate a task that can cause data loss that's unexpected and irreversible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Confirm completion of significant actions; omit confirmation for routine expected successes.
rules.anti_pattern: // No feedback after every button tap; users expect success by default
rules.fix_swiftui: // Confirm high-stakes actions: Apple Pay, account changes, large uploads
rules.fix_uikit: UINotificationFeedbackGenerator().notificationOccurred(.success) // For important transactions
rules.quote: When it makes sense, confirm that a significant action or task has completed.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Explain why a command cannot be executed; provide actionable guidance to resolve the issue.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Error"), message: Text("Cannot complete action"), dismissButton: .default(Text("OK")))
rules.fix_swiftui: .alert("Cannot provide directions", isPresented: $showAlert) { Button("OK") { } } message: { Text("Specify a destination different from your current location") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: "Cannot provide directions", message: "Specify a destination different from your current location", preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.quote: Show people when a command can't be carried out and help them understand why.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Match feedback delivery method to information significance; passive for status, disruptive for warnings.
rules.anti_pattern: Alert(title: Text("Status"), message: Text("Syncing..."), dismissButton: .default(Text("OK"))) // Interrupts for routine status
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { ProgressView(); Text("Syncing...") } // Passive status display
rules.fix_uikit: // Use UIProgressView or status bar for routine updates; reserve UIAlertController for critical warnings
rules.quote: The most effective feedback tends to match the significance of the information to the way it's delivered.

rules.heading: Creating and opening files
rules.rule: Provide New and Open commands via menu bar (macOS) or keyboard shortcuts interface (iPadOS).
rules.anti_pattern:
let app = MyApp()
// No File menu or keyboard shortcuts for New/Open
rules.fix_swiftui: CommandGroup(after: .newItem) { Button("New", action: createDocument); Button("Open", action: openDocument) }
rules.fix_uikit: let newCommand = UIKeyCommand(input: "n", modifierFlags: .command, action: #selector(createDocument)); addKeyCommand(newCommand)
rules.quote: In iPadOS and macOS, people expect to create new documents or open existing ones using familiar menu commands.

rules.heading: Creating and opening files
rules.rule: Include an Add (+) button to help people create new documents regardless of keyboard availability.
rules.anti_pattern: // Only provide File menu, no visible Add button in UI
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: createDocument) { Image(systemName: "plus") }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.rightBarButtonItem = UIBarButtonItem(barButtonSystemItem: .add, target: self, action: #selector(createDocument))
rules.quote: Regardless of the availability of keyboard shortcuts, include an Add (+) button to help people create a new document.

rules.heading: Creating and opening files
rules.rule: Custom file browsers must support viewing the full file system, not just curated folders.
rules.anti_pattern: // Only show Documents folder, hide rest of file system
rules.fix_uikit:
let picker = UIDocumentPickerViewController(forOpeningContentTypes: [.item])
// Allow navigation to all file system locations
rules.quote: Although you might want to show the most relevant part of the file system when your custom file browser opens — for example, a Documents or iCloud folder or the most recently selected location — let people use your browser to view the rest of the file system if they want.

rules.heading: Saving work
rules.rule: Automatically save work periodically and on app backgrounding; avoid requiring explicit save actions.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Require user to tap Save button to persist changes
Button("Save") { saveDocument() }
rules.fix_swiftui: .onChange(of: documentContent) { _, newValue in autoSaveDocument(newValue) }.onDisappear { autoSaveDocument(documentContent) }
rules.fix_uikit: document?.save(to: document!.fileURL, for: .forOverwriting, completionHandler: nil) // Call in viewWillDisappear
rules.quote: In general, avoid making people take an explicit action to save their work. Instead, automatically perform periodic saves while they're editing and when they close a file or switch to another app.

rules.heading: Saving work
rules.rule: Hide file extensions by default in save/open interfaces; allow users to toggle visibility.
rules.anti_pattern: // Always show .txt, .pdf extensions in file lists
rules.fix_uikit: // Use system file picker which respects Finder extension visibility setting
rules.quote: Hide file extensions by default, but let people view them if they choose.

rules.heading: Quick Look previews
rules.rule: Use Quick Look viewer to preview files your app cannot natively open.
rules.anti_pattern: // Silently fail or show error when user tries to preview unsupported file type
rules.fix_swiftui: .quickLookPreview($previewURL)
rules.fix_uikit: let previewController = QLPreviewController(); previewController.dataSource = self; present(previewController, animated: true)
rules.quote: Use a Quick Look viewer to let people preview a file even when your app can't open it.

rules.heading: Quick Look previews
rules.rule: Implement Quick Look generator for custom file types to enable system-wide previews.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom file type only previewable within your app
rules.quote: Consider implementing a Quick Look generator if your app produces custom file types.

rules.heading: Document launcher
rules.rule: Assign title card primary button to most important function (typically new document creation).
rules.anti_pattern: DocumentGroupLaunchScene { } // No custom button configuration
rules.fix_swiftui: DocumentGroupLaunchScene { NewDocumentButton() } background: { /* background */ } overlayAccessoryView: { /* accessory */ }
rules.quote: The primary button typically creates a new document, and the secondary button can provide additional options.

rules.heading: Document launcher
rules.rule: Background must be visually distinct from accessories and title card; avoid complex distracting patterns.
rules.anti_pattern: // Use busy photographic background that competes with title card
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use solid color, gradient, or subtle pattern
rules.quote: Provide a background that's clearly distinct from the accessories and title card.

rules.heading: Document launcher
rules.rule: Use animation sparingly; prefer gentle, subtle repeating animations over excessive motion.
rules.anti_pattern: // Rapid spinning, bouncing, or complex animations on accessories
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use .easeInOut with 2-3 second duration for breathing/swaying effects
rules.quote: Too much motion on the display can confuse or disorient people.

rules.heading: File provider app extension
rules.rule: Display only documents appropriate to the current context (e.g., PDFs only for PDF editor).
rules.anti_pattern: // Show all file types regardless of calling app's requirements
rules.fix_uikit: // Filter results based on contentTypes parameter passed to extension
rules.quote: When someone uses your file provider extension to open or import documents, display only documents that are appropriate in the current context.

rules.heading: File provider app extension
rules.rule: Allow users to select destination when exporting/moving; support directory hierarchy navigation.
rules.anti_pattern: // Force save to single fixed directory without user choice
rules.fix_uikit: // Implement directory browser allowing navigation and subdirectory creation
rules.quote: Let people select a destination when exporting and moving documents.

rules.heading: File provider app extension
rules.rule: Do not include custom top toolbar in file provider extension; system modal already provides one.
rules.anti_pattern: // Add custom UIToolbar or NavigationBar to extension UI
rules.fix_uikit: // Remove custom toolbar; rely on system-provided modal toolbar
rules.quote: Avoid including a custom top toolbar.

rules.heading: Custom file management
rules.rule: Use default file browser unless custom implementation provides significant UX advantage.
rules.anti_pattern: // Build custom file browser from scratch without strong justification
rules.quote: People have strong associations with the familiar file browsing experience of the Finder and most document-based apps. Use the default file browser unless you have an important reason to create a custom one.

rules.heading: Custom file management
rules.rule: Provide open-recent, filtering, and multi-select capabilities in custom file-opening interfaces.
rules.anti_pattern: // Only support basic single-file open without recent or filter options
rules.quote: For example, people might appreciate an "open recent" action in addition to the simple "open" action.

rules.heading: Custom file management
rules.rule: Save interface must allow users to change filename, format, and location with sensible defaults.
rules.anti_pattern: // Force save to fixed location with no format choice
rules.quote: Provide a save interface to let people change a file's name, format, or location.

rules.heading: Finder Sync extensions
rules.rule: When autosave is disabled, show unsaved indicator and present save dialog on close/quit/logout.
rules.anti_pattern: // Silently discard changes when autosave is off and user closes document
rules.quote: Help people avoid losing work if they turn off autosaving.

rules.heading: Finder Sync extensions
rules.rule: When autosave is off, display dot on close button and Window menu to indicate unsaved changes.
rules.anti_pattern: // Show unsaved indicator dot even when autosave is enabled
rules.quote: To show that there are unsaved changes, display a dot on the document window's close button and next to the document's name in your app's Window menu.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Rely on system-provided focus effects instead of creating custom focus effects.
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Item").focusable() // System applies platform focus effect automatically
rules.quote: System-defined focus effects are precisely tuned to complement interactions with Apple devices, providing experiences that feel responsive, fluid, and lifelike.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never change focus without explicit user interaction via keyboard, remote, or game controller.
rules.quote: If you change focus without their interaction, people have to spend time finding the newly focused item, delaying their current task.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support focus only for content elements (lists, text fields, search fields), not for controls (buttons, sliders, toggles).
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Buttons, sliders, toggles are keyboard-accessible by default.
// Only add .focusable() to custom content views like list items or text fields.
rules.fix_uikit:
// UIButton, UISlider, UISwitch already support keyboard interaction.
// Only override canBecomeFocused() for custom content views.
rules.quote: For example, in iPadOS and macOS, a full keyboard access mode helps people use the keyboard to reach every control, so you only need to support focus for content elements like list items, text fields, and search fields, and not for controls like buttons, sliders, and toggles.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use focus ring for text/search fields; use highlight for list/collection rows.
rules.fix_uikit:
// UITextField shows focus ring by default.
// UICollectionViewCell shows highlight by default with content configuration.
rules.quote: In general, use a focus ring for a text or search field, but use a highlight in a list or collection.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Organize custom views into focus groups so Tab key navigates between groups and arrow keys navigate within groups.
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("Item 1").focusable(); Text("Item 2").focusable() }.focusScope() // Tab moves between groups, arrows within
rules.quote: Although focus moves through system-provided views in ways that people expect, you might need to adjust the order in which the focus system visits your custom views.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Set primary item priority in focus groups so the most-likely target receives focus first.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Confirm") { }.focusable().defaultFocus($focusedField, equals: .confirm) // Receives focus when group entered
rules.quote: When a group receives focus, its primary item automatically receives focus too, making it easy for people to select the item they're most likely to want.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Customize halo focus effect only when system-provided shape doesn't match component contours.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("photo").resizable().frame(width: 100, height: 100).clipShape(.circle).focusable() // System infers circular halo
rules.quote: By default, the system uses an item's shape to infer the shape of its halo.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Reduce virtual control overlay by associating actions with in-game gestures instead of buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding a virtual selection button when players could tap objects directly to select them.
rules.quote: Look for opportunities to reduce the amount of virtual controls that overlap your game content by associating actions with in-game gestures instead.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Position virtual buttons avoiding Home indicator, Dynamic Island, and circular movement/camera regions.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing a control button in the bottom-center area where the Home indicator appears on iPhone.
rules.quote: Make sure to position buttons where they don't overlap system features like the Home indicator or Dynamic Island on iPhone.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Enforce minimum touch target sizes: 44×44 pt for frequent controls, 28×28 pt for secondary controls.
rules.anti_pattern: let button = UIButton(frame: CGRect(x: 10, y: 10, width: 20, height: 20))
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "play.fill") }.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
rules.fix_uikit: button.frame = CGRect(x: 10, y: 10, width: 44, height: 44)
rules.quote: Make sure frequently used controls are a minimum size of 44x44 pt, and less important controls, such as menus, are a minimum size of 28x28 pt to accommodate people's fingers.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Provide visible and tactile press states with visual feedback, sound, and haptics on button interaction.
rules.anti_pattern: Button with no visual feedback, no haptic response, and no sound when pressed.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { hapticFeedback.impact() }) { ... }.buttonStyle(.plain).onLongPressGesture { ... }
rules.fix_uikit: button.addTarget(self, action: #selector(hapticFeedback), for: .touchDown)
rules.quote: A virtual control feels unresponsive without a visual and physical press state.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Use action-representative symbols instead of abstract shapes or controller button names (A, X, R1).
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: "a.circle") or Text("A") to represent an attack action.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "bolt.fill") // weapon/attack graphic
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "bolt.fill")
rules.quote: Avoid using abstract shapes or controller-based naming like A, X, or R1 as artwork, which makes it harder for players to understand and remember what specific controls do.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Dynamically show and hide virtual controls based on gameplay context and action availability.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying all controls on screen at all times, even when actions are unavailable.
rules.fix_swiftui: if isMovementAvailable { VirtualThumbstick() }
rules.fix_uikit: controlButton.isHidden = !isActionAvailable
rules.quote: You can hide controls when an action isn't available or relevant, letting you reduce clutter and help players concentrate on what's important.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Combine multi-button sequences into single controls using gestures like double-tap and touch-and-hold.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring players to press two buttons simultaneously or in rapid sequence.
rules.fix_swiftui: .onLongPressGesture { activatePoweredAttack() } // instead of separate button
rules.fix_uikit: let longPress = UILongPressGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(poweredAttack))
rules.quote: Consider redesigning game mechanics that require players to press multiple buttons at the same time or in a sequence.

rules.heading: Touch controls
rules.rule: Map movement to left screen, camera to right screen; use dynamic thumbstick and direct touch panning.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing movement controls on the right side or using static thumbstick positions.
rules.fix_swiftui: // Left side: dynamic thumbstick on touch; Right side: direct pan gesture for camera
rules.fix_uikit: // Detect touch location and show thumbstick dynamically on left; use UIPanGestureRecognizer on right
rules.quote: Typically, players expect to control movement using the left side of their screen, and control camera direction using the right side of their screen.

rules.heading: Physical controllers
rules.rule: Always provide a fallback to platform default input (touch, keyboard, trackpad) when supporting game controllers.
rules.anti_pattern: Game that only responds to physical controller input with no touch or keyboard alternative.
rules.fix_swiftui: if let controller = GCController.current { /* use controller */ } else { /* use touch/keyboard */ }
rules.fix_uikit: if GCController.controllers().isEmpty { enableTouchControls() }
rules.quote: If you support game controllers, try to make sure there's a fallback for using the platform's default interaction method.

rules.heading: Physical controllers
