rules.rule: Automatically detect paired controller presence and profile; gracefully prompt connection if required.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring manual controller setup or crashing when controller is disconnected.
rules.fix_swiftui: NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(forName: NSNotification.Name.GCControllerDidConnect, object: nil, queue: .main) { _ in updateControllerUI() }
rules.fix_uikit: NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(self, selector: #selector(controllerConnected), name: NSNotification.Name.GCControllerDidConnect, object: nil)
rules.quote: Instead of having players manually set up a physical game controller, you can automatically detect whether a controller is paired and get its profile.

rules.heading: Physical controllers
rules.rule: Display controller labels and symbols matching the connected controller's actual branding, not framework names.
rules.anti_pattern: Always showing "A Button" when the connected controller labels it differently (e.g., "Cross" on PlayStation).
rules.fix_swiftui: Text(controller.extendedGamepad?.buttonA.localizedName ?? "A")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = controller.extendedGamepad?.buttonA.localizedName
rules.quote: Be sure to use the connected controller's labeling scheme when referring to controls or displaying related content in your interface.

rules.heading: Keyboards
rules.rule: Prioritize single-key commands for speed; map main actions to Space bar and menu items to first letters.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring Ctrl+Shift+Alt+K for a common action instead of a single key.
rules.fix_swiftui: .keyboardShortcut("i") // Inventory; .keyboardShortcut(.space) // main action
rules.quote: Single-key commands are generally easier and faster for players to perform, especially while they're simultaneously using a mouse or trackpad.

rules.heading: Keyboards
rules.rule: Remap Control key bindings to Command key on Apple keyboards for ergonomic reach near Space bar.
rules.anti_pattern: Using Control+W for a common action on Apple keyboards when Command+W is more ergonomic.
rules.fix_swiftui: .keyboardShortcut("w", modifiers: .command) // on Apple keyboards
rules.quote: For example, if a key binding uses the Control key (^) on a non-Apple keyboard, consider remapping it to the Command key (⌘) on an Apple keyboard.

rules.heading: Keyboards
rules.rule: Group related actions on physically adjacent keys (e.g., W/A/S/D for movement, nearby keys for related commands).
rules.anti_pattern: Mapping inventory categories to scattered keys like Q, Z, P, M instead of consecutive number keys.
rules.quote: If players navigate using the W, A, S, and D keys, consider using nearby keys to define other high-value commands.

rules.heading: Keyboards
rules.rule: Allow players to customize key bindings for personal comfort and play style.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoding key bindings with no settings UI to remap them.
rules.fix_swiftui: Form { TextField("Move Forward", text: $keyBindings.moveForward) }
rules.fix_uikit: UITextField for key binding input in settings view
rules.quote: Although players tend to expect a reasonable set of defaults, many people need to customize a game's key bindings for personal comfort and play style.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Choose circular or linear path representation based on available space and context.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a circular gauge in a constrained horizontal layout without considering linear alternative.
rules.fix_swiftui: Gauge(value: 0.7) { } .gaugeStyle(.linearCapacity) for horizontal space; .gaugeStyle(.circular) for square space.
rules.quote: A gauge uses a circular or linear path to represent a range of values, mapping the current value to a specific point on the path.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Use standard style for indicator or capacity style for fill-based value representation.
rules.anti_pattern: Mixing indicator and fill representations in the same gauge without clear visual distinction.
rules.fix_swiftui: Gauge(value: 0.7) { } .gaugeStyle(.linearCapacity) for fill; .gaugeStyle(.linear) for indicator.
rules.quote: A standard gauge displays an indicator that shows the current value's location; a gauge that uses the capacity style displays a fill that stops at the value's location on the path.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Use accessory variant for Lock Screen widgets to match watchOS complications appearance.
rules.anti_pattern: Using standard gauge style in Lock Screen widget instead of accessory variant.
rules.fix_swiftui: Gauge(value: 0.7) { } .gaugeStyle(.accessoryCircular) or .gaugeStyle(.accessoryLinear)
rules.quote: This variant — called accessory — works well in iOS Lock Screen widgets and anywhere you want to echo the appearance of complications.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide succinct labels describing current value and both range endpoints for VoiceOver accessibility.
rules.anti_pattern: Gauge(value: 0.7) { } without labels or with missing endpoint descriptions.
rules.fix_swiftui: Gauge(value: 0.7) { Label("Temperature", systemImage: "thermometer") } .gaugeStyle(.accessoryCircular) with min/max labels.
rules.quote: Write succinct labels that describe the current value and both endpoints of the range.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use gradient fill to communicate gauge purpose and reinforce value semantics.
rules.anti_pattern: Gauge(value: 0.7) { } .tint(.blue) with solid color for temperature or multi-semantic ranges.
rules.fix_swiftui: Gauge(value: 0.7) { } .tint(Gradient(colors: [.blue, .red])) for temperature range.
rules.quote: Consider filling the path with a gradient to help communicate the purpose of the gauge.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use continuous capacity style for large value ranges to avoid unusably small segments.
rules.anti_pattern: NSLevelIndicator with discrete style for range 0–1000 resulting in tiny segments.
rules.fix_uikit: NSLevelIndicator(frame: rect); levelIndicator.style = .continuousCapacity
rules.quote: Consider using the continuous style for large ranges.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Change fill color at significant range thresholds (low, high, mid) to communicate state.
rules.anti_pattern: NSLevelIndicator with default green fill across entire range without state indication.
rules.fix_uikit: levelIndicator.warningValue = 0.7; levelIndicator.criticalValue = 0.9 with color binding.
rules.quote: Consider changing the fill color to inform people about significant parts of the range.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Design AI experiences that are inclusive, carefully crafted, and protect privacy throughout.
rules.anti_pattern: Rapidly prototyping an AI feature without considering real-world edge cases, diverse user needs, or privacy implications.
rules.quote: Orient your design process around crafting AI experiences that are inclusive, designed with care, and protect privacy.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep people in control by enabling dismissal, revert, retry, and clearly identifying AI usage.
rules.anti_pattern: Automatically applying AI transformations without user confirmation or ability to undo; hiding AI involvement.
rules.quote: Give them the ability to dismiss new content they don't want, and revert or retry content transformations or other actions they don't agree with.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Test AI features across diverse users to identify and correct stereotypes and biases.
rules.anti_pattern: Deploying an AI feature trained on homogeneous data without testing for gender, cultural, or demographic bias.
rules.quote: Test your feature across a diverse set of people to identify and correct stereotypes, and ensure inclusive results.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer generative features only when they provide clear, specific value like time savings or creativity.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding AI generation to every feature regardless of whether it solves a real user problem.
rules.quote: Offer generative features when and where they provide clear and specific value, like time savings, improved communication, or enhanced creativity.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide non-AI fallbacks when possible so users can achieve goals without generative features.
rules.anti_pattern: Making AI generation mandatory for core app functionality with no alternative path.
rules.quote: When possible, consider offering a non-AI fallback.

rules.heading: Transparency
rules.rule: Never deceive users into thinking AI-generated content was authored by humans.
rules.anti_pattern: Presenting AI-generated text or images as human-created without disclosure.
rules.quote: Never trick someone into thinking they're interacting with or viewing content authored by a human if they're actually interacting with AI.

rules.heading: Transparency
rules.rule: Clearly communicate AI feature capabilities, limitations, and how to achieve good results upfront.
rules.anti_pattern: Launching an AI feature without explaining what it can/cannot do or providing usage guidance.
rules.quote: Clarifying your experience's capabilities and limitations helps people establish a mental model of your feature.

rules.heading: Privacy
rules.rule: Choose on-device models when possible; use server-based models only when necessary and with privacy safeguards.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending all user data to a server-based model without considering on-device alternatives or privacy impact.
rules.quote: On-device models keep people's information on their device, respond quickly, and work offline.

rules.heading: Privacy
rules.rule: Request explicit permission before using personal information or usage data with AI models.
rules.anti_pattern: Silently collecting and sending personal data, messages, or photos to an AI model without user consent.
rules.quote: Ask permission before using personal information and usage data.

rules.heading: Privacy
rules.rule: Disclose whether the model uses personal information for training and clearly explain data usage benefits.
rules.anti_pattern: Collecting data for model improvement without explaining to users how their data will be used or stored.
rules.quote: Articulate whether your model uses personal information for training and improvement.

rules.heading: Models and datasets
rules.rule: Train or customize models with diverse datasets and test to proactively mitigate bias and misinformation.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a homogeneous or biased dataset to train a model without testing for harmful stereotypes.
rules.quote: When you teach and evaluate your AI model, choose datasets that include a diverse range of subject matter representations.

rules.heading: Inputs
rules.rule: Clearly communicate that AI-generated content may contain errors and avoid using it for critical factual information.
rules.anti_pattern: Presenting AI-generated dates, names, or medical information as verified fact without disclaimers.
rules.quote: Generative models sometimes get details wrong, like dates of important events or information about people, so it's important to clearly communicate that AI-generated content may contain errors.

rules.heading: Inputs
rules.rule: Request confirmation before performing irreversible or potentially problematic tasks on behalf of users.
rules.anti_pattern: Automatically deleting photos or making purchases without explicit user confirmation.
rules.quote: Generally, ask for confirmation before performing a significant action on someone's behalf.

rules.heading: Outputs
rules.rule: Surface Edit, Undo, Retry, and Adjust controls near generated content and confirm when corrections take effect.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying generated content without any controls to refine, revert, or retry; no feedback when user adjusts output.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { /* undo */ }) { Label("Undo", systemImage: "arrow.uturn.backward") }
rules.fix_uikit: let undoButton = UIButton(type: .system); undoButton.setTitle("Undo", for: .normal);
rules.quote: For example, surfacing controls like Edit, Undo, Retry, or Adjust near generated content preserves people's agency while still letting them benefit from automation.

rules.heading: Outputs
rules.rule: Coach users toward better results when output is blocked or undesirable; offer example requests.
rules.anti_pattern: Silently blocking harmful requests without explaining why or suggesting how to rephrase.
rules.quote: Minimize scoped or blocked output by coaching people how to be more successful next time.

rules.heading: Outputs
rules.rule: Provide specific, reassuring feedback during generation instead of vague status messages.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing only "Processing…" or "Loading…" without describing what the model is actually doing.
rules.quote: Messages that describe what's actually happening can be more helpful than a vague status message.

rules.heading: Outputs
rules.rule: Consider offering multiple meaningfully different results so users can choose their preferred version.
rules.anti_pattern: Always presenting a single generated result without alternatives.
rules.quote: Offering people a choice can give them a greater sense of control and help bridge the gap between the model's interpretation and what someone actually wants.

rules.heading: Continuous improvement
rules.rule: Let users share feedback on outputs via voluntary, non-intrusive mechanisms like thumbs-up/down buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: Forcing users to provide detailed feedback or placing feedback prompts in disruptive locations.
rules.quote: Always make providing feedback voluntary.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide multiple input methods; never assume gesture-only interaction capability.
rules.anti_pattern: func handleTap() { performAction() } // No keyboard or voice alternative
rules.quote: People commonly prefer or need to use other inputs — such as their voice, keyboard, or Switch Control — to interact with their devices.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use familiar gestures (tap, swipe) only for their standard actions; avoid repurposing them.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Tap to delete instead of activate
Button(action: { deleteItem() }) { Text("Item") }
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Use tap for activation; provide delete via menu or swipe action
Button(action: { selectItem() }) { Text("Item") }
rules.quote: Avoid using a familiar gesture like tap or swipe to perform an action that's unique to your app; similarly, avoid creating a unique gesture to perform a standard action like activating a button or scrolling a long view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide immediate visual feedback during gesture recognition to signal intent and completion.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Gesture recognized but no feedback until action completes
let tap = UITapGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(handleTap))
rules.fix_swiftui: .onTapGesture { withAnimation { state.toggle() } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIView.animate(withDuration: 0.2) { view.alpha = 0.5 }
rules.quote: As people perform a gesture in your app, provide feedback that helps them predict its results and, if necessary, communicates the extent and type of movement required to complete the action.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Clearly communicate when a gesture is unavailable to prevent user confusion.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Locked object shows no visual indication when drag attempted
let drag = UIDragInteraction(delegate: self)
rules.fix_swiftui: .opacity(isLocked ? 0.5 : 1.0).allowsHitTesting(!isLocked)
rules.fix_uikit: view.isUserInteractionEnabled = !isLocked; view.alpha = isLocked ? 0.5 : 1.0
rules.quote: If you don't clearly communicate why a gesture doesn't work, people might think your app has frozen or they aren't performing the gesture correctly, leading to frustration.

rules.heading: Custom gestures
rules.rule: Add custom gestures only for specialized, frequent tasks not covered by standard gestures.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Custom gesture for basic navigation
let customSwipe = UISwipeGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(goBack))
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Use standard back button; add custom gesture only for game mechanics
NavigationLink(destination: detail) { Text("Back") }
rules.quote: Custom gestures work best when you design them for specialized tasks that people perform frequently and that aren't covered by existing gestures, like in a game or drawing app.

rules.heading: Custom gestures
rules.rule: Use custom gestures to supplement, not replace, standard navigation and action methods.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Only way to go back is custom swipe gesture
let swipe = UISwipeGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(goBack))
rules.quote: While you may supply a custom gesture to quickly access parts of your app, people also need simple, familiar ways to navigate and perform actions, even if it means an extra tap or two.

rules.heading: Custom gestures
rules.rule: Avoid custom gestures that conflict with system gestures (edge swipes, overlays, etc.).
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Use non-conflicting gesture or defer system gesture in games
.gesture(TapGesture().onEnded { _ in customAction() })
rules.fix_uikit: // Use center-screen gesture or UIGestureRecognizerDelegate to defer system gesture
rules.quote: It's important to avoid defining custom gestures that might conflict with these interactions, as people expect these controls to work consistently.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Support simultaneous gesture recognition in games with multiple onscreen controls (joystick, buttons).
rules.anti_pattern:
// Only one gesture recognized at a time
let tap = UITapGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(fire))
rules.fix_uikit:
tap.require(toFail: joystick) // Allow simultaneous recognition
view.addGestureRecognizer(tap)
view.addGestureRecognizer(joystick)
rules.quote: Although simultaneous gestures are unlikely to be useful in nongame apps, a game might include multiple onscreen controls — such as a joystick and firing buttons — that people can operate at the same time.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Keep interface layout and control sizes stable when supporting touch input on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Resize controls only for touch
if touchEnabled { button.frame.size = CGSize(width: 60, height: 60) }
rules.quote: In macOS, touch is secondary to keyboard and pointing device input. People switch between inputs frequently, and it's essential to keep the interface stable and predictable regardless of how someone interacts with it.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Enlarge tap targets for touch without increasing control visual size on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Increase control size for touch
if touchEnabled { button.frame.size = CGSize(width: 60, height: 60) }
rules.fix_swiftui:
Button(action: { }) { Text("Action") }
  .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44) // Tap target, not visual size
rules.fix_uikit:
// Use standard controls; system auto-configures tap targets
let button = UIButton(type: .system)
rules.quote: Instead of increasing the size of small controls, optimize them for touch by enlarging their tap targets to anticipate that interaction may start slightly outside of their visual bounds.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Provide expandable controls for small or densely packed touch targets on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Small controls remain small during touch
Button(action: { }) { Text("A") }.frame(width: 20, height: 20)
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Standard controls auto-expand; custom controls should too
Stepper(value: $count) // Auto-expands for touch
rules.fix_uikit: // Steppers, sliders, dials auto-expand; custom controls should show temporary enlarged variant
rules.quote: For small or densely packed controls, consider providing a temporary variant resized appropriately for touch that appears when someone taps the control.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Never use touch as the only way to access controls or features on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Touch-only control; no keyboard or trackpad alternative
if touchInput { performAction() }
rules.quote: Make sure all of your app's functions are available through input from a keyboard and pointing device.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Align macOS touch gestures with existing iPhone, iPad, trackpad, or Magic Mouse gestures.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Different swipe behavior on macOS touch vs. trackpad
if touchInput { swipeLeft() } else { swipeRight() }
rules.quote: Preserve gestures that may already exist for your app on iPhone or iPad, or on Mac with a trackpad or Magic Mouse.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Ensure custom gestures work for both touch and trackpad input on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Gesture only works with direct touch
let touch = UITouchGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(customAction))
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Support both direct and indirect input
.gesture(DragGesture().onEnded { _ in customAction() })
rules.quote: Supporting both direct and indirect touch input makes the gesture available to the widest audience.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer full-screen mode for games, media viewing, or immersive tasks requiring distraction-free focus.
rules.anti_pattern: A productivity app that never offers full-screen mode even when users would benefit from focused work.
rules.quote: People appreciate full-screen mode when they want to concentrate on a task or be immersed in content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Adjust layout subtly in full-screen mode; never programmatically resize the window.
rules.anti_pattern: window.frame = NSScreen.main?.frame ?? .zero // Programmatic resize causing jarring transitions
rules.fix_swiftui: Use adaptive layout modifiers like `.containerRelativeFrame()` to respond to available space.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement `viewWillTransition(to:with:)` to adjust layout proportions without resizing the window.
rules.quote: If you make such adjustments, be sure they're subtle enough to maintain a consistent interface and avoid causing visually jarring transitions between modes.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide persistent or easily revealed access to essential controls in full-screen mode.
rules.anti_pattern: A full-screen video player with no way to access playback controls without exiting full-screen.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `.overlay()` with gesture handlers to reveal controls on tap or swipe.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement `UIGestureRecognizer` to show/hide control overlays without exiting full-screen.
rules.quote: Continue to provide access to essential features and controls so people can complete their task without exiting full-screen mode.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow Dock access in full-screen non-game apps; defer gestures or hide Dock only in games.
rules.anti_pattern: preferredScreenEdgesDeferringSystemGestures = .all // Blocking Dock access in a productivity app
rules.fix_swiftui: Set `preferredScreenEdgesDeferringSystemGestures = .bottom` only for games; omit for other apps.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `preferredScreenEdgesDeferringSystemGestures` selectively; call `NSApplication.shared.presentationOptions.insert(.hideDock)` only in games.
rules.quote: Except in games, let people reveal the Dock while your iPadOS or macOS app is in full-screen mode.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Pause and save state when users switch away from full-screen experiences.
rules.anti_pattern: A full-screen game that continues running in the background without pausing or saving progress.
rules.fix_swiftui: Observe `scenePhase` and pause when transitioning to `.background` or `.inactive`.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement `UIApplicationDelegate.applicationDidEnterBackground(_:)` to pause and save state.
rules.quote: After people switch away from your full-screen experience, help them resume where they left off when they return.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Let users explicitly choose when to exit full-screen mode; never auto-exit.
rules.anti_pattern: Automatically exiting full-screen when a video finishes playing or a game level ends.
rules.fix_swiftui: Require explicit user action (button tap, keyboard shortcut) to exit full-screen.
rules.fix_uikit: Provide an exit button or respond to standard exit gestures; do not auto-dismiss.
rules.quote: Let people choose when to exit full-screen mode.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Hide toolbars and navigation controls to prioritize content; restore via familiar gestures.
rules.anti_pattern: Permanently hiding toolbars with no way to restore them; users cannot access navigation.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .automatic)` with tap/swipe gesture handlers to toggle visibility.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement `UIGestureRecognizer` to show/hide `UIToolbar` or `UINavigationBar` on tap or swipe.
rules.quote: If you implement such behavior, let people restore the hidden elements with a familiar gesture or action like tapping, swiping down, or moving the cursor to the top of the screen.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Defer system gestures only when necessary; preserve single-swipe exit by default.
rules.anti_pattern: preferredScreenEdgesDeferringSystemGestures = .bottom // Always deferring, breaking user expectations
rules.fix_swiftui: Set `preferredScreenEdgesDeferringSystemGestures = .bottom` only if single-swipe causes accidental exits.
rules.fix_uikit: Use `UIViewController.preferredScreenEdgesDeferringSystemGestures` conditionally for games with bottom-edge interactions.
rules.quote: Whenever possible, retain this behavior because it's familiar and what people expect.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use system-provided full-screen support via toggleFullScreen(_:) to handle hardware variations.
rules.anti_pattern: Implementing custom full-screen logic that ignores notch/camera housing areas.
rules.fix_swiftui: Call `NSWindow.toggleFullScreen(_:)` or use SwiftUI's native full-screen support.
rules.fix_uikit: Invoke `NSWindow.toggleFullScreen(_:)` to leverage system accommodation of hardware.
rules.quote: Using the system's full-screen support ensures that your full-screen window works well in all contexts.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Never change display mode automatically when entering full-screen; respect user control.
rules.anti_pattern: Automatically switching to high-refresh-rate or resolution mode when game enters full-screen.
rules.fix_swiftui: Leave display settings unchanged; let users control via System Settings.
rules.fix_uikit: Do not call `CGDisplaySetDisplayMode()` or similar APIs on full-screen entry.
rules.quote: People expect to be in control of their display mode, and changing it automatically doesn't improve performance.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Let users enter full-screen via standard controls; avoid custom window-mode menus.
rules.anti_pattern: A custom menu offering "Windowed", "Borderless", "Full Screen" options instead of using standard UI.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use the system's Enter Full Screen button or View menu item.
rules.fix_uikit: Provide standard full-screen entry via window title bar or Control-Command-F shortcut.
rules.quote: Prefer letting people use your window's Enter Full Screen button, View menu item, or the Control-Command-F keyboard shortcut.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use motion data only when it provides tangible user benefit; avoid collecting data without clear purpose.
rules.anti_pattern:
let motionManager = CMMotionManager()
motionManager.startAccelerometerUpdates() // No clear app benefit
rules.fix_uikit: Only call startAccelerometerUpdates() or startGyroUpdates() when the feature directly enhances user experience (e.g., fitness tracking, game controls).
rules.quote: Use motion data only to offer a tangible benefit to people.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide explanatory copy before requesting motion data permission; system includes it in the permission prompt.
rules.anti_pattern: motionManager.startAccelerometerUpdates() // No permission explanation provided to user
rules.fix_uikit: Include NSMotionUsageDescription in Info.plist with clear explanation of why motion data is needed.
rules.quote: If your experience needs to access motion data from a device, you must provide copy that explains why.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid using accelerometers or gyroscopes for direct interface manipulation outside active gameplay.
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve motion-based controls for gameplay contexts only; use standard gesture recognizers and scroll views for UI navigation.
rules.quote: Outside of active gameplay, avoid using accelerometers or gyroscopes for the direct manipulation of your interface.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid motion-based gestures that are difficult to replicate, physically challenging, or drain battery.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Requiring precise multi-axis tilt sequences for core app functionality
motionManager.startDeviceMotionUpdates(using: .xArbitraryZVertical)
rules.fix_uikit: Use motion data only for optional enhancements; provide alternative standard input methods for all critical tasks.
rules.quote: Some motion-based gestures may be difficult to replicate precisely, may be physically challenging for some people to perform, and may affect battery usage.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Create quick actions only for compelling, high-value tasks that users expect to perform frequently.
rules.anti_pattern: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "minor_task", localizedTitle: "View Settings") // Low-value action
rules.fix_swiftui: Prioritize actions like "Directions Home", "Create New Contact", "New Message" that deliver immediate value.
rules.fix_uikit: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "directions_home", localizedTitle: "Directions Home", localizedSubtitle: nil, icon: UIApplicationShortcutIcon(type: .location))
rules.quote: Create quick actions for compelling, high-value tasks.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide no more than four quick actions per app.
rules.anti_pattern: let items = (0..<8).map { i in UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "action_\(i)", localizedTitle: "Action \(i)") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Limit shortcutItems array to maximum 4 items.
rules.fix_uikit: UIApplication.shared.shortcutItems = Array(items.prefix(4))
rules.quote: You can provide a total of four.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Update dynamic quick actions only in predictable ways based on location, recent activity, time, or settings.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Randomly shuffle quick actions on every app launch
UIApplication.shared.shortcutItems = items.shuffled()
rules.fix_swiftui: Update actions based on observable state: current location, recent conversations, time-based rules, or user preferences.
rules.fix_uikit: Update shortcutItems in response to predictable events: location changes, app state updates, or user settings changes.
rules.quote: Make sure that actions change in ways that people can predict.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use succinct, action-focused titles that instantly communicate the result without app name or extraneous information.
rules.anti_pattern: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "action", localizedTitle: "MyApp - View Your Inbox with Unread Messages", localizedSubtitle: "Open the inbox")
rules.fix_swiftui: Use clear, concise titles: "Directions Home", "Create New Contact", "New Message".
rules.fix_uikit: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "new_message", localizedTitle: "New Message", localizedSubtitle: nil)
rules.quote: For each quick action, provide a succinct title that instantly communicates the results of the action.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep title and subtitle text short to avoid truncation and account for localization.
rules.anti_pattern: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "action", localizedTitle: "This is a very long title that will definitely get truncated on smaller devices", localizedSubtitle: "And an even longer subtitle with lots of extra context")
rules.fix_swiftui: Use concise, localization-friendly text: "Directions Home" instead of "Get directions to your home address".
rules.fix_uikit: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "directions", localizedTitle: "Directions Home", localizedSubtitle: "Current location")
rules.quote: Keep the text short to avoid truncation, and take localization into account as you write the text.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use SF Symbols or standard icons for quick action icons; never use emoji in place of symbols.
rules.anti_pattern: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "action", localizedTitle: "New Message", localizedSubtitle: nil, icon: UIApplicationShortcutIcon(templateImageName: "📧"))
rules.fix_swiftui: Use SF Symbols: UIApplicationShortcutIcon(systemImageName: "envelope.fill") or UIApplicationShortcutIcon(type: .compose)
rules.fix_uikit: let icon = UIApplicationShortcutIcon(systemImageName: "envelope.fill") // or use standard types like .compose, .location
rules.quote: Don't use an emoji in place of a symbol or interface icon.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure quick action icons are monochromatic and maintain contrast in Dark Mode.
rules.anti_pattern: let icon = UIApplicationShortcutIcon(templateImageName: "colorful_gradient_icon") // Full-color icon
rules.fix_swiftui: Use SF Symbols which are automatically monochromatic and adapt to Dark Mode.
rules.fix_uikit: let icon = UIApplicationShortcutIcon(systemImageName: "envelope.fill") // Automatically monochromatic and Dark Mode compatible
rules.quote: Emojis are full color, whereas quick action symbols are monochromatic and change appearance in Dark Mode to maintain contrast.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Optionally provide a subtitle to give additional context when the title alone is insufficient.
rules.anti_pattern: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "inbox", localizedTitle: "Inbox", localizedSubtitle: nil) // No context about unread count
rules.fix_swiftui: Include subtitle when helpful: UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "inbox", localizedTitle: "Inbox", localizedSubtitle: "3 unread")
rules.fix_uikit: let item = UIApplicationShortcutItem(type: "inbox", localizedTitle: "Inbox", localizedSubtitle: "3 unread", icon: UIApplicationShortcutIcon(type: .mail))
rules.quote: If you need to give more context, provide a subtitle too.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Enable iCloud automatically; offer a simple on/off choice only at first launch.
rules.anti_pattern: Repeatedly prompting users to enable iCloud or asking per-document whether to sync.
rules.quote: People turn on iCloud in Settings and expect apps to work with it automatically.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never ask users which individual documents to keep in iCloud; sync all content automatically.
rules.anti_pattern: Presenting a per-document or per-file iCloud storage management UI.
rules.quote: Most people expect all of their content to be available in iCloud and don't want to manage the storage of individual documents.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: For large documents, let users control download timing and indicate when newer versions exist.
rules.anti_pattern: Silently downloading large files without user control or indication of available updates.
rules.quote: If your app works with very large documents, it may be better to let people control when updated content is downloaded.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide subtle feedback when document downloads exceed a few seconds.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing no progress indication or feedback during long iCloud sync operations.
rules.quote: When a document is updating, provide subtle feedback if the download takes more than a few seconds.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Store only user-created content and app state in iCloud; never store regenerable app resources.
rules.anti_pattern: Storing app bundles, cached assets, or generated content in iCloud.
rules.quote: Use iCloud to store information people create and understand, and avoid using it for app resources or content you can regenerate.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not alert users when iCloud becomes unavailable; unobtrusively inform them changes won't sync.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying prominent alerts or error dialogs when iCloud is turned off or Airplane Mode is enabled.
rules.quote: If someone manually turns off iCloud or turns on Airplane Mode, you don't need to display an alert notifying them iCloud is unavailable.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Store only cross-device settings in iCloud; exclude device-specific or context-dependent preferences.
rules.anti_pattern: Syncing all app settings including device-specific ones like work-only or home-only preferences.
rules.quote: If you use iCloud to store settings, make sure it's for ones people want applied to all of their devices.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Always show a confirmation warning before deleting iCloud documents; deletion affects all devices.
rules.anti_pattern: Deleting iCloud documents without confirmation or warning the user about cross-device deletion.
rules.quote: When someone deletes a document in an app that supports iCloud, the document is removed from iCloud and all other devices too.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Automatically detect and resolve version conflicts; if manual resolution needed, use unobtrusive UI.
rules.anti_pattern: Ignoring conflicts, displaying prominent alerts, or delaying conflict resolution.
rules.quote: To the extent possible, try to detect and resolve version conflicts automatically.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include all iCloud content in app search results; users expect universal content availability.
rules.anti_pattern: Excluding iCloud-synced documents or files from search functionality.
rules.quote: People with iCloud accounts assume their content is universally available, and they expect search results to reflect this perspective.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: For games, use GameSave framework to synchronize player progress across devices.
rules.anti_pattern: Implementing custom iCloud sync logic for game saves without using GameSave framework.
rules.quote: Although you can implement this functionality yourself, the GameSave framework offers an efficient solution.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Create recognizable, highly simplified icon designs without excessive details that confuse or reduce readability.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 8)) // Too small, overly detailed custom icon with many visual elements
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 24)) // Use SF Symbols at readable size with minimal detail
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "star.fill")?.withConfiguration(UIImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: 24)) // Appropriate size and simplicity
rules.quote: Too many details can make an interface icon confusing or unreadable.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Maintain consistent size, detail level, stroke thickness, and perspective across all interface icons in your app.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 16, weight: .thin)); Image(systemName: "heart.fill").font(.system(size: 24, weight: .bold)) }
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 20, weight: .semibold)); Image(systemName: "heart.fill").font(.system(size: 20, weight: .semibold)) }
rules.fix_uikit: // Apply consistent UIImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: 20, weight: .semibold) to all icons
rules.quote: Whether you use only custom icons or mix custom and system-provided ones, all interface icons in your app need to use a consistent size, level of detail, stroke thickness (or weight), and perspective.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Match the visual weight of interface icons and adjacent text unless intentionally emphasizing one element.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 12, weight: .thin)); Text("Favorites").font(.system(size: 16, weight: .bold)) }
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 16, weight: .semibold)); Text("Favorites").font(.system(size: 16, weight: .semibold)) }
rules.fix_uikit: // Use matching UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 16, weight: .semibold) for both icon and text
rules.quote: In general, match the weights of interface icons and adjacent text.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Add padding to asymmetric custom icons to achieve optical centering rather than geometric centering.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("customDownloadIcon").frame(width: 24, height: 24) // Geometrically centered but optically misaligned
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("customDownloadIcon").padding(.top, 2) // Optically centered with padding adjustment
rules.fix_uikit: // Create asset with padding baked in, or use UIImageView with adjusted frame origin
rules.quote: If necessary, add padding to a custom interface icon to achieve optical alignment.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not provide custom selected-state versions for icons used in standard system components like toolbars and tab bars.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { Image("customTabIconSelected") } // Custom selected state in tab bar
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView { Image(systemName: "star.fill") } // System handles selected state automatically
rules.fix_uikit: // Use UITabBarItem with systemItem or standard SF Symbol; system manages appearance
rules.quote: You don't need to provide selected and unselected appearances for an icon that's used in standard system components such as toolbars, tab bars, and buttons.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use inclusive, gender-neutral human figures and avoid culturally ambiguous imagery in icons.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("womanUserIcon") // Gender-specific representation
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "person.crop.circle") // Gender-neutral SF Symbol
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "person.crop.circle") // Gender-neutral system icon
rules.quote: Use inclusive images.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include text in interface icons only when essential; localize and provide right-to-left variants if needed.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("textFormattingIconWithA") // Hardcoded character without localization
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "bold") // Use SF Symbol or provide localized variants
rules.fix_uikit: // Provide localized image assets with RTL variants in asset catalog
rules.quote: Include text in your design only when it's essential for conveying meaning.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use vector formats (PDF, SVG) or SF Symbols for custom interface icons, not PNG.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("customIcon.png") // PNG requires multiple high-resolution versions
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "customSymbol") // SF Symbol or Image("customIcon", bundle: .main) with PDF
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(named: "customIcon.pdf") // Vector format scales automatically
rules.quote: If you create a custom interface icon, use a vector format like PDF or SVG.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide alternative text labels (accessibility descriptions) for all custom interface icons.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("customIcon") // No accessibility label for VoiceOver
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("customIcon").accessibilityLabel("Delete item") // Descriptive label for VoiceOver
rules.fix_uikit: imageView.accessibilityLabel = "Delete item" // Enable VoiceOver description
rules.quote: Provide alternative text labels for custom interface icons.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid using replicas of Apple hardware products; use only Apple Design Resources or SF Symbols.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("customMacBookIcon") // Custom hardware replica becomes dated
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "macbook") // Use SF Symbol from Apple Design Resources
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "macbook") // System-provided hardware representation
rules.quote: Avoid using replicas of Apple hardware products.

rules.heading: Document icons
rules.rule: Design simple, recognizable document icon images that remain clear at sizes as small as 16x16 px.
rules.anti_pattern: // Complex document icon with fine details that blur at 16x16 px
rules.fix_uikit: // Create document icon with uncomplicated shapes and distinct colors for all sizes
rules.quote: Your document icon can display as small as 16x16 px, so you want to create designs that remain recognizable at every size.

rules.heading: Document icons
rules.rule: Reduce complexity in small document icon versions; remove or simplify details that blur at smaller sizes.
rules.anti_pattern: // Same detailed grid lines in 16x16 px as in 512x512 px version
rules.fix_uikit: // Thicken lines and reduce count for intermediate sizes; remove details entirely at 16x16 px
rules.quote: Icon details that are clear in large versions can look blurry and be hard to recognize in small versions.

rules.heading: Document icons
rules.rule: Avoid placing important content in the top-right corner of document icon background fill.
rules.anti_pattern: // Critical icon detail placed in top-right corner where folded corner mask appears
rules.fix_uikit: // Keep important content away from top-right; system masks and draws white folded corner there
rules.quote: Avoid placing important content in the top-right corner of your background fill.

rules.heading: Document icons
rules.rule: Define a margin of about 10% of canvas and keep most document icon center image within it for optical balance.
rules.anti_pattern: // Center image fills entire 256x256 px canvas without margin
rules.fix_uikit: // Keep center image within ~205x205 px area of 256x256 px canvas (10% margin)
rules.quote: Define a margin that measures about 10% of the image canvas and keep most of the image within it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use image view only for display; use button for interactive images.
rules.anti_pattern: let imageView = UIImageView(image: UIImage(named: "icon")); imageView.isUserInteractionEnabled = true; let tap = UITapGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(handleTap)); imageView.addGestureRecognizer(tap)
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { /* action */ }) { Image("icon") }
rules.fix_uikit: let button = UIButton(type: .system); button.setImage(UIImage(named: "icon"), for: .normal); button.addTarget(self, action: #selector(handleTap), for: .touchUpInside)
rules.quote: In rare cases where you might want an image to be interactive, configure a system-provided button to display the image instead of adding button behaviors to an image view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer SF Symbols or interface icons over image views for icon display.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("custom_icon") // when a symbol would suffice
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "star.fill")
rules.fix_uikit: let config = UIImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: 16, weight: .regular); UIImage(systemName: "star.fill", withConfiguration: config)
rules.quote: If you want to display an icon in your interface, consider using a symbol or interface icon instead of an image view.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Ensure text overlaid on images has sufficient contrast and visual separation.
rules.anti_pattern: ZStack { Image("background"); Text("Label").foregroundColor(.white) } // without shadow or background
rules.fix_swiftui: ZStack { Image("background"); Text("Label").foregroundStyle(.white).shadow(radius: 2) }
rules.fix_uikit: label.shadowColor = UIColor.black.cgColor; label.shadowOpacity = 0.5; label.shadowOffset = CGSize(width: 1, height: 1)
rules.quote: Take care when overlaying text on images.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Prescale all images in animated sequences to the same size for optimal performance.
rules.anti_pattern: var images = [UIImage(named: "frame1"), UIImage(named: "frame2"), UIImage(named: "frame3")]; imageView.animationImages = images // images have different dimensions
rules.fix_swiftui: // Ensure all images in sequence are same dimensions before creating animation
rules.fix_uikit: // Prescale all images to uniform size before assigning to animationImages
rules.quote: Aim to use a consistent size for all images in an animated sequence.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use image well for editable image views supporting copy, paste, drag, and delete.
rules.anti_pattern: NSImageView() // for user-editable image content
rules.quote: If your app needs an editable image view, use an image well.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use image button instead of image view for clickable images on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern: NSImageView(image: NSImage(named: "action")); imageView.addGestureRecognizer(NSClickGestureRecognizer())
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { /* action */ }) { Image("action") }
rules.quote: Use an image button instead of an image view to make a clickable image.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Display default image when image well content is cleared if an image is required.
rules.quote: If your image well requires an image, display the default image again if people clear the content of the image well.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Implement standard copy/paste menu items and keyboard shortcuts for image wells supporting these operations.
rules.quote: If your image well supports copy and paste, make sure the standard copy and paste menu items are available.

rules.heading: Resolution
rules.rule: Provide @1x, @2x, and @3x scale factor variants for all bitmap images in asset catalog.
rules.anti_pattern: let image = UIImage(named: "icon") // Missing @2x and @3x variants in Assets.xcassets
rules.fix_swiftui: Add icon@1x.png, icon@2x.png, icon@3x.png to Assets.xcassets; SwiftUI Image("icon") auto-selects.
rules.fix_uikit: Add icon@1x.png, icon@2x.png, icon@3x.png to Assets.xcassets; UIImage(named:) auto-selects.
rules.quote: Provide high-resolution assets for all bitmap images in your app, for every device you support.

rules.heading: Resolution
rules.rule: Name bitmap image files with @1x, @2x, or @3x suffix matching device scale factor requirements.
rules.anti_pattern: icon.png, icon_2x.png, icon_3x.png // Incorrect naming convention
rules.fix_swiftui: Rename to icon@1x.png, icon@2x.png, icon@3x.png in asset catalog.
rules.fix_uikit: Rename to icon@1x.png, icon@2x.png, icon@3x.png in asset catalog.
rules.quote: As you add each image to your project's asset catalog, identify its scale factor by appending "@1x," "@2x," or "@3x" to its filename.

rules.heading: Resolution
rules.rule: Design images at lowest resolution (@1x) and scale up to create @2x and @3x variants.
rules.anti_pattern: Design at @3x resolution first, then downscale to @1x causing quality loss.
rules.fix_swiftui: Create master design at @1x; export @2x and @3x by scaling up mathematically.
rules.fix_uikit: Create master design at @1x; export @2x and @3x by scaling up mathematically.
rules.quote: In general, design images at the lowest resolution and scale them up to create high-resolution assets.

rules.heading: Resolution
rules.rule: Position vector control points at whole values to align cleanly at 1x and higher resolutions.
rules.anti_pattern: Vector shape with control points at 10.5, 20.3 causing misalignment at @2x and @3x.
rules.fix_swiftui: Adjust vector paths so all control points use integer coordinates (10, 20, 30).
rules.fix_uikit: Adjust vector paths so all control points use integer coordinates (10, 20, 30).
rules.quote: When you use resizable vectorized shapes, you might want to position control points at whole values so that they're cleanly aligned at 1x.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include color profile with each image to ensure consistent color appearance across displays.
rules.anti_pattern: let image = UIImage(named: "photo") // Image lacks embedded color profile
rules.fix_swiftui: Export image with sRGB or Display P3 color profile embedded.
rules.fix_uikit: Export image with sRGB or Display P3 color profile embedded.
rules.quote: Include a color profile with each image.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Test images on a range of actual devices to verify appearance across resolutions and scales.
rules.anti_pattern: Deploy app without testing images on iPhone SE, iPhone Pro Max, iPad, and Mac.
rules.fix_swiftui: Run app on @2x (iPhone 12) and @3x (iPhone 14 Pro) devices; verify no pixelation or stretching.
rules.fix_uikit: Run app on @2x (iPhone 12) and @3x (iPhone 14 Pro) devices; verify no pixelation or stretching.
rules.quote: Always test images on a range of actual devices.

rules.heading: Inclusive by design
rules.rule: Investigate diverse user perspectives and goals before designing content and functionality.
rules.anti_pattern: Designing an app feature without considering how users of different ages, genders, races, abilities, or cultural backgrounds might interpret or use it.
rules.quote: To design an intuitive experience, you start by investigating people's goals and perspectives so you can present content that resonates with them.

rules.heading: Welcoming language
rules.rule: Use direct second-person pronouns (you/your) instead of indirect references like 'the user' or 'the player'.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("The user can tap the button to proceed") or UILabel with text "The player must complete this level"
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("You can tap the button to proceed")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "You can tap the button to proceed"
rules.quote: It typically works well to use you and your to address people directly.

rules.heading: Welcoming language
rules.rule: Avoid colloquial expressions; replace with plain language to improve clarity and translatability.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("This feature is grandfathered in") or UILabel with text "Don't worry, it's a piece of cake"
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("This feature is included for existing users")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "This feature is included for existing users"
rules.quote: Colloquial expressions are often culture-specific and can be difficult to translate.

rules.heading: Welcoming language
rules.rule: Define specialized or technical terms on first use; avoid assuming user knowledge.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Enable CORS to proceed") without explanation or UILabel with unexplained technical jargon
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Enable CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) to proceed")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Enable CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) to proceed"
rules.quote: Using specialized or technical terms can make your writing more succinct, but doing so excludes people who don't know what the terms mean.

rules.heading: Welcoming language
rules.rule: Use humor sparingly; it is subjective, difficult to translate, and risks confusing or insulting users.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Oops! You really messed that up, didn't you?") with sarcastic tone in error messages
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("This action could not be completed. Please try again.")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "This action could not be completed. Please try again."
rules.quote: Including humor in your experience risks confusing people who donʼt understand it, irritating people who tire of repeatedly encountering it, and insulting people who interpret it differently.

rules.heading: Gender identity
rules.rule: Avoid unnecessary gender references in copy; use gender-neutral language and pronouns.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("He or she can post recipes") or copy that assumes binary gender in user-facing text
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Subscribers can post recipes")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Subscribers can post recipes"
rules.quote: You can help everyone feel welcome in your app or game by avoiding unnecessary references to specific genders.

rules.heading: Gender identity
rules.rule: Provide inclusive gender options including nonbinary, self-identify, and decline to state when gender data is required.
rules.anti_pattern: Picker("Gender", selection: $gender) { Text("Male").tag("M"); Text("Female").tag("F") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Gender", selection: $gender) { Text("Male").tag("M"); Text("Female").tag("F"); Text("Nonbinary").tag("NB"); Text("Self-identify").tag("SI"); Text("Decline to state").tag("DTS") }
rules.fix_uikit: Add nonbinary, self-identify, and decline to state options to UIPickerView or UISegmentedControl
rules.quote: If you require this information — such as for health or legal reasons — consider providing inclusive options, such as nonbinary, self-identify, and decline to state.

rules.heading: Gender identity
rules.rule: Use nongendered human images and SF Symbols glyphs to represent generic people.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: "person.fill") when depicting a generic person, or using only male/female-specific glyphs
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "figure") or Image(systemName: "person")
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "figure") or UIImage(systemName: "person")
rules.quote: If you need to depict a generic person or people, use a nongendered human image to reinforce the message that generic person means human, not man or woman.

rules.heading: People and settings
rules.rule: Portray diverse human characteristics including race, age, body type, and physical capabilities in imagery.
rules.anti_pattern: A fitness app showing exercise moves demonstrated only by young, able-bodied people of one race.
rules.quote: As you create copy and images that represent people, portray a range of human characteristics and activities.

rules.heading: People and settings
rules.rule: Avoid stereotypical representations of occupations, behaviors, and roles that perpetuate real-world biases.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing only male doctors and female nurses, or depicting heroes and villains along racial stereotypes.
rules.quote: If you need to depict occupations or behaviors, avoid stereotypical representations, such as showing only male doctors, female nurses, or heroes and villains that may perpetuate real-world racial or gender stereotypes.

rules.heading: Avoiding stereotypes
rules.rule: Avoid designing based on narrow assumptions; use universal human experiences instead of context-specific ones.
rules.anti_pattern: Security questions like 'What was your favorite subject in college?' or 'What was the make of your first car?' that assume shared experiences.
rules.quote: Using a context-specific experience to communicate something is useless for everyone who doesn't share that context and effectively excludes them.

rules.heading: Accessibility
rules.rule: Support Apple accessibility features (VoiceOver, Display Accommodations, closed captioning, Switch Control, Speak Screen).
rules.anti_pattern: An app with no accessibility labels, images without alt text, or interactions that don't work with VoiceOver.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "plus") }.accessibilityLabel("Add item")
rules.fix_uikit: button.accessibilityLabel = "Add item"
rules.quote: People rely on Apple's accessibility features — such as VoiceOver, Display Accommodations, closed captioning, Switch Control, and Speak Screen — to customize their devices for their individual needs, so it's essential to support these features.

rules.heading: Accessibility
rules.rule: Avoid language that uses disability as a negative quality; include people with disabilities in diverse representations.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Don't be blind to these features") or imagery that excludes people with disabilities.
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Don't miss these features")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Don't miss these features"
rules.quote: Avoid images and language that exclude people with disabilities.

rules.heading: Languages
rules.rule: Use SF Symbols for glyphs to support localization and right-to-left language contexts.
rules.anti_pattern: Using custom PNG images for icons instead of SF Symbols, or hardcoded text strings without localization keys.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle") instead of Image("custom_checkmark")
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "checkmark.circle") instead of UIImage(named: "custom_checkmark")
rules.quote: Using SF Symbols for the glyphs in your app or game can also help streamline localization.

rules.heading: Languages
rules.rule: Be aware of culture-specific color meanings; verify color choices communicate consistently across locales.
rules.anti_pattern: Using white as the primary color for death/grief messaging in all locales without considering cultural context.
rules.quote: Colors often have strong culture-specific meanings, so it's essential to discover how people respond to specific colors in each locale you support.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support Full Keyboard Access to enable navigation and activation using only the keyboard.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .keyboardShortcut() and ensure all interactive elements are keyboard-accessible via focus engine.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIKeyCommand handlers and ensure canBecomeFocused returns true for interactive elements.
rules.quote: Available in iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS, Full Keyboard Access lets people navigate and activate windows, menus, controls, and system features using only the keyboard.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: On iPadOS, avoid custom keyboard navigation for controls; use Full Keyboard Access instead.
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove custom keyboard navigation; rely on system focus engine and Full Keyboard Access.
rules.fix_uikit: Remove custom UIKeyCommand handlers for button/control navigation; let Full Keyboard Access handle focus.
rules.quote: Although iPadOS supports keyboard navigation in text fields, text views, and sidebars, and provides APIs you can use to support it in collection views and other custom views, avoid supporting keyboard navigation for controls, such as buttons, segmented controls, and switches.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Respect standard keyboard shortcuts; only repurpose them if the standard action is irrelevant.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use standard shortcuts for their intended actions; create unique custom shortcuts for app-specific commands.
rules.fix_uikit: Assign UIKeyCommand with standard key equivalents only to their standard actions.
rules.quote: While using most apps, people generally expect to rely on the standard keyboard shortcuts that work in other apps and throughout the system.

rules.heading: Standard keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Do not repurpose standard keyboard shortcuts for custom actions unrelated to their standard meaning.
rules.fix_swiftui: Reserve Command-Q for quit; use unique shortcuts like Command-Shift-X for custom commands.
rules.fix_uikit: Only assign standard UIKeyCommand equivalents to their documented standard actions.
rules.quote: In general, don't repurpose standard keyboard shortcuts for custom actions.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Define custom keyboard shortcuts only for the most frequently used app-specific commands.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Too many custom shortcuts
Button("Action1").keyboardShortcut("1", modifiers: .command)
Button("Action2").keyboardShortcut("2", modifiers: .command)
Button("Action3").keyboardShortcut("3", modifiers: .command)
Button("Action4").keyboardShortcut("4", modifiers: .command)
rules.fix_swiftui: Limit custom shortcuts to 3–5 most-used commands; use menu items for less-frequent actions.
rules.fix_uikit: Register only high-frequency UIKeyCommand shortcuts; expose others via menus.
rules.quote: Define custom keyboard shortcuts for only the most frequently used app-specific commands.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Prefer Command as the primary modifier key; use Shift as secondary; avoid Control.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Incorrect modifier order and Control usage
Button("Action").keyboardShortcut("a", modifiers: [.control, .command])
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .keyboardShortcut("a", modifiers: .command) or .keyboardShortcut("a", modifiers: [.shift, .command])
rules.fix_uikit: Assign UIKeyCommand with input: "a" and modifierFlags: .command or [.shift, .command]
rules.quote: Prefer the Command key as the main modifier key in a custom keyboard shortcut.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: List multiple modifier keys in order: Control, Option, Shift, Command.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Incorrect modifier order
Button("Action").keyboardShortcut("a", modifiers: [.command, .shift, .option])
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .keyboardShortcut("a", modifiers: [.option, .shift, .command])
rules.fix_uikit: Set modifierFlags in correct order: UIKeyModifierControl | UIKeyModifierAlternate | UIKeyModifierShift | UIKeyModifierCommand
rules.quote: If you use more than one modifier key in a custom shortcut, always list them in this order: Control, Option, Shift, Command.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Avoid adding Shift to shortcuts using the upper character of a two-character key.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Incorrect: Shift-Command-Slash for Help
Button("Help").keyboardShortcut("/", modifiers: [.shift, .command])
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .keyboardShortcut("?", modifiers: .command) for Help (upper char of / key).
rules.fix_uikit: Set input: "?" with modifierFlags: .command (not Shift-Command-Slash).
rules.quote: Avoid adding Shift to a shortcut that uses the upper character of a two-character key.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Do not create new shortcuts by adding a modifier to an existing shortcut for an unrelated command.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Confusing: Shift-Command-Z for unrelated action (not Redo)
Button("Custom").keyboardShortcut("z", modifiers: [.shift, .command])
rules.fix_swiftui: Reserve Shift-Command-Z for Redo; use unique shortcuts like Command-Shift-X for unrelated commands.
rules.fix_uikit: Avoid modifier variants of established shortcuts; use distinct key combinations.
rules.quote: Avoid creating a new shortcut by adding a modifier to an existing shortcut for an unrelated command.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Use modifier keys in ways people expect: Command for grouping, Shift for constraining, arrow keys for incremental movement.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Unexpected modifier behavior
Button("Move").keyboardShortcut(.upArrow, modifiers: .option) // Confusing semantics
rules.fix_swiftui: Use arrow keys with .shift for selection extension; .command for group operations.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIKeyCommand handlers that respect standard modifier semantics.
rules.quote: For example, pressing Command while dragging moves items as a group, and pressing Shift while drag-resizing constrains resizing to the item's aspect ratio.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Avoid using Control as a modifier key; the system reserves it for system features.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Incorrect: Control as custom modifier
Button("Action").keyboardShortcut("a", modifiers: .control)
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .command, .shift, or .option instead; reserve Control for system shortcuts.
rules.fix_uikit: Avoid UIKeyModifierControl in custom shortcuts; use other modifiers.
rules.quote: Avoid using the Control key as a modifier.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Use Option modifier sparingly for less-common commands or power features.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Overusing Option for common actions
Button("Save").keyboardShortcut("s", modifiers: [.command, .option])
rules.fix_swiftui: Reserve Option for advanced/power-user features; use Command-S for Save.
rules.fix_uikit: Limit UIKeyModifierAlternate to infrequent or advanced commands.
rules.quote: Use the Option modifier sparingly for less-common commands or power features.

rules.heading: Custom keyboard shortcuts
rules.rule: Avoid combining non-Command modifiers with non-alphabetic characters to ensure keyboard compatibility.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Unsafe: Option-5 may generate '{' on French keyboard
Button("Action").keyboardShortcut("5", modifiers: .option)
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Command with any character; if using other modifiers, restrict to alphabetic keys.
rules.fix_uikit: Prefer Command modifier with all characters; use Option/Shift only with a–z.
rules.quote: It's usually safe to use the Command key as a modifier, but avoid using an additional modifier with characters that aren't available on all keyboards.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use Label for small uneditable text; use TextField for editable text; use TextView for large text.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Email", text: $email) // for display-only content
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Email") // or Label("Email", systemImage: "envelope")
rules.fix_uikit: UILabel() // instead of UITextField with isUserInteractionEnabled=false
rules.quote: Use a label to display a small amount of text that people don't need to edit.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer system fonts and ensure Dynamic Type support; custom fonts must maintain legibility.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Title").font(.custom("Comic Sans", size: 12))
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Title").font(.body) // or .system(.body, design: .default)
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body)
rules.quote: Prefer system fonts. A label can display plain or styled text, and it supports Dynamic Type (where available) by default.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use system label colors (label, secondary, tertiary, quaternary) to communicate text importance.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Subtitle").foregroundColor(.gray) // hardcoded color
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Subtitle").foregroundStyle(.secondary)
rules.fix_uikit: label.textColor = UIColor.secondaryLabel
rules.quote: Use system-provided label colors to communicate relative importance.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Make label text selectable if it contains useful information like errors, locations, or IP addresses.
rules.anti_pattern: Text(errorMessage) // non-selectable error text
rules.fix_swiftui: Text(errorMessage).textSelection(.enabled)
rules.fix_uikit: label.isUserInteractionEnabled = true; add UILongPressGestureRecognizer for copy
rules.quote: Make useful label text selectable. If a label contains useful information — like an error message, a location, or an IP address — consider letting people select and copy it for pasting elsewhere.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: On macOS, use NSTextField with isEditable=false to display uneditable label text.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTextView() // for display-only text on macOS
rules.fix_uikit: let field = NSTextField(); field.isEditable = false
rules.quote: To display uneditable text in a label, use the isEditable property of NSTextField.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Complete app launch and display first screen within 2 seconds to meet user expectations.
rules.anti_pattern: Performing heavy computation, network requests, or database queries on the main thread during app launch before showing the first screen.
rules.fix_uikit: Move blocking operations to background queues using DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated) before presenting the first view controller.
rules.quote: People want to start interacting with your app or game right away, and sometimes they don't want to wait more than a couple of seconds.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide a launch screen for iOS and iPadOS; macOS, visionOS, and watchOS do not require one.
rules.anti_pattern: Omitting a launch screen storyboard or XIB file from an iOS app, or attempting to add a launch screen to a macOS app.
rules.fix_uikit: Include a LaunchScreen.storyboard or LaunchScreen.xib in the Xcode project and set it in Build Settings under 'Launch Screen File'.
rules.quote: In iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS, the system displays your launch screen the moment your app or game starts and quickly replaces it with your first screen, giving people the impression that your experience is fast and responsive.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display splash screens only at the start of onboarding flow, not as the primary launch experience.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing a splash screen immediately when the app launches before any functional content is available.
rules.fix_swiftui: Conditionally show splash screen only when `isFirstLaunch` is true, within an onboarding flow view.
rules.fix_uikit: Present splash screen view controller only from within an onboarding flow, not from the app delegate's didFinishLaunchingWithOptions.
rules.quote: If you need a splash screen, consider displaying it at the beginning of your onboarding flow.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Restore app state on restart so users resume from their previous location without retracing steps.
rules.anti_pattern: Always launching to the root view or home screen, ignoring the user's previous navigation stack or scroll position.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @SceneStorage to persist navigation state and scroll positions; restore them in the view hierarchy on app relaunch.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIStateRestoration protocol and encode/decode view controller hierarchy and scroll offsets in encodeRestorableStateWithCoder.
rules.quote: Restore the previous state when your app restarts so people can continue where they left off.

rules.heading: Launch screens
rules.rule: Design launch screen to be nearly identical to the first screen to avoid visual flash on transition.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a launch screen with a different layout, colors, or elements than the first screen, causing a jarring visual transition.
rules.fix_uikit: Match the launch screen storyboard layout, background color, and safe area insets exactly to the first view controller's initial state.
rules.quote: Design a launch screen that's nearly identical to the first screen of your app or game.

rules.heading: Launch screens
rules.rule: Avoid including any text on launch screens because it cannot be localized.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding labels, buttons, or any text strings to the launch screen storyboard or XIB file.
rules.fix_uikit: Remove all UILabel, UIButton, and text-bearing views from LaunchScreen.storyboard; use only images and solid colors.
rules.quote: Avoid including text on your launch screen, even if your first screen displays text.

rules.heading: Launch screens
rules.rule: Do not use launch screen as a branding or advertising opportunity; avoid logos and splash-screen-like designs.
rules.anti_pattern: Including app logo, company name, tagline, or decorative graphics in the launch screen storyboard.
rules.fix_uikit: Remove all branding assets from LaunchScreen.storyboard except those that are permanent fixtures of the first screen.
rules.quote: Don't advertise. The launch screen isn't a branding opportunity.

rules.heading: Launch screens
rules.rule: Ensure launch screen matches device orientation and appearance mode (light/dark) at launch time.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a single launch screen that does not adapt to landscape orientation or dark mode appearance.
rules.fix_uikit: Create separate launch screen variants in LaunchScreen.storyboard using size classes and appearance traits, or use runtime configuration.
rules.quote: Also make sure that your launch screen matches the device's current orientation and appearance mode.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Launch in the device's current orientation if app supports both portrait and landscape; otherwise launch in supported orientation.
rules.anti_pattern: Always launching in portrait orientation regardless of device orientation, or forcing landscape-only app to launch in portrait.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use AppDelegate or SceneDelegate to detect current device orientation and configure initial view accordingly.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement supportedInterfaceOrientations in AppDelegate and set preferredInterfaceOrientationForPresentation based on UIDevice.current.orientation.
rules.quote: If your app or game supports both portrait and landscape modes, launch using the device's current orientation.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Landscape-only interface must respond correctly to both left and right device rotations.
rules.anti_pattern: Landscape-only app that only supports right rotation or crashes when rotated left.
rules.fix_uikit: Set supportedInterfaceOrientations to include both UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft and UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight.
rules.quote: Ensure a landscape-only interface responds correctly, regardless of whether people enter landscape orientation by rotating the device left or right.

rules.heading: Visual hierarchy
rules.rule: Place most important content near top and leading side following reading order.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { unimportantView; importantView }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { importantView; unimportantView }
rules.fix_uikit: Reorder subviews so critical content appears first in view hierarchy.
rules.quote: People often start by viewing content in reading order — that is, from top to bottom and from the leading to trailing side — so place the most important items near the top and leading side of the window or display.

rules.heading: Visual hierarchy
rules.rule: Use alignment and indentation to convey hierarchy and show content relationships.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack(alignment: .leading) { Text("Parent"); Text("Child") }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(alignment: .leading) { Text("Parent"); HStack { Spacer().frame(width: 16); Text("Child") } }
rules.fix_uikit: Apply leading margin constraints to child views to indent them relative to parent.
rules.quote: Alignment makes an app look neat and organized, and can help people track content while scrolling or moving their eyes.

rules.heading: Visual hierarchy
rules.rule: Group related items using negative space, containers, or separators to express relationships.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { item1; item2; item3; item4 }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { GroupBox { item1; item2 }; Divider(); GroupBox { item3; item4 } }
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIStackView with spacing and background colors to visually group related controls.
rules.quote: Group related items to clearly express related information or functions.

rules.heading: Visual hierarchy
rules.rule: Use Liquid Glass material and scroll edge effects to visually elevate controls above content.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Action").background(Color.white.opacity(0.5))
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Action").materialEffect(.ultraThin)
rules.fix_uikit: Apply UIBackgroundExtensionView or UIVisualEffectView with appropriate blur style.
rules.quote: Take advantage of the Liquid Glass material on all platforms that support it to provide a distinct appearance for your controls.

rules.heading: Adaptability
rules.rule: Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout to ensure interface adapts to device characteristics.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Content").frame(width: 320, height: 480)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Content").frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
rules.fix_uikit: Use NSLayoutConstraint with multiplier or UIStackView for flexible sizing.
rules.quote: Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout to ensure that your interface adapts to them.

rules.heading: Adaptability
rules.rule: Design layouts that adapt gracefully across rotations, resizes, and device switches.
rules.anti_pattern: if UIDevice.current.orientation == .portrait { portraitLayout } else { landscapeLayout }
rules.fix_swiftui: ViewThatFits { horizontalLayout; verticalLayout }
rules.fix_uikit: Use size classes and trait collections instead of device orientation.
