rules.quote: People expect your experience to remain familiar when they rotate their device, resize a window, add another display, or switch to a different device.

rules.heading: Adaptability
rules.rule: Support Dynamic Type by adjusting layout to accommodate larger text sizes.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Label").font(.system(size: 14)).lineLimit(1)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").font(.body).lineLimit(nil)
rules.fix_uikit: Set adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true and use preferredMaxLayoutWidth.
rules.quote: Apps that don't respond to this setting can be difficult or impossible to use for people who rely on this feature.

rules.heading: Adaptability
rules.rule: Test layouts across multiple devices, size classes, localizations, and text sizes.
rules.anti_pattern: Design only for iPhone 15 Pro in portrait mode.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Xcode previews with .previewDisplayName and .environment modifiers.
rules.fix_uikit: Test in Device Hub with different size classes and Dynamic Type settings.
rules.quote: Preview your app on multiple devices, using different size classes, localizations, and text sizes.

rules.heading: Size classes
rules.rule: Determine layout based on size classes, not device type or orientation.
rules.anti_pattern: if UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .phone { compactLayout } else { regularLayout }
rules.fix_swiftui: @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) var hSizeClass; if hSizeClass == .compact { ... }
rules.fix_uikit: Use traitCollection.horizontalSizeClass and traitCollection.verticalSizeClass.
rules.quote: Size classes describe the actual space available, regardless of whether an app is in portrait or landscape.

rules.heading: Size classes
rules.rule: Keep functionality constant across size classes; vary visibility and layout only.
rules.anti_pattern: if hSizeClass == .compact { limitedFeatures } else { allFeatures }
rules.fix_swiftui: NavigationSplitView { sidebar } detail: { detail } (visible in regular, hidden in compact)
rules.fix_uikit: Use UISplitViewController to show/hide sidebar based on size class.
rules.quote: Don't change your app's functionality based on the space it occupies.

rules.heading: Guides and safe areas
rules.rule: Respect safe areas to prevent obstruction by Dynamic Island, notches, or system UI.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Content").ignoresSafeArea()
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("Content") }.safeAreaInset(edge: .top) { topBar }
rules.fix_uikit: Use safeAreaLayoutGuide for all constraint anchors.
rules.quote: Respecting the safe area is essential to make sure system UI and hardware features like the Dynamic Island don't obstruct content and controls.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Avoid placing controls or critical information at the bottom of macOS windows.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { content; Spacer(); criticalButton }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { criticalButton; Spacer(); content }
rules.quote: People often move windows so that the bottom edge is below the bottom of the screen.

rules.heading: The two layers
rules.rule: Use Liquid Glass only in the functional layer (controls, navigation); never in the content layer.
rules.fix_swiftui: Move glassEffect to the toolbar or navigation bar, not to content rows or backgrounds.
rules.fix_uikit: Apply UIGlassEffect only to UINavigationBar, UITabBar, or custom floating controls, not to UITableViewCell or content containers.
rules.quote: Liquid Glass is the dynamic, translucent material Apple introduced in 2025 for the layer of controls and navigation that floats above an app's content.

rules.heading: Where the material belongs
rules.rule: Do not apply Liquid Glass to content-layer elements like cards, list rows, or app backgrounds.
rules.fix_swiftui: Reserve glassEffect for toolbars, tab bars, sidebars, sheets, and popovers only.
rules.fix_uikit: Apply glass only to UINavigationBar, UITabBar, UIToolbar, or custom floating controls.
rules.quote: Don't use Liquid Glass in the content layer.

rules.heading: Where the material belongs
rules.rule: Apply Liquid Glass effects sparingly; limit custom glass to the most important functional elements.
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply glassEffect to one or two primary actions per view, not to every button.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIGlassEffect on the most critical controls; avoid stacking glass on multiple custom elements.
rules.quote: Use Liquid Glass effects sparingly.

rules.heading: Which variant
rules.rule: Use clear Liquid Glass only for components that appear over visually rich backgrounds like photos or video.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .glassEffect(.regular) over plain or simple backgrounds; reserve .glassEffect(.clear) for media-rich contexts.
rules.fix_uikit: Apply UIGlassEffect with clear variant only when the underlying content is visually prominent (photos, video).
rules.quote: Only use clear Liquid Glass for components that appear over visually rich backgrounds.

rules.heading: Which variant
rules.rule: Add a dark dimming layer at ~35% opacity behind clear glass over bright media when legibility requires it.
rules.fix_swiftui: Layer a semi-transparent dark overlay (opacity ~0.35) between the image and the clear glass control.
rules.fix_uikit: Add a UIView with backgroundColor set to black at 0.35 opacity between the image and the glass effect view.
rules.quote: Decide whether clear glass needs a dimming layer.

rules.heading: Color on glass
rules.rule: Apply color sparingly to Liquid Glass; reserve it for primary actions and status indicators only.
rules.fix_swiftui: Color only one primary action per view; keep other controls monochrome.
rules.fix_uikit: Set tintColor on one prominent button; leave others with default monochromatic appearance.
rules.quote: Apply color sparingly to the Liquid Glass material, and to symbols or text on the material.

rules.heading: Color on glass
rules.rule: Emphasize a primary action by coloring the background, not the symbol or label.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .buttonStyle(.glassProminent) or apply tint to the button itself, not its label.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIButton.Configuration.prominentGlass() to color the background.
rules.quote: To emphasize a primary action, color the background rather than the symbol or label.

rules.heading: Color on glass
rules.rule: Avoid coloring the background of multiple controls in the same view.
rules.fix_swiftui: Color only one button per view; style others with .buttonStyle(.glass).
rules.fix_uikit: Apply Configuration.prominentGlass() to one button; use Configuration.glass() for others.
rules.quote: Refrain from adding color to the background of multiple controls.

rules.heading: Color on glass
rules.rule: Avoid using similar colors in control labels if the app background is colorful; prefer monochromatic or high-contrast accent.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use monochromatic toolbar or tab bar, or an accent color with strong differentiation from content.
rules.fix_uikit: Keep toolbar tintColor distinct from content-layer colors.
rules.quote: Avoid using similar colors in control labels if your app has a colorful background.

rules.heading: Color on glass
rules.rule: Apply app accent color judiciously; reserve it for primary actions and status indicators, not most controls.
rules.fix_swiftui: Color only the selected tab icon or one primary action; keep other tab labels monochromatic.
rules.fix_uikit: Apply tintColor to selected tab or primary button only.
rules.quote: Apply your app's accent color judiciously.

rules.heading: Review checklist
rules.rule: Glass appears only on floating controls and navigation; never on app backgrounds, cards, list rows, or content containers.
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply glassEffect only to toolbars, tab bars, sidebars, sheets, and popovers.
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve UIGlassEffect for UINavigationBar, UITabBar, UIToolbar, and custom floating controls.
rules.quote: Glass appears only on floating controls and navigation.

rules.heading: Review checklist
rules.rule: Limit custom glass surfaces to the few most important functional elements; stacked glass blurs hierarchy.
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply glassEffect to the container once, not to each child and parent.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIGlassContainerEffect to group related glass surfaces; avoid nested glass views.
rules.quote: Count the custom glass surfaces. More than the few most important functional elements is a defect.

rules.heading: SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit
rules.rule: Use standard bars and controls that adopt glass automatically; reach for glass APIs only for custom controls.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .toolbar with .glassEffect applied by the system, or wrap custom controls in GlassEffectContainer.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UINavigationBar or UIToolbar; apply UIGlassEffect only to custom floating views.
rules.quote: Standard bars, sheets, popovers, and controls adopt the material on their own.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer lists/tables for text-heavy content; use collections for large images or variable-sized items.
rules.anti_pattern:
let collectionView = UICollectionView(frame: .zero, collectionViewLayout: UICollectionViewFlowLayout())
// Displaying 500 rows of short text in a collection view instead of UITableView
rules.fix_swiftui: List { ForEach(textItems) { item in Text(item) } }
rules.fix_uikit: Use UITableView instead of UICollectionView for text-heavy, row-based content.
rules.quote: A table can include any type of content, but the row-based format is especially well suited to making text easy to scan and read.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow list reordering and editing in iOS/iPadOS; require explicit edit mode entry before item selection.
rules.fix_uikit: tableView.setEditing(true, animated: true) before allowing row selection; implement UITableViewDataSource deletion/reordering methods.
rules.quote: People appreciate being able to reorder a list, even if they can't add or remove items.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Persistently highlight selected rows in hierarchical navigation tables; briefly highlight in option-selection tables.
rules.fix_uikit: Keep row selected after navigation; deselect only when returning to the list.
rules.quote: In general, a table that helps people navigate through a hierarchy persistently highlights the selected row to clarify the path people are taking.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Keep item text succinct to minimize truncation, wrapping, and maximize readability.
rules.anti_pattern:
Text("This is an extremely long description of the item that contains multiple sentences and will definitely wrap across multiple lines making the row very tall and hard to scan quickly")
  .lineLimit(nil)
rules.fix_swiftui:
Text("Item Title")
  .lineLimit(1)
rules.fix_uikit:
label.numberOfLines = 1
label.text = "Item Title"
rules.quote: Short, succinct text can help minimize truncation and wrapping, making text easier to read and scan.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use middle ellipsis for clipped text to preserve both beginning and end for recognition.
rules.anti_pattern:
Text("VeryLongFileName.txt")
  .lineLimit(1)
  .truncationMode(.tail)
rules.fix_swiftui:
Text("VeryLongFileName.txt")
  .lineLimit(1)
  .truncationMode(.middle)
rules.fix_uikit: label.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingMiddle
rules.quote: Sometimes, an ellipsis in the middle of text can make an item easier to distinguish because it preserves both the beginning and the end of the content.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use descriptive column headings with title-case nouns/phrases and no ending punctuation.
rules.fix_swiftui: TableColumn(value: \.name, header: Text("User Name"))
rules.fix_uikit: tableColumn.headerCell.stringValue = "User Name"
rules.quote: Use nouns or short noun phrases with title-style capitalization, and don't add ending punctuation.

rules.heading: Style
rules.rule: Choose list/table style matching data structure and platform conventions (grouped, bordered, etc.).
rules.fix_uikit: tableView.style = .grouped // or .insetGrouped on iOS 13+
rules.quote: Choose a table or list style that coordinates with your data and platform.

rules.heading: Style
rules.rule: Use built-in row styles (UIListContentConfiguration, SwiftUI layouts) to arrange content consistently.
rules.fix_uikit:
var content = UIListContentConfiguration.cell()
content.image = UIImage(systemName: "photo")
content.text = "Title"
content.secondaryText = "Subtitle"
cell.contentConfiguration = content
rules.quote: Some platforms provide built-in row styles you can use to arrange content in list rows, such as the UIListContentConfiguration API you can use to lay out content in a list's rows, headers, and footers in iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Use disclosure indicator for hierarchical navigation; reserve info button for revealing row details only.
rules.anti_pattern:
cell.accessoryType = .detailDisclosureButton
// Used for navigating to nested list instead of revealing details
rules.fix_swiftui: NavigationLink(destination: DetailView()) { Text(item) }
rules.fix_uikit: cell.accessoryType = .disclosureIndicator
rules.quote: An info button — called a detail disclosure button when it appears in a list row — doesn't support navigation through a hierarchical table or list.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Avoid index on tables with trailing controls (disclosure indicators); index and controls conflict on trailing edge.
rules.fix_swiftui: List { ForEach(items) { item in Text(item.name) } }
rules.fix_uikit: tableView.sectionIndexTitles = nil
rules.quote: Because both the index and elements like disclosure indicators appear on the trailing side of a list, it can be difficult for people to use one element without activating the other.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Allow column header clicks to sort; reverse sort direction on repeated clicks.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Column headers are not clickable
// Users cannot sort the table
rules.fix_swiftui: Table(items, sortOrder: $sortOrder) { TableColumn("Name", value: \.name) }.onChange(of: sortOrder) { items.sort(using: $1) }
rules.quote: When it provides value, let people click a column heading to sort a table view based on that column.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Allow users to resize table columns to reveal clipped data and focus on different areas.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Column widths are fixed
// Users cannot adjust column width to see full content
rules.fix_swiftui: Table(items) { TableColumn("Name", value: \.name) }
rules.quote: Let people resize columns.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use alternating row colors in multicolumn tables to help track values across columns.
rules.fix_swiftui: Table(items) { TableColumn("Name", value: \.name); TableColumn("Email", value: \.email) }
rules.fix_uikit: tableView.usesAlternatingRowBackgroundColors = true
rules.quote: Alternating colors can help people track row values across columns, especially in a wide table.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use outline view instead of table view to present hierarchical data with disclosure triangles.
rules.fix_swiftui: OutlineGroup(hierarchicalItems, children: \.children) { item in Text(item.name) }
rules.quote: Use an outline view instead of a table view to present hierarchical data.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer Live Activities only for tasks and events with defined beginning and end, not exceeding eight hours.
rules.anti_pattern: // Starting a Live Activity for an indefinite background sync task let activity = try Activity<MyAttributes>.request(attributes: attrs, contentState: state, pushType: nil)
rules.fix_swiftui: // Only start Live Activity for time-bounded events like food delivery, rideshare, or sports matches with clear endpoints
rules.quote: Live Activities work best for tracking short to medium duration activities that don't exceed eight hours.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not use Live Activities to display ads, promotions, or sensitive information visible to casual observers.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Special offer: 50% off!") // or Text("Credit card: 1234-5678-9012-3456")
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Order #12345") // Show only task-related info; redact sensitive data or require tap to view
rules.quote: Don't use a Live Activity to display ads or promotions.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use large, medium-weight or heavier text; display small text sparingly to ensure legibility at a glance.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Status").font(.system(size: 10, weight: .light))
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Status").font(.system(size: 16, weight: .medium))
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 16, weight: .medium)
rules.quote: Use large, heavier-weight text — a medium weight or higher.

rules.heading: Creating Live Activity layouts
rules.rule: Support limited width presentations by adapting compact and minimal views to fit inside a 28pt-diameter circle.
rules.anti_pattern: @main struct MyLiveActivity: Widget { var body: some WidgetConfiguration { ActivityConfiguration(for: MyActivityAttributes.self) { context in Text("Full text that will truncate") } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: @Environment(\.isDynamicIslandLimitedInWidth) var limitedWidth; var body: some View { if limitedWidth { Text("Short") } else { Text("Full text") } }
rules.quote: To avoid truncated text in contexts with limited width like the Dynamic Island on iPhone in landscape, adapt your compact and minimal presentations to fit inside a 28pt-diameter circle.

rules.heading: Creating Live Activity layouts
rules.rule: Use ContainerRelativeShape for rounded corners instead of hard-coding radius values to match Live Activity corner radius.
rules.anti_pattern: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12).frame(width: 50, height: 50)
rules.fix_swiftui: ContainerRelativeShape().fill(Color.blue)
rules.quote: When you place a rounded element near the corner of a Live Activity, use ContainerRelativeShape to match the corner radius of the Live Activity instead of hard-coding a value for it.

rules.heading: Creating Live Activity layouts
rules.rule: Use consistent, concentric margins and inset containers; avoid drawing content to the edge of the Dynamic Island.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Text("Content").frame(maxWidth: .infinity) }.frame(maxWidth: .infinity) // stretches to edges
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("Content") }.padding(14) // standard margin
rules.quote: Use even, matching margins between rounded shapes and the edges of the Live Activity to ensure a harmonious fit.

rules.heading: Creating Live Activity layouts
rules.rule: Dynamically change Live Activity height on Lock Screen or expanded presentation based on available content.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Text("Driver info") }.frame(height: 100) // fixed height regardless of content
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { if hasDriverInfo { DriverDetailsView() } }.frame(height: hasDriverInfo ? 120 : 60)
rules.quote: Dynamically change the height of your Live Activity on the Lock Screen or in the expanded presentation.

rules.heading: Choosing colors
rules.rule: Ensure sufficient contrast for Lock Screen custom colors, especially on Always-On displays with reduced luminance.
rules.anti_pattern: ZStack { Color(red: 0.9, green: 0.9, blue: 0.9).ignoresSafeArea() Text("Info").foregroundColor(.white) }
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Info").foregroundStyle(.white).background(.black)
rules.quote: If you set a custom background color or image for the Lock Screen presentation, ensure sufficient contrast — especially for tint colors on devices that feature an Always-On display with reduced luminance.

rules.heading: Choosing colors
rules.rule: Tint Live Activity key line color to match content for visual coherence in Dark Mode.
rules.anti_pattern: // Default key line color doesn't match content colors
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use activitySystemActionForegroundColor(_:) to set key line color matching content
rules.quote: Tint your Live Activity's key line color so that it matches your content.

rules.heading: Adding transitions and animating content updates
rules.citation: live-activities.md › Adding transitions and animating content updates
rules.rule: Use animations with maximum duration of two seconds to reinforce information and highlight updates.
rules.anti_pattern: withAnimation(.linear(duration: 5)) { score = newScore }
rules.fix_swiftui: withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 1.5)) { score = newScore }
rules.quote: Live Activities use system and custom animations with a maximum duration of two seconds.

rules.heading: Offering interactivity
rules.rule: Limit interactive elements to one essential control directly related to the Live Activity; avoid cluttering with buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Button("Pause") {} Button("Skip") {} Button("Favorite") {} Button("Share") {} }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Pause") { /* pause action */ } // single essential control
rules.quote: If you offer interactivity, prefer limiting it to a single element to help people avoid accidentally tapping the wrong control.

rules.heading: Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity
rules.citation: live-activities.md › Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity
rules.rule: End Live Activity immediately when task or event ends; set custom dismissal time proportional to activity duration.
rules.anti_pattern: // Live Activity remains indefinitely after task completion
rules.fix_swiftui: // End activity: try await activity.end(using: finalState, dismissalPolicy: .after(Date(timeIntervalSinceNow: 1800))) // 30 min
rules.quote: Always end a Live Activity immediately when the task or event ends, and consider setting a custom dismissal time.

rules.heading: Compact presentation
rules.rule: Design leading and trailing compact elements to read as unified information with consistent color and typography.
rules.anti_pattern: // Leading: red text, trailing: blue text with different font sizes
rules.fix_swiftui: // Both elements use same color palette and font weight for visual cohesion
rules.quote: Though the TrueDepth camera separates the leading and trailing elements, design them to read as a single piece of information, and use consistent color and typography to help create a connection between both elements.

rules.heading: Lock Screen presentation
rules.rule: Use standard 14-point margins on Lock Screen to align with notification layout and avoid crowded edges.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Text("Info") }.padding(2) // too tight
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("Info") }.padding(14)
rules.quote: The standard layout margin for Live Activities on the Lock Screen is 14 points.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place live content in the first tab to minimize taps before playback begins.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { VStack { Text("VOD") }.tabItem { Label("VOD", systemImage: "play") }; VStack { Text("Live") }.tabItem { Label("Live", systemImage: "dot.radiowaves.left.and.right") } }
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView { LiveContentView().tabItem { Label("Live", systemImage: "dot.radiowaves.left.and.right") }; VODContentView().tabItem { Label("VOD", systemImage: "play") } }
rules.fix_uikit: tabBarController.viewControllers = [liveVC, vodVC]
rules.quote: When live content is in the first tab, people don't have to tap more than once to start viewing it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display Watch Now button that immediately starts full-screen playback without intermediate UI.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Watch Now") { showPlaybackSettings = true }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Watch Now") { startFullScreenPlayback() }.fullScreenCover(isPresented: $isPlaying) { VideoPlayerView() }
rules.fix_uikit: UIButton with action that immediately presents fullscreen AVPlayerViewController.
rules.quote: When people tap this button, it immediately disappears and playback begins, replacing your app's UI with a full-screen, immersive viewing experience.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Mark live content with visual indicators (badge, symbol, sash) to distinguish from VOD.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Image("thumbnail"); Text("Channel Name") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("thumbnail").overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) { Image(systemName: "dot.radiowaves.left.and.right").foregroundStyle(.red) }
rules.quote: You might display other channels in a collection row titled "Live" and give each item a visual indicator — such as a badge, symbol, or sash — that identifies it as live.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display progress indicator showing how much live content remains when jumping into in-progress streams.
rules.anti_pattern: VideoPlayer(player: avPlayer)
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { VideoPlayer(player: avPlayer); ProgressView(value: currentProgress, total: totalDuration) }
rules.fix_uikit: Add UIProgressView below AVPlayerViewController showing stream progress.
rules.quote: You can use a progress bar or other indicator to show people how much content remains.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display secondary actions (Record, Restart, Download, Favorite) in consistent order throughout app.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Button("Record") {}; Button("Favorite") {}; Button("Restart") {} }
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu { Button("Watch") {}; Button("Start Over") {}; Button("Record") {}; Button("Favorite") {} } label: { Image(systemName: "ellipsis") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu with UIActions in fixed order: Watch, Start Over, Record, Favorite.
rules.quote: Display these actions in the same order throughout your app — for example, Watch, Start Over, Record, and Favorite.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Apply subtle darkening to content footer to keep text legible and items visually distinct.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { VideoPlayer(); HStack { /* channel thumbnails */ } }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Spacer(); HStack { }.background(LinearGradient(colors: [.clear, .black.opacity(0.6)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)) }
rules.quote: Give it a subtle treatment, such as a darkening, to keep text legible and help all items remain visually distinct from the content playing behind it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Badge or tint progress bar of currently playing thumbnail in content footer.
rules.anti_pattern: ForEach(channels) { channel in Image(channel.thumbnail) }
rules.fix_swiftui: ForEach(channels) { channel in Image(channel.thumbnail).overlay(channel.id == currentChannel ? Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle.fill") : nil) }
rules.fix_uikit: Add badge overlay or tinted progress bar to UIImageView of current channel.
rules.quote: Make it easy for people to identify the thumbnail that represents the currently playing content by, for example, badging the thumbnail or tinting its progress bar.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use predictable, symmetric gestures to invoke and dismiss content footer (e.g., swipe up/down).
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { VideoPlayer(); HStack { /* footer */ } }.onTapGesture { toggleFooter() }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { }.gesture(DragGesture().onEnded { if $0.translation.height > 50 { dismissFooter() } else if $0.translation.height < -50 { showFooter() } })
rules.quote: Design a simple, predictable way for people to invoke and dismiss the content footer — for example, if swiping up invokes the footer, people would expect swiping down to dismiss it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide instant visual feedback when changing channels to confirm arrival and allow content load time.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Channel 5") { currentChannel = 5 }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Channel 5") { withAnimation { currentChannel = 5; showChannelIndicator = true } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIButton with action that animates channel change and displays confirmation overlay.
rules.quote: Provide instant visual feedback when people change channels.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Continue audio playback when browsing while live content plays; stop audio when leaving live tab.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView(selection: $tab) { LiveView(); BrowseView() }.onChange(of: tab) { /* no audio handling */ }
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView(selection: $tab) { LiveView(); BrowseView() }.onChange(of: tab) { newTab in if newTab != 0 { audioSession.setActive(false) } else { audioSession.setActive(true) } }
rules.fix_uikit: AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setActive(false) in viewWillDisappear of live tab.
rules.quote: When people navigate away from the live tab in your app, they leave the live-viewing context, so audio needs to stop.

rules.heading: EPG experience
rules.rule: Highlight current program, channel, and time prominently; make returning to live playback easy.
rules.anti_pattern: List(epgData) { program in Text(program.name) }
rules.fix_swiftui: ScrollViewReader { proxy in List(epgData) { program in Text(program.name).background(program.id == currentProgram.id ? Color.blue : .clear) }.onAppear { proxy.scrollTo(currentProgram.id) } }
rules.quote: When people first open the EPG, the current program, channel, and time needs to be easy to spot so they can instantly return to the current channel.

rules.heading: EPG experience
rules.rule: Provide My Channels or Favorites group for quick access to frequently viewed content in EPG.
rules.anti_pattern: List(allChannels) { channel in Text(channel.name) }
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("View", selection: $epgView) { Text("All").tag(0); Text("My Channels").tag(1) }.pickerStyle(.segmented)
rules.quote: Also consider providing a My Channels group or a Favorites group that gives people quick access to the content they view most often.

rules.heading: EPG experience
rules.rule: Organize EPG content into familiar categories (Movies, TV Shows, Kids, Sports, Popular).
rules.anti_pattern: List(allPrograms) { program in Text(program.name) }
rules.fix_swiftui: List { ForEach(categories, id: \.self) { category in Section(header: Text(category)) { ForEach(programs.filter { $0.category == category }) { program in Text(program.name) } } } }
rules.fix_uikit: UITableView with sections for each category.
rules.quote: For example, you might use categories like Movies, TV Shows, Kids, Sports, and Popular.

rules.heading: EPG experience
rules.rule: Allow EPG browsing without interrupting playback via PiP or background playback.
rules.anti_pattern: NavigationStack { LiveView() } // EPG navigation stops playback
rules.fix_swiftui: NavigationSplitView { EPGView() } detail: { VideoPlayer(player: avPlayer) } // PiP continues
rules.fix_uikit: AVPictureInPictureController to maintain playback while browsing EPG.
rules.quote: For example, you can continue playing content in a picture-in-picture (PiP) mode or in the background while people browse the EPG.

rules.heading: Cloud DVR
rules.rule: Expose Record control in info panel during live playback for immediate recording.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { VideoPlayer(); Text("Go to settings to record") }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { VideoPlayer(); Button("Record") { startRecording() } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIButton with Record action in info panel overlay.
rules.quote: While live-streaming, people want to reveal the info panel to start recording immediately.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display placeholder content immediately rather than blocking UI until loading completes.
rules.fix_swiftui: List(data ?? placeholderItems) { item in Text(item.name).redacted(reason: data == nil ? .placeholder : []) }
rules.quote: If you make people wait for loading to complete before displaying anything, they can interpret the lack of content as a problem with your app or game.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Load content in background to allow users to interact with other app features during loading.
rules.fix_swiftui: ZStack { GameCanvas(); if !levelLoaded { ProgressView() } }.task { await loadLevelInBackground(); levelLoaded = true }
rules.quote: Let people do other things in your app or game while they wait for content to load.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide engaging placeholder content (tips, hints, features) when loading unavoidably exceeds a few seconds.
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { ProgressView(); Text(tips[tipIndex]) }.onAppear { Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 3, repeats: true) { _ in tipIndex = (tipIndex + 1) % tips.count } }
rules.quote: If loading takes an unavoidably long time, give people something interesting to view while they wait.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use Background Assets framework to schedule large asset downloads after install or during updates.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use BackgroundAssets framework to schedule downloads: BADownloadRequest scheduled for post-install or update windows.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure URLSessionConfiguration with background session identifier and use BADownloadManager to schedule asset downloads.
rules.quote: Improve installation and launch time by downloading large assets in the background.

rules.heading: Showing progress
rules.rule: Use determinate progress indicator when load duration is known; indeterminate when duration is unknown.
rules.fix_swiftui: if let totalBytes = totalBytes { ProgressView(value: progress, total: Double(totalBytes)) } else { ProgressView() }
rules.quote: Clearly communicate that content is loading and how long it might take to complete.

rules.heading: Showing progress
rules.rule: For games, design custom loading views with animations matching game style instead of standard progress indicators.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("gameSpinner").rotationEffect(.degrees(rotation)).onAppear { withAnimation(.linear(duration: 1).repeatForever(autoreverses: false)) { rotation = 360 } }
rules.quote: For games, consider creating a custom loading view.

rules.heading: Planning your design
rules.rule: Design ML app UX by teaching the app to interpret data and react, not by designing reactions to static scenarios.
rules.anti_pattern: Hard-coding specific UI responses for every possible ML model output instead of designing adaptive, data-driven behavior.
rules.quote: Because a machine learning app bases its behavior on the data it receives — reacting to changing information and conditions — you can't design specific reactions to a static set of scenarios.

rules.heading: Critical or complementary
rules.rule: Prioritize accuracy and reliability for critical ML features; tolerate lower accuracy for complementary secondary features.
rules.anti_pattern: Deploying an ML-powered core feature (e.g., health diagnosis) with the same accuracy tolerance as a secondary feature (e.g., music recommendation).
rules.quote: In general, the more central a feature is to your app's purpose — like a personalized news feed for a news app — the more people expect accurate and reliable results.

rules.heading: Private or public
rules.rule: Prioritize accuracy and reliability for features using sensitive data; always protect user privacy regardless of data sensitivity.
rules.anti_pattern: Using health or financial data in an ML model without rigorous accuracy testing or privacy safeguards.
rules.quote: In general, the more sensitive the data, the more serious the consequences of inaccurate or unreliable results.

rules.heading: Proactive or reactive
rules.rule: Use additional data for proactive features to reduce intrusiveness and irrelevance, as users have less tolerance for low-quality proactive results.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing proactive ML suggestions (e.g., app shortcuts) with the same confidence threshold as reactive suggestions (e.g., keyboard completions).
rules.quote: Because people don't ask for the results that a proactive feature provides, they may have less tolerance for low-quality information.

rules.heading: Visible or invisible
rules.rule: Communicate reliability and gather feedback for invisible ML features; visible features naturally build user opinion through interaction.
rules.anti_pattern: Deploying an invisible ML feature (e.g., content ranking) without any UI affordance for users to understand or provide feedback on its reliability.
rules.quote: It's harder for an invisible feature to communicate its reliability — and potentially receive feedback — because people may not be aware of the feature at all.

rules.heading: Explicit feedback
rules.rule: Request explicit feedback only when necessary; prefer implicit feedback to avoid burdening users with extra work.
rules.anti_pattern: Prompting users for explicit feedback after every ML-powered action instead of inferring preferences from implicit signals.
rules.quote: Request explicit feedback only when necessary.

rules.heading: Explicit feedback
rules.rule: Use specific, consequence-focused language for feedback options; avoid vague terms like 'dislike' that obscure intent.
rules.anti_pattern: Offering feedback options labeled 'Like', 'Dislike', 'Maybe' without explaining what happens when users select each option.
rules.quote: Use simple, direct language to describe each explicit feedback option and its consequences.

rules.heading: Explicit feedback
rules.rule: Act immediately on explicit feedback and persist changes to build trust in the feedback mechanism.
rules.anti_pattern: Collecting explicit feedback (e.g., 'hide this content') but not removing the content from the user's view or allowing it to reappear elsewhere.
rules.quote: Act immediately when you receive explicit feedback and persist the resulting changes.

rules.heading: Implicit feedback
rules.rule: Always secure implicit feedback data and maintain strict privacy controls; inform users how their data is collected and shared.
rules.anti_pattern: Silently collecting user behavior data across apps without disclosure or providing users with privacy controls.
rules.quote: Always secure people's information.

rules.heading: Implicit feedback
rules.rule: Use multiple implicit feedback signals to avoid misinterpreting user intent and mitigate mistakes.
rules.anti_pattern: Inferring strong preference from a single user action (e.g., viewing a photo) without corroborating signals.
rules.quote: When possible, use multiple feedback signals to improve suggestions and mitigate mistakes.

rules.heading: Implicit feedback
rules.rule: Prioritize recent implicit feedback over historical data to reflect evolving user preferences and tastes.
rules.anti_pattern: Weighting old user behavior equally with recent behavior when generating ML recommendations.
rules.quote: Prioritize recent feedback.

rules.heading: Calibration
rules.rule: Only require calibration when the feature cannot function without initial user information; prefer implicit or explicit feedback otherwise.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring users to calibrate a feature that could work reasonably well without calibration data.
rules.quote: In general, only use calibration when your feature can't function without that initial information.

rules.heading: Calibration
rules.rule: Collect only essential calibration information; avoid asking for data users must look up or actions that are difficult.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting extensive calibration data or asking users to perform complex, error-prone actions during setup.
rules.quote: Collect only the most essential information.

rules.heading: Mistakes
rules.rule: Provide corrective actions or tools proportional to the severity and consequences of ML mistakes.
rules.anti_pattern: Offering the same generic 'undo' option for both minor mistakes (wrong keyboard suggestion) and critical ones (incorrect health recommendation).
rules.quote: Understand the significance of a mistake's consequences.

rules.heading: Corrections
rules.rule: Make corrections easy and familiar; show the steps the app took so users can refine or undo results using the same controls.
rules.anti_pattern: Hiding the ML automation steps and forcing users to learn a different correction interface than the one used for the original action.
rules.quote: Give people familiar, easy ways to make corrections.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Require accounts only when core functionality demands it; otherwise allow app use without sign-in.
rules.anti_pattern: var body: some View { SignInView() } // shown immediately on app launch
rules.fix_swiftui: if isAccountRequired { SignInView() } else { ContentView() }
rules.fix_uikit: if !isAccountRequired { presentContentViewController() } else { presentSignInViewController() }
rules.quote: Ask people to create an account only if your core functionality requires it; otherwise, let people enjoy your app or game without one.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Delay sign-in prompts until users attempt a feature requiring authentication.
rules.anti_pattern: // Force sign-in on app launch before any content is visible
rules.fix_swiftui: // Show sign-in only when user taps 'Purchase' or protected feature
rules.fix_uikit: // Present sign-in modally only when accessing protected functionality
rules.quote: Delay sign-in for as long as possible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer passkeys over passwords; use Sign in with Apple if passkeys unavailable.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Sign In") { presentPasswordEntry() }
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use ASAuthorizationController with passkey provider
rules.fix_uikit: let controller = ASAuthorizationController(authorizationRequests: [passkeyRequest])
rules.quote: If you don't use Sign in with Apple in your iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or visionOS app, prefer using a passkey.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Label authentication buttons with the specific method (e.g., 'Sign In with Face ID'), not generic text.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Sign In") { authenticateWithFaceID() }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Sign In with Face ID") { authenticateWithFaceID() }
rules.fix_uikit: button.setTitle("Sign In with Face ID", for: .normal)
rules.quote: Always identify the authentication method you offer.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Only reference biometric authentication methods available on the current device.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Sign In with Face ID") // on device without Face ID
rules.fix_swiftui: if LAContext().biometryType == .faceID { Button("Sign In with Face ID") {} }
rules.fix_uikit: if LAContext().biometryType == .faceID { showFaceIDButton() }
rules.quote: Refer only to authentication methods that are available in the current context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid in-app settings for biometric authentication; users control this at system level.
rules.anti_pattern: Toggle("Enable Face ID", isOn: $enableBiometric)
rules.fix_swiftui: // Remove in-app toggle; rely on system-level biometric settings
rules.fix_uikit: // Do not present UISwitch for biometric opt-in
rules.quote: In general, avoid offering an app-specific setting for opting in to biometric authentication.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never use 'passcode' to label account authentication fields; reserve it for device/Apple service unlock.
rules.anti_pattern: SecureField("Enter your passcode", text: $password)
rules.fix_swiftui: SecureField("Enter your password", text: $password)
rules.fix_uikit: passwordField.placeholder = "Enter your password"
rules.quote: Avoid using the term *passcode* to refer to account authentication.

rules.heading: Deleting accounts
rules.rule: Provide in-app account deletion or direct link to deletion webpage; never offer deactivation only.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Deactivate Account") { deactivateAccount() } // no deletion option
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Delete Account") { presentAccountDeletionFlow() }
rules.fix_uikit: button.addTarget(self, action: #selector(deleteAccount), for: .touchUpInside)
rules.quote: If you help people create an account within your app or game, you must also help them delete it, not just deactivate it.

rules.heading: Deleting accounts
rules.rule: Make account deletion discoverable; do not bury the link in Privacy Policy or Terms of Service.
rules.anti_pattern: // Deletion link only in Privacy Policy footer
rules.fix_swiftui: NavigationLink("Delete Account", destination: AccountDeletionView())
rules.fix_uikit: settingsViewController.addDeleteAccountButton()
rules.quote: Provide a clear way to initiate account deletion within your app or game.

rules.heading: Deleting accounts
rules.rule: Ensure account deletion flow is equally simple in-app and on website; avoid asymmetric complexity.
rules.anti_pattern: // In-app: 1 tap; Website: 5-step verification process
rules.fix_swiftui: // Match deletion steps and confirmations across platforms
rules.fix_uikit: // Ensure parity between app and web deletion flows
rules.quote: Provide a consistent account-deletion experience whether people perform it within your app or game or on the website.

rules.heading: Deleting accounts
rules.rule: Offer scheduled deletion option alongside immediate deletion for user convenience.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Delete Now") { deleteAccountImmediately() } // no scheduling option
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Schedule Deletion") { presentScheduleDeletionPicker() }
rules.fix_uikit: presentDeletionOptionsViewController()
rules.quote: Consider letting people schedule account deletion to occur in the future.

rules.heading: Deleting accounts
rules.rule: Inform users when deletion completes and provide status updates during the process.
rules.anti_pattern: // No feedback after deletion request submitted
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Your account will be deleted on \(deletionDate)"); notifyOnCompletion()
rules.fix_uikit: showDeletionProgressViewController(); notifyWhenComplete()
rules.quote: Tell people when account deletion will complete, and notify them when it's finished.

rules.heading: TV provider accounts
rules.rule: Never show sign-out option for system-level TV provider authentication; direct to Settings instead.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Sign Out") { signOutTVProvider() }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Sign Out") { openSettings("prefs:root=TVPROVIDER") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIApplication.shared.open(URL(string: "App-Prefs:root=TVPROVIDER")!)
rules.quote: Avoid displaying a sign-out option when people are signed in at the system level.

rules.heading: TV provider accounts
rules.rule: Never instruct users to sign out via privacy controls; TV provider controls are for app access only.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Sign out by disabling TV Provider in Settings > Privacy")
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Sign out in Settings > TV Provider")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Sign out in Settings > TV Provider"
rules.quote: Never instruct people to sign out by adjusting privacy controls.

rules.heading: Integrating with Focus
rules.rule: Classify notifications as communication or noncommunication; use SiriKit intents for direct communications.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending a messaging notification without adopting INSendMessageIntent, preventing Siri customization.
rules.fix_uikit: Adopt INSendMessageIntent and UNNotificationContentProviding for communication notifications.
rules.quote: If you support direct communications — like phone calls and messages — you use communication notifications; for all other types of tasks, you use noncommunication notifications.

rules.heading: Integrating with Focus
rules.rule: Specify a system-defined interruption level for every noncommunication notification sent.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending a noncommunication notification without setting UNNotificationInterruptionLevel.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UNNotificationInterruptionLevel to .passive, .active, .timeSensitive, or .critical on UNMutableNotificationContent.
rules.quote: You need to specify a system-defined interruption level for each noncommunication notification you send.

rules.heading: Integrating with Focus
rules.rule: Use Time Sensitive interruption level only for essential information requiring immediate attention.
rules.anti_pattern: Setting interruption level to .timeSensitive for a restaurant recommendation or non-urgent update.
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve .timeSensitive for account security issues, package deliveries, or time-critical events.
rules.quote: Time Sensitive. Information that directly impacts the person and requires their immediate attention, like an account security issue or a package delivery.

rules.heading: Integrating with Focus
rules.rule: Use Critical interruption level only for urgent health, safety, or governmental alerts with entitlement.
rules.anti_pattern: Setting interruption level to .critical for app feature announcements or non-emergency content.
rules.fix_uikit: Restrict .critical to health/safety/governmental notifications and obtain required entitlement from Apple.
rules.quote: Critical. Urgent information about health and safety that directly impacts the person and demands their immediate attention.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Accurately represent notification urgency to match actual priority and build user trust.
rules.anti_pattern: Using .timeSensitive or .critical interruption level for low-priority marketing or informational content.
rules.fix_uikit: Assign interruption levels conservatively; use .passive or .active for non-urgent notifications.
rules.quote: Build trust by accurately representing the urgency of each notification.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Time Sensitive notifications must describe events happening now or within one hour.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending a Time Sensitive notification about an event scheduled for next week or a generic reminder.
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve .timeSensitive for immediate or near-term events; use .active for future or recurring events.
rules.quote: To help people understand the benefits of letting Time Sensitive notifications break through a Focus or scheduled delivery, make sure the notification is about an event that's happening now or will happen within an hour.

rules.heading: Sending marketing notifications
rules.rule: Never send marketing or promotional notifications without explicit user permission.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending unsolicited promotional notifications to all users without opt-in consent.
rules.fix_uikit: Present an alert or modal requesting explicit permission before sending marketing notifications.
rules.quote: Don't use notifications to send marketing or promotional content unless people explicitly agree to receive such information.

rules.heading: Sending marketing notifications
rules.rule: Never use Time Sensitive interruption level for marketing or promotional notifications.
rules.anti_pattern: Setting interruption level to .timeSensitive for a promotional offer or marketing message.
rules.fix_uikit: Use .passive or .active for marketing notifications; never use .timeSensitive or .critical.
rules.quote: Never use the Time Sensitive interruption level to send a marketing notification.

rules.heading: Sending marketing notifications
rules.rule: Provide in-app settings screen allowing users to manage notification preferences.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting notification permission but offering no in-app way to disable or customize notifications.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement a settings screen in your app that mirrors system notification permissions and allows opt-out.
rules.quote: Make sure people can manage their notification settings within your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Make maps interactive; enable zoom, pan, and standard gestures users expect.
rules.fix_swiftui: Map().interactionModes([.pan, .zoom])
rules.fix_uikit: mapView.isZoomEnabled = true; mapView.isScrollEnabled = true
rules.quote: In general, make your map interactive.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Choose map emphasis style (default or muted) based on app content density and visual alignment needs.
rules.anti_pattern:
let config = MKStandardMapConfiguration()
// No emphasis style specified; unclear intent
rules.fix_swiftui: Map(position: .constant(.region(region))).mapStyle(.standard(emphasis: .muted))
rules.fix_uikit: let config = MKStandardMapConfiguration(emphasisStyle: .muted); mapView.preferredConfiguration = config
rules.quote: Pick a map emphasis style that suits the needs of your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer search combined with category filters to help users find places efficiently.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Map with no search or filtering capability
Map()
rules.fix_swiftui: Map().searchable(text: $searchText, prompt: "Find stores")
rules.fix_uikit: let searchBar = UISearchBar(); searchBar.delegate = self
rules.quote: Help people find places in your map.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use distinct styling (outline, color variation) to clearly identify selected map elements.
rules.anti_pattern:
annotationView.isSelected = true
// No visual change; selection state unclear
rules.fix_swiftui: Annotation("Place", coordinate: coordinate).tint(.blue)
rules.fix_uikit: annotationView.layer.borderColor = UIColor.systemBlue.cgColor; annotationView.layer.borderWidth = 2.0
rules.quote: Clearly identify elements that people select.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Cluster overlapping points of interest; expand clusters progressively as users zoom in.
rules.fix_swiftui: Map(position: $position) { ForEach(places) { Annotation($0.name, coordinate: $0.coordinate).tag($0.id) } }
rules.fix_uikit: annotationView.clusteringIdentifier = "cluster"
rules.quote: Cluster overlapping points of interest to improve map legibility.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep Apple logo and legal link visible; use 7pt side padding, 10pt top/bottom; avoid covering permanently.
rules.fix_swiftui: Map().safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { CustomFooter().padding(.horizontal, 7).padding(.vertical, 10) }
rules.fix_uikit: mapView.layoutMargins = UIEdgeInsets(top: 0, left: 7, bottom: 10, right: 7)
rules.quote: Help people see the Apple logo and legal link.

rules.heading: Custom information
rules.rule: Use annotations matching app visual style; customize tint color and icon (2–3 characters or image).
rules.anti_pattern:
let annotationView = MKAnnotationView()
// Uses default red tint; doesn't match app branding
rules.fix_swiftui: Annotation("🏪", coordinate: coordinate).tint(.blue)
rules.fix_uikit: annotationView.tintColor = .systemBlue; annotationView.image = UIImage(systemName: "mappin.circle.fill")
rules.quote: Use annotations that match the visual style of your app.

rules.heading: Custom information
rules.rule: Make standard map features (POI, territories, physical features) independently selectable with custom info.
rules.fix_swiftui: Map().mapFeatureSelectionAccessory { feature in VStack { Text(feature.title ?? ""); Text(feature.subtitle ?? "") } }
rules.fix_uikit: func mapView(_ mapView: MKMapView, viewFor annotation: MKAnnotation) -> MKAnnotationView? { return customView }
rules.quote: If you want to display custom information that's related to standard map features, consider making them independently selectable.

rules.heading: Custom information
rules.rule: Use overlays to define map areas; choose level (above roads or above labels) based on content abstraction needs.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Overlay placement unclear; may obscure critical map features
let overlay = MKPolygon(coordinates: coords, count: coords.count)
rules.fix_swiftui: Map() { MapPolyline(coordinates: coords).stroke(.blue, lineWidth: 2) }
rules.fix_uikit: let overlay = MKPolygon(coordinates: &coords, count: coords.count); mapView.addOverlay(overlay, level: .aboveRoads)
rules.quote: Use overlays to define map areas with a specific relationship to your content.

rules.heading: Custom information
rules.rule: Ensure sufficient contrast between custom controls and map; use stroke, shadow, or blend modes.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Search") { }.foregroundStyle(.white).background(.black.opacity(0.6)).clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 8)).shadow(radius: 2)
rules.fix_uikit: button.layer.borderColor = UIColor.black.cgColor; button.layer.borderWidth = 1.0; button.layer.shadowOpacity = 0.5
rules.quote: Make sure there's enough contrast between custom controls and the map.

rules.heading: Displaying place cards in a map
rules.citation: maps.md › Displaying place cards in a map
rules.rule: Choose place card style (automatic, callout, caption, sheet) matching map size and content context.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Always use full callout; wastes space on small maps
let style = MapItemDetailSelectionAccessoryStyle.callout(.full)
rules.fix_swiftui: Map().mapItemDetailSelectionAccessory(.automatic)
rules.fix_uikit: annotationView.detailCalloutAccessoryView = MKStandardMapConfiguration.SelectionAccessory.automatic
rules.quote: Consider your map presentation when choosing a style.

rules.heading: Displaying place cards in a map
rules.citation: maps.md › Displaying place cards in a map
rules.rule: Keep selected location visible on map when displaying place card; use offset to point to location.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Place card covers the selected location
placeCard.frame = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 300, height: 400)
rules.fix_swiftui: Map().mapItemDetailSelectionAccessory(.callout)
rules.fix_uikit: annotationView.centerOffset = CGPoint(x: 0, y: -50)
rules.quote: Keep the location on your map visible when displaying a place card.

rules.heading: Adding place cards outside of a map
rules.citation: maps.md › Adding place cards outside of a map
rules.rule: When displaying place card outside map, include embedded map in card; set displaysMap to true.
rules.fix_swiftui: .mapItemDetailSheet(item: $selectedPlace, displaysMap: true)
rules.fix_uikit:
let detail = MKMapItemDetailViewController(mapItem: item, displaysMap: true)
present(detail, animated: true)
rules.quote: If you don't display a place card directly within a map view, you must include a map in the place card.

rules.heading: Indoor maps
rules.rule: Adjust map detail by zoom level; show large areas always, progressively reveal details when zoomed in.
rules.quote: Adjust map detail based on the zoom level.

rules.heading: Indoor maps
rules.rule: Offer floor picker for multi-level venues; use concise floor numbers rather than names.
rules.anti_pattern:
// No floor picker; users cannot navigate between levels
Map()
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Floor", selection: $selectedFloor) { ForEach(1...5, id: \.self) { Text("\($0)").tag($0) } }
rules.fix_uikit: let segmented = UISegmentedControl(items: ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"])
rules.quote: Offer a floor picker if your venue includes multiple levels.

rules.heading: Liquid Glass
rules.rule: Use Liquid Glass only for controls and navigation layers, never in the content layer.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use standard materials for content-layer elements; reserve .glass() for tab bars, sidebars, and navigation-only components.
rules.quote: Don't use Liquid Glass in the content layer.

rules.heading: Liquid Glass
rules.rule: Apply Liquid Glass effects sparingly to custom controls; limit to most important functional elements.
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply .glass() only to primary interactive elements; use standard materials for secondary or decorative custom controls.
rules.quote: If you apply Liquid Glass effects to a custom control, do so sparingly.

rules.heading: Liquid Glass
rules.rule: Use clear Liquid Glass variant only for components over visually rich backgrounds like photos or videos.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Glass.regular for plain backgrounds; reserve Glass.clear for media-rich backgrounds to maintain immersion.
rules.quote: Only use clear Liquid Glass for components that appear over visually rich backgrounds.

rules.heading: Liquid Glass
rules.rule: Add 35% opacity dark dimming layer behind clear Liquid Glass over bright content for legibility.
rules.fix_swiftui: ZStack { Image("brightPhoto"); Color.black.opacity(0.35); Button("Play").glass(.clear) }
rules.quote: If the underlying content is bright, consider adding a dark dimming layer of 35% opacity.

rules.heading: Standard materials
rules.rule: Choose materials and effects by semantic meaning and use case, not by apparent color.
rules.anti_pattern: let blurEffect = UIBlurEffect(style: .light) // Selected for color appearance, not semantics
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .material(.thin) or .material(.regular) based on content hierarchy and contrast needs, not visual appearance.
rules.fix_uikit: Select UIBlurEffect.Style based on semantic context (e.g., .systemMaterial for standard content separation).
rules.quote: Avoid selecting a material or effect based on the apparent color it imparts to your interface, because system settings can change its appearance and behavior.

rules.heading: Standard materials
rules.rule: Always use system-defined vibrant colors on top of materials to ensure legibility across contexts.
rules.anti_pattern:
Text("Label")
  .foregroundColor(.black) // Custom color, not vibrant
  .background(Material.thin)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").foregroundStyle(.primary).background(.thinMaterial)
rules.fix_uikit: let vibrancy = UIVibrancyEffect(blurEffect: UIBlurEffect(style: .systemMaterial)); label.effect = vibrancy
rules.quote: When you use system-defined vibrant colors, you don't need to worry about colors seeming too dark, bright, saturated, or low contrast in different contexts.

rules.heading: Standard materials
rules.rule: Use thicker, more opaque materials for text and fine-featured elements; thinner for context retention.
rules.anti_pattern:
Text("Important Label")
  .background(Material.ultraThin) // Too translucent for fine text
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Important Label").background(.regularMaterial)
rules.fix_uikit: let blur = UIBlurEffect(style: .systemMaterial); blurView.effect = blur
rules.quote: Thicker materials, which are more opaque, can provide better contrast for text and other elements with fine features.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Avoid quaternaryLabel vibrancy on ultraThin and thin materials due to insufficient contrast.
rules.anti_pattern:
Text("Tertiary")
  .foregroundStyle(.quaternary)
  .background(Material.thin)
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .tertiaryLabel or .secondaryLabel on thin/ultraThin materials; reserve .quaternaryLabel for regular/thick.
rules.fix_uikit: Apply UIVibrancyEffectStyle.quaternaryLabel only with UIBlurEffect(style: .systemMaterial) or thicker.
rules.quote: In general, avoid using quaternary on top of the thin and ultraThin materials, because the contrast is too low.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Test vibrancy in custom macOS views across varied contexts to confirm it enhances appearance and communication.
rules.fix_uikit: Test NSVisualEffectView with vibrancy enabled in System Preferences light/dark modes and accessibility settings.
rules.quote: Test your interface in a variety of contexts to discover when vibrancy enhances the appearance and improves communication.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Choose macOS background blending mode (behind window or within window) to complement interface design.
rules.anti_pattern:
let effectView = NSVisualEffectView()
effectView.blendingMode = .withinWindow // Default without considering design intent
rules.fix_uikit: Explicitly set NSVisualEffectView.blendingMode to .behindWindow or .withinWindow based on layering strategy.
rules.quote: Choose a background blending mode that complements your interface design.

rules.heading: Labels
rules.rule: Write menu item labels using verbs or verb phrases that clearly describe the action.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "Settings", handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "View Settings", handler: { _ in })
rules.quote: In general, label a menu item that initiates an action using a verb or verb phrase that describes the action, such as View, Close, or Select.

rules.heading: Labels
rules.rule: Use title-style capitalization for menu item labels to maintain platform consistency.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "view settings", handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "View Settings", handler: { _ in })
rules.quote: To be consistent with platform experiences, use title-style capitalization.

rules.heading: Labels
rules.rule: Remove articles (a, an, the) from menu item labels to save space.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "View the Settings", handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "View Settings", handler: { _ in })
rules.quote: Remove articles like a, an, and the from menu-item labels to save space.

rules.heading: Labels
rules.rule: Append ellipsis (…) to menu item labels when the action requires additional information or choices.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "Export", handler: { _ in showExportDialog() })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Export…", handler: { _ in showExportDialog() })
rules.quote: Append an ellipsis to a menu item's label when the action requires more information before it can complete.

rules.heading: Labels
rules.rule: Show unavailable menu items as dimmed and non-interactive; keep menu open even if all items unavailable.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "Paste", attributes: .disabled, handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Paste", attributes: .disabled, handler: { _ in }) // menu remains open
rules.quote: Show people when a menu item is unavailable.

rules.heading: Icons
rules.rule: Use standard system icons for common actions like Share, Print, and Search.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "Share", image: UIImage(named: "customShare"), handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "square.and.arrow.up") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Share", image: UIImage(systemName: "square.and.arrow.up"), handler: { _ in })
rules.quote: The system provides standard icons to represent common actions like Share, Print, and Search.

rules.heading: Icons
rules.rule: Use menu item icons sparingly; only when they clearly represent the action or concept.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "Settings", image: UIImage(systemName: "star.fill"), handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Label("Settings", systemImage: "gear") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Settings", image: UIImage(systemName: "gear"), handler: { _ in })
rules.quote: Use menu item icons sparingly and with purpose.

rules.heading: Icons
rules.rule: Apply uniform visual treatment across menu items in the same group: all with icons or all without.
rules.anti_pattern: Group with Copy (icon), Paste (no icon), Delete (icon)
rules.quote: Apply a uniform visual treatment across menu items in the same group.

rules.heading: Organization
rules.rule: List important or frequently used menu items first to reduce scanning time.
rules.anti_pattern: UIMenu(children: [deleteAction, copyAction, pasteAction])
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(children: [pasteAction, copyAction, deleteAction])
rules.quote: Prefer listing important or frequently used menu items first.

rules.heading: Organization
rules.rule: Group logically related menu items together using separators to aid discoverability.
rules.anti_pattern: UIMenu(children: [copyAction, deleteAction, pasteAction])
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(children: [copyAction, pasteAction, UIMenu(options: .displayInline, children: [deleteAction])])
rules.quote: Consider grouping logically related items.

rules.heading: Organization
rules.rule: Keep logically related commands in the same group even if importance levels differ.
rules.anti_pattern: Separate Paste and Paste and Match Style into different groups
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(children: [pasteAction, pasteMatchStyleAction]) // same group
rules.quote: Prefer keeping all logically related commands in the same group, even if the commands don't all have the same importance.

rules.heading: Organization
rules.rule: Avoid excessively long menus; divide into separate menus or use submenus instead.
rules.anti_pattern: UIMenu(children: [action1, action2, ..., action20])
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(children: [submenu1, submenu2]) // or multiple menus
rules.quote: Be mindful of menu length.

rules.heading: Submenus
rules.rule: Use submenus sparingly; consider them when a term appears in more than two menu items.
rules.anti_pattern: UIMenu(children: [sortByDateAction, sortByScoreAction, sortByTimeAction])
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(title: "Sort by", children: [dateAction, scoreAction, timeAction])
rules.quote: Use submenus sparingly.

rules.heading: Submenus
rules.rule: Limit submenus to single level depth and approximately five items maximum.
rules.anti_pattern: UIMenu(children: [submenu1(children: [submenu2(children: [...])])])
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(children: [submenu1(children: [action1, action2, action3, action4, action5])])
rules.quote: Limit the depth and length of submenus.

rules.heading: Toggled items
rules.rule: Use changeable labels for toggled items to show current state (e.g., Show Map / Hide Map).
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "Map", handler: { _ in toggleMap() })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: isMapVisible ? "Hide Map" : "Show Map", handler: { _ in toggleMap() })
rules.quote: Consider using a changeable label that describes an item's current state.

rules.heading: Toggled items
rules.rule: Add verbs to toggled item labels if changeable labels alone are ambiguous.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "HDR On", handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Turn HDR On", handler: { _ in })
rules.quote: Include a verb if a changeable label isn't clear enough.

rules.heading: Toggled items
rules.rule: Use checkmarks to indicate currently active attributes in a list of toggled options.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAction(title: "Bold", handler: { _ in })
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Bold", state: isBold ? .on : .off, handler: { _ in })
rules.quote: Consider using a checkmark to show that an attribute is currently in effect.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use small or medium menu layouts to streamline choices; medium for three important actions.
rules.anti_pattern: UIMenu(preferredElementSize: .large, children: [action1, action2, action3])
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu(preferredElementSize: .medium, children: [scanAction, lockAction, pinAction])
rules.quote: Choose a small or medium menu layout when it can help streamline people's choices.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Present content modally only when it helps people focus or make choices affecting content or device.
rules.anti_pattern: Button { NavigationLink { ModalView() } } // Modal for trivial navigation without clear benefit
rules.fix_swiftui: .sheet(isPresented: $showModal) { ModalView() } // Only set showModal when action requires modal context
rules.fix_uikit: // Only call present() when modal task is necessary; use navigation for browsing
rules.quote: A modal experience takes people out of their current context and requires an action to dismiss, so it's important to use modality only when it helps people focus or make choices that affect their content or device.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep modal tasks simple, short, and streamlined to prevent users losing track of suspended context.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Modal with 5+ steps, nested NavigationStack, complex form
.sheet { NavigationStack { Form { /* many sections */ } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: .sheet { Form { /* single focused task, 1-3 steps */ } }
rules.fix_uikit: // Present modal with single, focused task; use navigation for multi-step flows outside modal
rules.quote: If a modal task is too complicated, people can lose track of the task they suspended when they entered the modal view, especially if the modal view obscures their previous context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid presenting hierarchies of views within a modal; provide single path and prevent mistaken dismiss buttons.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Modal with nested NavigationStack and multiple drill-down levels
.sheet { NavigationStack { List { NavigationLink { DetailView { NavigationLink { SubDetailView() } } } } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: .sheet { Form { /* single level, no nested navigation */ } }
rules.fix_uikit: // Present modal with flat structure; avoid nested UINavigationController inside modal
rules.quote: In particular, presenting a hierarchy of views within a modal task can make people forget how to retrace their steps.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use full-screen modal style for in-depth content or complex tasks to minimize distractions.
rules.anti_pattern: .sheet { VideoPlayerView() } // Video in sheet leaves parent visible, distracting
rules.fix_swiftui: .fullScreenCover(isPresented: $showVideo) { VideoPlayerView() }
rules.fix_uikit: vc.modalPresentationStyle = .fullScreen; present(vc, animated: true)
rules.quote: A modal experience that fills a window or the device display minimizes distractions, so it can work well for presenting videos, photos, or camera views, or to support a multistep task like marking up a document or editing a photo.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Always provide an obvious, platform-conventional way to dismiss a modal view.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Modal with no visible dismiss button or gesture support
.sheet(isPresented: $show) { VStack { Text("Content") } }
rules.fix_swiftui: .sheet(isPresented: $show) { VStack { HStack { Spacer(); Button("Done") { show = false } }; Text("Content") } }
rules.fix_uikit: // Add UIBarButtonItem with dismiss action in toolbar; support swipe-down gesture
rules.quote: Always give people an obvious way to dismiss a modal view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Confirm before closing a modal if dismissal could result in loss of user-generated content.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Modal form with unsaved changes, dismiss button closes without warning
Button("Cancel") { show = false }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Cancel") { showConfirmation = true }.confirmationDialog("Discard changes?", isPresented: $showConfirmation) { Button("Discard", role: .destructive) { show = false } }
rules.fix_uikit: // Present UIAlertController before dismissing if unsaved content exists
rules.quote: Regardless of whether people use a dismiss gesture or a button, if closing the view could result in the loss of user-generated content, be sure to explain the situation and give people ways to resolve it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide a clear title or descriptive text naming the modal view's task to help users maintain context.
rules.anti_pattern: .sheet(isPresented: $show) { VStack { Text("Enter data") } } // Vague task description
rules.fix_swiftui: .sheet(isPresented: $show) { VStack { Text("Add New Contact").font(.headline); Form { /* fields */ } } }
rules.fix_uikit: // Set UIViewController.title or add descriptive header to modal content
rules.quote: When you provide a title that names the modal view's task — or additional text that describes the task or provides guidance — you can help people keep their place in your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Dismiss a modal view before presenting another; never display multiple modals or alerts simultaneously.
rules.fix_swiftui: .sheet(isPresented: $show1) { Modal1() }
rules.fix_uikit: dismiss(animated: true) { self.present(nextVC, animated: true) }
rules.quote: Allowing multiple modal views to be visible at the same time tends to create visual clutter and can make your app seem scattered and disorganized.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Add motion purposefully to support experience; avoid gratuitous animation that distracts or causes discomfort.
rules.anti_pattern: withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 2.0)) { /* every state change */ } // excessive motion on frequent interactions
rules.fix_swiftui: Reserve animations for meaningful state transitions; use .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: isExpanded) only when semantically important.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIView.animate(withDuration:0.3) only for purposeful transitions; avoid animating every UI update.
rules.quote: Add motion purposefully, supporting the experience without overshadowing it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Make motion optional; never use animation as the sole way to communicate critical information.
rules.anti_pattern: if isSuccess { withAnimation { showCheckmark = true } } // only visual feedback, no haptics/audio
rules.fix_swiftui: Combine animation with haptics: withAnimation { showCheckmark = true }; try? hapticEngine.play(.success); also provide audio cue.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UINotificationFeedbackGenerator alongside UIView.animate; provide audio via AVAudioPlayer for critical feedback.
rules.quote: Make motion optional.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Supplement motion with haptics and audio to ensure information is accessible to all users.
rules.anti_pattern: withAnimation { showSuccess = true } // animation only, ignores accessibility settings
rules.fix_swiftui: @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) var reduceMotion; if !reduceMotion { withAnimation { ... } }; add haptics and audio.
rules.fix_uikit: Check UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled(); provide UINotificationFeedbackGenerator and audio alternatives.
rules.quote: To help everyone enjoy your app or game, supplement visual feedback by also using alternatives like haptics and audio to communicate.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Ensure feedback motion follows user gestures and expectations; avoid disorienting or counterintuitive animations.
rules.anti_pattern: // User slides down to reveal; dismiss by sliding left (gesture mismatch)
rules.fix_swiftui: Match animation direction to gesture: if dragAmount.height > 0 { dismiss with upward animation }.
rules.fix_uikit: Tie UIView.animate direction to UIPanGestureRecognizer direction; dismiss upward if revealed downward.
rules.quote: Strive for realistic feedback motion that follows people's gestures and expectations.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Keep feedback animations brief and precise to feel lightweight and convey information effectively.
rules.anti_pattern: withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 1.5)) { showSuccess = true } // too long, distracts from content
rules.fix_swiftui: withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) { showSuccess = true } // brief, precise timing
rules.fix_uikit: UIView.animate(withDuration: 0.3) { /* update */ } // keep under 400ms for feedback
rules.quote: Aim for brevity and precision in feedback animations.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Avoid animating frequent UI interactions; system already provides subtle animations for standard elements.
rules.anti_pattern: Button { action() }.buttonStyle(CustomAnimatedStyle()) // custom animation on every tap
rules.fix_swiftui: Use system button styles (.bordered, .filled) which include appropriate system animations.
rules.fix_uikit: Rely on UIButton's built-in highlight animation; avoid custom CABasicAnimation for standard interactions.
rules.quote: In apps, generally avoid adding motion to UI interactions that occur frequently.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Allow users to cancel motion; do not force them to wait for animations to complete.
rules.anti_pattern: withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 2.0)) { showModal = true } // user cannot dismiss until animation ends
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .transaction { $0.animation = nil } on user gesture to interrupt; allow immediate state change.
rules.fix_uikit: Call CATransaction.begin(); CATransaction.setCompletionBlock(nil); allow gesture to override animation.
rules.quote: Let people cancel motion.

rules.heading: Providing feedback
rules.rule: Use animated SF Symbols (v5+) where appropriate for visual feedback and consistency.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: "checkmark") // static symbol, no animation feedback
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "checkmark").symbolEffect(.bounce, options: .repeating) // animated feedback
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIImage(systemName:) with CABasicAnimation or newer symbol animation APIs.
rules.quote: Consider using animated symbols where it makes sense.

rules.heading: Leveraging platform capabilities
