rules.rule: Maintain 30–60 fps frame rate by default on each platform using appropriate graphics capabilities.
rules.anti_pattern: // Game renders at 120 fps on all devices, drains battery on older hardware
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Metal or SceneKit with platform-appropriate frame rate: preferredFramesPerSecond = 60 on standard devices.
rules.fix_uikit: Set MTKView.preferredFramesPerSecond = 60; use CADisplayLink with appropriate frame interval.
rules.quote: In most games, maintaining a consistent frame rate of 30 to 60 fps typically results in a smooth, visually appealing experience.

rules.heading: Leveraging platform capabilities
rules.rule: Let users customize game visual settings to optimize performance or battery life based on power availability.
rules.anti_pattern: // Game always runs at max graphics; no user control over quality settings
rules.fix_swiftui: Provide @State var powerMode: Bool; detect external power via ProcessInfo; offer graphics quality toggle.
rules.fix_uikit: Monitor UIDevice.current.batteryState; offer UISwitch to toggle between performance/battery-saver modes.
rules.quote: Let people customize the visual experience of your game to optimize performance or battery life.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Save and restore app context when users switch away, ensuring seamless continuation upon return.
rules.anti_pattern: func sceneWillResignActive(_ scene: UIScene) { /* no state saving */ }
rules.fix_swiftui: @Environment(\.scenePhase) var scenePhase; .onChange(of: scenePhase) { oldPhase, newPhase in if newPhase == .background { saveState() } }
rules.fix_uikit: func sceneWillResignActive(_ scene: UIScene) { saveAppState() } func sceneDidBecomeActive(_ scene: UIScene) { restoreAppState() }
rules.quote: Because you don't know when people will initiate multitasking, your app or game always needs to be prepared to save and restore their context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Pause games and media playback when users switch away; resume seamlessly when they return.
rules.anti_pattern: // Game continues running in background without pause
rules.fix_swiftui: .onChange(of: scenePhase) { _, newPhase in if newPhase == .background { pauseGame() } else if newPhase == .active { resumeGame() } }
rules.fix_uikit: func sceneWillResignActive(_ scene: UIScene) { pauseGameplay() }
rules.quote: Pause activities that require people's attention or active participation when they switch away.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Pause primary audio indefinitely on interruption; temporarily lower volume for brief interruptions like GPS notifications.
rules.anti_pattern: // Audio continues playing during incoming call without pause
rules.fix_uikit: AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setCategory(.playback, options: .duckOthers)
rules.quote: Pause audio indefinitely for primary audio interruptions, such as playing music, podcasts, or audiobooks.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Complete user-initiated background tasks (downloads, processing) before suspending, without requiring further input.
rules.anti_pattern: func sceneWillResignActive(_ scene: UIScene) { /* stops download immediately */ }
rules.fix_swiftui: .onChange(of: scenePhase) { _, newPhase in if newPhase == .background { continueBackgroundTask() } }
rules.fix_uikit: func sceneWillResignActive(_ scene: UIScene) { startBackgroundTask() }
rules.quote: When someone starts a task like downloading assets or processing a video file, they expect it to finish even if they switch away from your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Send notifications only for important or time-sensitive task completion; avoid notifying for routine secondary tasks.
rules.anti_pattern: UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request) // for every minor task completion
rules.fix_uikit: // Only notify for critical tasks: if isImportantTask { UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request) }
rules.quote: If people start an important or time-sensitive task in your app, and then switch away from it, they might appreciate receiving a notification when the task completes so they can switch back to your app and take the next step.

rules.heading: Phone (iOS)
rules.rule: Support Picture in Picture for video and FaceTime to enable concurrent app usage on iPhone.
rules.anti_pattern: // Video player does not implement AVPictureInPictureController
rules.fix_uikit: let pipController = AVPictureInPictureController(playerLayer: playerLayer); pipController?.delegate = self
rules.quote: On iPhone, multitasking lets people use FaceTime or watch a video in Picture in Picture while they also use a different app.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Support multiple open windows in the same app to allow users to view and interact with multiple app windows simultaneously.
rules.anti_pattern: // App only supports single window; no WindowGroup or multi-window support
rules.fix_swiftui: WindowGroup { ContentView() }
rules.fix_uikit: // Implement UIWindowSceneDelegate to support multiple windows
rules.quote: An individual app can also support multiple open windows, which lets people view and interact with more than one window in the same app at one time.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Adapt gracefully to different screen sizes when app opens in windowed mode on iPad.
rules.anti_pattern: // Layout hardcoded for full-screen iPad; breaks in windowed mode
rules.fix_uikit: // Use Auto Layout or UITraitCollection to respond to size changes
rules.quote: To help your app respond correctly when people open it while windowed, make sure it adapts gracefully to different screen sizes.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Do not attempt to control multitasking configurations or detect user-chosen multitasking modes.
rules.anti_pattern: // App tries to detect or enforce split-screen configuration
rules.fix_uikit: // Remove any code attempting to query or control multitasking state
rules.quote: Apps don't control multitasking configurations or receive any indication of the ones that people choose.

rules.heading: In-app tag reading
rules.rule: Use 'scan' and 'hold near' instead of 'tap' and 'touch' in NFC scanning instructions.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Tap your phone to the product to scan it.")
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Hold your iPhone near the product to scan it.")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Hold your iPhone near the product to scan it."
rules.quote: Use terms like *scan* and *hold near* instead of *tap* and *touch* when asking people to scan objects.

rules.heading: In-app tag reading
rules.rule: Avoid technical NFC terminology; use friendly, conversational terms instead.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Scan the NFC tag using Core NFC.")
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Scan the product.")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Scan the product."
rules.quote: To make it approachable, avoid referring to technical, developer-oriented terms like *NFC*, *Core NFC*, *Near-field communication*, and *tag*.

rules.heading: In-app tag reading
rules.rule: Provide complete sentence instructional text in sentence case with ending punctuation for scanning sheets.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("hold your iphone near the object")
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Hold your iPhone near the product to learn more about it.")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Hold your iPhone near the product to learn more about it."
rules.quote: Provide a complete sentence, in sentence case, with ending punctuation.

rules.heading: In-app tag reading
rules.rule: Identify the specific object to scan and revise text for subsequent scans.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Hold your iPhone near the object to scan.")
rules.fix_swiftui: Text(firstScan ? "Hold your iPhone near the product to learn more about it." : "Now hold your iPhone near another product.")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = firstScan ? "Hold your iPhone near the product to learn more about it." : "Now hold your iPhone near another product."
rules.quote: Identify the object to scan, and revise the text appropriately for subsequent scans.

rules.heading: Background tag reading
rules.rule: Provide in-app tag scanning for devices that don't support background tag reading.
rules.anti_pattern: // App only relies on background tag reading without in-app fallback
rules.fix_swiftui: // Implement NFCReaderSession for in-app scanning as fallback for unsupported devices
rules.fix_uikit: // Implement NFCReaderSession for in-app scanning as fallback for unsupported devices
rules.quote: Your app must still provide an in-app way to scan tags, for people with devices that don't support background tag reading.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Use distinct communication notification interface with prominent contact images and group names instead of app icon.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying app icon uniformly for both direct communication (calls, messages) and noncommunication notifications.
rules.quote: A notification related to direct communication — like a phone call or message — can provide an interface that's distinct from noncommunication notifications, featuring prominent contact images (or avatars) and group names instead of the app icon.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide concise, informative notifications with valuable information succinctly to respect user attention.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending verbose, low-value notifications that don't provide quick updates or actionable information.
rules.quote: Provide concise, informative notifications. People turn on notifications to get quick updates, so you want to provide valuable information succinctly.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never send multiple notifications for the same event even if user hasn't responded.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending repeated notifications for the same unaddressed event, filling Notification Center and causing users to disable app notifications.
rules.quote: Avoid sending multiple notifications for the same thing, even if someone hasn't responded.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid notifications that instruct users to perform specific tasks; use notification actions for simple tasks instead.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending notification with text like 'Open app and tap Settings to enable feature' without providing actionable notification buttons.
rules.quote: Avoid sending a notification that tells people to perform specific tasks within your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use alerts, not notifications, to display error messages to avoid user confusion.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying error messages via UNUserNotificationCenter instead of UIAlertController or SwiftUI Alert.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .alert() modifier for error presentation.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIAlertController with preferredStyle .alert for errors.
rules.quote: Use an alert — not a notification — to display an error message.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Handle foreground notifications gracefully by incrementing badges or subtly inserting data instead of displaying notifications.
rules.anti_pattern: Presenting full notification UI when app is in foreground, or ignoring foreground notification data entirely.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement userNotificationCenter(_:willPresent:withCompletionHandler:) to handle foreground notifications.
rules.quote: Handle notifications gracefully when your app is in the foreground. Your app's notifications don't appear when your app is in the front, but your app still receives the information.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never include sensitive, personal, or confidential information in notifications.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending notifications with full credit card numbers, passwords, medical data, or other private information.
rules.quote: Avoid including sensitive, personal, or confidential information in a notification.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Create short, contextual titles readable at a glance; use title-case capitalization with no ending punctuation.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing verbose titles like 'You have received a new notification from your application.' or 'new document.' with lowercase or punctuation.
rules.quote: Create a short title if it provides context for the notification content. Prefer brief titles that people can read at a glance, especially on Apple Watch, where space is limited.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Write succinct, complete notification content in sentence case with proper punctuation; avoid truncation.
rules.anti_pattern: Sending truncated messages like 'New message from John: Hey, how are you doing today and...' or incomplete sentences.
rules.quote: Write succinct, easy-to-read notification content. Use complete sentences, sentence case, and proper punctuation, and don't truncate your message — the system does this automatically when necessary.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Provide generic descriptive body text for hidden preview scenarios without revealing sensitive details.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing full message content in hiddenPreviewsBodyPlaceholder or generic text like 'New notification' without context.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UNNotificationCategory hiddenPreviewsBodyPlaceholder to 'Friend request', 'New comment', 'Reminder', or 'Shipment'.
rules.quote: Provide generically descriptive text to display when notification previews aren't available. In Settings, people can choose to hide notification previews for all apps.

rules.heading: Notification actions
rules.rule: Provide up to four beneficial actions that enable common, time-saving tasks without opening the app.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing eight action buttons or actions that don't save time, like 'View Details' that requires opening the app anyway.
rules.fix_uikit: Define UNNotificationAction objects and add to UNNotificationCategory with maxActions ≤ 4.
rules.quote: Provide beneficial actions that make sense in the context of your notification. Prefer actions that let people perform common, time-saving tasks that eliminate the need to open your app.

rules.heading: Notification actions
rules.rule: Prefer nondestructive actions; provide sufficient context for destructive actions to prevent unintended consequences.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing 'Delete' action without confirmation or context, or making destructive action the default.
rules.fix_uikit: Mark destructive UNNotificationAction with options: .destructive; ensure user has context before deletion.
rules.quote: Prefer nondestructive actions. If you must provide a destructive action, make sure people have enough context to avoid unintended consequences.

rules.heading: Notification actions
rules.rule: Provide a simple, recognizable SF Symbol icon for each notification action to reinforce meaning.
rules.anti_pattern: Using custom raster images or ambiguous icons for notification actions, or omitting icons entirely.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UNNotificationAction icon to SFSymbol via UNNotificationActionIcon(systemImageName:).
rules.quote: Provide a simple, recognizable interface icon for each notification action. An interface icon reinforces an action's meaning, helping people instantly understand what it does.

rules.heading: Badging
rules.rule: Never rely on badging as the only method to communicate essential information.
rules.anti_pattern: Using only badge count to indicate critical alerts, with no alternative UI in the app.
rules.quote: Make sure badging isn't the only method you use to communicate essential information. People can turn off badging for your app, so if you rely on it to show people when there's important information, people can miss the message.

rules.heading: Badging
rules.rule: Keep badges up to date by clearing them as soon as users view corresponding notifications.
rules.anti_pattern: Leaving badge count at 5 after user has read all 5 notifications, or never clearing badges.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UIApplication.shared.applicationIconBadgeNumber = 0 after user opens and views notifications.
rules.quote: Keep badges up to date. Update your app's badge as soon as people open the corresponding notifications.

rules.heading: Badging
rules.rule: Never create custom images or components that mimic badge appearance or behavior.
rules.anti_pattern: Drawing a custom red oval with number in corner of app icon, or creating a fake badge UI element.
rules.fix_uikit: Use only UIApplication.shared.applicationIconBadgeNumber; do not create custom badge-like UI.
rules.quote: Avoid creating a custom image or component that mimics the appearance or behavior of a badge.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Relate help directly to the precise action or task people are doing right now.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying generic help content unrelated to the user's current context or action.
rules.quote: In general, directly relate the help you provide to the precise action or task people are doing right now and make it easy for people to dismiss or avoid the help if they don't need it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use language and images consistent with the platform and current context.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing tvOS game controller images in a Siri Remote experience, or writing 'click' on iPhone instead of 'tap'.
rules.quote: Always make sure guidance is appropriate for the current context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid explaining how standard components work; describe only the specific action in your app.
rules.anti_pattern: Including lengthy explanations of how a standard UIButton or SwiftUI Button component works in general.
rules.quote: Avoid bloating your help content by explaining how standard components or patterns work.

rules.heading: Creating tips
rules.rule: Use tips only for simple features completable in three or fewer actions.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a tip for a feature requiring five steps or a complex multi-step workflow.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use TipKit with eligibility rules to gate tips to simple, discoverable features.
rules.quote: If a feature requires more than three actions, it's probably too complicated for a tip.

rules.heading: Creating tips
rules.rule: Keep tips to one or two sentences with direct, action-oriented language.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing a tip with three paragraphs of promotional content or unrelated feature descriptions.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use TipKit with concise, imperative copy: 'Tap the star to add to favorites.'
rules.quote: Keep your tips to one or two sentences and avoid including content that's promotional or related to a different feature or user flow.

rules.heading: Creating tips
rules.rule: Define eligibility rules to ensure tips reach only the intended audience.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying a tip about a feature to users who have already used it multiple times.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use TipKit parameter-based or event-based eligibility rules to gate tip display.
rules.quote: Use parameter-based or event-based eligibility rules to control when a tip appears, and only display a tip if someone might benefit from its use.

rules.heading: Creating tips
rules.rule: Include a filled symbol or image associated with the feature in the tip.
rules.anti_pattern: Omitting a visual indicator or using an unfilled variant when a recognizable symbol exists.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Image(systemName: "star.fill") in TipKit content to reinforce feature association.
rules.quote: If there's an image or symbol that people associate with the feature, consider including it in the tip, and prefer the filled variant.

rules.heading: Creating tips
rules.rule: Avoid repeating the same image in both the tip and the UI element it connects to.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing a star icon in both the tip and the adjacent favorite button.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use a different visual or omit the image from the tip if it directly connects to a UI element.
rules.quote: If the feature is represented by an image that the tip connects to directly, avoid repeating the same image in both the tip and the UI.

rules.heading: Creating tips
rules.rule: Use buttons in tips to direct people to settings or additional resources.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a tip with no actionable button when the feature has customizable settings.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add a Button action in TipKit to navigate to settings or a setup flow.
rules.quote: If your feature has settings people can customize, or you want to redirect people to an area where they can learn more about a feature, consider adding a button.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Describe only the specific control the tooltip is attached to, not nearby controls.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing a tooltip that explains both the current button and adjacent controls.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .help("Restore default settings") on a single control only.
rules.fix_uikit: Set toolTip on individual NSView/NSButton instances with focused descriptions.
rules.quote: When people want to know how to use a specific control, they don't want to learn how to use nearby controls or how to perform a larger task.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Begin tooltip descriptions with a verb explaining the action the control initiates.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing a tooltip as 'Default settings' instead of 'Restore default settings'.
rules.fix_swiftui: .help("Add or remove a language from the list")
rules.fix_uikit: toolTip = "Restore default settings"
rules.quote: Explain the action or task the control initiates.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Avoid repeating the control's name in its tooltip.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing a tooltip for a 'Save' button as 'Save: Save your document'.
rules.fix_swiftui: .help("Save your document")
rules.fix_uikit: toolTip = "Save your document"
rules.quote: In general, avoid repeating a control's name in its tooltip.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Limit tooltip content to 60–75 characters; use sentence fragments and omit articles.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing a tooltip with 150+ characters or complete sentences with articles: 'This button will save the document to your computer.'
rules.fix_swiftui: .help("Save document")
rules.fix_uikit: toolTip = "Save document"
rules.quote: As much as possible, limit tooltip content to a maximum of 60 to 75 characters (note that localization often changes the length of text).

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Use sentence case in tooltips; omit ending punctuation unless required by style.
rules.anti_pattern: Writing a tooltip in ALL CAPS or Title Case: 'SAVE YOUR DOCUMENT.' or 'Save Your Document.'
rules.fix_swiftui: .help("Save your document")
rules.fix_uikit: toolTip = "Save your document"
rules.quote: Use sentence case.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS, visionOS)
rules.rule: Provide context-sensitive tooltips that vary based on the control's state.
rules.anti_pattern: Using the same static tooltip text for a button regardless of its enabled/disabled state.
rules.fix_swiftui: Conditionally bind .help() based on state: .help(isEnabled ? "Save document" : "Enable to save")
rules.fix_uikit: Update toolTip dynamically when control state changes.
rules.quote: Consider offering context-sensitive tooltips.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Design onboarding with interactive tasks rather than passive instructional material.
rules.anti_pattern: struct OnboardingView: View { var body: some View { VStack { Text("Swipe to navigate"); Text("Tap to select"); Text("Long-press to delete") } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: struct OnboardingView: View { @State var isInteracting = false; var body: some View { VStack { Text("Try swiping now"); Rectangle().onTapGesture { isInteracting = true } } } }
rules.fix_uikit: Let users perform the actual action (e.g., tap a button, swipe a view) during onboarding rather than showing static text descriptions.
rules.quote: People tend to grasp and retain information better when they can actually perform the task they're learning about instead of just viewing instructional material.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Integrate context-specific tips near relevant interface areas instead of a single monolithic onboarding flow.
rules.anti_pattern: struct OnboardingView: View { var body: some View { VStack { Text("Feature 1"); Text("Feature 2"); Text("Feature 3"); Text("Feature 4") } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: import TipKit; struct FeatureView: View { var tip = MyTip(); var body: some View { Button("Action") { }.popoverTip(tip) } }
rules.fix_uikit: Display instructional content contextually near the relevant UI element rather than in a separate onboarding screen.
rules.quote: Integrating contextually relevant tips into your experience can help people learn about their current task while they make progress in your app or game.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep prerequisite onboarding brief and entertaining to avoid overwhelming users.
rules.anti_pattern: // Onboarding screen with 10+ text blocks explaining every feature in detail
rules.fix_swiftui: // Limit onboarding to 3–5 key screens with minimal text and interactive elements
rules.fix_uikit: Design onboarding to be completable in under 2 minutes with clear, concise messaging.
rules.quote: When onboarding is quick and entertaining, people are more likely to complete it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Make tutorials optional and accessible later via help, account, or settings.
rules.anti_pattern: // Force tutorial on every app launch; no way to access it later
rules.fix_swiftui: struct SettingsView: View { var body: some View { NavigationLink("View Tutorial") { TutorialView() } } }
rules.fix_uikit: Add a "Help" or "Tutorial" button in settings that users can tap to re-access onboarding.
rules.quote: If you let people skip the tutorial when they first launch your app or game, don't present it again on subsequent launches, but make sure it's easy for people to find if they want to view it later.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Focus onboarding on app-specific features, not system or device usage.
rules.anti_pattern: // Onboarding teaches how to use iOS gestures, Face ID, or system settings
rules.fix_swiftui: // Onboarding teaches app-specific workflows and features only
rules.fix_uikit: Assume users understand their device; teach only your app's unique functionality.
rules.quote: People enter your onboarding flow to learn about your app or game; they don't need to learn how to use the system or the device.

rules.heading: Additional content
rules.rule: Display splash screens briefly with clear, succinct graphics without delaying user interaction.
rules.anti_pattern: // Splash screen displayed for 5+ seconds with no visual feedback
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("splash").onAppear { DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1.5) { isDismissed = true } }
rules.fix_uikit: let splash = UIImageView(image: UIImage(named: "splash")); DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1.5) { splash.removeFromSuperview() }
rules.quote: Aim to display your splash screen just long enough for people to absorb the information at a glance without feeling that it's delaying their experience.

rules.heading: Additional content
rules.rule: Bundle sufficient media and content to prevent download delays before users can interact.
rules.anti_pattern: // App launches but requires 50 MB download before any feature is usable
rules.fix_swiftui: // Include core content in app bundle; defer non-essential assets to background download
rules.fix_uikit: Ensure users can start using the app immediately after launch without waiting for downloads.
rules.quote: People want to start using your app or game immediately after first launching it, whether they participate in an onboarding flow or skip it.

rules.heading: Additional content
rules.rule: Avoid displaying licensing details in onboarding; let App Store show agreements before download.
rules.anti_pattern: // Onboarding screen with full terms of service and privacy policy text
rules.fix_swiftui: // If required, integrate legal text minimally; rely on App Store for primary display
rules.fix_uikit: Display only essential legal notices; direct users to App Store for full agreements.
rules.quote: Let the App Store display agreements and disclaimers so people can read them before downloading your app or game.

rules.heading: Additional requests
rules.rule: Defer nonessential setup and customization; provide sensible defaults for immediate use.
rules.anti_pattern: // Onboarding requires users to configure 10+ settings before accessing app
rules.fix_swiftui: // Provide defaults; allow customization in settings after onboarding
rules.fix_uikit: Let users start immediately with preset configurations; move optional setup to preferences.
rules.quote: Provide reasonable default settings so most people can immediately start interacting with your app or game without performing additional configuration.

rules.heading: Additional requests
rules.rule: Integrate essential permission requests into onboarding to explain necessity and benefits.
rules.anti_pattern: // Permission request appears mid-feature with no context about why it's needed
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Allow Location") { CLLocationManager().requestWhenInUseAuthorization() }
rules.fix_uikit: CLLocationManager().requestWhenInUseAuthorization()
rules.quote: In this scenario, making the request during your onboarding flow gives you the opportunity to show people why your app or game needs their permission and the benefits of granting it.

rules.heading: Additional requests
rules.rule: Defer rating and purchase prompts until after users engage with the app.
rules.anti_pattern: // Rating prompt appears immediately after onboarding completes
rules.fix_swiftui: // Show rating prompt only after user completes a meaningful action or uses app for 5+ minutes
rules.fix_uikit: Delay review and purchase requests until users have demonstrated engagement.
rules.quote: People can be more likely to respond positively to such requests when they've had a chance to become engaged with your app or game.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use outline views only for hierarchical data; use tables for non-hierarchical data.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView displaying flat, non-hierarchical data without parent-child relationships.
rules.quote: Use a table instead of an outline view to present data that's not hierarchical.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Expose data hierarchy only in the first column; other columns display supplementary attributes.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView with disclosure triangles or hierarchy indicators in multiple columns.
rules.quote: Expose data hierarchy in the first column only.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use descriptive, title-case noun phrases as column headings without trailing colons.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTableColumn with headings like 'Name:', 'size', or 'modification date' (lowercase).
rules.quote: Use nouns or short noun phrases with title-style capitalization and no punctuation; in particular, avoid adding a trailing colon.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Always provide column headings in multi-column outline views; use labels for single-column views.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView with multiple columns but no headerView or missing column titles.
rules.quote: Always provide column headings in a multi-column outline view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Implement clickable column headings to sort outline view data in ascending or descending order.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView with non-interactive column headers; no sort functionality on header click.
rules.quote: Consider letting people click column headings to sort an outline view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow users to resize columns to accommodate varying data widths.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView with fixed column widths or resizingMask set to NSTableColumnNoResizing.
rules.quote: Let people resize columns.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support single-click disclosure triangle expansion and Option-click for recursive expansion.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView where disclosure triangles only respond to double-click or lack Option-click recursion.
rules.quote: Make it easy for people to expand or collapse nested containers.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Persist and restore outline view expansion state across sessions.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView that collapses all items on app relaunch; no saved expansion state.
rules.quote: Retain people's expansion choices.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Consider alternating row colors in multi-column outline views to aid row tracking.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView with uniform row background colors across all rows.
rules.quote: Consider using alternating row colors in multi-column outline views.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support single-click editing of outline view cells when semantically appropriate.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView cells requiring double-click to edit; no single-click edit mode.
rules.quote: In an editable outline view cell, people expect to be able to single-click a cell to edit its contents.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use centered ellipsis truncation instead of clipping to preserve text distinctiveness.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView cells with lineBreakMode set to NSLineBreakByClipping or NSLineBreakByTruncatingTail.
rules.quote: Consider using a centered ellipsis to truncate cell text instead of clipping it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include a search field in the toolbar for lengthy outline views to enable quick value lookup.
rules.anti_pattern: NSOutlineView with many rows but no search field or filtering mechanism.
rules.quote: Consider offering a search field to help people find values quickly in a lengthy outline view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use page controls only for ordered, flat page sequences; use sidebar or split view for hierarchical navigation.
rules.anti_pattern: Using UIPageControl to represent hierarchical categories or non-sequential content relationships.
rules.fix_uikit: Replace UIPageControl with UINavigationController, UISplitViewController, or custom sidebar for complex navigation.
rules.quote: Page controls don't represent hierarchical or nonsequential page relationships.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Center page control horizontally and position it near the bottom of the view.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing UIPageControl in top-right corner or off-center alignment.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UIPageControl.center.x = view.center.x and position with bottom constraint ~16-20pt from safe area.
rules.quote: Center a page control at the bottom of the view or window.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit page controls to approximately 10 or fewer dots; use grid or alternative layout for more pages.
rules.anti_pattern: Setting UIPageControl.numberOfPages = 25 without alternative navigation.
rules.fix_uikit: If numberOfPages > 10, replace with UICollectionView grid or custom paging layout.
rules.quote: More than about 10 dots are hard to count at a glance.

rules.heading: Customizing indicators
rules.rule: Design custom indicator images as simple, clear symbols without complex shapes, negative space, text, or inner lines.
rules.anti_pattern: Using detailed photographic icons or multi-color glyphs with inner detail as page control indicators.
rules.fix_uikit: Use SF Symbols (weight: regular, size: small) or minimal custom icons; set via preferredIndicatorImage and setIndicatorImage(_:forPage:).
rules.quote: Make sure custom indicator images are simple and clear.

rules.heading: Customizing indicators
rules.rule: Customize default indicator image only when it meaningfully enhances the page control's semantic purpose.
rules.anti_pattern: Changing preferredIndicatorImage to a decorative symbol unrelated to page content (e.g., star for generic pages).
rules.fix_uikit: Set preferredIndicatorImage only if all pages share a common semantic property (e.g., bookmark.fill for bookmark pages).
rules.quote: Customize the default indicator image only when it enhances the page control's overall meaning.

rules.heading: Customizing indicators
rules.rule: Use at most two distinct indicator images in a single page control to avoid cognitive overload.
rules.anti_pattern: Calling setIndicatorImage(_:forPage:) with 5+ unique images across different pages.
rules.fix_uikit: Limit to one default image (preferredIndicatorImage) and one special image for a single distinguished page (e.g., current location).
rules.quote: Avoid using more than two different indicator images in a page control.

rules.heading: Customizing indicators
rules.rule: Do not apply custom colors to indicator images; rely on system automatic coloring.
rules.anti_pattern: Tinting UIPageControl indicators with custom UIColor or applying colorMultiply modifier.
rules.fix_uikit: Remove tintColor overrides; allow system to automatically color indicators based on appearance and state.
rules.quote: Avoid coloring indicator images.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Disable animated page transitions during scrubbing; use animation only for discrete tap interactions.
rules.anti_pattern: Calling setCurrentPage(_:animated: true) inside a continuous scrubbing gesture handler.
rules.fix_uikit: Check UIPageControl.InteractionState; use animated: false for continuous scrubbing, animated: true only for discrete taps.
rules.quote: Avoid animating page transitions during scrubbing.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use automatic background style when page control is not the primary navigation; use prominent only when it is primary.
rules.anti_pattern: Setting backgroundStyle = .prominent on a secondary page control or .automatic on the main navigation control.
rules.fix_uikit: Set backgroundStyle to .automatic for secondary controls, .prominent for primary navigation, .minimal for position-only display.
rules.quote: Use this style when the page control isn't the primary navigational element in the UI.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Do not enable scrubbing when using minimal background style; use automatic or prominent for scrubbing support.
rules.anti_pattern: Setting backgroundStyle = .minimal and allowsContinuousInteraction = true simultaneously.
rules.fix_uikit: If scrubbing is required, change backgroundStyle to .automatic or .prominent; if minimal style, set allowsContinuousInteraction = false.
rules.quote: Avoid supporting the scrubber when you use the minimal background style.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use panels to provide quick access to controls or information related to active content.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a panel for unrelated or disconnected functionality that doesn't support the current task.
rules.quote: Use a panel to give people quick access to important controls or information related to the content they're working with.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use panels for inspector functionality that auto-updates when selection changes; use regular windows for static Info windows.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a panel to display static information that never changes based on selection, or using a regular window for dynamic inspector content.
rules.quote: An inspector displays the details of the currently selected item, automatically updating its contents when the item changes or when people select a new item.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer simple adjustment controls like sliders and steppers; avoid text input or multi-step selection in panels.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing complex text fields, pickers, or multi-step workflows inside a panel that require extensive user interaction.
rules.quote: Prefer simple adjustment controls in a panel.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Write brief, noun-based panel titles using title-style capitalization to describe purpose.
rules.anti_pattern: Using verbose titles, verb phrases, or lowercase titles like "font settings" instead of "Fonts".
rules.quote: Create a short title using a noun — or a noun phrase with title-style capitalization — that can help people recognize the panel onscreen.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Bring all open panels to front when app becomes active; hide all panels when app becomes inactive.
rules.anti_pattern: Leaving panels hidden when the app activates, or leaving panels visible when the app deactivates.
rules.quote: When your app becomes active, bring all of its open panels to the front, regardless of which window was active when the panel opened.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Exclude panels from the Window menu's documents list; use menu commands only for show/hide actions.
rules.anti_pattern: Including panels in the Window menu's document list or treating panels as standard app windows in the menu.
rules.quote: Avoid including panels in the Window menu's documents list.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid making a panel's minimize button available; panels display only when needed.
rules.anti_pattern: Enabling the minimize button on a panel or allowing panels to be minimized to the Dock.
rules.quote: In general, avoid making a panel's minimize button available.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Refer to panels by title in menus and help; omit the word 'panel' from menu commands.
rules.anti_pattern: Using menu items like "Show Panel" or "Hide Panel" instead of "Show Fonts" or "Show Inspector".
rules.quote: In menus, use the panel's title without including the term panel: for example, "Show Fonts," "Show Colors," and "Show Inspector."

rules.heading: HUD-style panels
rules.rule: Maintain consistent panel style when app switches between full-screen and windowed modes.
rules.anti_pattern: Switching from HUD style in full-screen to standard panel style in windowed mode, or vice versa.
rules.quote: Maintain one panel style when your app switches modes.

rules.heading: HUD-style panels
rules.rule: Use color sparingly in HUDs; rely on high-contrast accents to highlight important information.
rules.anti_pattern: Filling HUD panels with multiple bright colors or using saturated colors throughout the dark interface.
rules.quote: Use color sparingly in HUDs.

rules.heading: HUD-style panels
rules.rule: Keep HUDs small; do not obscure the content they adjust or compete for attention.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating large HUD panels that cover significant portions of the content or dominate the visual hierarchy.
rules.quote: Keep HUDs small.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place path controls in window body, never in toolbars or status bars.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar.addItem(NSPathControl()) // or statusBar.addSubview(pathControl)
rules.quote: Use a path control in the window body, not the window frame.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer standard path control style for linear file system hierarchy display.
rules.anti_pattern: pathControl.pathStyle = .popUp // when showing full linear path is primary use case
rules.quote: A linear list that includes the root disk, parent folders, and selected item.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use pop-up path control style when space is constrained or menu access is preferred.
rules.anti_pattern: pathControl.pathStyle = .standard // in narrow sidebar with limited width
rules.quote: A control similar to a pop-up button that shows the icon and name of the selected item.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support drag-and-drop onto editable path controls to select items and display paths.
rules.anti_pattern: pathControl.isEditable = true // without implementing NSDraggingDestination
rules.quote: If you make the control editable, people can drag an item onto the control to select the item and display its path in the control.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use pickers for medium-to-long lists; prefer pull-down buttons for short lists or tables for very large sets.
rules.anti_pattern: Picker { ForEach(3...5, id: \.self) { Text("Option \($0)") } } // Too few items
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu { ForEach(shortList, id: \.self) { Text($0) } } label: { Text("Choose") } // For short lists
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIMenu or UIPickerView based on list size; consider UITableViewController for very large sets.
rules.quote: Consider using a picker to offer medium-to-long lists of items.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Order picker values predictably and logically so users can anticipate hidden values.
rules.anti_pattern: Picker("Country", selection: $country) { ForEach(countries.shuffled(), id: \.self) { Text($0) } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Country", selection: $country) { ForEach(countries.sorted(), id: \.self) { Text($0) } }
rules.fix_uikit: Sort UIPickerView data source arrays alphabetically or by logical grouping before display.
rules.quote: Use predictable and logically ordered values.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display pickers in context below or near the edited field; avoid switching views to show a picker.
rules.anti_pattern: NavigationLink(destination: PickerView()) { Text("Select") } // Switches view
rules.fix_swiftui: .popover(isPresented: $showPicker) { Picker(...) } // In-place or popover display
rules.fix_uikit: Present UIPickerView in UIActionSheetController or as input accessory view, not full screen.
rules.quote: Avoid switching views to show a picker.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use minute intervals that divide evenly into 60 (e.g., 15, 30) instead of default 60 values.
rules.anti_pattern: DatePicker("Time", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.hourAndMinute]) // Default 60 minute values
rules.fix_swiftui: DatePicker("Time", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.hourAndMinute]); // Set minuteInterval via UIDatePicker
rules.fix_uikit: UIDatePicker().minuteInterval = 15 // Divides evenly into 60
rules.quote: Consider providing less granularity when specifying minutes in a date picker.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use compact date picker style when space is constrained; it displays a button opening a modal editor.
rules.anti_pattern: DatePicker("Date", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.date]) // Default style may not fit
rules.fix_swiftui: DatePicker("Date", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.date]).datePickerStyle(.compact)
rules.fix_uikit: UIDatePicker().preferredDatePickerStyle = .compact
rules.quote: Use a compact date picker when space is constrained.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use inline date picker style for time-only selection with wheels or calendar view for dates.
rules.anti_pattern: DatePicker("Date", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.date]) // May not show inline calendar
rules.fix_swiftui: DatePicker("Date", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.date]).datePickerStyle(.inline)
rules.fix_uikit: UIDatePicker().preferredDatePickerStyle = .inline
rules.quote: Inline — For time only, a button that displays wheels of values; for dates and times, an inline calendar view.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use wheels date picker style for scrolling wheels supporting keyboard data entry.
rules.anti_pattern: DatePicker("Time", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.hourAndMinute]) // Default may not be wheels
rules.fix_swiftui: DatePicker("Time", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.hourAndMinute]).datePickerStyle(.wheel)
rules.fix_uikit: UIDatePicker().preferredDatePickerStyle = .wheel
rules.quote: Wheels — A set of scrolling wheels that also supports data entry through built-in or external keyboards.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Choose textual date picker style for limited space and specific selections; graphical for browsing or ranges.
rules.anti_pattern: NSDatePicker() // No style specified; may not suit app context
rules.fix_swiftui: DatePicker("Date", selection: $date, displayedComponents: [.date]) // Platform-appropriate style
rules.fix_uikit: NSDatePicker().datePickerStyle = .textFieldAndStepper // or .graphical for calendar browsing
rules.quote: Choose a date picker style that suits your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Adjust relative independent volume levels; never override system volume governance.
rules.anti_pattern: audioEngine.outputVolume = 0.5  // Directly setting output volume instead of relative mix levels
rules.fix_uikit: Use AVAudioMix or per-node volume adjustments; let AVAudioSession.setActive() govern final output.
rules.quote: Your app can adjust relative, independent volume levels to achieve a great mix of audio, but the system volume always governs the final output.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use MPVolumeView for volume adjustments and audio output rerouting controls.
rules.anti_pattern: Slider(value: $volume, in: 0...1)  // Custom volume slider without rerouting support
rules.fix_uikit: let volumeView = MPVolumeView(frame: CGRect(...)); addSubview(volumeView)
rules.quote: Use the system-provided volume view to let people make audio adjustments.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Choose AVAudioSession.Category matching your app's audio role and silence-switch behavior.
rules.anti_pattern: try audioSession.setCategory(.playback)  // For a game soundtrack that should respect silent mode
rules.fix_uikit: try audioSession.setCategory(.soloAmbient) for game soundtracks; .playback for essential audio.
rules.quote: Choose an audio category that fits the way your app or game uses sound.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Respond to audio controls only when actively playing audio or in clear audio context.
rules.anti_pattern: // Respond to play/pause from Control Center even when app is backgrounded and not playing audio
rules.fix_uikit: Check AVAudioSession.isOtherAudioPlaying and app state before handling remote commands.
rules.quote: If your app is actively playing audio, in a clear audio-related context, or connected to a device that uses Bluetooth or AirPlay, it's fine to respond to audio controls.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never redefine audio control meanings; maintain consistent behavior across all apps.
rules.anti_pattern: // Remap play button to skip forward or pause button to mute
rules.fix_uikit: Use standard MPRemoteCommand handlers for play, pause, skip; don't reassign their semantics.
rules.quote: People expect audio controls to behave consistently in all apps, so it's essential to avoid redefining the meaning of an audio control in your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Create custom audio player controls only for commands the system doesn't support.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom play/pause button when standard MPRemoteCommandCenter controls exist
rules.fix_uikit: Use MPRemoteCommandCenter for standard controls; add custom controls only for unique skip increments.
rules.quote: Consider creating custom audio player controls only if you need to offer commands that the system doesn't support.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Flag audio session with notifyOthersOnDeactivation when temporarily interrupting other apps.
rules.anti_pattern: try audioSession.setActive(false)  // Without notifying other apps to resume
rules.fix_uikit: try audioSession.setActive(false, options: .notifyOthersOnDeactivation)
rules.quote: If your app can temporarily interrupt the audio of other apps, be sure to flag your audio session in a way that lets other apps know when they can resume.

rules.heading: Handling interruptions
rules.rule: Customize audio-session interruption handling based on app type and user expectations.
rules.anti_pattern: // Always pause audio on any interruption without checking if it's resumable
rules.fix_uikit: Inspect AVAudioSession.InterruptionType; media apps check .shouldResume; games auto-resume.
rules.quote: Determine how to respond to audio-session interruptions.

rules.heading: Handling interruptions
rules.rule: Check interruption type before auto-resuming; media apps verify resumable, games auto-resume.
rules.anti_pattern: // Media app always resumes playback after any interruption without checking type
rules.fix_uikit: if interruptionOptions.contains(.shouldResume) { resume() } for media; games skip check.
rules.quote: Use the interruption type and your app's type to decide whether to resume playback automatically.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use Audio Services for short sounds and vibrations on iOS and iPadOS.
rules.anti_pattern: let audioPlayer = AVAudioPlayer(...)  // For brief UI feedback sounds
rules.fix_uikit: AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1016)  // For haptic/sound feedback
rules.quote: Use the system's sound services to play short sounds and vibrations.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Silence nonessential sounds (effects, soundtracks) when device is in silent mode.
rules.anti_pattern: // Game soundtrack plays even when Ring/Silent switch is set to silent
rules.fix_uikit: Use AVAudioSession.Category .soloAmbient or .ambient to respect silent mode.
rules.quote: When a device is in silent mode, it plays only the audio that people explicitly initiate, like media playback, alarms, and audio/video messaging.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Pause playback immediately when headphones disconnect; auto-reroute when connecting.
rules.anti_pattern: // Playback continues through speaker after headphones disconnect
rules.fix_uikit: Observe AVAudioSession.routeChangeNotification; pause on .oldDeviceUnavailable.
rules.quote: When disconnecting headphones, they expect playback to pause immediately.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Allow audio output rerouting to AirPlay, Bluetooth, and other devices unless compelling reason exists.
rules.anti_pattern: // Hardcoded to internal speaker; no AirPlay or Bluetooth rerouting option
rules.fix_uikit: Use MPVolumeView or AVAudioSession to enable automatic rerouting.
rules.quote: Permit rerouting of audio when possible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use system-provided haptic patterns only for their documented meanings; avoid repurposing patterns.
rules.anti_pattern: Using UINotificationFeedbackGenerator.notificationOccurred(.success) to signal a negative outcome because it feels right contextually.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIImpactFeedbackGenerator or create custom haptics via CoreHaptics for non-standard meanings.
rules.quote: People recognize standard haptics because the system plays them consistently on interactions with standard controls.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Maintain consistent haptic-to-action mapping so users learn causal relationships between haptics and events.
rules.anti_pattern: Playing the same haptic pattern for both mission failure and level completion, causing user confusion.
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve specific haptic patterns for specific outcomes; use different patterns for positive vs. negative events.
rules.quote: It's important to build a clear, causal relationship between each haptic and the action that causes it so people learn to associate certain haptic patterns with certain experiences.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Synchronize haptic intensity and sharpness with accompanying visual animation and audio intensity.
rules.anti_pattern: Playing a soft, gentle haptic while a sharp, intense animation occurs simultaneously.
rules.fix_uikit: Adjust CHHapticEvent intensity and sharpness to match visual and audio feedback characteristics.
rules.quote: When visual, auditory, and tactile feedback are in harmony — as they generally are in the physical world — the user experience is more coherent and can seem more natural.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid overusing haptics; conduct user testing to find the balance between presence and fatigue.
rules.anti_pattern: Playing a haptic on every single keystroke or scroll event in a text editor.
rules.fix_uikit: Reserve haptics for significant discrete events; test frequency with real users to prevent habituation.
rules.quote: Sometimes a haptic can feel just right when it happens occasionally, but become tiresome when it plays frequently.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer short haptics for discrete events; avoid long-running haptics in non-game apps.
rules.anti_pattern: Playing a continuous 5-second haptic vibration while a user scrolls through a list in a productivity app.
rules.fix_uikit: Use transient CHHapticEvent patterns for app feedback; reserve continuous patterns for gameplay contexts.
rules.quote: In most apps, prefer playing short haptics that complement discrete events.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Always provide a user-facing toggle to disable or mute haptics.
rules.anti_pattern: An app that plays haptics with no settings option to turn them off.
rules.fix_uikit: Add a haptics toggle in Settings; check UserDefaults or app preferences before calling feedback generators.
rules.quote: Make haptics optional.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Verify haptic vibrations do not interfere with camera, gyroscope, or microphone functionality.
rules.anti_pattern: Playing strong haptics during video recording, causing vibration artifacts in the captured footage.
rules.fix_uikit: Test haptic playback during active camera/sensor use; suppress haptics when these features are in use.
rules.quote: Ensure that haptic vibrations don't disrupt experiences involving device features like the camera, gyroscope, or microphone.

rules.heading: Custom haptics
rules.rule: Vary custom haptic intensity and sharpness dynamically based on user input or context.
rules.anti_pattern: A game that plays the same impact haptic regardless of whether a character jumps from ground level or from a tall tree.
rules.fix_uikit: Use CHHapticEvent with intensity and sharpness parameters scaled to context (e.g., jump height, collision force).
rules.quote: You can design custom haptic patterns that vary dynamically, based on user input or context.

rules.heading: Custom haptics
rules.rule: Use transient events for brief taps or impulses; use continuous events for sustained vibrations.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a continuous haptic event to simulate a single button tap.
rules.fix_uikit: Use CHHapticEvent.EventType.hapticTransient for taps; use .hapticContinuous for sustained effects.
rules.quote: Transient events are brief and compact, often feeling like taps or impulses.

rules.heading: Custom haptics
rules.rule: Control haptic sharpness to convey intent: soft/organic vs. crisp/mechanical experiences.
rules.anti_pattern: Using maximum sharpness for a soft, organic experience like wind or water flow.
rules.fix_uikit: Set CHHapticEvent sharpness parameter to low/mid values for organic effects, high for mechanical precision.
rules.quote: You can think of sharpness as a way to abstract a haptic experience into the waveform that produces the corresponding physical sensations.

rules.heading: Phone (iOS)
rules.rule: Use standard UI components (toggles, sliders, pickers) that play system haptics automatically.
rules.anti_pattern: Building a custom toggle from scratch without integrating UISwitch, missing automatic haptic feedback.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UISwitch, UISlider, UIPickerView instead of custom implementations to inherit system haptics.
rules.quote: Use standard UI components — like toggles, sliders, and pickers — that play Apple-designed system haptics by default.

rules.heading: Notification
rules.rule: Use notification haptics to signal task or action outcomes (success, failure, warning).
rules.anti_pattern: Using UIImpactFeedbackGenerator for a check deposit confirmation instead of UINotificationFeedbackGenerator.
rules.fix_uikit: Call UINotificationFeedbackGenerator().notificationOccurred(.success/.warning/.error) for outcome feedback.
rules.quote: Notification haptics provide feedback about the outcome of a task or action, such as depositing a check or unlocking a vehicle.

rules.heading: Impact
rules.rule: Use impact haptics to complement visual experiences with physical metaphors (taps, thuds, collisions).
rules.anti_pattern: Using notification haptics when a view snaps into place instead of impact haptics.
rules.fix_uikit: Call UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .light/.medium/.heavy).impactOccurred() for physical metaphor feedback.
rules.quote: Impact haptics provide a physical metaphor you can use to complement a visual experience.

rules.heading: Selection
rules.rule: Use selection haptics to provide feedback while UI element values are actively changing.
rules.anti_pattern: Using impact haptics while a slider value is being dragged instead of selection haptics.
rules.fix_uikit: Call UISelectionFeedbackGenerator().selectionChanged() during value changes in sliders or pickers.
rules.quote: Selection haptics provide feedback while the values of a UI element are changing.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use the system video player instead of custom implementations to ensure familiar, consistent playback interactions.
rules.fix_swiftui: VideoPlayer(player: avPlayer)
rules.fix_uikit: let vc = AVPlayerViewController(); vc.player = avPlayer; present(vc, animated: true)
rules.quote: The built-in video player provides an exceptional video playback experience that offers consistent interactions and behaviors that let people concentrate on enjoying immersive content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display video content at its original aspect ratio without embedded letterbox or pillarbox padding.
rules.fix_swiftui: VideoPlayer(player: avPlayer).aspectRatio(16/9, contentMode: .fit)
rules.fix_uikit: playerViewController.videoGravity = .resizeAspect
rules.quote: Always display video content at its original aspect ratio.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide supplementary metadata (image, title, description) only when it adds value and doesn't obscure playback.
rules.anti_pattern:
let item = AVPlayerItem(url: videoURL)
// No metadata provided; missing context for viewers
rules.fix_uikit: let meta = AVMutableMetadataItem(); meta.value = "Title" as NSString; playerItem.externalMetadata = [meta]
rules.quote: Provide additional information when it adds value.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support Space key for play/pause on connected keyboards across all input devices.
rules.fix_uikit: addKeyCommand(UIKeyCommand(input: " ", modifierFlags: [], action: #selector(togglePlayPause)))
rules.quote: For example, people expect to press Space on a connected keyboard to play or pause media playback on Apple Vision Pro, Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Handle secondary audio correctly to prevent audio mixing when switching between full-screen and Picture in Picture modes.
rules.fix_uikit: try? AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setCategory(.playback, options: .duckOthers)
rules.quote: Avoid allowing audio from different sources to mix as viewers switch between modes.

rules.heading: Integrating with the TV app
rules.citation: playing-video.md › Integrating with the TV app
rules.rule: Present a black screen immediately upon app launch to maintain visual continuity with TV app transition.
rules.fix_uikit: view.backgroundColor = .black
rules.quote: Maintain visual continuity with this transition by immediately presenting your own black screen before starting to play or resume content.

rules.heading: Integrating with the TV app
rules.citation: playing-video.md › Integrating with the TV app
rules.rule: Begin playback immediately without splash screens, detail screens, or intro animations after TV app transition.
rules.fix_uikit: player.play()
rules.quote: Jump right from your app's black screen into content, and avoid displaying splash screens, detail screens, intro animations, or any other barriers that make it take longer to reach content.

rules.heading: Integrating with the TV app
rules.citation: playing-video.md › Integrating with the TV app
rules.rule: Automatically resume playback at the previous stopping point without prompting for confirmation.
rules.fix_uikit: player.seek(to: lastStopTime); player.play()
rules.quote: Avoid asking people if they want to resume playback.

rules.heading: Integrating with the TV app
rules.citation: playing-video.md › Integrating with the TV app
rules.rule: Automatically switch to the correct user profile specified by TV app before starting playback.
rules.fix_uikit: if let id = profileID { switchProfile(to: id) }; player.play()
rules.quote: Make your app automatically switch to this profile before starting playback.

rules.heading: Loading content
rules.rule: Show a black loading screen with centered activity spinner only if content takes more than two seconds to load.
rules.fix_swiftui: if isLoading && loadingTime > 2.0 { ZStack { Color.black; ProgressView() } }
rules.fix_uikit: if isLoading && loadingTime > 2.0 { view.backgroundColor = .black; let s = UIActivityIndicatorView(style: .large); s.center = view.center; view.addSubview(s); s.startAnimating() }
rules.quote: A loading screen is unnecessary if your content loads quickly, but if loading takes more than two seconds, consider showing a black loading screen with a centered activity spinner and no surrounding content.

rules.heading: Loading content
rules.rule: Begin playback as soon as sufficient content loads; continue loading remaining content in background.
rules.fix_uikit: loadInitialContent(); player.play(); loadRemainingContent(inBackground: true)
rules.quote: If you must display a loading screen, display it only until enough content loads for playback to begin.

rules.heading: Exiting playback
rules.rule: Display a contextually relevant detail view or menu when exiting playback, with option to resume.
rules.fix_uikit: showDetailView(for: currentContent); addResumePlaybackButton()
rules.quote: When exiting playback, display a detail view for the content the viewer was just watching and include an option to resume playback.

rules.heading: Exiting playback
rules.rule: Prepare exit view immediately after receiving playback notification to handle immediate user exit.
rules.fix_uikit: prepareExitView()
rules.quote: Prepare an exit view as soon as possible after receiving a playback notification so you're ready to display the view if people exit immediately after playback begins.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Respond consistently to mouse and trackpad gestures across all apps and contexts.
rules.anti_pattern: Implementing swipe-between-pages differently in document view vs. image gallery, breaking user expectations.
rules.quote: Be consistent when responding to mouse and trackpad gestures.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never redefine or override systemwide trackpad gestures like Mission Control or Dock reveal.
rules.anti_pattern: Intercepting three-finger swipe in a game to trigger custom action, blocking Mission Control access.
rules.quote: Avoid redefining systemwide trackpad gestures.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide identical interaction behavior across gesture, eye-tracking, pointer, and keyboard input modes.
rules.anti_pattern: Allowing object duplication via Option+drag with pointer but not with keyboard modifier+touch.
rules.quote: Provide a consistent experience in your app, whether people are using gestures, eyes, a pointing device, or a keyboard.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow pointer to reveal and hide auto-minimizing or fading controls on hover.
rules.anti_pattern: Keeping Safari toolbar permanently minimized without pointer-hover reveal capability.
rules.quote: Let people use the pointer to reveal and hide controls that automatically minimize or fade out.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Implement UIBandSelectionInteraction for multiple selection in custom views when needed.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom collection view that ignores pointer drag-to-select rectangle interaction.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIBandSelectionInteraction to enable pointer-drag multi-select in custom views.
rules.quote: When someone clicks and drags the pointer over multiple items to select them, the pointer expands into a visible rectangle that encompasses the selection.

rules.heading: Pointer shape and content effects
rules.citation: pointing-devices.md › Pointer shape and content effects
rules.rule: Distinguish pointer from touch input only when it provides measurable UX value.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding pointer-only scrubber precision without allowing touch-based playhead drag.
rules.quote: Distinguish between pointer and finger input only if it provides value.

rules.heading: Standard pointers and effects
rules.rule: Use system-provided content effects (highlight, lift, hover) for consistency with platform expectations.
rules.anti_pattern: Applying custom scale and shadow to bar buttons instead of using system highlight effect.
rules.quote: When possible, support the system-provided content effects.

rules.heading: Standard pointers and effects
rules.rule: Add 12–24 points of padding around interactive elements for comfortable hit regions.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing buttons with minimal padding, forcing users to be overly precise with pointer.
rules.quote: In general, it works well to add about 12 points of padding around elements that include a bezel; for elements without a bezel, it works well to add about 24 points of padding around the element's visible edges.

rules.heading: Standard pointers and effects
rules.rule: Create contiguous hit regions for custom bar buttons to avoid distracting highlight flicker.
rules.anti_pattern: Spacing bar buttons with gaps that cause highlight shape to disappear between buttons.
rules.quote: Create contiguous hit regions for custom bar buttons.

rules.heading: Customizing pointers
rules.rule: Use system pointer effects for custom elements that mimic standard UI behavior.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom toolbar buttons without highlight effect, making users think they're non-interactive.
rules.quote: Prefer system-provided pointer effects for custom elements that behave like standard elements.

rules.heading: Customizing pointers
rules.rule: Apply pointer effects consistently throughout the app to enable knowledge transfer between contexts.
rules.anti_pattern: Using different pointer effects for drawing areas in different parts of the same app.
rules.quote: Use pointer effects in consistent ways throughout your app.

rules.heading: Customizing pointers
rules.rule: Avoid purely decorative pointer and content effects that distract without providing value.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding animated color shifts to pointer on hover without functional purpose.
rules.quote: Avoid creating gratuitous pointer and content effects.

rules.heading: Customizing pointers
rules.rule: Keep custom pointer shapes simple and immediately recognizable without explanation.
rules.anti_pattern: Using complex, ambiguous custom pointer shape that requires instructional text to explain.
rules.quote: Keep custom pointer shapes simple.

rules.heading: Pointers
rules.rule: Apply semantically correct pointer style (arrow, link, iBeam, resize, etc.) matching element interaction type.
rules.anti_pattern: Using default arrow pointer for all interactive elements, including links and resizable frames.
rules.fix_swiftui: .pointerStyle(.link) for links; .pointerStyle(.horizontalText) for text fields; .pointerStyle(.columnResize) for dividers.
rules.fix_uikit: NSCursor.pointingHand for links; NSCursor.iBeam for text; NSCursor.columnResize for vertical dividers.
rules.quote: macOS offers a variety of standard pointer styles, which your app can use to communicate the interactive state of an interface element or the result of a drag operation.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use pop-up buttons only for mutually exclusive options; use pull-down buttons for actions or multi-select.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Menu for actions/multi-select; use Picker or custom pop-up for mutually exclusive state.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIMenu with UIAction for actions; use UIPickerView or custom control for state selection.
rules.quote: Use a pop-up button to present a flat list of mutually exclusive options or states.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Set a sensible default selection that most users are likely to want.
rules.fix_swiftui: @State var size = "M" // Set default to most common choice
rules.fix_uikit: popUpButton.selectItem(at: 1) // Select most likely option by default
rules.quote: Provide a useful default selection.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use a descriptive label or button title to help users predict options without opening the menu.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu { ... } label: { Text("⋯") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu { ... } label: { Text("Font Size") }
rules.fix_uikit: popUpButton.setTitle("Font Size", for: .normal)
rules.quote: Give people a way to predict a pop-up button's options without opening it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer pop-up buttons when space is limited and not all options need constant visibility.
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Select", selection: $choice) { ForEach(options, id: \.self) { Text($0) } }
rules.quote: Consider using a pop-up button when space is limited and you don't need to display all options all the time.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include a Custom option in the menu to avoid cluttering the interface with rarely-used items.
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu { Button("Red") {}; Button("Blue") {}; Divider(); Button("Custom") { showColorPicker() } } label: { Text("Color") }
rules.quote: If necessary, include a Custom option in a pop-up button's menu to provide additional items that are useful in some situations.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: In popovers or modals, use pop-up buttons instead of disclosure indicators for list item options.
rules.fix_swiftui: List { HStack { Text("Option"); Spacer(); Menu { } label: { Text("Select") } } }
rules.quote: Within a popover or modal view, consider using a pop-up button instead of a disclosure indicator to present multiple options for a list item.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit popover content to a few related tasks; avoid exposing excessive functionality.
rules.fix_swiftui: Reduce content to 3–5 core controls; move secondary tasks to separate sheets or modals.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UIPopoverPresentationController.preferredContentSize to compact dimensions; limit subviews.
rules.quote: Because a popover disappears after people interact with it, limit the amount of functionality in the popover to a few related tasks.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Position popover arrow to point directly at the triggering element; avoid covering it.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `.popover(item:content:)` with explicit sourceFrame or arrowEdge to anchor correctly.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UIPopoverPresentationController.sourceView and sourceRect to the button's frame.
rules.quote: Make sure a popover's arrow points as directly as possible to the element that revealed it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Always save work when a nonmodal popover auto-closes; discard only on explicit Cancel.
rules.fix_swiftui: Save $draftText to persistent storage before popover dismisses; only clear on explicit cancel action.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement popoverPresentationControllerDidDismissPopover(_:) to persist edits; discard only if Cancel tapped.
rules.quote: Always save work when automatically closing a nonmodal popover.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display only one popover at a time; never cascade or nest popovers.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use a single @State var activePopover: PopoverType? to track one popover; dismiss before opening next.
rules.fix_uikit: Dismiss the current UIPopoverPresentationController before presenting a new one.
rules.quote: Show one popover at a time.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never display alerts, sheets, or other views on top of a popover; only alerts are permitted.
rules.fix_swiftui: Dismiss popover before presenting sheet; reserve overlays for alerts only.
rules.fix_uikit: Dismiss UIPopoverPresentationController before presenting UIAlertController or UISheetPresentationController.
rules.quote: Don't show another view over a popover.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use Close/Cancel/Done buttons only for clarity; omit if popover auto-closes on selection.
rules.fix_swiftui: Omit Close button if popover auto-dismisses on selection; include only if confirming save/discard.
rules.fix_uikit: Add UIButton for Close only when user must confirm destructive or ambiguous action.
rules.quote: A Close button, including Cancel or Done, is worth including if it provides clarity, like exiting with or without saving changes.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Animate popover size changes smoothly to avoid appearing as a replacement.
rules.fix_swiftui: Wrap size change in `.withAnimation { isExpanded.toggle() }` to animate frame transition.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIView.animate(withDuration:) to resize UIPopoverPresentationController.preferredContentSize.
rules.quote: Provide a smooth transition when changing the size of a popover.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid using 'popover' in help text; refer to specific task or selection instead.
rules.anti_pattern: "Tap the Settings button at the bottom of the popover to configure options."
rules.fix_swiftui: Update help text to: "Tap the Settings button to configure options."
rules.fix_uikit: Update UIAccessibilityHint to omit 'popover'; describe the action directly.
rules.quote: Avoid using the word popover in help documentation.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never use popovers to display warnings; use alerts instead.
rules.fix_swiftui: Replace with `.alert("Warning", isPresented: $showWarning) { ... }`
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIAlertController(style: .alert) instead of UIPopoverPresentationController.
rules.quote: Avoid using a popover to show a warning.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Avoid popovers in compact size classes; use full-screen sheets instead.
rules.fix_swiftui: Check horizontalSizeClass and present sheet in compact, popover in regular: `if sizeClass == .compact { .sheet(...) } else { .popover(...) }`
rules.fix_uikit: Check traitCollection.horizontalSizeClass; present UISheetPresentationController for compact, UIPopoverPresentationController for regular.
rules.quote: Avoid displaying popovers in compact views.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Consider allowing users to detach popovers into persistent panels on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
NSPopover()
// Popover always attached; cannot be dragged into separate panel
rules.fix_swiftui: Use NSPopover with detachable property enabled (SwiftUI wrapping).
rules.fix_uikit: Set NSPopover.behavior = .transient or .semitransient; enable detachable for persistent panels.
rules.quote: Consider letting people detach a popover.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Maintain similar appearance when detached popover becomes a panel to preserve context.
rules.anti_pattern:
NSPopover() // Attached popover
// When detached, panel has completely different styling, colors, or layout
rules.fix_swiftui: Use consistent styling for both attached and detached states.
rules.fix_uikit: Apply same NSAppearance and visual properties to detached NSPanel.
rules.quote: Make minimal appearance changes to a detached popover.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow single-click/tap to close one popover and open another without extra gestures.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use single @State var activePopover: PopoverID? to toggle directly: `activePopover = .optionB`
rules.fix_uikit: Dismiss current popover and present next in one gesture handler.
