rules.quote: When possible, let people close one popover and open another with a single click or tap.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Size popovers only large enough to display content and point to source; avoid oversizing.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use `.frame(width: 200, height: 100)` or let content size naturally; system adjusts if needed.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UIPopoverPresentationController.preferredContentSize to minimal dimensions fitting content.
rules.quote: Avoid making a popover too big.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place Print action in standard system locations: File menu (macOS), toolbar button or action sheet (iOS/iPadOS).
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Print") { } placed in a random custom menu without discoverable placement.
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { Button(action: { showPrintOptions = true }) { Image(systemName: "printer") } }
rules.fix_uikit: Add Print to UIMenu in File menu (macOS) or present UIActivityViewController with UIPrintInteractionController (iOS).
rules.quote: Help people find your print action by placing it in standard system locations.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Disable or hide Print action when no content exists or no printers are available.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Print") { printDocument() }.disabled(false) // always enabled regardless of printer availability
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Print") { printDocument() }.disabled(printers.isEmpty || content.isEmpty)
rules.fix_uikit: printButton.isEnabled = !printers.isEmpty && hasContent
rules.quote: If there's nothing onscreen to print, or no printers are available, dim the Print item in a macOS app's File menu and remove the Print action from the Action sheet in an iOS or iPadOS app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use system-provided print UI to present standard options like page range, copies, and duplex when supported.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom form with TextField for page range instead of using UIPrintInteractionController.printInfo.jobName.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use UIPrintInteractionController.shared with printInfo configured for supported options.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure UIPrintInteractionController.shared.printInfo with pageRange, numberOfCopies, and duplex settings.
rules.quote: If it makes sense to offer options like selecting a page range, requesting multiple copies, or printing on both sides — and the printer supports the options — use the system-provided view to present them.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Create custom print panel categories for app-specific options not provided by the system.
rules.anti_pattern: Implementing page range, orientation, and scaling options in a custom dialog instead of using system print panel.
rules.quote: If your macOS app offers app-specific print options that the system doesn't offer, consider creating a custom category for the print panel.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Present page setup dialog for document-specific page size, orientation, and scaling settings.
rules.anti_pattern: Including page orientation and scaling options in the main print panel instead of a dedicated page setup dialog.
rules.quote: If your app supports document-specific page settings, consider presenting a page setup dialog.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Clearly communicate interdependencies between print options to prevent invalid configurations.
rules.anti_pattern: Allowing transparency printing to remain enabled when double-sided printing is selected without visual feedback.
rules.quote: Make sure interdependencies between options are clear.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use disclosure controls to hide advanced print options until needed; label them as Advanced Options.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing all print options at once without grouping or collapsing advanced settings.
rules.fix_swiftui: DisclosureGroup("Advanced Options") { /* advanced controls */ }
rules.quote: Separate advanced features from frequently used features.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Provide live preview of print setting effects when feasible to help users understand changes.
rules.anti_pattern: Tone control slider with no visual feedback until print preview is generated.
rules.quote: Consider letting people preview the effect of a setting.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Persist modified print settings with the document for reuse across print sessions.
rules.anti_pattern: Resetting all print settings to defaults each time the document is opened.
rules.quote: Consider storing modified settings with the document.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Request access only to data your app actually needs for its core features.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting camera, contacts, and location permissions at launch before users engage with features requiring them.
rules.quote: Request access only to data that you actually need.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Be transparent about how your app collects, uses, and shares people's data.
rules.anti_pattern: Collecting location data without explaining its use in the app's privacy policy or purpose strings.
rules.quote: Be transparent about how your app collects and uses people's data.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Process sensitive data on-device using local ML models rather than sending to remote servers.
rules.anti_pattern: Uploading all user audio to a cloud server for processing instead of using on-device ML inference.
rules.quote: Process data on the device where possible.

rules.heading: Requesting permission
rules.rule: Request permission only when the user actively engages with a feature requiring that data or resource.
rules.anti_pattern: Calling requestWhenInUseAuthorization() or requestAlwaysAndWhenInUseAuthorization() in AppDelegate.didFinishLaunchingWithOptions before user interaction.
rules.quote: Request permission only when your app clearly needs access to the data or resource.

rules.heading: Requesting permission
rules.rule: Avoid requesting permission at app launch unless the data or resource is required for core functionality.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting microphone access in didFinishLaunchingWithOptions for an app where recording is optional.
rules.quote: Avoid requesting permission at launch unless the data or resource is required for your app to function.

rules.heading: Requesting permission
rules.rule: Write purpose strings in active voice, specific, brief, and complete; use sentence case with a period.
rules.anti_pattern: Purpose string: "Microphone access is needed for a better experience." (passive, vague, no justification).
rules.fix_swiftui: Purpose string: "The app records during the night to detect snoring sounds." (active, specific, clear justification).
rules.fix_uikit: Purpose string: "The app records during the night to detect snoring sounds." (active, specific, clear justification).
rules.quote: Write copy that clearly describes how your app uses the ability, data, or resource you're requesting.

rules.heading: Pre-alert screens, windows, or views
rules.citation: privacy.md › Pre-alert screens, windows, or views
rules.rule: Include only one button in pre-alert screens; use neutral labels like 'Continue' or 'Next', never 'Allow'.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom pre-alert screen with an 'Allow' button that visually mimics the system alert's allow button, confusing user intent.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use a single 'Continue' button in the custom view that opens the system permission alert.
rules.fix_uikit: Use a single 'Continue' button in the custom view that opens the system permission alert.
rules.quote: Include only one button and make it clear that it opens the system alert.

rules.heading: Pre-alert screens, windows, or views
rules.citation: privacy.md › Pre-alert screens, windows, or views
rules.rule: Do not include close, cancel, or alternative action buttons in pre-alert screens unless required for legal consent.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom pre-alert screen with a 'Skip' or 'Not Now' button allowing users to bypass the system permission alert.
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove all buttons except the single 'Continue' button that leads to the system alert.
rules.fix_uikit: Remove all buttons except the single 'Continue' button that leads to the system alert.
rules.quote: Don't include additional actions in your custom screen or window, unless needed to obtain a legal consent.

rules.heading: Tracking requests
rules.rule: Never precede App Tracking Transparency alert with custom screens that confuse, mislead, or manipulate user choice.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom screen offering incentives (e.g., 'Allow tracking to unlock a discount'), displaying a fake alert image, or annotating the alert.
rules.fix_swiftui: Display the system App Tracking Transparency alert directly without preceding custom messaging.
rules.fix_uikit: Display the system App Tracking Transparency alert directly without preceding custom messaging.
rules.quote: Never precede the system-provided alert with a custom screen or window that could confuse or mislead people.

rules.heading: Location button
rules.rule: Use the location button to provide lightweight, one-time location sharing for specific features.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting 'Always' location authorization for a feature that only needs location once per user action.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use LocationButton from CoreLocationUI to grant temporary one-time location access.
rules.fix_uikit: Use CLLocationButton from CoreLocationUI to grant temporary one-time location access.
rules.quote: Consider using the location button to give people a lightweight way to share their location for specific app features.

rules.heading: Location button
rules.rule: Customize location button title, glyph style, colors, and corner radius only; do not alter other visual attributes.
rules.anti_pattern: Modifying the location button's size, shape, or adding custom overlays beyond the documented customization options.
rules.fix_swiftui: LocationButton(.currentLocation) { }.labelStyle(.titleAndIcon).foregroundStyle(.white).tint(.blue).clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 8))
rules.fix_uikit: let btn = CLLocationButton(); btn.label = .currentLocation; btn.tintColor = .systemBlue; btn.cornerRadius = 8
rules.quote: To help people recognize and trust location buttons, you can't customize the button's other visual attributes.

rules.heading: Protecting data
rules.rule: Use passkeys or biometric authentication (Face ID, Touch ID) instead of passwords for authentication.
rules.anti_pattern: Storing and validating user passwords in plain text or using only password-based authentication without 2FA.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use AuthenticationServices with passkeys or LocalAuthentication for biometric verification.
rules.fix_uikit: Use AuthenticationServices with passkeys or LocalAuthentication for biometric verification.
rules.quote: Avoid relying solely on passwords for authentication.

rules.heading: Protecting data
rules.rule: Store sensitive information in a keychain, never in plain-text files or UserDefaults.
rules.anti_pattern: Storing API tokens, passwords, or credit card data in UserDefaults or as plain-text files.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Keychain services via Security framework to store sensitive credentials.
rules.fix_uikit: Use Keychain services via Security framework to store sensitive credentials.
rules.quote: Store sensitive information in a keychain.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Sign macOS apps distributed outside the App Store with a valid Developer ID certificate.
rules.anti_pattern: Distributing a macOS app outside the App Store without Developer ID signing.
rules.quote: Sign your app with a valid Developer ID.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Enable app sandboxing in macOS apps to protect user data and system resources from malware.
rules.anti_pattern: Submitting a macOS app to the App Store without sandboxing enabled in Xcode capabilities.
rules.quote: Protect people's data with app sandboxing.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use determinate progress indicators when task duration is known; reserve indeterminate for unquantifiable operations.
rules.anti_pattern:
ProgressView(value: nil) // indeterminate
// used for file download with known size
rules.fix_swiftui: ProgressView(value: downloadProgress, total: totalSize) // determinate when duration known
rules.fix_uikit: progressView.progress = Float(downloadedBytes) / Float(totalBytes)
rules.quote: When possible, use a determinate progress indicator.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Report advancement accurately in determinate indicators; even out pace to avoid deceptive completion timing.
rules.fix_swiftui: let linearProgress = elapsedTime / totalEstimatedTime // smooth, proportional advancement
rules.fix_uikit: progressView.progress = Float(bytesDownloaded) / Float(totalBytes) // proportional to actual work
rules.quote: Be as accurate as possible when reporting advancement in a determinate progress indicator.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep progress indicators animating continuously; stationary indicators signal stalled or frozen app.
rules.fix_swiftui: ProgressView(value: currentProgress).onReceive(timer) { _ in currentProgress = calculateProgress() }
rules.fix_uikit: timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 0.1) { _ in progressView.progress = Float(calculateProgress()) }
rules.quote: Keep progress indicators moving so people know something is continuing to happen.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Transition from indeterminate to determinate progress bar when task duration becomes quantifiable.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Stays indeterminate even after duration becomes known
ProgressView() // indeterminate spinner throughout
rules.fix_swiftui: if let total = knownFileSize { ProgressView(value: downloadedBytes, total: total) } else { ProgressView() }
rules.fix_uikit: if let total = totalBytes { progressView.progress = Float(current) / Float(total) } else { activityIndicator.startAnimating() }
rules.quote: When possible, switch a progress bar from indeterminate to determinate.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never transition between circular activity indicator and linear progress bar styles.
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Use consistent style; switch only value/total parameters
ProgressView(value: progress, total: total)
rules.fix_uikit: // Use same UIProgressView instance; update progress property only
rules.quote: Don't switch from the circular style to the bar style.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display accurate, succinct contextual descriptions; avoid vague terms like 'loading' or 'authenticating'.
rules.anti_pattern:
ProgressView()
  .label { Text("Loading...") }
rules.fix_swiftui: ProgressView(value: progress) { Text("Downloading photo (\(Int(progress * 100))%)") }
rules.fix_uikit: progressView.accessibilityLabel = "Downloading photo"
rules.quote: If it's helpful, display a description that provides additional context for the task.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Position progress indicators consistently across platforms and within/between apps for reliable discoverability.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Progress indicator placed in different locations
// depending on context or screen size
rules.fix_uikit: // Always add to same superview/position
rules.quote: Display a progress indicator in a consistent location.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide Cancel or Pause buttons when feasible to halt processing without negative side effects.
rules.fix_uikit:
let cancelButton = UIButton()
cancelButton.addTarget(self, action: #selector(cancel), for: .touchUpInside)
rules.quote: When it's feasible, let people halt processing.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Show alert confirming cancellation when halting process causes data loss or negative consequences.
rules.fix_swiftui: .alert("Cancel Download?", isPresented: $showCancellationAlert) { Button("Resume") { }; Button("Discard", role: .destructive) { cancelDownload() } }
rules.fix_uikit: let alert = UIAlertController(title: "Cancel Download?", message: "Progress will be lost.", preferredStyle: .alert); alert.addAction(UIAlertAction(title: "Discard", style: .destructive))
rules.quote: Let people know when halting a process has a negative consequence.

rules.heading: Refresh content controls
rules.rule: Perform automatic periodic content updates; don't require manual refresh for every update.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Only updates when user manually pulls to refresh
refreshControl.addTarget(self, action: #selector(refresh), for: .valueChanged)
rules.fix_swiftui: List { }.refreshable { await fetchLatestContent() }.task { startPeriodicUpdates() }
rules.fix_uikit: timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 300) { _ in self.fetchLatestContent() }
rules.quote: Perform automatic content updates.

rules.heading: Refresh content controls
rules.rule: Use refresh control title only to show content metadata (e.g., last update time), not usage instructions.
rules.fix_uikit: refreshControl.attributedTitle = NSAttributedString(string: "Last checked: \(lastUpdateTime)")
rules.quote: Supply a short title only if it adds value.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Prefer circular activity indicator (spinner) for background operations or space-constrained contexts on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Uses linear progress bar for background server task
ProgressView() // indeterminate linear bar
rules.fix_swiftui:
ProgressView()
  .progressViewStyle(.circular) // spinner for background task
rules.quote: Prefer an activity indicator (spinner) to communicate the status of a background operation or when space is constrained.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Omit labels on spinning progress indicators; animation alone signals active process on macOS.
rules.fix_swiftui:
ProgressView()
  .progressViewStyle(.circular) // No label needed
rules.quote: Avoid labeling a spinning progress indicator.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use pull-down buttons only for commands or items directly related to the button's primary action.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { Button("Unrelated Action") {} }) { Label("Settings", systemImage: "gear") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu(content: { Button("Add Photo") {} Button("Add Video") {} }) { Label("Add", systemImage: "plus") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIMenu with UIAction children that all relate to the button's declared purpose.
rules.quote: Use a pull-down button to present commands or items that are directly related to the button's action.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not hide all primary view actions inside a single pull-down button.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { Button("Save") {} Button("Delete") {} Button("Share") {} }) { Label("Actions", systemImage: "ellipsis") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button("Save") {} followed by Menu(content: { Button("Archive") {} }) { Label("More", systemImage: "ellipsis") }
rules.fix_uikit: Place critical actions as separate UIButton instances; use UIMenu only for secondary actions.
rules.quote: Avoid putting all of a view's actions in one pull-down button.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include minimum three menu items; use alternative components for one or two items.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { Button("Option A") {} }) { Label("Choose", systemImage: "ellipsis") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Toggle or Picker for single/dual selections; reserve Menu for three+ items.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UISwitch or UISegmentedControl for 1–2 choices; UIMenu for 3+ actions.
rules.quote: Because people have to interact with a pull-down button before they can view its menu, listing a minimum of three items can help the interaction feel worthwhile.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid excessive menu items; balance menu length to prevent slow item discovery.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { ForEach(1...50, id: \.self) { i in Button("Item \(i)") {} } }) { Label("Menu") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Limit to 5–10 most relevant items; use submenus or alternative navigation for larger lists.
rules.fix_uikit: Constrain UIMenu children count; consider UITableViewController for extensive lists.
rules.quote: Listing too many items in a pull-down button's menu can slow people down because it takes longer to find a specific item.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display menu title only if it adds meaning; rely on button content and item labels for context.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { Button("Sort A–Z") {} }, label: { Text("Sort Options") })  // redundant title
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu(content: { Button("Sort A–Z") {} }) { Label("Sort", systemImage: "arrow.up.arrow.down") }
rules.fix_uikit: Omit UIMenu.title unless it disambiguates multiple menu contexts.
rules.quote: Display a succinct menu title only if it adds meaning.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Mark destructive actions in red and require confirmation via action sheet or popover.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { Button("Delete") { performDelete() } }) { Label("Actions") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu(content: { Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { showConfirmation = true } }) { Label("Actions") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAction(title: "Delete", attributes: .destructive) with UIAlertController confirmation.
rules.quote: Let people know when a pull-down button's menu item is destructive, and ask them to confirm their intent.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include interface icons with menu items only when they clarify meaning; use SF Symbols.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { Button(action: {}) { Label("Save", systemImage: "star") } }) { Label("Actions") }
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu(content: { Button(action: {}) { Label("Save", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.down") } }) { Label("Actions") }
rules.fix_uikit: Attach UIImage from SF Symbols only when it disambiguates the action.
rules.quote: Include an interface icon with a menu item when it provides value.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use a More button to present secondary items when space is constrained, balancing convenience against discoverability.
rules.anti_pattern: Menu(content: { Button("Archive") {} Button("Mute") {} }) { Label("More", systemImage: "ellipsis") }  // unclear what 'More' contains
rules.fix_swiftui: Menu(content: { Button("Archive") {} Button("Mute") {} }) { Label("More", systemImage: "ellipsis") }  // with clear primary actions visible
rules.fix_uikit: Place primary actions as UIButton; use UIMenu with ellipsis for secondary/tertiary actions only.
rules.quote: Consider using a More pull-down button to present items that don't need prominent positions in the main interface.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Enable inline rank adjustment without requiring navigation to separate editing screens.
rules.anti_pattern: Presenting a list of ranked items where users must open a detail view or modal to change any rating.
rules.quote: When presenting a list of ranked items, let people adjust the rank of individual items inline without navigating to a separate editing screen.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use star symbols for rating indicators; if replacing with custom symbols, ensure purpose is immediately clear.
rules.anti_pattern: Replacing stars with ambiguous symbols like hearts, circles, or domain-specific icons without clear visual or contextual indication that they represent a rating scale.
rules.quote: If you replace the star with a custom symbol, make sure that its purpose is clear.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display only complete symbols; round rating values to whole numbers, never show partial or fractional symbols.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying a 3.5-star rating by rendering three full stars and one half-filled star, or using opacity/clipping to show partial symbols.
rules.quote: A rating indicator doesn't display partial symbols; it rounds the value to display complete symbols only.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Maintain consistent spacing between symbols; do not expand or shrink symbols to fit component width.
rules.anti_pattern: Stretching or compressing star symbols horizontally to fill a fixed-width container, or varying the gap between symbols based on available space.
rules.quote: Within a rating indicator, symbols are always the same distance apart and don't expand or shrink to fit the component's width.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Request ratings only after users demonstrate engagement, not on first launch or during onboarding.
rules.fix_swiftui: Track user engagement milestones (level completion, task completion) before triggering RequestReviewAction in a conditional block.
rules.fix_uikit: Call SKStoreReviewController.requestReview() only after detecting significant user engagement via analytics or state tracking.
rules.quote: Ask for a rating only after people have demonstrated engagement with your app or game.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid requesting ratings during active tasks or gameplay; prompt only at natural stopping points.
rules.fix_swiftui: Defer RequestReviewAction until after task completion or game level completion, using state-based conditional triggers.
rules.fix_uikit: Call SKStoreReviewController.requestReview() in completion handlers or after detecting natural breaks in user flow.
rules.quote: Avoid interrupting people while they're performing a task or playing a game.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Space rating requests at least one to two weeks apart; avoid repeated prompts.
rules.fix_swiftui: Implement throttling logic storing last prompt timestamp; only trigger RequestReviewAction if 7–14 days have elapsed.
rules.fix_uikit: Track SKStoreReviewController.requestReview() timestamps in UserDefaults; enforce minimum interval before next call.
rules.quote: Avoid pestering people.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use system-provided rating prompt (RequestReviewAction or SKStoreReviewController); never build custom rating UI.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use RequestReviewAction to trigger the system-provided in-app rating prompt.
rules.fix_uikit: Call SKStoreReviewController.requestReview() to display the system-consistent rating interface.
rules.quote: Prefer the system-provided prompt.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Weigh benefits of resetting app summary rating against reduced total rating visibility and download impact.
rules.anti_pattern: // Resetting rating summary on every minor version bump without considering user perception impact
rules.quote: Weigh the benefits of resetting your summary rating against the potential disadvantage of showing fewer ratings.

rules.heading: Text alignment
rules.rule: Adjust text alignment to match interface direction; reverse LTR left-alignment to RTL right-alignment.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Hello").lineLimit(1) // Always left-aligned, ignores RTL context
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Hello").multilineTextAlignment(.leading) // Uses semantic leading/trailing
rules.fix_uikit: label.textAlignment = .natural // Uses NSTextAlignmentNatural for automatic RTL support
rules.quote: Adjust text alignment to match the interface direction, if the system doesn't do so automatically.

rules.heading: Text alignment
rules.rule: Align paragraphs (3+ lines) by language, not context; keep 1-2 line blocks context-aligned.
rules.anti_pattern: Text(arabicParagraph).multilineTextAlignment(.trailing) // Forces RTL alignment regardless of content
rules.fix_swiftui: Text(arabicParagraph).multilineTextAlignment(.leading) // Respects language of content
rules.fix_uikit: label.textAlignment = .natural // System determines alignment by language
rules.quote: Align a paragraph based on its language, not on the current context.

rules.heading: Text alignment
rules.rule: Use consistent alignment for all items in a list, reversing all items including different scripts.
rules.anti_pattern: ForEach(items) { item in Text(item).multilineTextAlignment(item.isArabic ? .trailing : .leading) }
rules.fix_swiftui: ForEach(items) { item in Text(item).multilineTextAlignment(.leading) } // Consistent for all
rules.fix_uikit: for item in items { label.textAlignment = .natural } // All items use same natural alignment
rules.quote: Use a consistent alignment for all text items in a list.

rules.heading: Numbers and characters
rules.rule: Never reverse digit order within a single number; preserve "541", phone, or card number order.
rules.anti_pattern: let reversed = String(phoneNumber.reversed()); Text(reversed) // Breaks phone number
rules.fix_swiftui: Text(phoneNumber) // Display digits in original order
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = phoneNumber // Never reverse individual number sequences
rules.quote: Don't reverse the order of numerals in a specific number.

rules.heading: Numbers and characters
rules.rule: Reverse numeral order in progress/counting sequences for RTL; never flip individual numerals.
rules.anti_pattern: Slider(value: $val, in: 1...10) // Numerals 1-10 not reversed in RTL
rules.fix_swiftui: // Reverse label positions: Text("10") ... Slider ... Text("1") in RTL
rules.fix_uikit: // Reorder UILabel positions for min/max values in RTL context
rules.quote: Reverse the order of numerals that show progress or a counting direction; never flip the numerals themselves.

rules.heading: Controls
rules.rule: Flip progress controls (sliders, progress bars) and their min/max glyphs in RTL context.
rules.anti_pattern: Slider(value: $val, in: 0...100) // Slider direction unchanged in RTL
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use .environment(\._layoutDirection, .rightToLeft) or system-provided RTL flipping
rules.fix_uikit: // UISlider automatically flips in RTL; ensure min/max images also flip
rules.quote: Flip controls that show progress from one value to another.

rules.heading: Controls
rules.rule: Flip navigation controls (back, next, previous) to match RTL reading order; back points right in RTL.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "chevron.left") } // Always points left
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "chevron.left").flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection(true) }
rules.fix_uikit: button.semanticContentAttribute = .forceLeftToRight // Or use .forceRightToLeft in RTL
rules.quote: Flip controls that help people navigate or access items in a fixed order.

rules.heading: Controls
rules.rule: Preserve direction of controls referring to actual directions or onscreen areas; never flip them.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "arrow.right").flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection(true) } // Wrong for directional control
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "arrow.right") } // No flipping for actual direction
rules.fix_uikit: button.semanticContentAttribute = .forceLeftToRight // Preserve actual direction
rules.quote: Preserve the direction of a control that refers to an actual direction or points to an onscreen area.

rules.heading: Controls
rules.rule: Increase RTL font size ~2 points when balancing Arabic/Hebrew text with uppercase Latin text.
rules.anti_pattern: Text(arabicLabel).font(.system(size: 12)) // Same size as Latin uppercase
rules.fix_swiftui: Text(arabicLabel).font(.system(size: 14)) // Increase by ~2 points for visual balance
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 14) // Increase RTL font size
rules.quote: To visually balance Arabic or Hebrew text with Latin text that uses all capitals, it often works well to increase the RTL font size by about 2 points.

rules.heading: Images
rules.rule: Avoid flipping photographs, illustrations, or artwork; create new versions if reading-direction-dependent.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("photo").flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection(true) // Flips photo in RTL
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(isRTL ? "photo_rtl" : "photo") // Use separate localized image asset
rules.fix_uikit: imageView.image = UIImage(named: isRTL ? "photo_rtl" : "photo")
rules.quote: Avoid flipping images like photographs, illustrations, and general artwork.

rules.heading: Images
rules.rule: Reverse image positions when order is meaningful (chronological, alphabetical, favorite).
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Image("first"); Image("second"); Image("third") } // Order unchanged in RTL
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { ForEach(images.reversed()) { Image($0) } } // Reverse order in RTL
rules.fix_uikit: stackView.semanticContentAttribute = .forceLeftToRight // Or reorder subviews
rules.quote: Reverse the positions of images when their order is meaningful.

rules.heading: Interface icons
rules.rule: Flip interface icons representing text or reading direction (left-aligned bars become right-aligned).
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: "text.alignleft") // Always left-aligned, ignores RTL
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "text.alignleft").flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection(true)
rules.fix_uikit: image.flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection = true // SF Symbols handle RTL variants
rules.quote: Flip interface icons that represent text or reading direction.

rules.heading: Interface icons
rules.rule: Flip icons depicting forward/backward motion; forward motion matches reading direction.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: "speaker.wave.1") // Sound waves always from left
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "speaker.wave.1").flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection(true)
rules.fix_uikit: image.flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection = true // Flip motion direction in RTL
rules.quote: Flip an interface icon that shows forward or backward motion.

rules.heading: Interface icons
rules.rule: Never flip logos, universal signs, or marks; display in original form regardless of language.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("companyLogo").flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection(true) // Flips logo in RTL
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("companyLogo") // No flipping; always display original
rules.fix_uikit: image.flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection = false // Preserve logo orientation
rules.quote: Don't flip logos or universal signs and marks.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support default scrolling gestures and keyboard shortcuts; implement elastic behavior users expect.
rules.anti_pattern:
let scrollView = UIScrollView()
scrollView.isScrollEnabled = false // Disables standard gestures
rules.fix_swiftui: ScrollView { ... } // Automatically supports standard gestures
rules.fix_uikit:
scrollView.isScrollEnabled = true
scrollView.bounces = true // Enable elastic behavior
rules.quote: People are accustomed to the systemwide scrolling behavior and expect it to work everywhere.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Make scrollable content apparent by displaying partial content at view edges or visual cues.
rules.fix_swiftui: ScrollView { VStack(spacing: 0) { ForEach(items) { item in Text(item) } } }.scrollIndicators(.visible)
rules.fix_uikit: scrollView.showsVerticalScrollIndicator = true
rules.quote: Because scroll indicators aren't always visible, it can be helpful to make it obvious when content extends beyond the view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never nest scroll views with identical orientation; horizontal inside vertical is acceptable.
rules.fix_uikit: // Use UICollectionView or UITableView instead of nested UIScrollView
rules.quote: Nesting scroll views that have the same orientation can create an unpredictable interface that's difficult to control.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support page-by-page scrolling with fixed content units when appropriate for content structure.
rules.fix_swiftui: ScrollView { VStack { ForEach(pages) { page in PageView(page) } } }.scrollTargetBehavior(.paging)
rules.fix_uikit: scrollView.isPagingEnabled = true
rules.quote: Consider supporting page-by-page scrolling if it makes sense for your content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Set appropriate minimum and maximum zoom scale limits to prevent unusable magnification levels.
rules.anti_pattern:
scrollView.minimumZoomScale = 0.1
scrollView.maximumZoomScale = 10.0 // Single character fills screen
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use reasonable bounds, e.g., 1.0 to 3.0 for text
rules.fix_uikit:
scrollView.minimumZoomScale = 1.0
scrollView.maximumZoomScale = 3.0
rules.quote: If you support zoom, set appropriate maximum and minimum scale values.

rules.heading: Scroll edge effects
rules.rule: Prefer automatic scroll edge effect style; use soft or hard only after thorough testing.
rules.fix_swiftui: ScrollView { content }.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.automatic)
rules.fix_uikit: scrollView.scrollEdgeEffect = UIScrollEdgeEffect(style: .automatic)
rules.quote: Prefer the automatic scroll edge effect style.

rules.heading: Scroll edge effects
rules.rule: Apply scroll edge effects only when scroll view sits behind floating interface elements.
rules.fix_swiftui: ZStack { ScrollView { content }.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.automatic); VStack { FloatingToolbar(); Spacer() } }
rules.quote: Only use a scroll edge effect when a scroll view is behind floating interface elements.

rules.heading: Scroll edge effects
rules.rule: Apply exactly one scroll edge effect per view; maintain consistent height across split-view panes.
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { ScrollView { content1 }.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.automatic); ScrollView { content2 }.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.automatic) }
rules.quote: Apply one scroll edge effect per view.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Show page control in page-by-page scroll mode; hide scroll indicator on same axis to avoid redundancy.
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { ScrollView { content }.scrollTargetBehavior(.paging).scrollIndicators(.hidden); PageControl(currentPage: $page, numberOfPages: pages.count) }
rules.fix_uikit: scrollView.showsVerticalScrollIndicator = false
rules.quote: Consider showing a page control when a scroll view is in page-by-page mode.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use small or mini scroll bars in space-constrained panels; maintain consistent size across all controls.
rules.anti_pattern:
NSScrollView()
// Default scroll bar size in tight panel
rules.quote: When space is tight, you can use smaller scroll bars in panels that need to coexist with other windows.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use placeholder text to reinforce search scope and educate users about searchable content.
rules.anti_pattern: SearchField() // no placeholder text provided
rules.fix_swiftui: .searchable(text: $query, prompt: "Search your library")
rules.fix_uikit: searchBar.placeholder = "Search your library"
rules.quote: Use placeholder text to help people know what they can search for.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Start search immediately as users type to provide continuously refined, responsive results.
rules.anti_pattern: func searchButtonClicked(_ searchBar: UISearchBar) { performSearch() } // only on button tap
rules.fix_swiftui: .onChange(of: query) { performSearch($0) }
rules.fix_uikit: func searchBar(_ searchBar: UISearchBar, textDidChange searchText: String) { performSearch(searchText) }
rules.quote: If possible, start search immediately when a person types.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display recent searches or predictive suggestions to help users search faster.
rules.anti_pattern: // No suggestions shown until user types and results appear
rules.fix_swiftui: .searchSuggestions { suggestedTerms }
rules.fix_uikit: searchResultsController.searchResultsUpdater = self // show suggestions before search begins
rules.quote: Consider showing suggested search terms.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prioritize most relevant results first and categorize them to minimize scrolling.
rules.anti_pattern: results.sorted { $0.id < $1.id } // arbitrary ordering
rules.fix_swiftui: results.sorted { $0.relevanceScore > $1.relevanceScore }
rules.fix_uikit: results.sort { $0.relevanceScore > $1.relevanceScore }
rules.quote: Provide the most relevant search results first to minimize the need for someone to scroll to find what they're looking for.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include a scope bar or filter control to let users narrow search results.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search results shown without filtering options
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Scope", selection: $scope) { ForEach(scopes, id: \.self) { Text($0) } }
rules.fix_uikit: searchController.searchBar.scopeButtonTitles = ["All", "Contacts", "Groups"]
rules.quote: Consider letting people filter search results.

rules.heading: Scope bars and tokens
rules.rule: Use scope bars only for clearly defined, mutually exclusive search categories.
rules.anti_pattern: scopeBar.items = ["All", "Recent", "Starred", "Archived", "Drafts", "Sent"] // too many overlapping categories
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Mailbox", selection: $scope) { ForEach(["All", "Inbox", "Sent"], id: \.self) { Text($0) } }
rules.fix_uikit: searchBar.scopeButtonTitles = ["All", "Inbox", "Sent"]
rules.quote: Use a scope bar to filter among clearly defined search categories.

rules.heading: Scope bars and tokens
rules.rule: Default scope bars to broader scope; let users refine as needed.
rules.anti_pattern: scopeBar.selectedSegmentIndex = 3 // defaulting to narrow scope like "Archived"
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Scope", selection: $scope) { Text("All").tag("all") }.pickerStyle(.segmented)
rules.fix_uikit: searchBar.selectedScopeButtonIndex = 0 // "All" or broadest option
rules.quote: Default to a broader scope and let people refine it as they need.

rules.heading: Scope bars and tokens
rules.rule: Use tokens to visually encapsulate and allow editing of common search filter terms.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search terms shown as plain text without visual distinction
rules.fix_swiftui: TokenField(tokens: $selectedTokens) // encapsulates terms visually
rules.fix_uikit: // Use NSTokenField on macOS or custom token UI on iOS
rules.quote: Use tokens to filter by common search terms or items.

rules.heading: Search as a tab
rules.rule: Use standard tab style to provide suggestions, promote discovery, and encourage exploration.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search tab immediately shows keyboard without landing page or suggestions
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView { SearchLandingView().tabItem { Label("Search", systemImage: "magnifyingglass") } }
rules.fix_uikit: let searchVC = SearchLandingViewController(); tabBarController.viewControllers?.append(searchVC)
rules.quote: Choose the standard tab style to provide suggestions, promote discovery, and encourage exploration.

rules.heading: Search as a tab
rules.rule: Use button appearance style to help users quickly find what they need with immediate keyboard.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search tab navigates to landing page instead of immediately focusing field
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView { SearchButtonView().tabItem { Label("Search", systemImage: "magnifyingglass") } }
rules.fix_uikit: let searchVC = SearchButtonViewController(); tabBarController.viewControllers?.append(searchVC)
rules.quote: Choose the button appearance to help people quickly find what they need.

rules.heading: Search in a toolbar
rules.rule: Place search at bottom toolbar when space allows; prioritizes easy reach.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar.items = [searchItem] // placed at top when bottom space is available
rules.fix_swiftui: .toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .bottomBar) { SearchField() } }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationController?.toolbar.items = [searchBarItem] // bottom placement
rules.quote: Place search at the bottom if there's room.

rules.heading: Search in a toolbar
rules.rule: Place search at top toolbar when bottom content is critical or no bottom toolbar exists.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search placed at bottom, covering critical content like event passes
rules.fix_swiftui: .toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { SearchField() } }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.searchController = UISearchController(searchResultsController: nil)
rules.quote: Place search at the top when itʼs important to defer to content at the bottom of the screen, or thereʼs no bottom toolbar.

rules.heading: Search as an inline field
rules.citation: search-fields.md › Search as an inline field
rules.rule: Position inline search directly above the list it searches; pin to top when scrolling.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search field placed below list or not pinned during scroll
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { SearchField().searchable(text: $query); List { /* content */ } }
rules.fix_uikit: tableView.tableHeaderView = searchBar // pins to top during scroll
rules.quote: When at the top, position an inline search field above the list it searches, and consider pinning it to the top toolbar when scrolling.

rules.heading: Tablet and desktop (iPadOS, macOS)
rules.rule: Place search at trailing side of toolbar for common uses, especially split-view apps.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search placed at leading side or in sidebar instead of toolbar trailing
rules.fix_swiftui: .toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { SearchField() } }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.searchController = UISearchController(searchResultsController: nil)
rules.quote: Put a search field at the trailing side of the toolbar for many common uses.

rules.heading: Tablet and desktop (iPadOS, macOS)
rules.rule: Include search at sidebar top when filtering navigation or content hierarchy.
rules.anti_pattern: // Search placed in toolbar instead of sidebar for deep navigation filtering
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { SearchField().searchable(text: $query); Sidebar() }
rules.fix_uikit: sidebarViewController.view.addSubview(searchBar) // at top of sidebar
rules.quote: Include search at the top of the sidebar when filtering content or navigation there.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Position search prominently in toolbar, tab bar, or primary navigation if search is core to app.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Search") }.padding(.trailing, 100)
rules.fix_swiftui: .toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { SearchField("Search", text: $query) } }
rules.fix_uikit: searchController = UISearchController(searchResultsController: nil); navigationItem.searchController = searchController
rules.quote: If search is important, give it a primary position in your app or view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide one clearly identified search location for app-wide content discovery; use local search only for distinct sections.
rules.anti_pattern: Multiple SearchField instances scattered across different views without clear hierarchy or scope indication.
rules.fix_swiftui: .searchable(text: $query, placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always))
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.searchController = UISearchController(searchResultsController: nil)
rules.quote: Aim to make your app's content searchable through a single location.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display current search scope via placeholder text, scope bar, or title to clarify what is being searched.
rules.anti_pattern: SearchField(text: $query) without any indication of scope or context.
rules.fix_swiftui: SearchField("Search songs", text: $query, prompt: Text("Search in \(currentScope)"))
rules.fix_uikit: searchBar.placeholder = "Search in \(currentScope)"
rules.quote: Clearly display the current scope of a search.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer recent searches or predictive suggestions to reduce typing and accelerate search discovery.
rules.anti_pattern: SearchField(text: $query) with no suggestions or recent search history displayed.
rules.fix_swiftui: .searchSuggestions { ForEach(recentSearches, id: \.self) { suggestion in Text(suggestion) } }
rules.fix_uikit: searchResultsController.updateSearchResults(for: searchController)
rules.quote: Provide suggestions to make searching easier.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide a way to clear search history and consider privacy when displaying it in shared or public contexts.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying all search history without a clear delete option or privacy warning.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { searchHistory.removeAll() }) { Label("Clear History", systemImage: "trash") }
rules.fix_uikit: let clearButton = UIBarButtonItem(title: "Clear", style: .plain, target: self, action: #selector(clearHistory))
rules.quote: Take privacy into consideration before displaying search history.

rules.heading: Systemwide search
rules.rule: Index app content with metadata and make it searchable via Spotlight for system-wide discovery.
rules.anti_pattern: App with rich content but no CoreSpotlight indexing or CSSearchableItem registration.
rules.fix_uikit: let item = CSSearchableItem(uniqueIdentifier: id, domainIdentifier: "com.app.domain", attributeSet: attributes); CSSearchableIndex.default().indexSearchableItems([item], completionHandler: nil)
rules.quote: Make your app's content searchable in Spotlight.

rules.heading: Systemwide search
rules.rule: Supply CSImportExtension Spotlight plug-in for custom file types to enable metadata extraction and indexing.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom file format handled by app but no CSImportExtension defined in Info.plist.
rules.fix_uikit: Define com.apple.spotlight.importer in Info.plist with CSImportExtension class conforming to CSImportExtension protocol
rules.quote: Define metadata for custom file types you handle.

rules.heading: Systemwide search
rules.rule: Integrate Spotlight search within app context to enable advanced file-search capabilities on current selection.
rules.anti_pattern: App with no integration of Spotlight search results or filtering within its own UI.
rules.fix_uikit: let query = CSSearchQuery(queryString: searchTerm, attributes: nil); query.start() to display filtered results
rules.quote: Use Spotlight to offer advanced file-search capabilities within the context of your app.

rules.heading: Systemwide search
rules.rule: Use system-provided open and save views with built-in search instead of custom file dialogs.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom file browser UI without search capability or system integration.
rules.fix_swiftui: FileDocument with .fileImporter or .fileMover modifiers
rules.fix_uikit: UIDocumentPickerViewController(forOpeningContentTypes: [.item])
rules.quote: Prefer using the system-provided open and save views.

rules.heading: Systemwide search
rules.rule: Implement Quick Look generator for custom file types to enable Spotlight and system preview support.
rules.anti_pattern: Custom file format with no QLGenerator or Quick Look preview extension defined.
rules.fix_uikit: Define com.apple.quicklook.thumbnail in Info.plist with QLGenerator class conforming to QLThumbnailProvider
rules.quote: Implement a Quick Look generator if your app produces custom file types.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use segmented control only for closely related choices affecting object, state, or view.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a segmented control for unrelated navigation options like "Home", "Settings", "About".
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker(selection: $choice) { ForEach(relatedOptions) { ... } }.pickerStyle(.segmented)
rules.fix_uikit: UISegmentedControl(items: closelyRelatedChoices) with target-action for state changes.
rules.quote: Use a segmented control to provide closely related choices that affect an object, state, or view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep control types consistent; do not mix action and selection state segments.
rules.anti_pattern: let control = UISegmentedControl(items: ["Select", "Delete", "Share"]); control.addTarget(self, action: #selector(performAction), for: .valueChanged) // mixing selection and action
rules.fix_swiftui: Use separate Picker for selection state or separate Buttons for actions, never both in one segmented control.
rules.fix_uikit: Create either a selection-only UISegmentedControl or use momentary mode for action-only buttons, not both.
rules.quote: Keep control types consistent within a single segmented control.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit segments to five to seven in wide interface, five on iPhone.
rules.anti_pattern: let control = UISegmentedControl(items: ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I", "J"])
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker(selection: $choice) { ForEach(Array(options.prefix(5))) { ... } }.pickerStyle(.segmented)
rules.fix_uikit: UISegmentedControl(items: Array(options.prefix(5)))
rules.quote: Limit the number of segments in a control.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep segment size consistent with equal width and similar icon/title widths.
rules.anti_pattern: Segments with varying content widths: "A", "Very Long Label", "B" causing visual imbalance.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use consistent label lengths or fixed frame widths: Picker { ... }.pickerStyle(.segmented).frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
rules.fix_uikit: Set equal widths via layout constraints or UISegmentedControl.apportionsSegmentWidthsByContent = false
rules.quote: In general, keep segment size consistent.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use either text or images in a single control, not a mix of both.
rules.anti_pattern: let control = UISegmentedControl(items: [UIImage(systemName: "star"), "Text Label", UIImage(systemName: "heart")])
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker(selection: $choice) { ForEach(options) { Label($0.name, systemImage: $0.icon) } }.pickerStyle(.segmented) // all images with labels
rules.fix_uikit: UISegmentedControl(items: [UIImage(systemName: "star"), UIImage(systemName: "heart"), UIImage(systemName: "bolt")])
rules.quote: Prefer using either text or images — not a mix of both — in a single segmented control.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use content with similar size in each segment to maintain visual balance.
rules.anti_pattern: Segments with "X", "Very Long Text", "Y" where content fills some but not others.
rules.fix_swiftui: Ensure all labels have similar character count or use fixed sizing.
rules.fix_uikit: Normalize content widths or use consistent image sizes across all segments.
rules.quote: As much as possible, use content with a similar size in each segment.

rules.heading: Content
rules.rule: Use nouns or noun phrases with title-style capitalization for segment labels.
rules.anti_pattern: let control = UISegmentedControl(items: ["show all", "hide details", "edit mode"])
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker(selection: $choice) { Text("All Items"); Text("Details"); Text("Edit") }.pickerStyle(.segmented)
rules.fix_uikit: UISegmentedControl(items: ["All Items", "Details", "Edit"])
rules.quote: Use nouns or noun phrases for segment labels.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use segmented control to switch between closely related subviews, not separate app sections.
rules.anti_pattern: Using segmented control in main navigation: "Home", "Explore", "Profile" — use TabView instead.
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker(selection: $activeTab) { Text("New Event"); Text("New Reminder") }.pickerStyle(.segmented) for related subviews.
rules.fix_uikit: UISegmentedControl for related subviews; use UITabBarController for separate app sections.
rules.quote: Consider a segmented control to switch between closely related subviews.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use introductory text and labels to clarify segmented control purpose on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern: NSSegmentedControl with only icons and no accompanying text or tooltips.
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("Alignment"); Picker(selection: $alignment) { ... }.pickerStyle(.segmented) }
rules.fix_uikit: Add NSTextField above NSSegmentedControl and set tooltip for each segment via setToolTip.
rules.quote: Consider using introductory text to clarify the purpose of a segmented control.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use tab view in main window area for view switching, not segmented control.
rules.anti_pattern: Using NSSegmentedControl in main window content area for major view switching.
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView(selection: $activeTab) { ... } for main window view switching.
rules.fix_uikit: NSTabView for main window; NSSegmentedControl only in toolbar or inspector.
rules.quote: Use a tab view in the main window area — instead of a segmented control — for view switching.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Support spring loading on Magic Trackpad for segment activation via drag and force click.
rules.anti_pattern: NSSegmentedControl without spring loading support on macOS with Magic Trackpad.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use native Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) which supports spring loading by default.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement NSDraggingDestination protocol and handle spring loading in NSSegmentedControl subclass.
rules.quote: Consider supporting spring loading.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide default settings that deliver the best experience to the largest number of users.
rules.anti_pattern: Launching an app and immediately prompting users to configure performance settings before they can use the app.
rules.quote: Aim to provide default settings that give the best experience to the largest number of people.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Minimize the number of settings offered to avoid overwhelming users and making settings harder to discover.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing 50+ customizable options across multiple nested settings screens.
rules.quote: Minimize the number of settings you offer.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Make settings available using platform-standard access patterns (Command-Comma on macOS, Escape in games).
rules.anti_pattern: Placing settings behind a custom menu icon instead of using Command-Comma keyboard shortcut on macOS.
rules.quote: Make settings available in ways people expect.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid using settings to request setup information obtainable through automatic detection or system state.
rules.anti_pattern: Asking users to manually select a connected controller when the system can auto-detect it.
rules.quote: Avoid using settings to ask for setup information you can get in other ways.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Respect systemwide settings and never duplicate global options like accessibility or authentication in custom settings.
rules.anti_pattern: Adding a custom Dark Mode toggle in app settings that mirrors the system-wide Dark Mode setting.
rules.quote: Respect people's systemwide settings and avoid including redundant versions of them in your custom settings area.

rules.heading: General settings
rules.rule: Place only general, infrequently changed settings in custom settings areas to minimize user interruption.
rules.anti_pattern: Putting frequently-adjusted options like volume or brightness in the settings area instead of in-context controls.
rules.quote: Put general, infrequently changed settings in your custom settings area.

rules.heading: Task-specific options
rules.rule: Provide task-specific options inline within the relevant screen rather than in a separate settings area.
rules.anti_pattern: Requiring users to leave a list view and navigate to settings to access filtering or sorting options.
rules.quote: When possible, prefer letting people modify task-specific options without going to your settings area.

rules.heading: System settings
rules.rule: Add only the most rarely changed options to the system-provided Settings app.
rules.anti_pattern: Exposing every app setting in the system Settings app, cluttering the global settings interface.
rules.quote: Add only the most rarely changed options to the system-provided Settings app.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Include a Settings item in the App menu; avoid adding settings buttons to window toolbars.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing a Settings button in the main window toolbar instead of in the App menu.
rules.fix_uikit: Add NSMenuItem with title 'Settings' to the app's main NSMenu; implement standard Command-Comma action.
rules.quote: Include a settings item in the App menu.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Dim the minimize and maximize buttons in settings windows to discourage persistent docking.
rules.anti_pattern: Leaving minimize and maximize buttons fully enabled in a settings window.
rules.fix_uikit: Set NSWindow.standardWindowButton(.miniaturizeButton).isEnabled = false and maximizeButton.isEnabled = false.
rules.quote: Dim a settings window's minimize and maximize buttons.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use a noncustomizable toolbar in settings windows that always indicates the active pane button.
rules.anti_pattern: Allowing users to customize the settings window toolbar or hiding the active pane indicator.
rules.fix_uikit: Set NSToolbar.allowsUserCustomization = false; ensure active button remains visually highlighted.
rules.quote: In your settings window, use a noncustomizable toolbar that remains visible and always indicates the active toolbar button.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Update the settings window title to reflect the currently visible pane or use 'App Name Settings'.
rules.anti_pattern: Keeping the window title as 'Settings' regardless of which pane is displayed.
rules.fix_uikit: Update NSWindow.title when switching panes; use format 'AppName Settings' for single-pane windows.
rules.quote: Update the window's title to reflect the currently visible pane.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Restore the most recently viewed pane when the settings window reopens.
rules.anti_pattern: Always opening the settings window to the first pane, forcing users to re-navigate to their previous pane.
rules.fix_uikit: Store the active pane identifier in UserDefaults and restore it when the settings window is created.
rules.quote: Restore the most recently viewed pane.

rules.heading: Rendering modes
rules.rule: Confirm symbol rendering mode works well in every context before shipping.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "cloud.sun.rain.fill").symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical).foregroundStyle(.blue)
rules.fix_uikit: let config = UIImage.SymbolConfiguration(hierarchicalColor: .systemBlue); let image = UIImage(systemName: "cloud.sun.rain.fill", withConfiguration: config)
rules.quote: Confirm that a symbol's rendering mode works well in every context.

rules.heading: Rendering modes
rules.rule: Use system-provided colors for symbols to ensure Dark Mode and accessibility adaptation.
rules.anti_pattern:
Image(systemName: "leaf")
  .foregroundColor(Color(red: 0.2, green: 0.8, blue: 0.2))
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "leaf").foregroundStyle(.green)
rules.fix_uikit: let image = UIImage(systemName: "leaf")?.withTintColor(.systemGreen, renderingMode: .alwaysOriginal)
rules.quote: Regardless of rendering mode, using system-provided colors ensures that symbols automatically adapt to accessibility accommodations and appearance modes like vibrancy and Dark Mode.

rules.heading: Gradients
rules.rule: Use gradients on symbols at larger sizes for best visual effect.
rules.anti_pattern:
Image(systemName: "star.fill")
  .font(.system(size: 12))
  .foregroundStyle(LinearGradient(gradient: Gradient(colors: [.blue, .purple]), startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 48)).foregroundStyle(LinearGradient(colors: [.blue, .purple], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
rules.quote: Gradients render for symbols of any size, but look best at larger sizes.

rules.heading: Variable color
rules.rule: Use variable color to communicate change, not depth; use Hierarchical mode for depth.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "speaker.wave.3").symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical).foregroundStyle(.blue)
rules.fix_uikit: let config = UIImage.SymbolConfiguration(hierarchicalColor: .systemBlue); let image = UIImage(systemName: "speaker.wave.3", withConfiguration: config)
rules.quote: Use variable color to communicate change — don't use it to communicate depth.

rules.heading: Weights and scales
rules.rule: Specify symbol scale to adjust emphasis relative to adjacent text without disrupting weight matching.
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Image(systemName: "star.fill").imageScale(.large); Text("Favorite").font(.system(size: 16, weight: .regular)) }
rules.fix_uikit: let config = UIImage.SymbolConfiguration(scale: .large); let image = UIImage(systemName: "star.fill", withConfiguration: config)
rules.quote: Specifying a scale lets you adjust a symbol's emphasis compared to adjacent text, without disrupting the weight matching with text that uses the same point size.

rules.heading: Design variants
rules.rule: Use fill variant for selection and emphasis; use outline variant in toolbars and lists.
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView { Text("Home").tabItem { Label("Home", systemImage: "house.fill") } }
rules.fix_uikit: let tabItem = UITabBarItem(title: "Home", image: UIImage(systemName: "house.fill"), tag: 0)
rules.quote: The solid areas in a fill variant tend to give a symbol more visual emphasis, making it a good choice for iOS tab bars and swipe actions and places where you use an accent color to communicate selection.

rules.heading: Design variants
rules.rule: Use slash variant to show unavailable items or actions; use enclosed variants for small-size legibility.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "speaker.slash") }.disabled(true)
rules.fix_uikit: let button = UIButton(); button.setImage(UIImage(systemName: "speaker.slash"), for: .disabled)
rules.quote: For example, you could use the slash variant of a symbol to show that an item or action is unavailable, or use the fill variant to indicate selection.

rules.heading: Animations
rules.rule: Apply symbol animations judiciously; too many animations overwhelm interface and distract users.
rules.anti_pattern:
Image(systemName: "star.fill")
  .symbolEffect(.bounce)
  .symbolEffect(.pulse)
  .symbolEffect(.rotate)
  .symbolEffect(.scale)
  // Multiple simultaneous animations
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "star.fill").symbolEffect(.bounce, options: .repeat(1))
rules.quote: Apply symbol animations judiciously.

rules.heading: Animations
rules.rule: Ensure animations serve clear purpose in communicating symbol intent; avoid confusing combinations.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle").symbolEffect(.bounce)
rules.quote: Make sure that animations serve a clear purpose in communicating a symbol's intent.

rules.heading: Animations
rules.rule: Use symbol animations to communicate information efficiently without excessive visual space.
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Image(systemName: "arrow.down").symbolEffect(.rotate); Text("Loading...") }
rules.quote: Use symbol animations to communicate information more efficiently.

rules.heading: Custom symbols
rules.rule: Assign negative side margins to custom symbols with badges to aid optical horizontal alignment.
rules.quote: Assign negative side margins to your custom symbol if necessary.

rules.heading: Custom symbols
rules.rule: Test custom symbol animations with all presets; draw whole shapes to preserve layer information.
rules.quote: Test animations for custom symbols.

rules.heading: Custom symbols
rules.rule: Provide alternative text labels for custom symbols to enable VoiceOver accessibility.
rules.anti_pattern:
Image(systemName: "custom.symbol")
// No accessibility label provided
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "custom.symbol").accessibilityLabel("Download")
rules.fix_uikit: let image = UIImage(systemName: "custom.symbol"); image?.accessibilityLabel = "Download"
rules.quote: Provide alternative text labels for custom symbols.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Sheets in iOS/iPadOS can be modal or nonmodal; choose based on whether users need to affect the parent view.
rules.anti_pattern: Always using modal sheets even when users need to interact with the parent view simultaneously.
rules.fix_swiftui: .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) for nonmodal sheets; use .sheet(isPresented:) for modal.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UISheetPresentationController.detents and configure modality via UIModalPresentationStyle.
rules.quote: In iOS and iPadOS, a sheet can be either modal or nonmodal.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Provide Cancel or Close button to dismiss without saving; pair Done button with Cancel or Back.
rules.anti_pattern: Providing only a Done button with no Cancel or Back alternative for dismissal.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add both Button("Cancel") { dismiss() } and Button("Done") { save(); dismiss() } in toolbar.
rules.fix_uikit: Add UIBarButtonItem for Cancel and Done in navigationItem.leftBarButtonItem and rightBarButtonItem.
rules.quote: The Cancel (or Close) button dismisses a sheet without saving any changes.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display only one sheet at a time; close the first sheet before displaying a new one.
rules.anti_pattern: Presenting a second sheet while the first is still visible, causing navigation confusion.
rules.fix_swiftui: Dismiss the first sheet before triggering the second: dismiss(); DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter { isShowingSecond = true }
rules.fix_uikit: Call dismiss(animated:completion:) on the first sheet, then present the second in the completion block.
rules.quote: Display only one sheet at a time from the main interface.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: For complex or prolonged flows, use full-screen modal, separate window, or immersive experience instead of sheet.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a sheet for multi-step document editing, video playback, or camera capture workflows.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .fullScreenCover for videos/photos; consider NavigationStack for multi-step flows.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIModalPresentationStyle.fullScreen for complex workflows; open NSWindow for macOS document editing.
rules.quote: For complex or prolonged user flows, consider alternatives to sheets.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never show Cancel, Done, and Back buttons together; avoid all three simultaneously.
rules.anti_pattern: Toolbar with all three buttons: Cancel, Done, and Back visible at once.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use either (Cancel + Done), (Cancel + Back), or (Done + Back) based on sheet purpose.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure navigationItem with only two of the three button types.
rules.quote: Avoid showing all three buttons — Cancel, Done, and Back — together.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Place Cancel button on leading edge of top toolbar; Done button on trailing edge for single-view sheets.
rules.anti_pattern: Cancel button on trailing edge or Done button on leading edge of sheet toolbar.
rules.fix_swiftui: .toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .navigationBarLeading) { Button("Cancel") {} } ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .navigationBarTrailing) { Button("Done") {} } }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.leftBarButtonItem = cancelButton; navigationItem.rightBarButtonItem = doneButton;
rules.quote: In iOS and iPadOS, for sheets with a single view, the Cancel button belongs on the leading edge of the top toolbar.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Include grabber in resizable sheets to show users they can drag to resize and cycle detents.
rules.anti_pattern: Resizable sheet without a grabber; users cannot visually discover resize capability.
rules.fix_swiftui: .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) automatically includes grabber; ensure it's visible.
rules.fix_uikit: sheetPresentationController.prefersGrabberVisible = true;
rules.quote: Include a grabber in a resizable sheet.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Support medium detent in iPhone sheets for progressive disclosure unless full-height content is essential.
rules.anti_pattern: Forcing sheets to always expand to full height, hiding supplementary content until scroll.
rules.fix_swiftui: .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) to allow both heights.
rules.fix_uikit: sheetPresentationController.detents = [.medium(), .large()];
rules.quote: In an iPhone app, consider supporting the medium detent to allow progressive disclosure of the sheet's content.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Support swiping to dismiss sheets; show confirmation action sheet if unsaved changes exist.
rules.anti_pattern: Disabling swipe-to-dismiss without user confirmation when unsaved changes are present.
rules.fix_swiftui: Allow swipe by default; use .interactiveDismissDisabled(false) and present confirmation alert on swipe.
rules.fix_uikit: Set isModalInPresentation = true only when unsaved changes exist; present UIAlertController to confirm.
rules.quote: Support swiping to dismiss a sheet.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Prefer page or form sheet presentation styles in iPadOS for consistent default sizing and centered layout.
rules.anti_pattern: Using fullScreen or popover styles in iPadOS when page/form sheet would provide better UX.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .sheet with default presentation; SwiftUI adapts to page/form on iPadOS.
rules.fix_uikit: Set modalPresentationStyle = .pageSheet or .formSheet on UIViewController.
rules.quote: Prefer using the page or form sheet presentation styles in an iPadOS app.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Present sheets in reasonable default size appropriate for content; support resizing when beneficial.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoding sheet size too small for content or forcing fixed size when resizing would improve usability.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .frame(minWidth:minHeight:) to set appropriate defaults; allow resizing via window properties.
rules.quote: Present a sheet in a reasonable default size.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Allow users to interact with other app windows without dismissing the sheet first.
rules.anti_pattern: Blocking all other windows until the sheet is dismissed; preventing access to other documents.
rules.fix_swiftui: Ensure sheet does not set isModal = true for non-critical sheets; allow window switching.
rules.quote: Let people interact with other app windows without first dismissing a sheet.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use panel instead of sheet when users need to repeatedly provide input and observe results.
rules.anti_pattern: Using a sheet for find-and-replace or other iterative workflows requiring continuous observation.
rules.quote: Use a panel instead of a sheet if people need to repeatedly provide input and observe results.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Extend content beneath sidebar using horizontal scroll or background extension effect to reinforce separation.
rules.anti_pattern: NavigationView { Sidebar().frame(width: 200) } without backgroundExtensionEffect or scroll, causing content to appear cut off.
rules.quote: To reinforce the separation, you can extend content beneath the sidebar either by letting it horizontally scroll or by applying a background extension effect.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow users to customize sidebar contents and order to reflect their priorities.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoded sidebar items with no edit mode or drag-to-reorder capability.
rules.fix_swiftui: Implement .onMove(perform:) and .onDelete(perform:) on sidebar List or ForEach.
rules.fix_uikit: UICollectionView with drag-and-drop delegates and edit mode.
rules.quote: When possible, let people customize the contents of a sidebar.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use disclosure controls to manage deep content hierarchies and keep sidebar vertical space manageable.
rules.anti_pattern: Sidebar with 5+ levels of nested items all expanded by default, causing excessive scrolling.
rules.fix_swiftui: Wrap nested items in DisclosureGroup(isExpanded:) to collapse/expand sections.
rules.fix_uikit: Use NSOutlineView or UICollectionView with outline layout for collapsible sections.
rules.quote: Using disclosure controls helps keep the sidebar's vertical space to a manageable level.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use SF Symbols or custom symbols instead of bitmap images to represent sidebar items.
rules.anti_pattern: Sidebar items using .png or .jpg bitmap images; Image("myIcon.png").
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "folder.fill") or custom symbol from SF Symbols app.
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName:) for SF Symbols.
rules.quote: SF Symbols provides a wide range of customizable symbols you can use to represent items in your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Allow users to hide and show sidebar using platform-specific interactions; avoid hiding by default.
rules.anti_pattern: Sidebar hidden on app launch with no discoverable toggle; or only accessible via deep settings menu.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .navigationBarLeading) { Button(action: { showSidebar.toggle() }) } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIBarButtonItem with toggle action; or edge swipe gesture recognizer.
rules.quote: Avoid hiding the sidebar by default to ensure that it remains discoverable.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit sidebar hierarchy to two levels maximum; use split view for deeper hierarchies.
rules.anti_pattern: Sidebar with 3+ nested levels: Folders > Subfolders > Items > Subitems all in one sidebar.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use NavigationSplitView with 3 columns: sidebar, content list, detail view.
rules.fix_uikit: UISplitViewController with multiple view controllers.
rules.quote: In general, show no more than two levels of hierarchy in a sidebar.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use succinct, descriptive labels for two-level sidebar groups; omit unnecessary words.
rules.anti_pattern: Sidebar group labels like "All of your favorite saved items and collections" or "The things you have bookmarked".
rules.fix_swiftui: Use concise labels: "Favorites", "Saved", "Collections" instead of verbose descriptions.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UICollectionViewListCell text to short, clear labels.
rules.quote: If you need to include two levels of hierarchy in a sidebar, use succinct, descriptive labels to title each group.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use app accent color for sidebar icons by default; apply fixed colors sparingly for semantic meaning.
rules.anti_pattern: All sidebar icons hardcoded to random colors (red, blue, green) without semantic purpose; or ignoring system accent color on macOS.
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "star.fill").foregroundStyle(.yellow)
rules.fix_uikit: imageView.tintColor = .systemYellow
rules.quote: When they do this, they expect all sidebar icons to appear in that color, so make sure your sidebar icons display the color people choose.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use sidebarAdaptable tab view style to present sidebar or tab bar with automatic platform adaptation.
rules.anti_pattern: Manual if-else logic to switch between TabView and NavigationSplitView based on device; hardcoded sidebar always shown.
rules.fix_swiftui: TabView { ... }.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)
rules.quote: When you use the sidebarAdaptable style of tab view to present a sidebar, you choose whether to display a sidebar or a tab bar when your app opens.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Prefer tab bar over sidebar on mobile; use sidebar style only when tab bar cannot fit all main areas.
rules.anti_pattern: Sidebar as primary navigation on iPhone with only 3-4 main areas that fit in a tab bar.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use TabView with tab bar style first; upgrade to sidebarAdaptable only if more areas needed.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UITabBarController for main navigation.
rules.quote: Consider using a tab bar first.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Apply UICollectionLayoutListConfiguration.Appearance.sidebar when using UIKit collection view for sidebar.
rules.anti_pattern: UICollectionView with default appearance or .plain appearance instead of .sidebar.
