rules.fix_uikit: var config = UICollectionLayoutListConfiguration(appearance: .sidebar); let layout = UICollectionViewCompositionalLayout(section: section(config))
rules.quote: If you're not using SwiftUI to create a sidebar, you can use the UICollectionLayoutListConfiguration.Appearance.sidebar appearance of a collection view list layout.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Sidebar row height, text, and glyph size adapt to small, medium, or large sidebar size; respect user General settings.
rules.anti_pattern: Hardcoded sidebar item height or font size that ignores system sidebar size preference.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .sidebarStyle(.automatic) or .sidebarStyle(.expanded); SwiftUI handles sizing automatically.
rules.fix_uikit: NSSplitViewController automatically respects sidebar size settings.
rules.quote: A sidebar's row height, text, and glyph size depend on its overall size, which can be small, medium, or large.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Automatically hide and reveal sidebar when container window resizes to optimize content space.
rules.anti_pattern: Sidebar remains visible at fixed width even when window is resized to very narrow width, crowding content.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use NavigationSplitView with .navigationSplitViewStyle(.automatic) to auto-collapse on resize.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement NSSplitViewController delegate methods to collapse/expand based on window size.
rules.quote: Consider automatically hiding and revealing a sidebar when its container window resizes.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Avoid placing critical information or actions at sidebar bottom; users may hide bottom edge when moving windows.
rules.anti_pattern: Delete button, logout action, or important status indicator placed at bottom of sidebar.
rules.fix_swiftui: Move critical actions to toolbar or top of sidebar; use bottom area only for secondary options.
rules.fix_uikit: Place critical controls in top sections of sidebar or in window toolbar.
rules.quote: Avoid putting critical information or actions at the bottom of a sidebar.

rules.heading: Offering Sign in with Apple
rules.citation: sign-in-with-apple.md › Offering Sign in with Apple
rules.rule: Display brief, approachable description of sign-in benefits before requesting authentication.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing a Sign in with Apple button without context or explanation of why sign-in is needed.
rules.quote: People need to understand why you're asking them to sign in, so it can work well to display a brief, approachable description of sign-in benefits.

rules.heading: Offering Sign in with Apple
rules.citation: sign-in-with-apple.md › Offering Sign in with Apple
rules.rule: Delay sign-in requests until after users explore core app functionality and understand its value.
rules.anti_pattern: Presenting Sign in with Apple button on app launch before any content is accessible.
rules.quote: People often abandon apps when they're forced to sign in before doing anything useful.

rules.heading: Collecting data
rules.rule: Clearly distinguish required data from optional data and explain why each is needed.
rules.anti_pattern: Requesting additional user data without indicating whether it is required or optional.
rules.quote: Clarify whether the additional data you request is required or just recommended.

rules.heading: Collecting data
rules.rule: Never request a password from users who are actively using Sign in with Apple.
rules.anti_pattern: Prompting users to enter a password after they have authenticated via Sign in with Apple.
rules.quote: Unless people have stopped using Sign in with Apple with your app or website, don't ask for a password.

rules.heading: Collecting data
rules.rule: Respect private relay email addresses and do not request personal email when relay address is provided.
rules.anti_pattern: Asking users for their personal email address after they have chosen to share a private relay address.
rules.quote: It's essential to respect this choice and avoid overriding it by asking for a personal email address.

rules.heading: Displaying buttons
rules.rule: Make Sign in with Apple button no smaller than other sign-in buttons and avoid requiring scrolling.
rules.anti_pattern: Placing a Sign in with Apple button below the fold or making it significantly smaller than competing sign-in options.
rules.quote: Make a Sign in with Apple button no smaller than other sign-in buttons, and avoid making people scroll to see the button.

rules.heading: Using the system-provided buttons
rules.rule: Use system-provided ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton to ensure Apple-approved appearance and accessibility.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a custom button from scratch instead of using ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton from AuthenticationServices framework.
rules.fix_uikit: Use ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton from AuthenticationServices framework.
rules.quote: When you use the system-provided APIs to create a Sign in with Apple button, you get the following advantages.

rules.heading: White
rules.rule: Use white button style exclusively on dark backgrounds with sufficient contrast.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying a white Sign in with Apple button on a light or white background.
rules.fix_swiftui: Set button style to white only when background is dark.
rules.fix_uikit: Set ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton.Style to .white only on dark backgrounds.
rules.quote: Use this style on dark backgrounds that provide sufficient contrast.

rules.heading: Black
rules.rule: Use black button style only on white or light backgrounds; never on black or dark backgrounds.
rules.anti_pattern: Displaying a black Sign in with Apple button on a dark or black background.
rules.fix_swiftui: Set button style to black only when background is white or light.
rules.fix_uikit: Set ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton.Style to .black only on light backgrounds.
rules.quote: Use this style on white or light-color backgrounds that provide sufficient contrast; don't use it on black or dark backgrounds.

rules.heading: Button size and corner radius
rules.citation: sign-in-with-apple.md › Button size and corner radius
rules.rule: Adjust corner radius to match other buttons in app; maintain minimum 140pt width and 30pt height.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a Sign in with Apple button smaller than 140pt wide or 30pt tall, or with inconsistent corner radius.
rules.fix_swiftui: Set .frame(minWidth: 140, minHeight: 30) and .cornerRadius to match app design.
rules.fix_uikit: Set frame to minimum 140x30 points and cornerRadius property to match UI style.
rules.quote: Maintain the minimum button size and margin around the button in iOS, macOS, and the web.

rules.heading: Creating a custom Sign in with Apple button
rules.citation: sign-in-with-apple.md › Creating a custom Sign in with Apple button
rules.rule: Ensure custom button is instantly recognizable as Sign in with Apple; App Review evaluates all custom buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a custom button that deviates significantly from standard appearance, making it unrecognizable.
rules.quote: Always make sure that people can instantly identify your custom button as a Sign in with Apple button.

rules.heading: Creating a custom Sign in with Apple button
rules.citation: sign-in-with-apple.md › Creating a custom Sign in with Apple button
rules.rule: Use only official Apple logo artwork from Apple Design Resources; never create custom Apple logo.
rules.anti_pattern: Designing or drawing a custom Apple logo instead of downloading official artwork from Apple Design Resources.
rules.quote: Use only the logo artwork downloaded from Apple Design Resources; never create a custom Apple logo.

rules.heading: Custom buttons with a logo and text
rules.citation: sign-in-with-apple.md › Custom buttons with a logo and text
rules.rule: Use only approved titles: 'Sign in with Apple', 'Sign up with Apple', or 'Continue with Apple'.
rules.anti_pattern: Using custom button titles like 'Login with Apple' or 'Register with Apple' instead of approved variants.
rules.quote: Use only Sign in with Apple, Sign up with Apple, or Continue with Apple.

rules.heading: Custom logo-only buttons
rules.rule: Maintain 1:1 aspect ratio for logo-only buttons; do not add horizontal padding or crop artwork.
rules.anti_pattern: Cropping the Apple logo artwork or adding extra padding to a logo-only button.
rules.quote: A logo-only Sign in with Apple button always has a 1:1 aspect ratio, and the artwork already includes the correct padding on all sides.

rules.heading: Getting your app to work with Siri
rules.citation: siri.md › Getting your app to work with Siri
rules.rule: Implement App Intents framework to expose app actions and entities to Apple Intelligence and Siri.
rules.anti_pattern:
// App has no App Intents implementation
// Siri cannot discover or invoke app features
rules.quote: In order for an app to work with Siri, the app has to make its features and content available to Apple Intelligence using the App Intents framework.

rules.heading: Getting your app to work with Siri
rules.citation: siri.md › Getting your app to work with Siri
rules.rule: Associate app features with app schema domains for built-in Apple Intelligence logic and natural conversation support.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Custom intent implementation without leveraging existing schema domains
// Misses built-in system knowledge for common domains like email or music
rules.quote: Apps in common domain areas like email, music, or photos can use the system's existing knowledge to access built-in logic for handling requests through a wider range of options with natural conversation and deeper contextual understanding.

rules.heading: Sharing contextual information
rules.rule: Annotate views and content with app entities to provide Siri contextual information about onscreen elements.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Views lack entity annotations
// Siri cannot understand what user refers to during conversation
rules.quote: An app can tell the system what's onscreen by annotating its views and other content with app entities.

rules.heading: Sharing contextual information
rules.rule: Donate app entities to Spotlight index to make content searchable via Spotlight and Siri.
rules.anti_pattern:
// App content never donated to Spotlight
// Users cannot find app data through Spotlight or Siri search
rules.quote: To provide content information to the system, an app can donate entities to the on-device Spotlight index, which makes the app's information available to someone searching in Spotlight or with Siri.

rules.heading: Sharing contextual information
rules.rule: Donate user actions as intents to help Siri anticipate and surface relevant future actions.
rules.anti_pattern:
// No intent donations for user actions
// Siri cannot predict or suggest relevant actions
rules.quote: An app can also tell the system about actions a person takes while using it by donating the actions as intents.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use familiar, natural terminology for content and actions that users recognize and expect.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Intent named "AudioFilePlayable" instead of "Song"
// Users cannot naturally refer to content via Siri
rules.quote: Using language for your features and content that people are most likely to recognize makes interacting with your app through Siri more natural and intuitive.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Donate only personally relevant content to Spotlight, not entire app catalog.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Donate all 10,000 products to Spotlight
// Clutters search results with irrelevant items
rules.quote: Instead of telling Spotlight about all of your app's content, consider things that are particularly relevant to someone's personal context — things they've recently searched for, their favorite items or bookmarks, or the content of a wishlist.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never include advertisements, marketing, or in-app purchase pitches in Siri-delivered content.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Siri response includes: "Try our premium plan for $9.99!"
// Violates Siri content guidelines
rules.quote: Don't include advertisements, marketing, or in-app purchase sales pitches in content that Siri delivers.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide custom Siri responses only when built-in responses are insufficient.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Custom response for every standard action
// Overrides Siri's natural language handling
rules.quote: Only provide a custom response if built-in responses don't meet your app's needs.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Write Siri response dialogue that is clear, descriptive, and conveys action outcomes precisely.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Response: "Which one?"
// Ambiguous and unclear to user
rules.quote: An effective response clearly conveys what happens when Siri performs the action.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Keep Siri responses succinct and context-aware to avoid repetitive or irritating dialogue.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Response: "I'm about to play your favorite song, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' by Queen, which is 5 minutes and 55 seconds long, released in 1975..."
// Verbose and repetitive
rules.quote: Keep responses as succinct as possible.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Design Siri responses to work both audibly and visually without depending on visual elements for essential information.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Response relies on visual chart; audio says "See the graph above"
// Fails for audio-only contexts like AirPods
rules.quote: Provide responses that Siri can deliver audibly and visually.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Avoid unnecessary pronouns in Siri responses to create inclusive interactions.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Response: "What's his or her name?"
// Assumes gender; excludes non-binary users
rules.quote: Create welcoming interactions for everyone by avoiding specific pronouns when they're not necessary.

rules.heading: Editorial guidelines
rules.rule: Never impersonate Siri or reproduce Siri functionality; do not use reserved phrases like 'Call 911' or 'Hey Siri'.
rules.anti_pattern:
// App response: "Hey Siri here, calling 911 for you"
// Impersonates Siri and uses reserved phrases
rules.quote: Never impersonate Siri, attempt to reproduce the functionality that Siri provides, or provide a response that appears to come from Apple.

rules.heading: Editorial guidelines
rules.rule: Omit app name from Siri responses; system provides verbal and visual attribution.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Response: "MyApp has completed your order"
// Redundantly includes app name
rules.quote: Omit your app name from responses.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Customize slider appearance to blend with app design and communicate intent.
rules.anti_pattern:
let slider = UISlider()
// Using default appearance without customization for domain-specific meaning
rules.fix_swiftui: Slider(value: $value, in: 0...100).tint(.blue)
rules.fix_uikit: slider.minimumTrackTintColor = .systemBlue; slider.maximumTrackTintColor = .systemGray5
rules.quote: You can adjust a slider's appearance — including track color, thumb image and tint color, and left and right icons — to blend with your app's design and communicate intent.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place minimum values on leading side and maximum on trailing side for horizontal sliders.
rules.anti_pattern: Slider(value: $value, in: 100...0) // Reversed range breaks convention
rules.fix_swiftui: Slider(value: $value, in: 0...100)
rules.fix_uikit: slider.minimumValue = 0; slider.maximumValue = 100
rules.quote: People expect the minimum and maximum sides of sliders to be consistent in all apps, with minimum values on the leading side and maximum values on the trailing side (for horizontal sliders) and minimum values at the bottom and maximum values at the top (for vertical sliders).

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Supplement sliders with text field and stepper for wide value ranges.
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Slider(value: $value, in: 0...1000); TextField("Value", value: $value, format: .number); Stepper("", value: $value) }
rules.quote: Especially when a slider represents a wide range of values, people may appreciate seeing the exact slider value and having the ability to enter a specific value in a text field.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Never use slider for audio volume control; use volume view instead.
rules.anti_pattern: Slider(value: $volume, in: 0...1) // For audio volume adjustment
rules.fix_swiftui: MPVolumeView()
rules.fix_uikit: let volumeView = MPVolumeView(frame: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 200, height: 50))
rules.quote: Don't use a slider to adjust audio volume.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use tick marks in macOS sliders to help users pinpoint specific values.
rules.anti_pattern: NSSlider() // Without tick marks for value clarity
rules.quote: Sliders in macOS can also include tick marks, making it easier for people to pinpoint a specific value within the range.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Provide live feedback as slider value changes to show results in real time.
rules.fix_swiftui: Slider(value: $value, in: 0...100).onChange(of: value) { updatePreview($0) }
rules.fix_uikit: slider.addTarget(self, action: #selector(sliderValueChanged), for: .valueChanged)
rules.quote: Live feedback shows people results in real time.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use horizontal slider for fixed start/end ranges; circular slider for repeating values.
rules.anti_pattern: // Using horizontal slider for 0-360 degree rotation
rules.fix_swiftui: // Use circular slider for rotation or repeating values
rules.quote: A horizontal slider is ideal when moving between a fixed starting and ending point. Use circular sliders when values repeat or continue indefinitely.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use sentence-style capitalization for slider labels ending with colon.
rules.anti_pattern: Label("OPACITY LEVEL:", systemImage: "circle.fill")
rules.fix_swiftui: Label("Opacity level:", systemImage: "circle.fill")
rules.fix_uikit: label.text = "Opacity level:"
rules.quote: Labels generally use sentence-style capitalization and end with a colon.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Add tick mark labels for clarity; label minimum and maximum at minimum.
rules.anti_pattern: NSSlider() // With tick marks but no labels
rules.quote: It's unnecessary to label every tick mark unless doing so is needed to reduce confusion. In many cases, labeling only the minimum and maximum values is sufficient.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Provide tooltip showing thumb value when pointer hovers over slider.
rules.anti_pattern: NSSlider() // Without tooltip on hover
rules.fix_uikit: slider.toolTip = "Current value: \(slider.doubleValue)"
rules.quote: It's also a good idea to provide a tooltip that displays the value of the thumb when people hold their pointer over it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure sufficient contrast between custom content and system background in light and dark modes.
rules.anti_pattern: Using gray text on light gray background or low-contrast colors without testing both appearances.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use semantic colors like .primary, .secondary; test with .preferredColorScheme(.light/.dark); maintain WCAG AA contrast ratios.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIColor.label, UIColor.secondaryLabel; test with UITraitCollection.current.userInterfaceStyle.
rules.quote: Check for sufficient contrast between the snippet's custom content and the system-provided background in both light and dark appearances, and keep consistent margins for the content within the view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit custom view height to maximum 400 points; omit content exceeding this constraint.
rules.anti_pattern: Creating a snippet custom view with frame(maxHeight: 600) or content that exceeds 400 points.
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply .frame(maxHeight: 400) to the custom view; deep-link to app for additional details.
rules.fix_uikit: Set heightAnchor.constraint(lessThanOrEqualToConstant: 400); truncate or paginate content.
rules.quote: To ensure all content is visible, create custom views that are no taller than the 400-point maximum height.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use descriptive, action-specific labels for confirmation snippet primary buttons instead of generic labels.
rules.anti_pattern: Labeling a coffee-ordering confirmation button 'OK', 'Proceed', or 'Continue' instead of 'Order'.
rules.fix_swiftui: Set confirmationActionName to a specific verb matching the intent (e.g., 'Order', 'Send', 'Schedule').
rules.quote: You can choose an appropriate label from among those that the system provides, or you can supply a custom label. For example, when designing a snippet to order coffee, labeling the primary button Order is clearer than labeling it OK or Proceed.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Communicate snippet purpose visually via custom view; do not rely solely on dialogue text in visual representation.
rules.anti_pattern: Designing a snippet that displays only the Siri dialogue text without a meaningful custom view.
rules.fix_swiftui: Create a rich custom view that conveys the snippet's purpose independently; omit dialogue from visual display.
rules.quote: Don't rely on showing the dialogue text to convey a snippet's purpose. While the spoken app intent dialogue is essential for interactions when someone isn't looking at the screen, prefer to omit it from a snippet's visual representation and use the custom view to convey its information instead.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep snippet content concise and legible; deep-link to app for detailed information in result snippets.
rules.anti_pattern: Packing a result snippet with paragraphs of text, tables, or complex layouts instead of summarizing.
rules.fix_swiftui: Limit text to 1–2 lines; use Link(destination:) to deep-link to full content in app.
rules.quote: Snippets exist to facilitate lightweight, quick interactions, so it's important to keep their content short and easily legible. For a result snippet, if you need to provide more detail, deep-link to the content in your app instead of including it in the custom view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Account for user's preferred text size setting when sizing snippet content.
rules.anti_pattern: Using fixed font sizes or hardcoded line heights that don't scale with Dynamic Type.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .font(.body), .font(.caption); test with .dynamicTypeSize(.xxxLarge).
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:); set adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true.
rules.quote: When considering the amount of text to include, be mindful that fonts draw at various sizes based on a person's preferred text size setting.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Persistently highlight the current selection in each pane that leads to the detail view.
rules.anti_pattern: NavigationSplitView { ... } without applying .tag() or selection binding to visually distinguish the active item in the sidebar.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @State var selection and apply .tag(item) to NavigationLink, ensuring selected state renders with distinct background or accent color.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UISplitViewController.primaryBackgroundStyle and ensure UITableViewCell.isSelected updates the cell's appearance via UITableViewDelegate.didSelectRowAt.
rules.quote: To support navigation, persistently highlight the current selection in each pane that leads to the detail view.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Consider letting people drag and drop content between panes to move content across hierarchy levels.
rules.anti_pattern: Split view with no drag-and-drop support; users cannot move items between the sidebar and detail panes.
rules.fix_swiftui: Implement .onDrop(of:delegate:) and .onDrag() modifiers on list items to enable cross-pane content movement.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UITableViewDropDelegate and UITableViewDragDelegate on both source and destination table views.
rules.quote: Consider letting people drag and drop content between panes.

rules.heading: Phone (iOS)
rules.rule: Use split view only in regular horizontal size class, not compact (portrait iPhone).
rules.anti_pattern: NavigationSplitView { ... } displayed on iPhone in portrait without checking horizontalSizeClass or hiding the sidebar.
rules.fix_swiftui: Wrap NavigationSplitView in a conditional: if horizontalSizeClass == .regular { NavigationSplitView { ... } } else { NavigationStack { ... } }
rules.fix_uikit: Check traitCollection.horizontalSizeClass and use UISplitViewController only when .regular; use UINavigationController for compact.
rules.quote: Prefer using a split view in a regular — not a compact — environment.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Design split view layout to adapt to narrow, compact, and intermediate iPad window widths.
rules.anti_pattern: NavigationSplitView with fixed pane widths that break or truncate content when iPad window is resized to narrow width.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use GeometryReader to measure available width and conditionally show/hide panes or adjust column visibility based on size classes.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UISplitViewControllerDelegate.splitViewController(_:collapseSecondaryViewController:onto:) to handle width transitions.
rules.quote: Account for narrow, compact, and intermediate window widths.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Set reasonable defaults for minimum and maximum pane sizes to keep dividers visible and usable.
rules.anti_pattern: VSplitView { ... } without setting minValue/maxValue constraints, allowing panes to collapse and hide the divider.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .frame(minWidth:maxWidth:) on each pane to enforce minimum width (e.g., 100pt) and maximum width constraints.
rules.fix_uikit: Set NSSplitView.setPosition(_:ofDividerAt:) with minWidth and maxWidth via NSSplitViewDelegate.splitView(_:constrainMinCoordinate:ofSubviewAt:).
rules.quote: Set reasonable defaults for minimum and maximum pane sizes.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Consider letting people hide panes when it reduces distractions or provides more editing space.
rules.anti_pattern: Split view with all panes always visible; no option to hide the navigator or inspector pane.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add @State var showNavigator and conditionally include panes: if showNavigator { ... }; provide toolbar button to toggle.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement NSSplitViewDelegate to collapse/expand panes and add toolbar button with action to toggle pane visibility.
rules.quote: Consider letting people hide a pane when it makes sense.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Provide multiple ways (toolbar button, menu command, keyboard shortcut) to reveal hidden panes.
rules.anti_pattern: Hidden pane with no visible UI control or keyboard shortcut to restore it; users cannot discover how to show it.
rules.fix_swiftui: Add toolbar button with .keyboardShortcut() and menu item in app menu that both toggle @State var showPane.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement toolbar button action and NSMenuItem with keyEquivalent that call NSSplitView.setPosition(_:ofDividerAt:).
rules.quote: Provide multiple ways to reveal hidden panes.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Prefer thin divider style (1 point width) unless strong linear elements require thicker divider for distinction.
rules.anti_pattern: VSplitView or NSSplitView with thick divider style applied by default without justification.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use default divider style; if customization needed, apply minimal thickness via .frame(width: 1).
rules.fix_uikit: Set NSSplitView.dividerStyle = .thin; only use .thick if table rows on both sides have strong linear elements.
rules.quote: Prefer the thin divider style.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place blurred view behind status bar using scroll edge effect to keep status bar readable.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Text("Header") }.ignoresSafeArea() // Content bleeds under transparent status bar
rules.fix_swiftui: ScrollView { ... }.scrollEdgeEffect(.automatic, edges: .top)
rules.fix_uikit: scrollView.scrollEdgeEffect = UIScrollEdgeEffect(style: .automatic)
rules.quote: Prefer using a scroll edge effect to place a blurred view behind the status bar.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not make content behind status bar appear interactive when it is not.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap me") }.frame(maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top) // Button appears under status bar
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Spacer().frame(height: 44) // Safe area inset; Button(action: {}) { Text("Tap me") } }
rules.fix_uikit: button.frame = CGRect(x: 0, y: UIApplication.shared.statusBarFrame.height, width: 100, height: 44)
rules.quote: If controls are visible behind the status bar, people may attempt to interact with them and be unable to do so.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Temporarily hide status bar only during full-screen media; provide discoverable gesture to restore.
rules.anti_pattern: override var prefersStatusBarHidden: Bool { true } // Permanently hidden, no way to restore
rules.fix_swiftui: @State var isHidden = false; var body: some View { ZStack { ... }.statusBar(hidden: isHidden).onTapGesture { isHidden.toggle() } }
rules.fix_uikit: override var prefersStatusBarHidden: Bool { isViewingFullScreenPhoto } // Toggle on tap gesture
rules.quote: Temporarily hide these elements to provide a more immersive experience.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never permanently hide the status bar; always allow users to restore it with a simple gesture.
rules.anti_pattern: override var prefersStatusBarHidden: Bool { true } // No way to show time or connectivity info
rules.fix_swiftui: @State var statusBarHidden = false; .onTapGesture { statusBarHidden.toggle() }
rules.fix_uikit: let tapGesture = UITapGestureRecognizer(target: self, action: #selector(toggleStatusBar)); view.addGestureRecognizer(tapGesture)
rules.quote: Avoid permanently hiding the status bar.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Place stepper adjacent to a labeled field that displays the current value being modified.
rules.anti_pattern: Stepper("Quantity", value: $count) without a Text or TextField showing the actual value nearby.
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Text("Quantity: \(count)"); Stepper("", value: $count) }
rules.fix_uikit: Add UILabel displaying the value next to UIStepper in the same container view.
rules.quote: A stepper sits next to a field that displays its current value, because the stepper itself doesn't display a value.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Pair stepper with text field when users may need to enter large or varied values directly.
rules.anti_pattern: Stepper alone for a printing dialog where users frequently enter arbitrary page counts or copy quantities.
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { TextField("Copies", value: $copies, format: .number); Stepper("", value: $copies, in: 1...999) }
rules.fix_uikit: Add UITextField alongside UIStepper for direct numeric input.
rules.quote: Consider pairing a stepper with a text field when large value changes are likely.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure the label or context makes clear which value the stepper modifies.
rules.anti_pattern: Multiple steppers in a form without distinct labels; ambiguous which field each stepper controls.
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Text("Font Size"); Stepper("", value: $fontSize) } with clear labeling.
rules.fix_uikit: Assign descriptive accessibilityLabel to UIStepper; place near labeled UILabel.
rules.quote: Make the value that a stepper affects obvious.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Support Shift-click on macOS steppers to increment by 10× the default step for large value ranges.
rules.anti_pattern: NSStepper without Shift-click handling; users forced to click many times for large adjustments.
rules.fix_swiftui: Stepper with custom onEditingChanged or gesture handling to detect Shift modifier.
rules.quote: For large value ranges, consider supporting Shift-click to change the value quickly.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use tab bars for navigation between sections, not for actions; use toolbars for controls.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { ... }.tabItem { Button("Action") { performAction() } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Move action buttons to .toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { Button(...) } }
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIToolbar or UIBarButtonItem for actions, reserve UITabBarController for section navigation.
rules.quote: A tab bar lets people navigate among different sections of an app, like the Alarm, Stopwatch, and Timer tabs in the Clock app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Keep tab bar visible during navigation; hide only when modal views cover it temporarily.
rules.anti_pattern: navigationController?.hidesBarsOnSwipe = true // hides tab bar during scroll
rules.fix_swiftui: Use modal sheets or fullScreenCover for temporary overlays; keep TabView visible in main navigation.
rules.fix_uikit: Set hidesBottomBarWhenPushed = true only for modal presentations, not regular navigation.
rules.quote: If you hide the tab bar, people can forget which area of the app they're in.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Limit tab count to match app hierarchy complexity; prefer fewer tabs or sidebar for complex structures.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { ForEach(1...12, id: \.self) { i in Text("Tab \(i)").tabItem { Label("T\(i)", systemImage: "\(i).circle") } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Reduce to 4–5 primary tabs; use NavigationSplitView or sidebar for additional sections.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure UITabBarController with ≤5 viewControllers; use UISplitViewController for complex hierarchies.
rules.quote: As a representation of your app's hierarchy, it's important to weigh the complexity of additional tabs against the need for people to frequently access each section; keep in mind that it's generally easier to navigate among fewer tabs.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid overflow tabs; limit visible tabs to prevent More tab and hidden content.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { ForEach(tabs, id: \.id) { tab in ... } } // 8+ tabs on iPhone causes More tab
rules.fix_swiftui: Keep tab count ≤5 on iPhone; use tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable) on iPad for overflow.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure UITabBarController with ≤5 items; use moreNavigationController only as fallback.
rules.quote: If horizontal space limits the number of visible tabs, the trailing tab becomes a More tab in iOS and iPadOS, revealing the remaining items in a separate list.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never disable or hide tab bar buttons; always show all tabs even if content is empty.
rules.anti_pattern: tabItem.isEnabled = false // when section has no data
rules.fix_swiftui: Keep all tabs enabled; show empty state message explaining why content is unavailable.
rules.fix_uikit: Keep all UITabBarItems enabled; display UIViewController with empty state view.
rules.quote: Don't disable or hide tab bar buttons, even when their content is unavailable.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include tab labels beneath or beside icons; use single words for clarity.
rules.anti_pattern: .tabItem { Image(systemName: "star.fill") } // no label
rules.fix_swiftui: .tabItem { Label("Favorites", systemImage: "star.fill") }
rules.fix_uikit: tabBarItem = UITabBarItem(title: "Favorites", image: UIImage(systemName: "star.fill"), tag: 0)
rules.quote: A tab label appears beneath or beside a tab bar icon, and can aid navigation by clearly describing the type of content or functionality the tab contains.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use SF Symbols for tab bar icons; prefer filled symbols for platform consistency.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("custom-icon") // custom raster icon instead of SF Symbol
rules.fix_swiftui: Label("Home", systemImage: "house.fill")
rules.fix_uikit: UIImage(systemName: "house.fill")
rules.quote: When you use SF Symbols, tab bar icons automatically adapt to different contexts.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use badges only for critical information; reserve for new or updated content requiring attention.
rules.anti_pattern: tabItem.badgeValue = "5" // for every notification, diluting impact
rules.fix_swiftui: .badge(unreadCount > 0 ? "!" : nil) // only for critical alerts
rules.fix_uikit: tabBarItem.badgeValue = criticalAlert ? "!" : nil
rules.quote: Reserve badges for critical information so you don't dilute their impact and meaning.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid similar colors between tab labels and content backgrounds; use monochromatic or high-contrast accent colors.
rules.anti_pattern: UITabBar().tintColor = .systemBlue // with bright blue content layer
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .foregroundStyle(.gray) for tabs with colorful content; or choose accent with high contrast.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UITabBar.tintColor to monochromatic or sufficiently differentiated accent.
rules.quote: If your app already has bright, colorful content in the content layer, prefer a monochromatic appearance for tab bars, or choose an accent color with sufficient visual differentiation.

rules.heading: Phone (iOS)
rules.rule: Position tab bar at bottom of screen on iPhone; use Liquid Glass background allowing content peek-through.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { ... }.tabViewStyle(.page) // page style instead of bottom tab bar
rules.fix_swiftui: Use default TabView style (bottom tab bar with Liquid Glass on iOS).
rules.fix_uikit: UITabBarController automatically positions tab bar at bottom with system materials.
rules.quote: A tab bar floats above content at the bottom of the screen.

rules.heading: Phone (iOS)
rules.rule: For tab bars with accessories (e.g., MiniPlayer), support minimize behavior on scroll.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { ... } // no minimize behavior for attached accessory
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply .tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.automatic) to TabView with accessory.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UITabBarController.minimizeBehavior = .automatic for attached accessories.
rules.quote: For tab bars with an attached accessory, like the MiniPlayer in Music, you can choose to minimize the tab bar and move the accessory inline with it when a person scrolls down.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: On iPad, display tab bar at top; support conversion to sidebar via tabViewStyle modifier.
rules.anti_pattern: TabView { ... } // uses default bottom tab bar on iPad
rules.fix_swiftui: .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable) or .tabViewStyle(.tabBarOnly) for top positioning.
rules.fix_uikit: Configure UITabBarController; use UISplitViewController for sidebar conversion.
rules.quote: The system displays a tab bar near the top of the screen.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Prefer tab bar for primary navigation; offer sidebar conversion for complex apps.
rules.anti_pattern: Always use sidebar on iPad regardless of app complexity.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable) to let users convert tab bar to sidebar.
rules.fix_uikit: Start with UITabBarController; migrate to UISplitViewController if needed.
rules.quote: A tab bar provides access to the sections of your app that people use most.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Allow users to customize tab bar by selecting frequently used items; default to ≤5 tabs.
rules.anti_pattern: Fixed tab bar with no customization option.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use TabViewCustomization to enable user-driven tab selection and reordering.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UITab.Placement customization for user-preferred tab visibility.
rules.quote: If you let people select their own tabs, aim for a default list of five or fewer to preserve continuity between compact and regular view sizes.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use tab views only to present closely related, mutually exclusive content areas.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTabView with unrelated tabs like Settings, Help, and Debug logs.
rules.quote: Use a tab view to present closely related areas of content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Ensure controls within a pane affect only that pane's content, not other tabs.
rules.anti_pattern: A checkbox in Tab A that filters data displayed in Tab B.
rules.quote: Make sure the controls within a pane affect content only in the same pane.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Label each tab with a descriptive noun or short noun phrase in title-case capitalization.
rules.anti_pattern: Tab labels like "click here", "data", or "settingsPanel" without title case.
rules.quote: Provide a label for each tab that describes the contents of its pane.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use tabbed controls instead of pop-up buttons for tab switching when feasible.
rules.anti_pattern: Replacing NSTabView with an NSPopUpButton to switch between content panes.
rules.quote: Avoid using a pop-up button to switch between tabs.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never provide more than six tabs in a single tab view.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTabView with 8 or more tabs displayed simultaneously.
rules.quote: Avoid providing more than six tabs in a tab view.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: Inset tab views with a margin of window-body area on all sides for clean layout.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTabView extending to all window edges without inset margins.
rules.quote: In general, inset a tab view by leaving a margin of window-body area on all sides of a tab view.

rules.heading: Anatomy
rules.rule: When hiding the tabbed control, choose borderless, bezeled, or line-bordered content area styling.
rules.anti_pattern: Hiding NSTabView's control without defining a clear visual boundary for the content area.
rules.quote: When you hide the tabbed control, the content area can be borderless, bezeled, or bordered with a line.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use TextField for small amounts of text; use TextEditor or TextViews for larger text input.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Enter your bio", text: $bio) // for multi-paragraph user biography
rules.fix_swiftui: TextEditor(text: $bio) // for larger text blocks
rules.fix_uikit: UITextView instead of UITextField for multi-line content
rules.quote: Use a text field to request a small amount of information, such as a name or an email address.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Always use SecureField for sensitive data like passwords, never plain TextField.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Password", text: $password) // exposes password in plaintext
rules.fix_swiftui: SecureField("Password", text: $password)
rules.fix_uikit: textField.isSecureTextEntry = true
rules.quote: Always use a secure text field when your app asks for sensitive data, such as a password.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Size text field width to match anticipated input quantity to guide user expectations.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Name", text: $name).frame(width: 500) // for a 3-character field
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Name", text: $name).frame(width: 120) // proportional to expected input
rules.fix_uikit: textField.frame.size.width = 120 // match content expectations
rules.quote: To the extent possible, match the size of a text field to the quantity of anticipated text.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Stack multiple text fields vertically with consistent spacing and widths for organized layout.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { TextField("First", text: $first); TextField("Last", text: $last) } // horizontal stacking
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(spacing: 16) { TextField("First", text: $first); TextField("Last", text: $last) }.frame(maxWidth: 300)
rules.fix_uikit: stackView.axis = .vertical; stackView.spacing = 16
rules.quote: Stack multiple text fields vertically when possible, and use consistent widths to create a more organized layout.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Include placeholder text or separate label to communicate field purpose before user types.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("", text: $email) // no hint about expected content
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Email", text: $email) // placeholder text visible when empty
rules.fix_uikit: textField.placeholder = "Email"
rules.quote: Show a hint in a text field to help communicate its purpose.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Validate field data at appropriate times: on field exit for email, before exit for passwords.
rules.anti_pattern: // No validation until form submission
rules.fix_swiftui: .onChange(of: email) { newValue in validateEmail(newValue) } // validate on change
rules.fix_uikit: textFieldDidEndEditing(_:) // validate when focus leaves field
rules.quote: Validate fields when it makes sense.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use NumberFormatter for numeric input to restrict to digits and format appropriately.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Amount", text: $amount) // accepts any character
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Amount", value: $amount, format: .number) // numeric-only input
rules.fix_uikit: let formatter = NumberFormatter(); textField.formatter = formatter
rules.quote: Use a number formatter to help with numeric data.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Configure line breaks to clip, wrap, or truncate text based on field requirements.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Name", text: $name) // default clips without indication
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Name", text: $name).lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.tail)
rules.fix_uikit: textField.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
rules.quote: Adjust line breaks according to the needs of the field.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use expansion tooltip on macOS to reveal full text when field content is clipped.
rules.anti_pattern: // Clipped text with no way to view full content
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Name", text: $name).help(name) // tooltip shows full text on hover
rules.quote: Consider using an expansion tooltip to show the full version of clipped or truncated text.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Display appropriate keyboard type matching content type (numbers, URLs, email, etc.).
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Phone", text: $phone).keyboardType(.default) // shows full QWERTY
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Phone", text: $phone).keyboardType(.phonePad)
rules.fix_uikit: textField.keyboardType = .phonePad
rules.quote: In iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, and visionOS apps, show the appropriate keyboard type.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Display Clear button in trailing end of text field to allow quick content erasure.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Search", text: $query) // no clear button, user must tap Delete repeatedly
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Search", text: $query).clearButtonMode(.whileEditing)
rules.fix_uikit: textField.clearButtonMode = .whileEditing
rules.quote: Display a Clear button in the trailing end of a text field to help people erase their input.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use leading images to indicate field purpose; trailing images/buttons for additional features.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Search", text: $query) // no visual affordance for purpose or actions
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Image(systemName: "magnifyingglass"); TextField("Search", text: $query); Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "bookmark") } }
rules.fix_uikit: textField.leftView = UIImageView(image: UIImage(systemName: "magnifyingglass"))
rules.quote: Use images and buttons to provide clarity and functionality in text fields.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use ComboBox when pairing text input with predefined list of choices on macOS.
rules.anti_pattern: TextField("Country", text: $country) // no list of valid options
rules.fix_swiftui: ComboBox(selection: $country, options: countries) // text input + dropdown list
rules.quote: Consider using a combo box if you need to pair text input with a list of choices.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use text views for long, editable, or specially formatted text; prefer labels or text fields for small amounts.
rules.anti_pattern: Using TextEditor to display a single line of static text or a short label.
rules.fix_swiftui: Replace with Text() for static content or TextField() for single-line editable input.
rules.fix_uikit: Replace UITextView with UILabel for static text or UITextField for single-line input.
rules.quote: Use a text view when you need to display text that's long, editable, or in a special format.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Maintain text legibility by adopting Dynamic Type and testing with accessibility options enabled.
rules.anti_pattern: TextEditor with fixed font size: TextEditor(text: $content).font(.system(size: 14))
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .font(.body) or .font(.system(.body, design: .default)) to respect Dynamic Type.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UITextView.font using UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:) instead of fixed sizes.
rules.quote: It's a good idea to adopt Dynamic Type so your text still looks good if people change text size on their device.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Enable text selection for useful information like error messages, serial numbers, or IP addresses.
rules.anti_pattern: TextEditor(text: $content).disabled(true) for read-only display of copyable data.
rules.fix_swiftui: Use TextEditor with isEditable: false but selectable: true, or apply .textSelection(.enabled).
rules.fix_uikit: Set UITextView.isSelectable = true and UITextView.isEditable = false for read-only copyable content.
rules.quote: If a text view contains useful information such as an error message, a serial number, or an IP address, consider letting people select and copy it for pasting elsewhere.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Set the appropriate keyboard type for the content being entered to streamline data entry.
rules.anti_pattern: TextEditor(text: $email) without specifying .keyboardType(.emailAddress)
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply .keyboardType(.emailAddress) for email, .keyboardType(.numberPad) for numbers, etc.
rules.fix_uikit: Set UITextView.keyboardType = .emailAddress or appropriate UIKeyboardType value.
rules.quote: To streamline data entry, the keyboard you display when editing a text view needs to be appropriate for the type of content.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support default system-defined menus in standard order; never hide unavailable items, disable them instead.
rules.anti_pattern: if !canCopy { menu.removeItem(copyMenuItem) } // Hiding instead of disabling
rules.fix_uikit: copyMenuItem.isEnabled = canCopy
rules.quote: Always show the same set of menu items.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use system standard icons for common actions like Copy, Share, Delete; reuse icons consistently across UI.
rules.anti_pattern: let customCopyIcon = NSImage(named: "my_copy_icon") // Custom icon for standard action
rules.fix_uikit: let copyIcon = NSImage(systemSymbolName: "doc.on.doc", accessibilityDescription: nil)
rules.quote: Use the same icons as the system to represent actions such as Copy, Share, and Delete, wherever they appear.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support keyboard shortcuts defined for standard menu items; define custom shortcuts only when necessary.
rules.anti_pattern: copyMenuItem.keyEquivalent = "c" // Overriding standard Cmd+C
rules.fix_uikit: copyMenuItem.keyEquivalent = "c"; copyMenuItem.keyEquivalentModifierMask = .command
rules.quote: People expect to use the keyboard shortcuts they already know for standard menu items, like Copy, Cut, Paste, Save, and Print.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use short, one-word menu titles; if multi-word, apply title-style capitalization.
rules.anti_pattern: menu.title = "copy and paste options" // Multi-word, lowercase
rules.fix_uikit: menu.title = "Edit" // One word, or "Copy and Paste" with title case
rules.quote: Prefer short, one-word menu titles.

rules.heading: App menu
rules.rule: Display About menu item first with separator after it; use app name ≤16 characters without version number.
rules.anti_pattern: aboutItem.title = "About MyApplication v2.1.0" // Too long, includes version
rules.fix_uikit: aboutItem.title = "About MyApp"; menu.insertItem(NSMenuItem.separator(), at: 1)
rules.quote: Display the About menu item first.

rules.heading: File menu
rules.rule: Use descriptive item type in New menu (e.g., 'New Event', 'New Calendar'), not generic 'New Document'.
rules.anti_pattern: newItem.title = "New" // Generic, unclear what is created
rules.fix_uikit: newItem.title = "New Event" // Specific to app domain
rules.quote: For *Item*, use a term that names the type of item your app creates.

rules.heading: File menu
rules.rule: In Open Recent submenu, display document names not file paths; order by most-recently-opened first.
rules.anti_pattern: recentItem.title = "/Users/name/Documents/project/file.txt" // Full path shown
rules.fix_uikit: recentItem.title = "file.txt" // Filename only, ordered by recency
rules.quote: List document and filenames that people recognize in the submenu; don't display file paths.

rules.heading: File menu
rules.rule: Prefer Duplicate over Save As, Export, Copy To, Save To; clarifies relationship between original and new file.
rules.anti_pattern: menu.addItem(withTitle: "Save As...", action: #selector(saveAs), keyEquivalent: "")
rules.fix_uikit: menu.addItem(withTitle: "Duplicate", action: #selector(duplicate), keyEquivalent: "")
rules.quote: Prefer Duplicate to menu items like Save As, Export, Copy To, and Save To because these items don't clarify the relationship between the original file and the new one.

rules.heading: Edit menu
rules.rule: Clarify Undo/Redo targets by appending action name (e.g., 'Undo Paste and Match Style', 'Undo Typing').
rules.anti_pattern: undoItem.title = "Undo" // Generic, no context
rules.fix_uikit: undoItem.title = "Undo Paste and Match Style" // Specific action appended
rules.quote: Clarify the target of the undo.

rules.heading: Edit menu
rules.rule: Use 'Delete' menu item, not 'Erase' or 'Clear', to match Delete key naming consistency.
rules.anti_pattern: menu.addItem(withTitle: "Clear", action: #selector(clear), keyEquivalent: "")
rules.fix_uikit: menu.addItem(withTitle: "Delete", action: #selector(delete), keyEquivalent: "")
rules.quote: Provide a Delete menu item instead of an Erase or Clear menu item.

rules.heading: View menu
rules.rule: Provide View menu even if app supports only subset of standard view functions (e.g., full-screen only).
rules.anti_pattern: // Omit View menu entirely if app has no toolbar
rules.fix_uikit: viewMenu.addItem(withTitle: "Enter Full Screen", action: #selector(enterFullScreen), keyEquivalent: "")
rules.quote: Provide a View menu even if your app supports only a subset of the standard view functions.

rules.heading: View menu
rules.rule: Reflect current state in show/hide item titles: 'Show Toolbar' when hidden, 'Hide Toolbar' when visible.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbarItem.title = "Toggle Toolbar" // Doesn't reflect current state
rules.fix_uikit: toolbarItem.title = isToolbarVisible ? "Hide Toolbar" : "Show Toolbar"
rules.quote: Ensure that each show/hide item title reflects the current state of the corresponding view.

rules.heading: App-specific menus
rules.rule: Provide app-specific menus for custom commands; list in menu bar even if available elsewhere in UI.
rules.anti_pattern: // Omit History menu from menu bar; only expose via context menu
rules.fix_uikit: menuBar.addItem(withTitle: "History", action: nil); historyMenu.addItems(...)
rules.quote: Provide app-specific menus for custom commands.

rules.heading: Window menu
rules.rule: Provide Window menu even if app has only one window; include Minimize and Zoom for Full Keyboard Access.
rules.anti_pattern: // Omit Window menu if app is single-window
rules.fix_uikit: windowMenu.addItem(withTitle: "Minimize", action: #selector(minimize), keyEquivalent: "m")
rules.quote: Provide a Window menu even if your app has only one window.

rules.heading: Dynamic menu items
rules.rule: Avoid making dynamic menu item the only way to accomplish a task; offer alternative UI paths.
rules.anti_pattern: // Only expose 'Minimize All' via Option+click; no other way to minimize all
rules.fix_uikit: minimizeAllItem.isAlternate = true; // Also provide UI button for minimize all
rules.quote: Avoid making a dynamic menu item the only way to accomplish a task.

rules.heading: Dynamic menu items
rules.rule: Require only single modifier key to reveal dynamic menu item; avoid multi-key combinations.
rules.anti_pattern: item.keyEquivalentModifierMask = [.command, .shift, .option] // Three modifiers
rules.fix_uikit: item.keyEquivalentModifierMask = .option // Single modifier only
rules.quote: Require only a single modifier key to reveal a dynamic menu item.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Ensure all app functions accessible via UI; don't rely on menu bar as catch-all for hidden functionality.
rules.anti_pattern: // Advanced feature only in menu bar, no UI button or alternative access
rules.fix_uikit: // Provide UI button in addition to menu bar item for all functions
rules.quote: Because the menu bar is often hidden when running an app full screen, ensure that people can access all of your app's functions through its UI.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Reserve YourAppName > Settings for opening app's page in iPadOS Settings; link internal prefs separately.
rules.anti_pattern: settingsItem.title = "Settings"; settingsItem.action = openInternalPreferences
rules.fix_uikit: settingsItem.title = "Settings"; settingsItem.action = openIPadOSSettings; // Separate item for internal prefs
rules.quote: Reserve the YourAppName > Settings menu item for opening your app's page in iPadOS Settings.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use toggles only for binary state choices; use other components for multi-option selection.
rules.anti_pattern: Toggle { } // used to select from 3+ items instead of Picker
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker(selection: $value) { ForEach(options) { ... } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIPickerView or UISegmentedControl for multi-option selection
rules.quote: A toggle always lets people manage the state of something, so if you need to support other types of actions — such as choosing from a list of items — use a different component, like a pop-up button.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Communicate toggle state visually with shape, fill, or icon changes; never rely on color alone.
rules.anti_pattern: // Only changing color from gray to red for on/off state
rules.fix_swiftui: Toggle(isOn: $value) { Label("Setting", systemImage: isValue ? "checkmark.circle.fill" : "circle") }
rules.fix_uikit: UISwitch with onTintColor + custom appearance for additional visual cues
rules.quote: Make sure the visual differences in a toggle's state are obvious.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use switch toggle style only within list rows; use toggle buttons elsewhere.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Toggle("Setting", isOn: $value).toggleStyle(.switch) } // outside list
rules.fix_swiftui: List { Toggle("Setting", isOn: $value).toggleStyle(.switch) }
rules.fix_uikit: UITableViewCell with UISwitch, or UIButton with changesSelectionAsPrimaryAction outside lists
rules.quote: Use the switch toggle style only in a list row.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Preserve default green switch color unless app accent color provides sufficient contrast.
rules.anti_pattern: Toggle(isOn: $value).tint(.red) // arbitrary color change
rules.fix_swiftui: Toggle(isOn: $value).tint(.accentColor) // or omit for default green
rules.fix_uikit: uiSwitch.onTintColor = UIColor.systemGreen // or app accent with contrast check
rules.quote: Change the default color of a switch only if necessary.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Outside lists, use toggle buttons with icons and background changes, not switches.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Toggle("Filter", isOn: $filtered).toggleStyle(.switch) }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { filtered.toggle() }) { Image(systemName: "line.3.horizontal.decrease") }.foregroundStyle(.blue)
rules.fix_uikit: UIButton with changesSelectionAsPrimaryAction and custom background for states
rules.quote: Outside of a list, use a button that behaves like a toggle, not a switch.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Place toggles in window body only; avoid toolbar, status bar, or window frame.
rules.anti_pattern: ToolbarItem { Toggle("Setting", isOn: $value) }
rules.fix_swiftui: Form { Toggle("Setting", isOn: $value) } // in window body
rules.fix_uikit: NSButton in NSView, not NSToolbar or NSStatusBar
rules.quote: Use switches, checkboxes, and radio buttons in the window body, not the window frame.

rules.heading: Switches
rules.rule: Prefer switches for high-emphasis settings controlling multiple features; use checkboxes for single settings.
rules.anti_pattern: Toggle("Bold", isOn: $bold).toggleStyle(.switch) // single setting
rules.fix_swiftui: Toggle("Bold", isOn: $bold) // default checkbox style for single setting
rules.quote: Prefer a switch for settings that you want to emphasize.

rules.heading: Switches
rules.rule: Use mini switches in grouped forms for consistent row height; regular switches for primary settings.
rules.anti_pattern: Form { Toggle("Setting", isOn: $value).toggleStyle(.switch) } // default size in grouped form
rules.fix_swiftui: Form { Toggle("Setting", isOn: $value).toggleStyle(.switch).controlSize(.mini) }
rules.quote: Within a grouped form, consider using a mini switch to control the setting in a single row.

rules.heading: Checkboxes
rules.rule: Use checkboxes to present hierarchical settings with alignment and indentation for dependencies.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Toggle("Parent", isOn: $p); Toggle("Child", isOn: $c) } // no visual hierarchy
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(alignment: .leading) { Toggle("Parent", isOn: $p); Toggle("Child", isOn: $c).padding(.leading, 20) }
rules.quote: Use a checkbox instead of a switch if you need to present a hierarchy of settings.

rules.heading: Checkboxes
rules.rule: Reflect mixed checkbox state when subordinate checkboxes have differing states.
rules.anti_pattern: // Parent checkbox always on/off, ignoring mixed state of children
rules.fix_swiftui: Toggle("All Styles", isOn: $allOn).onChange(of: allOn) { updateChildren() }
rules.quote: Accurately reflect a checkbox's state in its appearance.

rules.heading: Radio buttons
rules.rule: Use radio buttons for 2–5 mutually exclusive options; use Picker for more than five.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { ForEach(1...10, id: \.self) { i in Toggle("Option \(i)", isOn: $selected) } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Picker("Option", selection: $selected) { ForEach(1...10, id: \.self) { Text("Option \($0)") } }
rules.quote: Avoid listing too many radio buttons in a set.

rules.heading: Radio buttons
rules.rule: For single on/off setting, prefer checkbox over single radio button for clarity.
rules.anti_pattern: // Single radio button to toggle setting on/off
rules.fix_swiftui: Toggle("Enable Feature", isOn: $enabled) // checkbox style
rules.quote: To present a single setting that can be on or off, prefer a checkbox.

rules.heading: Radio buttons
rules.rule: Use consistent horizontal spacing for radio buttons; measure longest label and apply uniformly.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Button("A") { }; Button("Very Long Option") { }; Button("B") { } } // inconsistent spacing
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack(spacing: 24) { ForEach(options) { opt in Button(opt) { } } }
rules.quote: Use consistent spacing when you display radio buttons horizontally.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide context menus on tokens to offer additional options or information.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTokenField with tokens that have no contextual menu or right-click support.
rules.quote: People often benefit from a context menu with additional options or information about a token.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support multiple text-to-token conversion triggers beyond comma (e.g., Return key).
rules.anti_pattern: NSTokenField configured to convert text to tokens only on comma input.
rules.quote: By default, text people enter turns into a token whenever they type a comma. You can specify additional shortcuts, such as pressing Return, that also invoke this action.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Adjust token suggestion delay to avoid distracting users during typing.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTokenField with completionDelay set to 0, showing suggestions immediately while user types.
rules.quote: If your app suggests tokens, consider adjusting the delay to a comfortable level.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Choose toolbar items deliberately; define which items move to overflow menu as toolbar narrows.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("A") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("B") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("C") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("D") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .automatic placement for secondary items; define explicit overflow behavior via ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .secondaryAction).
rules.fix_uikit: Set toolbarItems array with only essential items; use UIBarButtonItem.SystemItem.flexibleSpace to manage layout.
rules.quote: People need to be able to distinguish and activate each item, so you don't want to put too many items in the toolbar.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Do not manually add overflow menu; system automatically manages it in macOS and iPadOS.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom overflow menu added manually in toolbar
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove custom overflow implementation; rely on system-managed ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .secondaryAction).
rules.fix_uikit: Remove custom UIMenu overflow; system UIBarButtonItem automatically overflows.
rules.quote: The system automatically adds an overflow menu in macOS or iPadOS when items no longer fit. Don't add an overflow menu manually, and avoid layouts that cause toolbar items to overflow by default.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Reduce custom toolbar backgrounds and tinted controls; use content layer color and ScrollEdgeEffectStyle instead.
rules.anti_pattern: .toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Action") {} }.background(Color.blue) } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Remove custom .background modifiers; use .scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.automatic) on ScrollView to distinguish toolbar from content.
rules.fix_uikit: Avoid UIToolbar.appearance().barTintColor; use system defaults and UIScrollView.scrollEdgeAppearance.
rules.quote: Any custom backgrounds and appearances you use might overlay or interfere with background effects that the system provides.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid applying similar color to toolbar item labels and content layer backgrounds.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Text("Action").foregroundColor(.blue) } } // content also bright blue
rules.fix_swiftui: Use default monochromatic toolbar appearance; prefer .foregroundStyle(.primary) or system defaults.
rules.fix_uikit: Use system tintColor; avoid custom tintColor matching content background.
rules.quote: If your app already has bright, colorful content in the content layer, prefer using the default monochromatic appearance of toolbars.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer standard components in toolbar; ensure custom components have corner radii concentric with bar corners.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 4).overlay(Text("Custom")) } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use Button, TextField, or standard SwiftUI components; if custom, apply .cornerRadius matching toolbar design.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIButton, UITextField; custom views must match UIToolbar corner radius.
rules.quote: By default, standard buttons, text fields, headers, and footers have corner radii that are concentric with bar corners.

rules.heading: Titles
rules.rule: Provide useful window title; avoid titling with app name alone.
rules.anti_pattern: navigationItem.title = "MyApp"
rules.fix_swiftui: .navigationTitle("Current Note") or .navigationTitle("") if context is clear.
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.title = "Inbox" or leave empty if content provides context.
rules.quote: Don't title windows with your app name. Your app's name doesn't provide useful information about your content hierarchy or any window or area in your app, so it doesn't work well as a title.

rules.heading: Titles
rules.rule: Write concise title under 15 characters; distill window or view purpose.
rules.anti_pattern: navigationItem.title = "This is a very long title that describes everything"
rules.fix_swiftui: .navigationTitle("Inbox")
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.title = "Drafts"
rules.quote: Aim for a word or short phrase that distills the purpose of the window or view, and keep the title under 15 characters long so you leave enough room for other controls.

rules.heading: Navigation
rules.rule: Use standard Back and Close buttons with standard symbols; do not use text labels.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .navigationBarLeading) { Button("Back") { navigationController?.popViewController(animated: true) } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use NavigationStack with automatic back button; customize via .navigationBackButtonHidden(false).
rules.fix_uikit: Use UINavigationController default back button or backBarButtonItem with Image(systemName: "chevron.left").
rules.quote: Prefer the standard symbols for each, and don't use a text label that says Back or Close.

rules.heading: Actions
rules.rule: Provide actions supporting main tasks; prioritize frequently used or highest-level commands.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Obscure Feature") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Save") {} } // core action
rules.fix_uikit: toolbarItems = [UIBarButtonItem(barButtonSystemItem: .save, target: self, action: #selector(save))]
rules.quote: In general, prioritize the commands that people are most likely to want.

rules.heading: Actions
rules.rule: Make toolbar item meaning clear; prefer recognizable symbols over ambiguous text.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("X") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Image(systemName: "xmark") }
rules.fix_uikit: UIBarButtonItem(image: UIImage(systemName: "xmark"), style: .plain, target: self, action: #selector(close))
rules.quote: Don't make people guess or experiment to figure out what a toolbar item does.

rules.heading: Actions
rules.rule: Use .prominent style for key actions like Done or Submit; place on trailing side.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Done") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) { Button("Done") {}.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent) }
rules.fix_uikit: UIBarButtonItem(title: "Done", style: .done, target: self, action: #selector(done))
rules.quote: Use the `.prominent` style for key actions such as Done or Submit. This separates and tints the action so there's a clear focal point.

rules.heading: Item groupings
rules.rule: Group toolbar items logically by function and frequency of use.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Save") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Delete") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Format") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .principal) { Button("Save") {}; Button("Delete") {} } // group related actions
rules.fix_uikit: toolbarItems = [saveButton, deleteButton, formatButton] // ordered by function
rules.quote: Group toolbar items logically by function and frequency of use.

rules.heading: Item groupings
rules.rule: Group navigation controls and critical actions in dedicated, visually distinct sections.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Back") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Edit") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .navigationBarLeading) { Button("Back") {} }; ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .principal) { Button("Edit") {} }
rules.fix_uikit: navigationItem.leftBarButtonItem = backButton; toolbarItems = [editButton]
rules.quote: Group navigation controls and critical actions like Done, Close, or Save in dedicated, familiar, and visually distinct sections.

rules.heading: Item groupings
rules.rule: Keep actions with text labels separate; insert fixed space between text-labeled buttons.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Save") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Delete") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .principal) { Button("Save") {}; Spacer().frame(width: 8); Button("Delete") {} }
rules.fix_uikit: toolbarItems = [saveButton, UIBarButtonItem.SystemItem.fixedSpace, deleteButton]
rules.quote: If your toolbar includes multiple text-labeled buttons, the text of those buttons may appear to run together, making the buttons indistinguishable. Add separation by inserting fixed space between the buttons.

rules.heading: Phone (iOS)
rules.rule: Prioritize only most important items for main toolbar; create More menu for additional items.
rules.anti_pattern: toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("A") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("B") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("C") {} }; ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("D") {} } }
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Save") {} }; ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .secondaryAction) { Button("Archive") {}; Button("Delete") {} }
rules.fix_uikit: toolbarItems = [saveButton]; moreButton with UIMenu containing archive, delete actions.
rules.quote: Because space is so limited, carefully consider which actions are essential to your app and include those first.

rules.heading: Phone (iOS)
rules.rule: Use large title to help people stay oriented as they navigate and scroll.
rules.anti_pattern: navigationItem.title = "Inbox" // standard title only
rules.fix_swiftui: .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.large)
rules.fix_uikit: navigationController?.navigationBar.prefersLargeTitles = true
rules.quote: By default, a large title transitions to a standard title as people begin scrolling the content, and transitions back to large when people scroll to the top, reminding them of their current location.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Make every toolbar item available as command in menu bar; toolbar cannot be only place for commands.
rules.anti_pattern: // Save action only in toolbar, not in File menu
rules.fix_swiftui: ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Button("Save") { save() } } // also add to File menu
rules.quote: Make every toolbar item available as a command in the menu bar. Because people can customize the toolbar or hide it, it can't be the only place that presents a command.

rules.heading: Ensuring legibility
rules.rule: Use minimum font sizes: 11pt (iOS/iPadOS), 10pt (macOS) for all text.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Small text").font(.system(size: 9))
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Small text").font(.system(size: 11))
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 11)
rules.quote: Follow the recommended default and minimum text sizes for each platform — for both custom and system fonts — to ensure your text is legible on all devices.

rules.heading: Ensuring legibility
rules.rule: Avoid Ultralight, Thin, and Light font weights; prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Header").fontWeight(.thin)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Header").fontWeight(.semibold)
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 17, weight: .semibold)
rules.quote: In general, avoid light font weights. For example, if you're using system-provided fonts, prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold font weights, and avoid Ultralight, Thin, and Light font weights, which can be difficult to see, especially when text is small.

rules.heading: Conveying hierarchy
rules.rule: Adjust font weight, size, and color to emphasize important information and maintain visual hierarchy.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Text("Title").font(.body); Text("Subtitle").font(.title) }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("Title").font(.title).fontWeight(.bold); Text("Subtitle").font(.body) }
rules.fix_uikit: titleLabel.font = UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 28, weight: .bold)
rules.quote: Adjust font weight, size, and color as needed to emphasize important information and help people visualize hierarchy.

rules.heading: Conveying hierarchy
rules.rule: Minimize the number of typefaces used; avoid mixing many different typefaces in one interface.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Text("A").font(.custom("Helvetica", size: 16)); Text("B").font(.custom("Georgia", size: 16)); Text("C").font(.custom("Courier", size: 16)) }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("A").font(.system(size: 16)); Text("B").font(.system(size: 16)); Text("C").font(.system(size: 16)) }
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIFont.systemFont consistently across all labels
rules.quote: Minimize the number of typefaces you use, even in a highly customized interface.

rules.heading: Using system fonts
rules.rule: Use Font.Design.default or Font.Design.serif; do not embed system fonts in your app.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Body").font(.custom("SFPro-Regular", size: 17))
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Body").font(.system(design: .default))
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 17)
rules.quote: You can use the constants defined in Font.Design to access all system fonts — don't embed system fonts in your app or game.

rules.heading: Using system fonts
rules.rule: Use built-in text styles (body, headline, caption) to ensure Dynamic Type and accessibility support.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Content").font(.system(size: 17))
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Content").font(.body)
rules.fix_uikit: label.font = UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body)
rules.quote: Consider using the built-in text styles. The system-defined text styles give you a convenient and consistent way to convey your information hierarchy through font size and weight.

rules.heading: Using system fonts
rules.rule: Use loose leading for wide columns; use tight leading only for constrained single-line or two-line text.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Long passage").lineSpacing(0)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Long passage").lineSpacing(4)
rules.fix_uikit: paragraphStyle.lineSpacing = 4
rules.quote: For example, when you display text in wide columns or long passages, more space between lines (loose leading) can make it easier for people to keep their place while moving from one line to the next.

rules.heading: Using custom fonts
rules.rule: Custom fonts must implement Dynamic Type and accessibility features (Bold Text, Larger Text).
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Custom").font(.custom("MyFont", size: 17))
rules.fix_swiftui: Apply custom font with .dynamicTypeSize modifier and respond to accessibility settings
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIContentSizeCategoryDidChangeNotification observer for custom fonts
rules.quote: If you use a custom font, make sure it implements the same behaviors.

rules.heading: Supporting Dynamic Type
rules.rule: Set numberOfLines to 0 or use .lineLimit(.max) to prevent text truncation at large font sizes.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Long text").lineLimit(1)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Long text").lineLimit(.max)
rules.fix_uikit: label.numberOfLines = 0
