rules.quote: You can prevent text truncation in a label by configuring it to use as many lines as needed to display a useful amount of text.

rules.heading: Supporting Dynamic Type
rules.rule: Scale meaningful interface icons with Dynamic Type; use SF Symbols for automatic scaling.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(systemName: "star").font(.system(size: 16))
rules.fix_swiftui: Image(systemName: "star").font(.body)
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIImage(systemName:) with preferredFont size
rules.quote: When you use SF Symbols, you get icons that scale automatically with Dynamic Type size changes.

rules.heading: Supporting Dynamic Type
rules.rule: At large font sizes, use stacked layouts instead of inline items to prevent text crowding and truncation.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Text("Title"); Text("12:30 PM") }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(alignment: .leading) { Text("Title"); Text("12:30 PM").font(.caption) }
rules.fix_uikit: Use vertical UIStackView for large accessibility categories
rules.quote: To improve readability, consider using a stacked layout where text appears above secondary items.

rules.heading: Supporting Dynamic Type
rules.rule: Maintain consistent information hierarchy at all font sizes; keep primary elements at the top.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Spacer(); Text("Primary"); Text("Secondary") }
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) { Text("Primary").font(.title); Text("Secondary").font(.body) }
rules.fix_uikit: Arrange primary views before secondary views in view hierarchy
rules.quote: Maintain a consistent information hierarchy regardless of the current font size.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Use dynamic system font variants (controlContentFont, labelFont, systemFont) to match standard macOS controls.
rules.anti_pattern: NSTextField().font = NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: 13)
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Label").font(.system(size: 13))
rules.fix_uikit: textField.font = NSFont.controlContentFont(ofSize: 13)
rules.quote: When necessary, use dynamic system font variants to match the text in standard controls.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Describe undo/redo results in alerts or menu labels to help users predict outcomes.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAlertController(title: "Undo?", message: nil, preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.fix_swiftui: .alert("Undo Typing", isPresented: $showUndoAlert) { Button("Undo") { } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: "Undo Typing", message: nil, preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.quote: Help people predict the results of undo and redo as much as possible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Highlight or scroll to show the result of undo/redo when the affected content is off-screen.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Undo deletion silently without scrolling to restored paragraph
undoManager?.undo()
rules.fix_swiftui: ScrollViewReader { proxy in proxy.scrollTo(restoredParagraphID, anchor: .center) }
rules.fix_uikit: scrollView.scrollRectToVisible(restoredParagraphFrame, animated: true)
rules.quote: Show the results of an undo or redo.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Support unlimited undo/redo without arbitrary limits on action count.
rules.anti_pattern: if undoManager.undoCount < 10 { undoManager.registerUndo(...) }
rules.fix_swiftui: undoManager?.registerUndo(withTarget: self) { _ in self.revert() }
rules.fix_uikit: undoManager?.registerUndo(withTarget: self, selector: #selector(revert))
rules.quote: Let people undo multiple times.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Consider grouping related incremental actions into a single undo step.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Each slider adjustment registers separate undo
slider.onChange { value in undoManager?.registerUndo(...) }
rules.fix_swiftui: undoManager?.beginUndoGrouping(); adjustments.forEach { undoManager?.registerUndo(...) }; undoManager?.endUndoGrouping()
rules.fix_uikit: undoManager?.beginUndoGrouping(); adjustments.forEach { undoManager?.registerUndo(...) }; undoManager?.endUndoGrouping()
rules.quote: Consider giving people the option to revert multiple changes at once.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide undo/redo buttons only when necessary; prefer system-supported methods.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("Undo") { undoManager?.undo() }.frame(width: 44, height: 44)
rules.fix_swiftui: // Rely on keyboard shortcuts and system gestures; omit dedicated buttons
rules.fix_uikit: // Use Edit menu and keyboard shortcuts instead of toolbar buttons
rules.quote: Provide undo and redo buttons only when necessary.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Do not redefine three-finger swipe or shake gestures for undo/redo.
rules.fix_swiftui: // Allow system to handle three-finger swipe and shake; do not override
rules.fix_uikit: // Allow system to handle three-finger swipe and shake; do not override
rules.quote: Avoid redefining standard gestures for undo and redo.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Provide concise one- or two-word descriptions after "Undo " or "Redo " prefix in alerts.
rules.anti_pattern: UIAlertController(title: "Undo the action that was just performed", message: nil, preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.fix_swiftui: .alert("Undo Name", isPresented: $showAlert) { Button("Undo") { } }
rules.fix_uikit: UIAlertController(title: "Undo Name", message: nil, preferredStyle: .alert)
rules.quote: Briefly and precisely describe the operation to be undone or redone.

rules.heading: Desktop (macOS)
rules.rule: Place undo and redo commands in the Edit menu with Command–Z and Shift–Command–Z shortcuts.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Undo only accessible via custom toolbar button
Button("Undo") { undoManager?.undo() }
rules.fix_swiftui: CommandGroup(replacing: .undoRedo) { Button("Undo") { undoManager?.undo() }.keyboardShortcut("z", modifiers: .command) }
rules.quote: Place undo and redo commands in the Edit menu and support the standard keyboard shortcuts.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Match keyboard type to content being edited; use semantic text input types for automatic system optimization.
rules.anti_pattern:
TextField("Email", text: $email)
  .keyboardType(.default)
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Email", text: $email).keyboardType(.emailAddress).textContentType(.emailAddress)
rules.fix_uikit: textField.keyboardType = .emailAddress; textField.textContentType = .emailAddress
rules.quote: Choose a keyboard that matches the type of content people are editing.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Customize Return key type to clarify the text-entry action and match app context.
rules.anti_pattern:
TextField("Search", text: $query)
  .keyboardType(.default)
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Search", text: $query).submitLabel(.search)
rules.fix_uikit: textField.returnKeyType = .search
rules.quote: Consider customizing the Return key type if it helps clarify the text-entry experience.

rules.heading: Custom input views
rules.rule: Ensure custom input views provide clear benefits and make sense within app context to avoid user confusion.
rules.fix_swiftui:
// Custom input view with app-specific functionality (e.g., Numbers spreadsheet entry)
@State var customInputView: UIInputViewController? = SpecializedNumericEntry()
rules.quote: Make sure your custom input view makes sense in the context of your app.

rules.heading: Custom input views
rules.rule: Play standard keyboard sound on key taps in custom input views for familiar tactile feedback.
rules.anti_pattern:
// Custom input view with no sound feedback
button.addTarget(self, action: #selector(handleKeyTap), for: .touchUpInside)
rules.fix_uikit: UIDevice.current.playInputClick()
rules.quote: Play the standard keyboard sound while people type.

rules.heading: Custom keyboards
rules.rule: Provide obvious, intuitive keyboard-switching mechanism matching Globe key behavior of system keyboard.
rules.quote: Provide an obvious and easy way to switch between keyboards.

rules.heading: Custom keyboards
rules.rule: Avoid duplicating system Emoji/Globe and Dictation keys that appear automatically beneath custom keyboards.
rules.fix_uikit:
// Omit Emoji/Globe and Dictation keys; system provides them automatically
// Only include custom keys specific to your keyboard
rules.quote: Avoid duplicating system-provided keyboard features.

rules.heading: Custom keyboards
rules.rule: Provide in-app keyboard tutorial explaining selection, activation, usage, and switching back to standard keyboard.
rules.quote: Consider providing a keyboard tutorial in your app.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Use keyboard layout guide to keep important interface elements visible and integrate keyboard as part of layout.
rules.fix_uikit: view.keyboardLayoutGuide.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: scrollView.bottomAnchor).isActive = true
rules.quote: Use the keyboard layout guide to make the keyboard feel like an integrated part of your interface.

rules.heading: Mobile (iOS, iPadOS)
rules.rule: Position custom controls above keyboard thoughtfully; apply Liquid Glass for visual consistency with system appearance.
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Input", text: $text).toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard) { Button("Action") { } } }
rules.fix_uikit: textField.inputAccessoryView = UIToolbar(frame: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: view.bounds.width, height: 44))
rules.quote: Place custom controls above the keyboard thoughtfully.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Provide descriptive accessibility labels for all key interface elements beyond system defaults.
rules.anti_pattern: Button() { Text("✓") } // No accessibilityLabel provided
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Text("✓") }.accessibilityLabel("Confirm action")
rules.fix_uikit: button.accessibilityLabel = "Confirm action"
rules.quote: VoiceOver uses alternative labels (which aren't visible onscreen) to audibly describe your app's interface.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Provide accessibility descriptions for all meaningful images that convey content information.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("chart") // No accessibility description for content-bearing image
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("chart").accessibilityLabel("Sales trend showing 25% growth")
rules.fix_uikit: imageView.accessibilityLabel = "Sales trend showing 25% growth"
rules.quote: If you don't describe key images in your app's content, people can't use VoiceOver to fully experience them within your app.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Provide concise descriptions of infographics and make interactive elements accessible to VoiceOver.
rules.anti_pattern: Chart { /* interactive chart with no accessibility */ }
rules.fix_swiftui: Chart { /* ... */ }.accessibilityLabel("Monthly revenue chart").accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
rules.fix_uikit: chartView.accessibilityLabel = "Monthly revenue chart"; chartView.accessibilityElements = [...]
rules.quote: Provide a concise description of each infographic that explains what it conveys.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Hide decorative images from VoiceOver to reduce cognitive load and respect user time.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("decorativeBorder").accessibilityLabel("Border") // Unnecessary for VoiceOver
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("decorativeBorder").accessibilityHidden(true)
rules.fix_uikit: decorativeImageView.isAccessibilityElement = false
rules.quote: Excluding these images shows respect for people's time and reduces cognitive load when they use VoiceOver.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Provide unique, descriptive titles and headings that convey page purpose and information structure.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Page").font(.title) // Generic title without accessibility context
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Sales Report Q4 2024").font(.title).accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)
rules.fix_uikit: titleLabel.accessibilityTraits = .header; titleLabel.accessibilityLabel = "Sales Report Q4 2024"
rules.quote: The title is the first information someone receives from an assistive technology when arriving on a page or screen in your app.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Explicitly describe visual relationships between elements to VoiceOver using grouping and ordering.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Image("photo"); Text("Caption") } // VoiceOver reads image, then caption separately
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Image("photo"); Text("Caption") }.accessibilityElement(children: .combine).accessibilityLabel("Photo with caption")
rules.fix_uikit: containerView.shouldGroupAccessibilityChildren = true
rules.quote: Examine your app for places where relationships among elements are visual only.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Post accessibility notifications when content or layout changes to keep VoiceOver users informed.
rules.anti_pattern: isLoading = false // UI updates without notifying VoiceOver
rules.fix_swiftui: isLoading = false; AccessibilityNotification.Announcement("Data loaded").post()
rules.fix_uikit: UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, argument: "Data loaded")
rules.quote: It's crucial to report visible changes so VoiceOver and other assistive technologies can help people update their understanding of the content.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Identify headings, links, and content types to enable VoiceOver rotor navigation.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Section").font(.headline) // Heading not marked for rotor
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Section").font(.headline).accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)
rules.fix_uikit: headingLabel.accessibilityTraits = .header
rules.quote: You can help people navigate content in your app by identifying these elements to the rotor.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Provide forward and back navigation controls when web view displays multiple pages.
rules.anti_pattern:
let webView = WKWebView()
// No navigation buttons provided; users cannot traverse visited pages
rules.fix_swiftui: Add NavigationStack or custom back/forward buttons bound to WKWebView.goBack() and goForward() methods.
rules.fix_uikit: Add UIBarButtonItem instances to UINavigationBar calling webView.goBack() and webView.goForward() when canGoBack/canGoForward are true.
rules.quote: If people are likely to use your web view to visit multiple pages, allow forward and back navigation, and provide corresponding controls to initiate these features.

rules.heading: Overview
rules.rule: Do not replicate Safari browser functionality; use web views only for embedded content within app context.
rules.fix_swiftui: Limit web view to displaying specific embedded HTML or single-purpose web content; delegate general browsing to Safari via SFSafariViewController or ASWebAuthenticationSession.
rules.fix_uikit: Use SFSafariViewController for user-initiated web browsing; reserve WKWebView for app-controlled embedded content only.
rules.quote: Attempting to replicate the functionality of Safari in your app is unnecessary and discouraged.

rules.heading: System family widgets
rules.rule: Support only widget sizes appropriate to each platform per the system family widget size table.
rules.anti_pattern: let widget = WidgetConfiguration.stateless(kind: "MyWidget", provider: Provider()) { entry in MyWidgetView() }.supportedFamilies([.systemSmall, .systemExtraLarge]) // on iPhone, which doesn't support extra large
rules.fix_swiftui: .supportedFamilies([.systemSmall, .systemMedium, .systemLarge]) // for iPhone
rules.quote: The following table shows supported contexts for each system family widget size:

rules.heading: Accessory widgets
rules.rule: Accessory widgets appear only on Lock Screen of iPhone and iPad; accessory corner only on Apple Watch.
rules.anti_pattern: let widget = WidgetConfiguration.stateless(kind: "MyAccessory", provider: Provider()) { entry in MyAccessoryView() }.supportedFamilies([.accessoryCorner]) // on iPhone Lock Screen
rules.fix_swiftui: .supportedFamilies([.accessoryCircular, .accessoryInline, .accessoryRectangular]) // for iPhone/iPad Lock Screen
rules.quote: They appear on the following devices:

rules.heading: Appearances
rules.rule: Implement rendering modes (full-color, accented, vibrant) appropriate to widget context and platform.
rules.anti_pattern: struct MyWidget: Widget { var body: some WidgetConfiguration { StatelessConfiguration(kind: "MyWidget", provider: Provider()) { entry in MyWidgetView() } } } // ignores rendering mode requirements
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @Environment(\.widgetRenderingMode) to detect mode and adapt colors, opacity, and contrast accordingly.
rules.quote: Each appearance described above includes a rendering mode that depends on the platform and a person's appearance settings:

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Choose simple ideas directly related to app purpose; include timely, relevant content and functionality.
rules.anti_pattern: struct MyWidget: Widget { var body: some WidgetConfiguration { StatelessConfiguration(kind: "MyWidget", provider: Provider()) { entry in Image("AppIcon") } } } // replicates app icon with no additional value
rules.quote: Choose simple ideas that relate to your app's main purpose.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prefer dynamic information that changes throughout the day to encourage frequent viewing.
rules.anti_pattern: struct MyWidget: Widget { var body: some WidgetConfiguration { StatelessConfiguration(kind: "MyWidget", provider: Provider()) { entry in Text("Static Company Name") } } } // never changes
rules.quote: Prefer dynamic information that changes throughout the day.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer widgets in multiple sizes only when each size adds distinct value; avoid simply expanding smaller content.
rules.anti_pattern: .supportedFamilies([.systemSmall, .systemMedium, .systemLarge, .systemExtraLarge]) // all sizes show identical single data point
rules.fix_swiftui: .supportedFamilies([.systemSmall, .systemMedium]) // small shows price, medium adds chart
rules.quote: Offer widgets in multiple sizes when doing so adds value.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Balance information density: avoid sparse layouts and overly dense layouts; prioritize glanceability.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack(spacing: 1) { Text("A"); Text("B"); Text("C"); Text("D"); Text("E"); Text("F"); Text("G"); Text("H") } // 8 lines crammed into small widget
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) { Text("Current: 72°F").font(.headline); Text("High: 85°F").font(.caption) } // essential info only
rules.quote: Balance information density.

rules.heading: Updating widget content
rules.rule: Use system functionality to automatically refresh dates and times; preserve update opportunities.
rules.anti_pattern: struct MyProvider: TimelineProvider { func getTimeline(in context: Context, completion: @escaping (Timeline<Entry>) -> ()) { let entries = (0..<60).map { i in Entry(date: Date().addingTimeInterval(Double(i) * 60)) }; completion(Timeline(entries: entries, policy: .atEnd)) } } // manual date updates waste refresh budget
rules.fix_swiftui: Use @State and Timer to let system handle date refresh, or use .systemSmall with Text(entry.date, style: .time) for automatic updates.
rules.quote: Use system functionality to refresh dates and times in your widget.

rules.heading: Adding interactivity
rules.rule: Ensure widget interactions deep link to relevant app content, not generic app launch.
rules.anti_pattern: Button(action: { openURL(URL(string: "myapp://")!) }) { Text("Open") } // launches app root, not relevant detail
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: { openURL(URL(string: "myapp://stock/AAPL")!) }) { Text("AAPL: $150") } // deep links to stock detail
rules.quote: Ensure that a widget interaction opens your app at the right location.

rules.heading: Choosing margins and padding
rules.rule: Use standard 16-point margins for most widgets; use 11-point margins only for tight groupings.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { MyContent() }.padding(4) // too tight, cluttered appearance
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { MyContent() }.padding(16) // standard margin
rules.quote: Use the standard margin width for widgets — 16 points for most widgets — to avoid crowding their edges and creating a cluttered appearance.

rules.heading: Choosing margins and padding
rules.rule: Coordinate content corner radius with widget corner radius using ContainerRelativeShape.
rules.anti_pattern: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).fill(Color.blue) // hardcoded radius may not match widget
rules.fix_swiftui: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).fill(Color.blue).clipShape(ContainerRelativeShape()) // adapts to widget
rules.quote: Coordinate the corner radius of your content with the corner radius of the widget.

rules.heading: Displaying text in widgets
rules.rule: Avoid font sizes smaller than 11 points; use system font and SF Symbols for readability.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Updated: 3:45 PM").font(.system(size: 8)) // too small, unreadable
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Updated: 3:45 PM").font(.caption) // 11pt minimum
rules.quote: In general, display text using fonts at 11 points or larger.

rules.heading: Displaying text in widgets
rules.rule: Always use text elements and styles; never rasterize text to preserve VoiceOver accessibility.
rules.anti_pattern: Image(uiImage: renderTextAsImage("Hello")) // rasterized, not accessible
rules.fix_swiftui: Text("Hello").font(.system(.body)) // native text element
rules.quote: Avoid rasterizing text.

rules.heading: Using color
rules.rule: Convey meaning without relying solely on color; use text and iconography in addition to color.
rules.anti_pattern: HStack { Circle().fill(Color.red); Circle().fill(Color.green) } // color alone conveys status, not accessible
rules.fix_swiftui: HStack { Image(systemName: "xmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(.red); Text("Error") }
rules.quote: Convey meaning without relying on specific colors to represent information.

rules.heading: Full-color
rules.rule: Support light and dark appearances; use semantic system colors or asset variants for dynamic adaptation.
rules.anti_pattern: ZStack { Color.white; MyContent() } // hardcoded white, breaks in dark mode
rules.fix_swiftui: ZStack { Color(UIColor { $0.userInterfaceStyle == .dark ? UIColor.black : UIColor.white }); MyContent() }
rules.quote: Support light and dark appearances.

rules.heading: Accented
rules.rule: Group widget components into accented and primary groups using widgetAccentable modifier.
rules.anti_pattern: VStack { Text("Title"); Text("Value") } // no accent grouping applied
rules.fix_swiftui: VStack { Text("Title").widgetAccentable(false); Text("Value").widgetAccentable(true) }
rules.quote: Group widget components into an accented and a primary group.

rules.heading: Vibrant
rules.rule: In vibrant mode, use opaque grayscale values and sufficient contrast; render content at full opacity.
rules.anti_pattern: Image("myImage").opacity(0.5) // semi-transparent reduces vibrant effect
rules.fix_swiftui: Image("myImage") // full opacity; use white/light gray for prominent content
rules.quote: Render content like images, numbers, and text at full opacity.

rules.heading: Previews and placeholders
rules.rule: Design realistic previews and placeholder content that represent actual widget capabilities.
rules.anti_pattern: #Preview { MyWidget() } // blank or generic preview
rules.fix_swiftui: #Preview { MyWidget().previewContext(WidgetPreviewContext(family: .systemMedium)) } // with realistic data
rules.quote: Design a realistic preview to display in the widget gallery.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Windows must adapt fluidly to different sizes to support multitasking and multiwindow workflows.
rules.anti_pattern: struct ContentView: View { var body: some View { Text("Fixed width").frame(width: 400) } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use adaptive layouts with GeometryReader or .windowResizability(.contentMinSize) to respond to size changes.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement Auto Layout constraints or UITraitCollection observers to adapt to window size changes.
rules.quote: Make sure that your windows adapt fluidly to different sizes to support multitasking and multiwindow workflows.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Open new windows only when it meaningfully supports multitasking or context preservation, not as default behavior.
rules.anti_pattern: Button("View Details") { openWindowAction(id: "detail") } // Opens window for every tap
rules.fix_swiftui: Provide explicit user controls (context menu, File menu command) to open windows via OpenWindowAction.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIWindowScene.ActivationInteraction only for intentional user gestures, not automatic actions.
rules.quote: Avoid opening new windows as default behavior unless it makes sense for your app.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Offer users the option to view content in a new window via context menu or File menu.
rules.anti_pattern: // No menu option to open content in new window
rules.fix_swiftui: Add .contextMenu or File menu command with OpenWindowAction to let users choose window presentation.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement UIContextMenuInteraction or menu actions that trigger UIWindowScene.ActivationInteraction.
rules.quote: Consider letting people view content in a new window using a command in a context menu or in the File menu.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Never create custom window frames or controls; use system-provided windows exclusively.
rules.anti_pattern: struct CustomWindow: View { var body: some View { ZStack { RoundedRectangle().stroke() } } }
rules.fix_swiftui: Use native Window and Scene APIs; avoid custom frame drawing or control replication.
rules.fix_uikit: Use UIWindow and system-provided window controls; do not override window appearance.
rules.quote: Avoid making custom window frames or controls, and don't try to replicate the system-provided appearance.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use the term 'window' in user-facing content; avoid 'scene' or other implementation-specific terminology.
rules.anti_pattern: Text("Open this scene in a new view")
rules.fix_swiftui: Replace all user-facing references with 'window': Text("Open this window")
rules.fix_uikit: Use 'window' in UI labels, help text, and documentation.
rules.quote: Use the term window in user-facing content.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Position toolbar buttons inward from the leading edge to avoid overlap with windowed mode window controls.
rules.anti_pattern: ToolbarItem(placement: .navigationBarLeading) { Button("Action") {} } // Hides behind window controls
rules.fix_swiftui: Use .toolbar(placement: .automatic) or move buttons to .navigationBarTrailing or center positions.
rules.fix_uikit: Offset UIBarButtonItem from leading edge or use UIBarButtonItemGroup with flexible spacing.
rules.quote: Make sure window controls don't overlap toolbar items.

rules.heading: Tablet (iPadOS)
rules.rule: Support gesture-based window opening (e.g., pinch-to-expand) for intuitive multiwindow workflows.
rules.anti_pattern: // No gesture support for opening content in new window
rules.fix_swiftui: Implement gesture handlers that trigger OpenWindowAction.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement collectionView(_:sceneActivationConfigurationForItemAt:point:) or UIWindowScene.ActivationInteraction.
rules.quote: Consider letting people use a gesture to open content in a new window.

rules.heading: macOS window anatomy
rules.rule: Understand macOS window structure: frame (top, includes controls and toolbar) and body area (resizable edges).
rules.anti_pattern: // Placing controls in body area instead of frame
rules.fix_swiftui: Use native window APIs; frame elements are system-managed.
rules.fix_uikit: Use NSWindow and NSWindowController; do not manually position frame elements.
rules.quote: The frame of a window appears above the body area and can include window controls and a toolbar.

rules.heading: macOS window states
rules.rule: Ensure custom windows use system-defined appearances for main, key, and inactive states.
rules.anti_pattern: // Custom window styling that doesn't update when window state changes
rules.fix_swiftui: Use native Window APIs; system handles state-based appearance automatically.
rules.fix_uikit: Use NSWindow and observe window state changes to update appearance (title bar colors, vibrancy).
rules.quote: Make sure custom windows use the system-defined appearances.

rules.heading: macOS window states
rules.rule: Avoid placing critical information or actions in a bottom bar; users often hide the bottom edge.
rules.anti_pattern: // Critical save button in bottom bar where it may be hidden
rules.fix_swiftui: Place critical actions in toolbar or main content area.
rules.fix_uikit: Use status bar only for non-critical metadata; place actions in NSToolbar.
rules.quote: Avoid putting critical information or actions in a bottom bar, because people often relocate a window in a way that hides its bottom edge.

rules.heading: macOS window states
rules.rule: Use bottom bar only for small, content-related metadata; prefer inspector panels for extensive information.
rules.anti_pattern: // Large form or detailed settings in bottom bar
rules.fix_swiftui: Use split view with inspector on trailing side for detailed information.
rules.fix_uikit: Implement NSSplitViewController with inspector panel instead of bottom bar.
rules.quote: If you must include one, use it only to display a small amount of information directly related to a window's contents or to a selected item within it.

rules.heading: Getting started
rules.rule: Establish consistent app voice reflecting values; create and reference common terminology list.
rules.anti_pattern: Using inconsistent vocabulary across screens (e.g., 'Save' in one flow, 'Store' in another; mixing formal and casual tone unpredictably).
rules.quote: Create a list of common terms, and reference that list to keep your language consistent.

rules.heading: Getting started
rules.rule: Vary tone based on context and situational factors, not just voice.
rules.anti_pattern: Using identical tone for both error states and success states; same wording for critical alerts and celebratory confirmations.
rules.quote: Once you've established your app's voice, vary your tone based on the situation.

rules.heading: Getting started
rules.rule: Use simple, plain language avoiding jargon and gendered terminology for universal accessibility.
rules.anti_pattern: Using technical jargon ('instantiate', 'serialize'), gendered terms ('he/she'), or complex vocabulary in UI copy.
rules.quote: Choose simple, plain language and write with accessibility and localization in mind, avoiding jargon and gendered terminology.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Label buttons and links with verbs; avoid cute phrasing; use descriptive link text over 'Click here'.
rules.anti_pattern: Button labels like 'Let's do it!', 'Go!', or links saying 'Click here' instead of 'Send', 'Learn more about UX Writing'.
rules.fix_swiftui: Button(action: {}) { Text("Send") } instead of Button(action: {}) { Text("Let's do it!") }
rules.fix_uikit: button.setTitle("Send", for: .normal) instead of button.setTitle("Let's do it!", for: .normal)
rules.quote: When labeling buttons and links, it's almost always best to use a verb.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Apply consistent capitalization rules (title case or sentence case) per UI element type throughout app.
rules.anti_pattern: Mixing title case and sentence case for button labels; using title case for some alerts and sentence case for others.
rules.quote: Choose a style for each UI element type and use it consistently throughout your app — for example, title case for all alerts or sentence case for all headlines.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use consistent action labels across multi-step flows; begin with 'Get Started', end with 'Done'.
rules.anti_pattern: Using 'Next' in step 1, 'Continue' in step 2, 'Proceed' in step 3; ending with 'Finish' instead of 'Done'.
rules.quote: Begin with language like "Get Started" to indicate you're starting a flow.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Avoid possessive pronouns ('my', 'your'); use 'we' sparingly; maintain consistent perspective.
rules.anti_pattern: Using 'Your Favorites' instead of 'Favorites'; error message 'We're having trouble loading this content' instead of 'Unable to load content'.
rules.quote: Possessive pronouns like my and your are often unnecessary to establish context.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Use device-appropriate gesture terminology: 'tap' for touch devices, not 'click'.
rules.anti_pattern: Saying 'Click to select' on iPhone or iPad; using 'tap' in macOS documentation.
rules.quote: Make sure you describe gestures correctly on each device — for example, not saying "click" for a touch device like iPhone or iPad where you mean "tap."

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Provide clear next steps and actionable guidance on empty/blank screens.
rules.anti_pattern: Showing empty state with no explanation or call-to-action; displaying 'No items' without suggesting what user can do.
rules.quote: An empty screen can be daunting if it isn't obvious what to do next, so guide people on actions they can take, and give them a button or link to do so if possible.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Write error messages that avoid blame, explain the problem, and provide actionable solutions.
rules.anti_pattern: Error messages like 'That password is too short', 'Oops! Invalid input', or 'Don't use numbers or symbols'.
rules.quote: When an error message is necessary, display it as close to the problem as possible, avoid blame, and be clear about what someone can do to fix it.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Label settings clearly and simply; add explanations describing on-state behavior.
rules.anti_pattern: Vague setting labels like 'Advanced Options'; explaining both on and off states instead of just on-state.
rules.quote: Describe what it does when turned on, and people can infer the opposite.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Label text fields clearly; use hint/placeholder text showing format; display errors adjacent to field.
rules.anti_pattern: Unlabeled text fields; placeholder 'Enter text'; error message 'Invalid name' with no guidance; scolding tone 'Don't use numbers'.
rules.fix_swiftui: TextField("Your name", text: $name) with error displayed below
rules.fix_uikit: textField.placeholder = "name@example.com"; show error label next to field
rules.quote: Show errors right next to the field, and instruct people how to enter the information correctly, rather than scolding them for not following the rules.

rules.heading: Best practices
rules.rule: Prioritize information hierarchy; place most important content first; break complex ideas across screens.
rules.anti_pattern: Burying critical information below secondary details; cramming multiple unrelated ideas into one screen.
rules.quote: Pay attention to the order of elements on a screen, and put the most important information first.
